children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines)
<s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to the Blessed Lady, the Noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: ASP_1: sarvākārajñatācaryā prathamaḥ parivartaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter One: The Practice of Omniscience.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ, sarvairarhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravairniḥkleśairvaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñairājñairājāneyairmahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyairapahṛtabhārairanuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramiprāptairekaṃ pudgalaṃ sthāpayitvā yaduta āyuṣmantamānandam //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain, together with a great assembly of monks—twelve hundred and fifty monks in all, all of them <s>Arhats</s>, with <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) extinguished, free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), self-mastered, with minds well-liberated, with wisdom well-liberated, thoroughbreds, noble steeds, great <s>Nāgas</s>, who had done what was to be done, accomplished what was to be accomplished, laid down the burden, attained their own goal—

body.text: tatra khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthaviramāmantrayate sma - pratibhātu te subhūte bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitāmārabhya yathā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prajñāpāramitā niryāyuriti //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the Elder, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Let it occur to you, <s>Subhūti</s>, to expound the <s>Praj��āpāramitā</s> to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>—how the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> go forth in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitadabhavat - kimayamāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthavira ātmīyena svakena prajñāpratibhānabalādhānena svakena prajñāpratibhānabalādhiṣṭhānena bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitāmupadekṣyati utāho buddhānubhāveneti?
body.translated_text: Then the following thought occurred to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Will this Elder, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, expound the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> by his own power of wisdom and eloquence, by his own empowerment of wisdom and eloquence? Or will he do so through the <s>Buddha</s>'s supernatural power?"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya imamevarūpaṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - yatkiṃcidāyuṣman śāriputra bhagavataḥ śrāvakā bhāṣante deśayanti upadiśanti udīrayanti prakāśayanti saṃprakāśayanti, sa sarvastathāgatasya puruṣakāro veditavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yo hi tathāgatena dharmo deśitaḥ, tatra dharmadeśanāyāṃ śikṣamāṇāste tāṃ dharmatāṃ sākṣātkurvanti dhārayanti, tāṃ dharmatāṃ sākṣātkṛtya dhārayitvā yadyadeva bhāṣante, yadyadeva deśayanti, yadyadeva upadiśanti, yadyadevodīrayanti, yadyadeva
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s supernatural power, having perceived with his mind the mental deliberation in the mind of the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, said to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Whatever the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples) of the Blessed One speak, teach, instruct, utter, illuminate, and fully illuminate—all of that is to be understood as the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: prakāśayanti, yadyadeva saṃprakāśayanti, sarvaṃ taddharmatayā aviruddham / tathāgatadharmadeśanāyā eva āyuṣman śāriputra eṣa niṣyandaḥ yatte kulaputrā upadiśantastāṃ dharmatāṃ dharmatayā na virodhayanti //
body.translated_text: Whatever they illuminate, whatever they fully illuminate—all of that is not in conflict with the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>). It is indeed the outflow of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, O Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that those sons of good family, in their instruction, do not contradict that <s>dharmatā</s> by means of <s>dharmatā</s>."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena bhagavantametadavocat - yadbhagavānevamāha - pratibhātu te subhūte bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitāmārabhya yathā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ niryāyuriti / bodhisattvo bodhisattva iti yadidaṃ bhagavannucyate, katamasyaitadbhagavan dharmasyādhivacanaṃ yaduta bodhisattva iti? nāhaṃ bhagavaṃstaṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi yaduta bodhisattva iti / tamapyahaṃ bhagavan dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi yaduta prajñāpāramitā nāma / so 'haṃ bhagavan bodhisattvaṃ vā bodhisattvadharmaṃ vā avindan anupalabhamāno 'samanupaśyan, prajñāpāramitāmapyavindan anupalabhamāno 'samanupaśyan katamaṃ bodhisattvaṃ katamasyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadiṣyāmi anuśāsiṣyāmi? api tu khalu punarbhagavan sacedevaṃ bhāṣyamāṇe deśyamāne upadiśyamāne bodhisattvasya cittaṃ nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate na viṣīdati na viṣādamāpadyate, nāsya vipṛṣṭhībhavati mānasam, na bhagnapṛṣṭhībhavati, notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate, eṣa eva bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāmanuśāsanīyaḥ / eṣaivāsya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā veditavyā / eṣo 'vavādaḥ prajñāpāramitāyām / sacedevaṃ tiṣṭhati, eṣaivāsyāvavādānuśāsanī //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s supernatural power, said to the Blessed One: "The Blessed One has said: 'Let it occur to you, <s>Subhūti</s>, to expound the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>—how the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> go forth in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Now, O Blessed One, '<s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Bodhisattva</s>'—this is what is said. Of what <s>dharma</s>, O Blessed One, is this the designation?

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāvayatā evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yathā asau śikṣyamāṇastenāpi bodhicittena na manyeta / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi - taccittamacittam / prakṛtiścittasya prabhāsvarā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O Blessed One, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, should train thus: even while training, he should not conceive of that <s>bodhicitta</s> (thought of awakening). For what reason? Because that <s>citta</s> (mind) is <s>acitta</s> (non-mind). The nature of the mind is luminous (<s>prabhāsvarā</s>).

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte asti taccittaṃ yaccittamacittam? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat kiṃ punarāyuṣman śāriputra yā acittatā, tatra acittatāyāmastitā vā nāstitā vā vidyate vā upalabhyate vā? śāriputra āha - na hyetadāyuṣman subhūte /
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does that mind which is non-mind exist?" When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> replied to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "But, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that state of non-mind, can existence or non-existence be found or apprehended?" <s>Śāriputra</s> replied: "No indeed,

body.text: subhūtirāha - sacedāyuṣman śāriputra tatra acittatāyāmastitā vā nāstitā vā na vidyate vā nopalabhyate vā, api nu te yukta eṣa paryanuyogo bhavati yadāyuṣmān śāriputra evamāha - asti taccittaṃ yaccittamacittamiti? evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kā punareṣā āyuṣman subhūte acittatā? subhūtirāha - avikārā āyuṣman śāriputra avikalpā acittatā //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "If, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that state of non-mind, neither existence nor non-existence is found or apprehended, is it then appropriate for the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> to ask: 'Does that mind which is non-mind exist?'" When this was said, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> replied to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "What then, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is this

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmate subhūtaye sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhvāyuṣman subhūte / yathāpi nāma tvaṃ bhagavatā araṇāvihāriṇāmagratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭo nirdiśasi /
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> expressed his approval to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Well said, well said, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>! Rightly indeed has the Blessed One designated you as foremost among those who dwell in the <s>araṇā</s>-vihāra (abode of non-conflict), and you teach accordingly."

body.text: ataś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherupaparīkṣitavyaḥ, avirahitaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā veditavyaḥ / śrāvakabhūmāv api śikṣitukāmena iyameva
body.translated_text: Therefore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mah��sattva</s> who is <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible) from <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) should be examined [in this way], and a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should be understood as inseparable from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Even by one who wishes to train in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple) stage, this very

body.text: prajñāpāramitā śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā / ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yogamāpattavyam / pratyekabuddhabhūmāv api śikṣitukāmena iyameva prajñāpāramitā śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā / ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yogamāpattavyam / bodhisattvabhūmāv api śikṣitukāmena iyameva prajñāpāramitā śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā / ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyāmupāyakauśalyasamanvāgatena sarvabodhisattvadharmasamudāgamāya yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? ihaiva hi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vistareṇa sarvabodhisattvadharmā upadiṣṭāḥ, yatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyaṃ yogamāpattavyam / anuttarāyām api samyaksaṃbodhau śikṣitukāmena iyameva prajñāpāramitā śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā / ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyāmupāyakauśalyasamanvāgatena sarvabuddhadharmasamudāgamāya yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? ihaiva hi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vistareṇa sarvabuddha dharmā upadiṣṭāḥ, yatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyaṃ yogamāpattavyam //
body.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be heard, taken up, retained, recited, mastered, and propagated. One should train right here in the <s>Prajñ��pāramitā</s> and devote oneself to it. Even by one who wishes to train in the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage, this very <s>Prajñāp��ramitā</s> should be heard, taken up, retained, recited, mastered, and propagated. One should train right here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and devote oneself to it.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - yo 'haṃ bhagavan etadeva bodhisattvanāmadheyaṃ na vedmi nopalabhe na samanupaśyāmi, prajñāpāramitām api na vedmi nopalabhe na samanupaśyāmi / so 'haṃ bhagavan etadeva bodhisattvanāmadheyamavindan anupalabhamāno 'samanupaśyan prajñāpāramitām api avindan anupalabhamāno 'samanupaśyan katamaṃ bodhisattvaṃ katamasyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadiṣyāmi anuśāsiṣyāmi? etadeva bhagavan kaukṛtyaṃ syāt, yo 'haṃ vastvavindan anupalabhamāno 'samanupaśyan nāmadheyamātreṇa āyavyayaṃ kuryāṃ yaduta bodhisattva iti / api tu khalu punarbhagavaṃstad api nāmadheyaṃ na sthitaṃ nāsthitaṃ na viṣṭhitaṃ nāviṣṭhitam / tatkasya hetoḥ? avidyamānatvena tasya nāmadheyasya / evaṃ tannāmadheyaṃ na sthitaṃ nāsthitaṃ na viṣṭhitaṃ nāviṣṭhitam / sacedbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya evaṃ gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ deśyamānāyāmupadiśyamānāyāṃ cittaṃ nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate na viṣīdati na viṣādamāpadyate, nāsya vipṛṣṭhībhavati mānasam, na bhagnapṛṣṭhībhavati, notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate / adhimucyate 'dhyāśayena avirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā veditavyaḥ, sthito 'vinivartanīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau, susthito 'sthānayogena / punaraparaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayatā na rūpe sthātavyaṃ na vedanāyāṃ na saṃjñāyāṃ na saṃskāreṣu, na vijñāne sthātavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ? sacedrūpe tiṣṭhati, rūpābhisaṃskāre carati, na carati prajñāpāramitāyām / evaṃ sacedvedanāyāṃ saṃjñāyāṃ saṃskāreṣu / sacedvijñāne tiṣṭhati, vijñānābhisaṃskāre carati, na carati prajñāpāramitāyām / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi abhisaṃskāre caran prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇāti, nāpi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyate, nāpi prajñāpāramitāṃ paripūrayate / aparipūrayamāṇaḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ na niryāsyati
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, I do not find, do not apprehend, do not perceive this very designation '<s>Bodhisattva</s>'; and I also do not find, do not apprehend, do not perceive the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Not finding, not apprehending, not perceiving this very designation '<s>Bodhisattva</s>', and also not finding [the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]—

body.text: sarvajñatāyāmaparigṛhītaṃ parigṛhṇan / tatkasya hetoḥ? rūpaṃ hi aparigṛhītaṃ prajñāpāramitāyām / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ hi aparigṛhītaṃ prajñāpāramitāyām / yaś ca rūpasyāparigrahaḥ, na tadrūpam / evaṃ yo vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām / yo vijñānasyāparigrahaḥ, na tadvijñānam / sāpi prajñāpāramitā aparigṛhītā / evaṃ hyatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritavyam / ayaṃ ca bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sarvadharmāparigṛhīto nāma samādhirvipulaḥ puraskṛtaḥ apramāṇaniyato 'sādhāraṇaḥ / sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ sāpi sarvajñatā aparigṛhītā, na hi nimittato grahītavyā / sacennimittato grahītavyā abhaviṣyat, na ceha śreṇikaḥ parivrājakaḥ śraddhāmalapsyata / tatra hi śreṇikaḥ parivrājakaḥ sarvajñajñāne adhimucya śraddhānusārī prādeśikena jñānenāvatīrṇaḥ / so 'vatīrya na rūpaṃ parigṛhṇīte / evaṃ na vedanāṃ na saṃjñāṃ na saṃskārān / na vijñānaṃ parigṛhṇīte / nāpi tatra prītisukhena tajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / nādhyātmaṃ rūpasya tajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / na vahirdhā rūpasya tajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / nādhyātmabahirdhā rūpasya tajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / nāpyanyatra rūpāttajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / evaṃ nādhyātmaṃ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām / nādhyātmaṃ vijñānasya tajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / na vahirdhā vijñānasya tajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / nādhyātmavahirdhā vijñānasya tajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / nāpyanyatra vijñānāttajjñānaṃ samanupaśyati / atra padaparyāye śreṇikaḥ parivrājako 'dhimuktaḥ / so 'tra sarvatra śraddhānusārī sarvajñajñāne dharmatāṃ pramāṇīkṛtya evamadhimukta iti / tena na kaściddharmaḥ parigṛhītaḥ / nāpi sa kaściddharmo ya upalabdhaḥ, yaṃ gṛhṇīyānmuñcedvā / sa nirvāṇam api na manyate / iyam api bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā veditavyā yadrūpaṃ na parigṛhṇīte / evaṃ yadvedanāṃ saṃjñāṃ saṃskārān / yadvijñānaṃ na parigṛhṇīte / na cāntarā parinirvāti, aparipūrṇairdaśabhistathāgatabalaiścaturbhistathāgatavaiśāradyairaṣṭādaśabhiś ca āveṇikairbuddhadharmaiḥ / tasmādiyam api bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā veditavyā //
body.translated_text: grasping the ungraspable in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). For what reason? Form is indeed ungrasped in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). Likewise feeling, perception, and mental formations. Consciousness is indeed ungrasped in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And that which is the non-grasping of form—that is not form. Likewise that which is the non-grasping of feeling, perception, and mental formations. That which is the non-grasping of consciousness—that is not consciousness. That <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too is ungrasped. Thus indeed should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> here. And this is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called 'non-grasping of all <s>dharmas</s>'—vast, preeminent, immeasurably determined, and not shared with any <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones). That <s>sarvajñatā</s> too is ungrasped—it should not be grasped through signs. For if it were to be grasped through signs, then the wanderer <s>Śreṇika</s> would not have obtained faith here. For the wanderer <s>Śreṇika</s>, having aspired to the knowledge of the omniscient, as a faith-follower, descended with partial knowledge. Having descended, he does not grasp form. Likewise he does not grasp feeling, perception, or mental formations. He does not grasp consciousness. Nor does he see that knowledge there with joy and happiness. He does not see that knowledge internally with regard to form. He does not see that knowledge externally with regard to form. He does not see that knowledge both internally and externally with regard to form. Nor does he see that knowledge apart from form. Likewise he does not see it internally with regard to feeling, perception, or mental formations. He does not see that knowledge internally with regard to consciousness. He does not see that knowledge externally with regard to consciousness. He does not see that knowledge both internally and externally with regard to consciousness. Nor does he see that knowledge apart from consciousness. In this exposition of words, the wanderer <s>Śreṇika</s> has aspired. He is a faith-follower everywhere in the knowledge of the omniscient, having taken the nature of <s>dharmas</s> as his standard, and thus has aspired—therefore he has not grasped any <s>dharma</s>. Nor is there any <s>dharma</s> that is found, which he would grasp or release. He does not even conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, should be understood as the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>—that he does not grasp form, likewise that he does not grasp feeling, perception, or mental formations, that he does not grasp consciousness. Yet he does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the interval, with the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers unfulfilled, the four <s>Tathāgata</s> confidences, and the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. Therefore this too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, should be understood as the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayatā evamupaparīkṣitavyamevamupanidhyātavyam - katamaiṣā prajñāpāramitā? kasya caiṣā prajñāpāramitā? kiṃ yo dharmo na vidyate nopalabhyate, sā prajñāpāramiteti? sacedevamupaparīkṣamāṇaḥ evamupanidhyāyan nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate na viṣīdati na viṣādamāpadyate, nāsya vipṛṣṭhībhavati mānasam, na bhagnapṛṣṭhībhavati, notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate, avirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitayā veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, should examine thus, should reflect thus: 'What is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? And whose is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? Is it that a <s>dharma</s> that is not found, not apprehended—is that the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' If, examining thus, reflecting thus, he does not shrink back, does not withdraw, does not become dejected, does not fall into despondency, his mind does not turn away, his back does not break, he is not frightened, not terrified, does not fall into terror—then that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should be known as not separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kiṃ kāraṇamāyuṣman subhūte avirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitayā veditavyaḥ? yadā rūpameva virahitaṃ rūpasvabhāvena, evaṃ yadā vedanaiva saṃjñaiva saṃskārā eva, yadā vijñānameva virahitaṃ vijñānasvabhāvena, yadā prajñāpāramitaiva virahitā prajñāpāramitāsvabhāvena, yadā sarvajñataiva virahitā sarvajñatāsvabhāvena //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: For what reason, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> be known as not separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? When form itself is separated from the own-nature of form, when feeling itself, perception itself, mental formations themselves, when consciousness itself is separated from the own-nature of consciousness, when <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself is separated from the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, when <s>sarvajñatā</s> itself is separated from the own-nature of <s>sarvajñatā</s>?

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - etametadāyuṣman śāriputra evam etat / rūpamevāyuṣman śāriputra virahitaṃ rūpasvabhāvena / evaṃ vedanaiva saṃjñaiva saṃskārā eva / vijñānamevāyuṣman śāriputra virahitaṃ vijñānasvabhāvena / prajñāpāramitaiva āyuṣman śāriputra virahitā prajñāpāramitāsvabhāvena / sarvajñataiva āyuṣman śāriputra virahitā sarvajñatāsvabhāvena / prajñāpāramitālakṣaṇenāpi prajñāpāramitā virahitā / lakṣaṇasvabhāvenāpi lakṣaṇaṃ virahitam / lakṣyasvabhāvenāpi lakṣyaṃ virahitam / svabhāvalakṣaṇenāpi svabhāvo virahitaḥ //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, just so. Form itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is separated from the own-nature of form. Likewise feeling itself, perception itself, and mental formations themselves. Consciousness itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is separated from the own-nature of consciousness. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is separated from the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. <s>Sarvajñatā</s> itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is separated from the own-nature of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is separated even from the characteristic of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A characteristic is separated even from the own-nature of a characteristic. The characterized is separated even from the own-nature of the characterized. Own-nature is separated even from the characteristic of own-nature.

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'tra śikṣiṣyate, sa niryāsyati sarvajñatāyām? āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - evametadāyuṣman śāriputra, evam etat / yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'tra śikṣiṣyate, sa niryāsyati sarvajñatāyām / tatkasya hetoḥ? ajātā hyanirjātā hyāyuṣman śāriputra sarvadharmāḥ / evaṃ carata āyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sarvajñatā āsannībhavati / yathā yathā sarvajñatā āsannībhavati, tathā tathā sattvaparipācanāya kāyacittapariśuddhirlakṣaṇapariśuddhiḥ buddhakṣetraśuddhiḥ / buddhaiś ca samavadhānaṃ bhavati / evaṃ ca punarāyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran sarvajñatāyā āsannībhavati //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, will the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who trains in this emerge in <s>sarvajñatā</s>? The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said: Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, just so. The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who trains in this will emerge in <s>sarvajñatā</s>. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are unborn and un-emerged. When the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices thus, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>sarvajñatā</s> draws near. As <s>sarvajñatā</s> draws near, so too does the purification of body and mind for the ripening of beings, the purification of marks, the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And there comes an encounter with <s>Buddhas</s>. Thus indeed, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> draws near to <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

body.text: punaraparamāyuṣmān subhūtirbodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamārabhyaivamāha - sacedrūpe carati, nimitte carati / sacedrūpanimitte carati, nimitte carati / sacedrūpaṃ nimittamiti carati, nimitte carati / sa cedrūpasyotpāde carati, nimitte carati / sacedrūpasya nirodhe carati, nimitte carati / sacedrūpasya vināśe carati, nimitte carati / sacedrūpaṃ śūnyamiti carati, nimitte carati / ahaṃ carāmīti carati, nimitte carati / ahaṃ bodhisattva iti carati, nimitte carati / ahaṃ bodhisattva iti hyupalambha eva sa carati / evaṃ sacedvidanāyāṃ saṃjñāyāṃ saṃskāreṣu / sacedvijñāne carati, nimitte carati / sacedvijñānanimitte carati, nimitte carati sacedvijñānaṃ nimittamiti carati, nimitte carati / sacedvijñānasyotpāde carati, nimitte carati / sacedvijñānasya nirodhe carati, nimitte carati / sacedvijñānasya vināśe carati, nimitte carati / sacedvijñānaṃ śūnyamiti carati, nimitte carati / ahaṃ carāmīti carati, nimitte carati / ahaṃ bodhisattva iti carati, nimitte carati / ahaṃ bodhisattva iti hyupalambha eva sa carati / sacetpunarasyaivaṃ bhavati - ya evaṃ carati, sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, sa prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayatīti, nimitta eva sa carati / ayaṃ bodhisattvo 'nupāyakuśalo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, speaking with reference to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, said thus: If he practices in form, he practices in signs. If he practices in the sign of form, he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'form is a sign,' he practices in signs. If he practices in the arising of form, he practices in signs. If he practices in the cessation of form, he practices in signs. If he practices in the destruction of form, he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'form is empty,' he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'I am practicing,' he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'I am a <s>bodhisattva</s>,' he practices in signs. For 'I am a <s>bodhisattva</s>'—that is indeed practicing in apprehension. Likewise, if in feeling, in perception, in mental formations. If he practices in consciousness, he practices in signs. If he practices in the sign of consciousness, he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'consciousness is a sign,' he practices in signs. If he practices in the arising of consciousness, he practices in signs. If he practices in the cessation of consciousness, he practices in signs. If he practices in the destruction of consciousness, he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'consciousness is empty,' he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'I am practicing,' he practices in signs. If he practices thinking 'I am a <s>bodhisattva</s>,' he practices in signs. For 'I am a <s>bodhisattva</s>'—that is indeed practicing in apprehension. If furthermore he thinks 'one who practices thus is practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he is cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'—he is indeed practicing in signs. This <s>bodhisattva</s> should be known as unskilled in means.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kathaṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte caran bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - sacedāyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na rūpe carati, na rūpanimitte carati, na rūpaṃ nimittamiti carati, na rūpasyotpāde carati, na rūpasya nirodhe
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: But how then, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: If, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not practice in form, does not practice in the sign of form, does not practice thinking 'form is a sign,' does not practice in the arising of form, does not practice in the cessation of form,

body.text: carati, na rūpasya vināśe carati, na rūpaṃ śūnyamiti carati, nāhaṃ carāmīti carati, nāhaṃ bodhisattva iti carati / evaṃ sacenna vedanāyāṃ na saṃjñāyāṃ na saṃskāreṣu / sacenna vijñāne carati, na vijñānanimitte carati, na vijñānaṃ nimittamiti carati, na vijñānasyotpāde carati, na vijñānasya nirodhe carati, na vijñānasya vināśe carati, na vijñānaṃ śūnyamiti carati, nāhaṃ carāmīti carati, nāhaṃ bodhisattva iti carati / sacetpunarnāsyaivaṃ bhavati - ya evaṃ carati, sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, sa prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayatīti / evaṃ caran bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām / sa hi caraṃścarāmīti nopaiti, na carāmīti nopaiti, carāmi ca na carāmi ceti nopaiti, naiva carāmi na na carāmīti nopaiti, cariṣyāmīti nopaiti, na cariṣyāmīti nopaiti, cariṣyāmi ca na cariṣyāmi ceti nopaiti, naiva cariṣyāmi na cariṣyāmīti nopaiti / tatkasya hetornopaiti? sarvadharmā hyanupagatā anupāttāḥ / ayamucyate sarvadharmānupādāno nāma samādhirbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya, vipulaḥ puraskṛto 'pramāṇaniyato 'sādhāraṇaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ / anenaiva samādhinā viharan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate //
body.translated_text: does not practice in the destruction of form, does not practice thinking 'form is empty,' does not practice thinking 'I am practicing,' does not practice thinking 'I am a <s>bodhisattva</s>.' Likewise if he does not [practice] in feeling, in perception, in mental formations. If he does not practice in consciousness, does not practice in the sign of consciousness, does not practice thinking 'consciousness is a sign,' does not practice in the arising of consciousness, does not practice in the cessation of consciousness, does not practice in the destruction of consciousness, does not practice thinking 'consciousness is empty,' does not practice thinking 'I am practicing,' does not practice thinking 'I am a <s>bodhisattva</s>.' If furthermore he does not think 'one who practices thus is practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he is cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'—thus the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For practicing thus, he does not arrive at 'I am practicing,' does not arrive at 'I am not practicing,' does not arrive at 'I am both practicing and not practicing,' does not arrive at 'I am neither practicing nor not practicing,' does not arrive at 'I shall practice,' does not arrive at 'I shall not practice,' does not arrive at 'I shall both practice and not practice,' does not arrive at 'I shall neither practice nor not practice.' For what reason does he not arrive? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are unapproached and unappropriated. This is called the <s>samādhi</s> of non-appropriation of all <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>—vast, preeminent, immeasurably determined, and not shared with any <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Abiding in just this <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> quickly attains unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: buddhānubhāvena āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthavira evamāha - vyākṛto 'yaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pūrvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, yo 'nena samādhinā viharati / sa tam api samādhiṃ na samanupaśyati, na ca tena samādhinā manyate - ahaṃ samāhitaḥ, ahaṃ samādhiṃ samāpatsye, ahaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadye, ahaṃ samādhisamāpannaḥ, iti, evaṃ tasya sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ na saṃvidyate //
body.translated_text: By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the elder, spoke thus: This <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, has been predicted by the former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones for unsurpassed perfect awakening—the one who abides in this <s>samādhi</s>. He does not even perceive that <s>samādhi</s>, nor does he think through that <s>samādhi</s>: 'I am concentrated,' 'I shall enter the <s>samādhi</s>,' 'I am entering the <s>samādhi</s>,' 'I have entered the <s>samādhi</s>.' Thus for him, nothing whatsoever in any way is found.

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - katamenāyuṣman subhūte samādhinā viharan bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairvyākriyate 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? śakyaḥ sa samādhirdarśayitum? subhūtirāha - no hīdamāyuṣman śāriputra / tatkasya hetoḥ? tam api hi sa kulaputraḥ samādhiṃ na jānāti, na saṃjānīte / āyuṣmān śāriputra āha - na jānāti na saṃjānīte ityāyuṣman subhūte vadasi? āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - na jānāti na saṃjānīte ityāyuṣman śāriputra vadāmi / tatkasya hetorna jānāti na saṃjānīte? avidyamānatvena tasya samādhestaṃ samādhiṃ na jānāti na saṃjānīte / atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmate subhūtaye sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu subhūte / evametatsubhūte, evam etat / yathāpi nāma tathāgatānubhāvena te pratibhāti, tathāgatādhiṣṭhānenopadiśasi / evaṃ cātra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ? evaṃ hi śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣate //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Abiding in which <s>samādhi</s>, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones? Can that <s>samādhi</s> be shown? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. For what reason? Because that son of good family does not even know or recognize that <s>samādhi</s>. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said: You say, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, 'does not know, does not recognize'? The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said: I say, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, 'does not know, does not recognize.' For what reason does he not know, not recognize? Because that <s>samādhi</s> is non-existent—he does not know or recognize that <s>samādhi</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave his approval to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Well done, well done, <s>Subhūti</s>! Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, just so. As indeed the inspired utterance comes to you through the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s power, so you teach through the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment. And thus the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should train here. For what reason? Because training thus, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantametadavocat - evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bhagavan bodhisattvo
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: Training thus, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the <s>bodhisattva</s>

body.text: mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣate? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣate //
body.translated_text: <s>mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: Training thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantametadavocat - evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ katamasmin dharme śikṣate? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na kasmiṃściddharme śikṣate / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi te śāriputra dharmāstathā saṃvidyante yathā bālapṛthagjanā aśrutavanto 'bhiniviṣṭāḥ / āyuṣmān śāriputra āha - kathaṃ tarhi te bhagavan saṃvidyante? bhagavānāha - yathā śāriputra na saṃvidyante, tathā saṃvidyante evamavidyamānāḥ / tenocyante avidyeti / tān bālapṛthagjanā aśrutavanto 'bhiniviṣṭāḥ / tairasaṃvidyamānāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kalpitāḥ / te tān kalpayitvā dvayorantayoḥ saktāḥ tān dharmānna jānanti na paśyanti / tasmātte 'saṃvidyamānān sarvadharmān kalpayanti / kalpayitvā dvāvantāvabhiniviśante abhiniviśya tannidānamupalambhaṃ niśritya atītān dharmān kalpayanti, anāgatān dharmān kalpayanti, pratyutpannān dharmān kalpayanti te kalpayitvā nāmarūpe 'bhiniviṣṭāḥ / tairasaṃvidyamānāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kalpitāḥ / te tānasaṃvidyamānān sarvadharmān kalpayanto yathābhūtaṃ mārgaṃ na jānanti na paśyanti / yathābhūtaṃ mārgamajānanto 'paśyanto na niryānti traidhātukāt, na budhyante bhūtakoṭim / tena te bālā iti saṃjñāṃ gacchanti / te satyaṃ dharmaṃ na śraddhadhati / na khalu punaḥ śāriputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā kaṃciddharmamabhiniviśante //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in this way, in what <s>dharma</s> does he train?" When this was said, the Blessed One replied to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "When training in this way, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not train in any <s>dharma</s>. For what reason? Because those <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, do not exist in the way that—

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantametadavocat - evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate? bhagavānāha - evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyām api na śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvadharmeṣu śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate, sarvajñatāyā āsannībhavati, sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyati //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in this way, does he train in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)?" The Blessed One replied: "When training in this way, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not train even in <s>sarvajñatā</s>. When training in this way, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in all <s>dharmas</s>. When training in this way—

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - yo bhagavan evaṃ paripṛcchet - kimayaṃ māyāpuruṣāḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣiṣyate, sarvajñatāyā āsannībhaviṣyati, sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyatīti? tasya bhagavan evaṃ paripṛcchataḥ kathaṃ nirdeṣṭavyaṃ syāt? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - tena hi subhūte tvāmevātra pratiprakṣyāmi / yathā te kṣamate, tathā vyākuryāḥ / sādhu bhagavannityāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavānetadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte anyā sā māyā, anyattadrūpam, anyā sā māyā, anyā sā vedanā / anyā sā saṃjñā, anye te saṃskārāḥ / anyā sā māyā, anyattadvijñānam? subhūtirāha - na hyetadbhagavan / na hi bhagavan anyā sā māyā anyattadrūpam / rūpameva bhagavan māyā, māyaiva rūpam / na hi bhagavan anyā sā māyā anyā sā vedanā, anyā sā saṃjñā anye te saṃskārāḥ / vedanā saṃjñā
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: 'Will this illusory person train in <s>sarvajñatā</s>, draw near to <s>sarvajñatā</s>, go forth in <s>sarvajñatā</s>?'—O Blessed One, when asked thus, how should it be explained?" When this was said, the Blessed One replied to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Then,

body.text: saṃskārā eva bhagavan māyā, māyaiva vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / na bhagavan anyā sā māyā anyattadvijñānam / vijñānameva bhagavan māyā, māyaiva vijñānam //
body.translated_text: the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), O Blessed One, are indeed illusion; illusion is indeed feeling, perception, and formations. O Blessed One, illusion is not other than consciousness, nor is consciousness other than illusion. Consciousness itself, O Blessed One, is illusion; illusion itself is consciousness."

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte atraiṣāṃ saṃjñā samajñā prajñaptirvyavahāraḥ pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu yaduta bodhisattva iti? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata / tena hi bhagavan bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñapāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇena māyāpuruṣeṇeva śikṣitavyaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tatkasya hetoḥ? sa eva hi bhagavan māyāpuruṣo dhārayitavyo yaduta pañcopādānaskandhāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan māyopamaṃ rūpamuktaṃ bhagavatā / yacca rūpaṃ tatṣaḍindriyaṃ te pañca skandhāḥ / tathā hi bhagavan māyopamā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārā uktāḥ / tathā hi bhagavan māyopamaṃ vijñānamuktaṃ bhagavatā / yacca vijñānaṃ tatṣaḍindriyaṃ te pañca skandhāḥ / mā bhagavan navayānasaṃprasthitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā utrasiṣuḥ saṃtrasiṣuḥ saṃtrāsamāpatsyante / bhagavānāha - yadi subhūte navayānasaṃprasthitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ pāpamitrahastagatā bhaviṣyanti, utrasiṣyanti saṃtrasiṣyanti saṃtrāsamāpatsyante / atha cetsubhūte navayānasaṃprasthitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kalyāṇamitrahastagatā bhaviṣyanti, notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is the concept, designation, convention, and verbal usage '<s>Bodhisattva</s>' [to be found] in the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging)?" When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> replied to the Blessed One: "So it is, Blessed One; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>. Therefore, O Blessed One, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, when training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, like an illusory person—"

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - kāni punarbhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kalyāṇamitrāṇi veditavyāni? bhagavānāha - ya enaṃ pāramitāsu avavadanti anuśāsati / ye 'smai mārakarmāṇyupadiśanti / evaṃ māradoṣā boddhavyāḥ - ime māradoṣāḥ / evaṃ mārakarmāṇi boddhavyāni - imāni mārakarmāṇi / tāni tvayā buddhvā vivarjayitavyānīti / imāni subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhasya mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya mahāyānasamārūḍhasya kalyāṇamitrāṇi veditavyāni / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - yadbhagavānevamāha - imāni subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhasya mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya mahāyānasamārūḍhasya kalyāṇamitrāṇi veditavyānīti / yacca bodhisattvo mahāsattva iti bhagavannucyate, tatra bodhisattva iti bhagavan kaḥ padārtha? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - apadārthaḥ subhūte bodhisattvapadārthaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvadharmāṇāṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'saktatāyāṃ śikṣate / sarvadharmāṇāṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nubodhanārthena asaktatāyāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / bodhyarthena tu subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate / subhūtirāha - yatpunarbhagavānevamāha - bodhisattvo mahāsattva iti, kena kāraṇena bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate? bhagavānāha - mahataḥ sattvarāśermahataḥ sattvanikāyasya agratāṃ kārayiṣyati, tenārthena bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "What, O Blessed One, should be understood as the spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>?" The Blessed One replied: "Those who instruct and teach him in the <s>Pāramitās</s>. Those who point out to him the deeds of <s>Māra</s>. 'The faults of <s>Māra</s> should be understood thus—these are <s>Māra</s>'s faults. The deeds of <s>Māra</s> should be understood thus—these are <s>Māra</s>'s deeds.'"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantametadavocat - mamāpi bhagavan pratibhātiyenārthena bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate / bhagavānāha - pratibhātu te śāriputra yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase / āyuṣmān śāriputra āha - mahatyā ātmadṛṣṭyāḥ sattvadṛṣṭyāḥ jīvadṛṣṭyāḥ pudgaladṛṣṭyāḥ
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Blessed One: "I too, O Blessed One, have an insight as to the meaning in which a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> is so called." The Blessed One said: "Let it be spoken, <s>Śāriputra</s>, now that you consider it the right time." The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said: "It is for the abandonment of the great [wrong] views—the view of self, the view of a being, the view of a life-force, the view of a person,

body.text: bhavadṛṣṭyāḥ vibhavadṛṣṭyāḥ ucchedadṛṣṭyāḥ śāśvatadṛṣṭyāḥ svakāyadṛṣṭyāḥ, etāsāmevamādyānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ prahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyatīti, tenārthena bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate / atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - mamāpi bhagavan pratibhāti yenārthena bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate / bhagavānāha - pratibhātu te subhūte yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase / subhūtirāha - bodhisattvo mahāsattva iti bhagavannucyate / yad api tadbhagavan bodhicittaṃ sarvajñatācittamanāsravaṃ cittamasamaṃ cittaṃ asamasamaṃ cittamasādhāraṇaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ, tatrāpi citte asakto 'paryāpannaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tatsarvajñatācittamanāsravamaparyāpannaṃ tat, yad api tatsarvajñatācittamanāsravamaparyāpannam / tatrāpi citte asakto 'paryāpannaḥ / tenārthena bodhisattvo mahāsattva iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati //
body.translated_text: the view of existence, the view of non-existence, the view of annihilation, the view of eternalism, the view of a personal body—it is for the abandonment of these and such [wrong] views that he will teach the <s>Dharma</s>; in this sense, he is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>." Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "I too, O Blessed One, have an insight as to the meaning in which a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> is so called—"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kena kāraṇena āyuṣman subhūte tatrāpi citte asakto 'paryāpannaḥ? subhūtirāha - acittatvādāyuṣman śāriputra tatrāpi citte asakto 'paryāpannaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "For what reason, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are you unattached and unbound even to that mind?" <s>Subhūti</s> replied: "Because of the non-mind nature (<s>acittatva</s>), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, one is unattached and unbound even to that mind."

body.text: śāriputra āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte asti taccittaṃ yaccittamacittam? subhūtirāha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman śāriputra tatra acittatāyāmastitā vā nāstitā vā vidyate vā upalabhyate vā? śāriputra āha - no hīdamāyuṣman subhūte / subhūtirāha - tadyadi āyuṣman śāriputra tatra acittatāyāmastitā vā nāstitā vā na vidyate vā nopalabhyate vā, tatkathamāyuṣmān śāriputra evamāha - asti taccittaṃ yaccittamacittamiti? śāriputra āha - sādhu sādhu āyuṣman subhūte / yathāpi nāma tvaṃ bhagavatā araṇāvihāriṇāmagratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭo nirdiśasi //
body.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: "But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does that mind which is non-mind exist?" <s>Subhūti</s> replied: "But, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that state of non-mind, can existence or non-existence be found or apprehended?" <s>Śāriputra</s> said: "No indeed, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>." <s>Subhūti</s> replied: "If, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that state of non-mind, neither existence nor non-existence is found or apprehended—"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputro bhagavantametadavocat - mahāsattvo mahāsattva iti yadidaṃ bhagavannucyate, mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhaḥ sa sattvaḥ / mahāyānasaṃprasthito mahāyānasamārūḍhaś ca sa sattvaḥ / tasmātsa mahāsattvo mahāsattva iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> said to the Blessed One: "'<s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Mahāsattva</s>'—this is what is said, O Blessed One. That being is one who has girded on the great armor. That being has set out in the Great Vehicle and has mounted the Great Vehicle. Therefore he is reckoned as a '<s>Mahāsattva</s>.'"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddho mahāyānasaṃnaddha iti yadidaṃ bhagavannucyate, kiyatā bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddho bhavati ? bhagavānāha - iha subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaivaṃ bhavati - aprameyā mayā sattvāḥ parinirvāpayitavyā iti / asaṃkhyeyā mayā sattvāḥ parinirvāpayitavyā iti / na ca te santi yairye parinirvāpayitavyā iti / sa tāṃstāvataḥ sattvān parinirvāpayati / na ca sa kaścitsattvo yaḥ parinirvṛto yena ca parinirvāpito bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? dharmataiṣā subhūte dharmāṇāṃ māyādharmatāmupādāya syāt / yathāpi nāma subhūte dakṣo māyākaro vā māyākārāntevāsī vā caturmahāpathe mahāntaṃ janakāyamabhinirmimīte / abhinirmāya tasyaiva mahato janakāyasyāntardhānaṃ kuryāt / tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu tatra kenacitkaściddhato vā mṛto vā nāśito vā antarhito vā? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - evameva subhūte bodhisattvo
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "'Girded with the great armor, girded with the Great Vehicle'—this is what is said, O Blessed One. To what extent, O Blessed One, is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> girded with the great armor?" The Blessed One replied: "Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> thinks thus: 'Immeasurable are the beings who must be led by me to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>'—

body.text: mahāsattvo 'prameyānasaṃkhyeyān sattvān parinirvāpayati / na ca sa kaścitsattvo yaḥ parinirvṛto yena ca parinirvāpito bhavati / sacedbodhisattvo mahāsattva imaṃ nirdeśamevaṃ nirdiśyamānaṃ śrutvā notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate, iyatā ayaṃ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddho veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: the <s>Mahāsattva</s> leads immeasurable, innumerable beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Yet there is no being whatsoever who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> or by whom [another] has been led to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, upon hearing this exposition being thus expounded, does not become frightened, terrified, or alarmed—to this extent, <s>Subhūti</s>, is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> girded with the great armor.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - yathāhaṃ bhagavan bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, tathā asaṃnāhasaṃnaddho batāyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo veditavyaḥ / bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / asaṃnāhasaṃnaddho batāyaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo veditavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? akṛtā hi subhūte sarvajñatā avikṛtā anabhisaṃskṛtā / te 'pi sattvā akṛtā avikṛtā anabhisaṃskṛtāḥ, yeṣāṃ sattvānāmarthāya ayaṃ saṃnāhasaṃnaddhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "As I understand the meaning of the Blessed One's words, O Blessed One, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should be understood as one who has donned the armor of non-armor." The Blessed One said: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should be understood as one who has donned the armor of non-armor. For what reason? Because <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), O <s>Subhūti</s>, is uncreated, unaltered, and unconditioned. And those beings too are uncreated, unaltered, and unconditioned—those beings for whose sake he has donned this armor."

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan rūpamabaddhamamuktam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / tathā hi bhagavan vijñānamabaddhamamuktam / rūpatathatāpi bhagavan abaddhā amuktā / evaṃ vedanātathatāpi saṃjñātathatāpi saṃskāratathatāpi / vijñānatathatāpi bhagavan abaddhā amuktā //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "So it is, O Blessed One; so it is, O <s>Sugata</s>. For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, <s>rūpa</s> (form) is unbound and unreleased. Likewise <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), and <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). Because, O Blessed One, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is unbound and unreleased. The <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of <s>rūpa</s> too, O Blessed One, is unbound and unreleased. Likewise the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>vedanā</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃjñā</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃskāras</s>. The <s>tathatā</s> of <s>vijñāna</s> too, O Blessed One, is unbound and unreleased."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - rūpamāyuṣman subhūte abaddhamamuktamiti vadasi / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānamāyuṣman subhūte abaddhamamuktamiti vadasi / rūpatathatāpi āyuṣman subhūte abaddhā amukteti vadasi / evaṃ vedanātathatāpi saṃjñātathatāpi saṃskāratathatāpi / vijñānatathatāpyāyuṣman subhūte abaddhā amukteti vadasi / atha katamattadāyuṣman subhūte rūpaṃ yadrūpamabaddhamamuktamiti vadasi? evaṃ katamā sā vedanā, katamā sā saṃjñā, katame te saṃskārāḥ? katamattadāyuṣman subhūte vijñānaṃ yadvijñānamabaddhamamuktamiti vadasi? katamā sā āyuṣman subhūte rūpatathatā yā rūpatathatāpyabaddhā amukteti vadasi? evaṃ katamā sā vedanātathatā saṃjñātathatā saṃskāratathatā? katamā sā āyuṣman subhūte vijñānatathatā yā vijñānatathatāpyabaddhā amukteti vadasi? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇaṃ maitrāyaṇīputrametadavocat - yadāyuṣman pūrṇa māyāpuruṣasya rūpaṃ tadabaddhamamuktam / evaṃ yā māyāpuruṣasya vedanā, yā māyāpuruṣasya saṃjñā, ye māyāpuruṣasya saṃskārāḥ / yadāyuṣman pūrṇa māyāpuruṣasya vijñānaṃ tadabaddhamamuktam / yā āyuṣman pūrṇa māyāpuruṣasya rūpatathatā sā abaddhā amuktā / evaṃ yā māyāpuruṣasya vedanātathatā saṃjñātathatā saṃskāratathatā / yā āyuṣman pūrṇa māyāpuruṣasya vijñānatathatā sā abaddhā amuktā / tatkasya hetoḥ? asadbhūtatvādabaddhā amuktā, viviktatvādabaddhā amuktā, anutpannatvādabaddhā amuktā / ayaṃ sa bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhasya mahāyānasaṃprasthitasya mahāyānasamārūḍhasya mahāsaṃnāho 'saṃnāhaḥ / evamukte āyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputrastūṣṇīmabhūt //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "You say, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, that <s>rūpa</s> (form) is unbound and unreleased. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, and <s>saṃskāras</s>. You say, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, that <s>vijñāna</s> is unbound and unreleased. You say, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, that the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>rūpa</s> is unbound and unreleased. Likewise the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>vedanā</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃjñā</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃskāras</s>. You say, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, that the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>vijñāna</s> is unbound and unreleased. But what is that <s>rūpa</s>, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, which you say is unbound and unreleased? Likewise what is that <s>vedanā</s>, what is that <s>saṃjñā</s>, what are those <s>saṃskāras</s>? What is that <s>vijñāna</s>, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, which you say is unbound and unreleased? What is that <s>tathatā</s> of <s>rūpa</s>, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, which you say is unbound and unreleased? Likewise what is that <s>tathatā</s> of <s>vedanā</s>, <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃskāras</s>? What is that <s>tathatā</s> of <s>vijñāna</s>, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, which you say is unbound and unreleased?" When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>: "The <s>rūpa</s> of a magical person (<s>māyā-puruṣa</s>), Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>—that is unbound and unreleased. Likewise the <s>vedanā</s> of a magical person, the <s>saṃjñā</s> of a magical person, the <s>saṃskāras</s> of a magical person. The <s>vijñāna</s> of a magical person, Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>—that is unbound and unreleased. The <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>rūpa</s> of a magical person, Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>—that is unbound and unreleased. Likewise the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>vedanā</s> of a magical person, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃjñā</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃskāras</s>. The <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>vijñāna</s> of a magical person, Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>—that is unbound and unreleased. For what reason? Because, being unreal, it is unbound and unreleased; because, being isolated, it is unbound and unreleased; because, being unarisen, it is unbound and unreleased. This is the great armor of non-armor of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who has donned the great armor, who has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, who has mounted the <s>Mahāyāna</s>." When this was said, the Venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> remained silent.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - evaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "Thus, O Blessed One, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>,

body.text: mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhaḥ san mahāyānasaṃprasthito mahāyānasamārūḍho bhavati / katamacca tanmahāyānam? kathaṃ vā tatsaṃprasthito veditavyaḥ? kuto vā tanmahāyānaṃ niryāsyati? kena vā tanmahāyānaṃ saṃprasthitam? kva vā tanmahāyānaṃ sthāsyati? ko vā anena mahāyānena niryāsyati? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - mahāyānamiti subhūte aprameyatāyā etadadhivacanam / aprameyamiti subhūte apramāṇatvena / yad api subhūte evaṃ vadasi - kathaṃ vā tatsaṃprasthito veditavyaḥ? kuto vā tanmahāyānaṃ niryāsyati? kena vā tanmahāyānaṃ saṃprasthitam? kva vā tanmahāyānaṃ sthāsyati? ko vā anena mahāyānena niryāsyatīti? pāramitābhiḥ saṃprasthitaḥ / traidhātukānniryāsyati / yenārambaṇaṃ tena saṃprasthitam / sarvajñatāyāṃ sthāsyati / bodhisattvo mahāsattvo niryāsyati, api tu khalu punarna kutaścinniryāsyati / na kenāpi saṃprasthitam / na kvacitsthāsyati / api tu sthāsyati sarvajñatāyāmasthānayogena / nāpi kaścittena mahāyānena niryāto nāpi niryāsyati nāpi niryāti / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaś ca niryāyāt, yena ca niryāyāt, ubhāvetau dharmau na vidyete nopalabhyete / evamavidyamāneṣu sarvadharmeṣu katamo dharmaḥ katamena dharmeṇa niryāsyati? evaṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāyānasaṃnaddho mahāyānasaṃprasthito mahāyānasamārūḍho bhavati //
body.translated_text: having donned the great armor, has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and mounted the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. But what is that <s>Mahāyāna</s>? And how is one to be understood as having set forth in it? And from where will that <s>Mahāyāna</s> go forth? And by whom has that <s>Mahāyāna</s> been set forth? And where will that <s>Mahāyāna</s> stand? And who will go forth by this <s>Mahāyāna</s>?" When this was said, the Blessed One said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "'<s>Mahāyāna</s>' (<s>Great Vehicle</s>), O <s>Subhūti</s>—this is a designation for immeasurability. 'Immeasurable,' O <s>Subhūti</s>, because it is beyond measure. As for your question: 'How is one to be understood as having set forth in it? From where will that <s>Mahāyāna</s> go forth? By whom has that <s>Mahāyāna</s> been set forth? Where will that <s>Mahāyāna</s> stand? Who will go forth by this <s>Mahāyāna</s>?'—It has been set forth through the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). It will go forth from the triple realm (<s>traidhātuka</s>). That by which there is an object—by that it has been set forth. It will stand in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> will go forth. And yet, it will not go forth from anywhere. It has not been set forth by anyone. It will not stand anywhere. And yet it will stand in <s>sarvajñatā</s> through the yoga of non-standing. Nor has anyone gone forth by that <s>Mahāyāna</s>, nor will anyone go forth, nor is anyone going forth. For what reason? Both the one who would go forth and that by which one would go forth—both these <s>dharmas</s> are not found and are not apprehended. When all <s>dharmas</s> are thus non-existent, which <s>dharma</s> will go forth by which <s>dharma</s>? Thus, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> has donned the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [armor], has set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and has mounted the <s>Mahāyāna</s>."

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - mahāyānaṃ mahāyānamiti bhagavannucyate / sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokamabhibhavanniryāsyati ākāśasamatayā atimahattayā tanmahāyānam / yathā ākāśe aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmavakāśaḥ, evameva bhagavan asmin yāne aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmavakāśaḥ / anena bhagavan paryāyeṇa mahāyānamidaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām / naivāsyāgamo dṛśyate, naivāsya nirgamo dṛśyate, nāpyasya sthānaṃ saṃvidyate / evamasya bhagavan mahāyānasya naiva pūrvānta upalabhyate, nāpyaparānta upalabhyate, nāpi madhya upalabhyate / atha samaṃ bhagavaṃstadyānam / tasmānmahāyānaṃ mahāyānamityucyate / atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmate subhūtaye sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu subhūte / evametatsubhūte, evam etat / evaṃ mahāyānamidaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām / atra śikṣitvā bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sarvajñatā anuprāptā, anuprāpsyate anuprāpyate ca //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "'<s>Mahāyāna</s>, <s>Mahāyāna</s>'—thus it is called, O Blessed One. Overcoming the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, it will go forth—through its sameness with space, through its supreme greatness, that <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Just as in space there is room for immeasurable, innumerable beings, just so, O Blessed One, in this vehicle there is room for immeasurable, innumerable beings. By this manner, O Blessed One, this is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Neither its coming is seen, nor its going is seen, nor is its standing found. Thus, O Blessed One, neither the prior end of this <s>Mahāyāna</s> is apprehended, nor the posterior end, nor the middle. And that vehicle, O Blessed One, is equal [to space]. Therefore it is called '<s>Mahāyāna</s>, <s>Mahāyāna</s>.'" Then the Blessed One expressed his approval to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>! So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. This is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Having trained herein, <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) has been attained by <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, will be attained, and is being attained."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputro bhagavantametadavocat - ayaṃ bhagavan subhūtiḥ sthaviraḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kṛtaśo 'dhīṣṭo mahāyānamupadeṣṭavyaṃ manyate / atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - nāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ vyatikramya mahāyānamavocam / bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / anulomatvaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitāyā mahāyānamupadiśasi / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - buddhānubhāvādbhagavan / api nu khalu punarbhagavan pūrvāntato bodhisattvo nopaiti, aparāntato bodhisattvo nopaiti, madhyato bodhisattvo nopaiti / tatkasya hetornopaiti? rūpāparyantatayā hi bodhisattvāparyantatā veditavyā, evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> said to the Blessed One: "This Elder <s>Subhūti</s>, O Blessed One, the foremost exponent of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, considers the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to be taught [thus]." Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "I have not spoken of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> in a way that goes beyond the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, O Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "Indeed not, <s>Subhūti</s>. You teach the <s>Mahāyāna</s> in conformity with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>." When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, O Blessed One. But, O Blessed One, does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> not come from the prior end, does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> not come from the posterior end, does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> not come from the middle? For what reason does he not come? Because, through the limitlessness of <s>rūpa</s> (form), the limitlessness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood; likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>.

body.text: vijñānāparyantatayā hi bodhisattvāparyantatā veditavyā / rūpaṃ bodhisattva iti nopaiti / idam api na vidyate nopalabhyate / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ bodhisattva iti nopaiti, idam api na vidyate nopalabhyate / evaṃ bhagavan sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ bodhisattvadharmamanupalabhamāno nāhaṃ bhagavan taṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi yasyaitannāmadheyaṃ yaduta bodhisattva iti / prajñāpāramitām api na samanupaśyāmi nopalabhe / sarvajñatām api na samanupaśyāmi nopalabhe / so 'haṃ bhagavan sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ taṃ dharmamanupalabhamāno 'samanupaśyan katamaṃ dharmaṃ katamena dharmeṇa katamasmin dharme 'vavadiṣyāmi anuśāsiṣyāmi? buddha iti bhagavan nāmadheyamātram etat / bodhisattva iti bhagavan nāmadheyamātram etat / prajñāpāramiteti bhagavan nāmadheyamātram etat / tacca nāmadheyamanabhinirvṛttam / yathā ātmā ātmeti ca bhagavannucyate, atyantatayā ca bhagavannanabhinirvṛtta ātmā / evamasvabhāvānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ katamattadrūpaṃ yadagrāhyamanabhinirvṛttam? katame te vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ? katamattadvijñānaṃ yadagrāhyamanabhinirvṛttam? evameteṣāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yā asvabhāvatā, sā anabhinirvṛttiḥ / yā ca sarvadharmāṇāmanabhinirvṛttirna te dharmāḥ / tatkimanabhinirvṛttimanabhinirvṛttyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadiṣyāmyanuśāsiṣyāmi? na cānyatra bhagavan anabhinirvṛttitaḥ sarvadharmā vā buddhadharmā vā bodhisattvadharmā vā upalabhyante, yo vā bodhāya caret / sacedbhagavan evaṃ bhāṣyamāṇe evaṃ deśyamāne evamupadiśyamāne bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya cittaṃ nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate na viṣīdati na viṣādamāpadyate, nāsya vipṛṣṭhībhavati mānasaṃ na bhagnapṛṣṭhībhavati notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate, evaṃ veditavyam - caratyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyām / bhāvayatyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitām / upaparīkṣate 'yaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitām / upanidhyāyatyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāmiti / tatkasya hetoḥ? yasmin hi samaye bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ imān dharmān prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vyupaparīkṣate, tasmin samaye na rūpamupaiti, na rūpamupagacchati, na rūpasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati, na rūpasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati / evaṃ na vedanāṃ na saṃjñāṃ na saṃskārān / na vijñānamupaiti, na vijñānamupagacchati, na vijñānasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati, na vijñānasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi yo rūpasyānutpādo na tadrūpam / yo rūpasyāvyayo na tadrūpam / ityanutpādaś ca rūpaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / ityavyayaś ca rūpaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / yatpunaretaducyate rūpamiti, advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā / evaṃ tathā hi yo vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām / tathā hi yo vijñānasyānutpādo na tadvijñānam, yo vijñānasyāvyayo na tadvijñānam / ityanutpādaś ca vijñānaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / ityavyayaś ca vijñānaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / yatpunaretaducyate vijñānamiti, advayastaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā / evaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarvākāraṃ sarvadharmān vyupaparīkṣamāṇaḥ tasmin samaye na rūpamupaiti, na rūpamupagacchati, na rūpasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati, na rūpasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati / evaṃ na vedanāṃ na saṃjñāṃ na saṃskārān / na vijñānamupaiti,
body.translated_text: Through the limitlessness of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), the limitlessness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be understood. '<s>Rūpa</s> is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'—this does not come about. This too is not found, not apprehended. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. '<s>Vijñāna</s> is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'—this does not come about; this too is not found, not apprehended. Thus, O Blessed One, not apprehending the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s> in any way whatsoever, completely, I do not perceive that <s>dharma</s> whose designation is '<s>Bodhisattva</s>.' I also do not perceive or apprehend the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. I also do not perceive or apprehend <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). Not apprehending, not perceiving that <s>dharma</s> in any way whatsoever, completely—which <s>dharma</s> shall I instruct and counsel in which <s>dharma</s>, regarding which <s>dharma</s>? '<s>Buddha</s>'—O Blessed One, this is a mere designation. '<s>Bodhisattva</s>'—O Blessed One, this is a mere designation. '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'—O Blessed One, this is a mere designation. And that designation is unproduced. Just as the self (<s>ātman</s>)—'the self, the self' is said, O Blessed One, and yet, O Blessed One, ultimately the self is unproduced. Thus, of all <s>dharmas</s> that are without own-nature, which is that <s>rūpa</s> that is ungraspable and unproduced? What are those <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>? What is that <s>vijñāna</s> that is ungraspable and unproduced? Thus, the absence of own-nature of all these <s>dharmas</s>—that is their non-production. And the non-production of all <s>dharmas</s>—those are not [truly] <s>dharmas</s>. How then shall I instruct and counsel in non-production within the non-production of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? And apart from non-production, O Blessed One, neither all <s>dharmas</s> nor <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> nor <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are apprehended, nor [is there] one who would practice for awakening. If, O Blessed One, when it is thus spoken, thus taught, thus instructed, the mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not sink, does not withdraw, does not despair, does not fall into despondency, does not turn away in thought, does not become broken in spirit, does not tremble, does not become terrified, does not fall into terror—then it should be understood: 'This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> cultivates the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> examines the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> contemplates the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> examines these <s>dharmas</s> in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, at that time he does not approach <s>rūpa</s>, does not go to <s>rūpa</s>, does not perceive the arising of <s>rūpa</s>, does not perceive the cessation of <s>rūpa</s>. Likewise he does not [approach] <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. He does not approach <s>vijñāna</s>, does not go to <s>vijñāna</s>, does not perceive the arising of <s>vijñāna</s>, does not perceive the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s>. For what reason? Because the non-arising of <s>rūpa</s> is not <s>rūpa</s>. The non-decay of <s>rūpa</s> is not <s>rūpa</s>. Thus non-arising and <s>rūpa</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. Thus non-decay and <s>rūpa</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. And when '<s>rūpa</s>' is spoken of, this designation has been made for what is non-dual. Similarly for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. The non-arising of <s>vijñāna</s> is not <s>vijñāna</s>; the non-decay of <s>vijñāna</s> is not <s>vijñāna</s>. Thus non-arising and <s>vijñāna</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. Thus non-decay and <s>vijñāna</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. And when '<s>vijñāna</s>' is spoken of, this designation has been made for what is non-dual. Thus, O Blessed One, while examining all <s>dharmas</s> in every aspect within the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, at that time he does not approach <s>rūpa</s>, does not go to <s>rūpa</s>, does not perceive the arising of <s>rūpa</s>, does not perceive the cessation of <s>rūpa</s>. Likewise he does not [approach] <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. He does not approach <s>vijñāna</s>,

body.text: na vijñānamupagacchati, na vijñānasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati, na vijñānasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi yo rūpasyānutpādo na tadrūpam / yo rūpasyāvyayo na tadrūpam / ityanutpādaś ca rūpaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / ityavyayaś ca rūpaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / yatpunaretaducyate rūpamiti, advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā / evaṃ tathā hi yo vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām / tathā hi yo vijñānasyānutpādo na tadvijñānam, yo vijñānasyāvyayo na tadvijñānam / ityanutpādaś ca vijñānaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / ityavyayaś ca vijñānaḥ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / yatpunaretaducyate vijñānamiti, advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā //
body.translated_text: does not go to <s>vijñāna</s>, does not perceive the arising of <s>vijñāna</s>, does not perceive the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s>. For what reason? Because the non-arising of <s>rūpa</s> is not <s>rūpa</s>. The non-decay of <s>rūpa</s> is not <s>rūpa</s>. Thus non-arising and <s>rūpa</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. Thus non-decay and <s>rūpa</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. And when '<s>rūpa</s>' is spoken of, this designation has been made for what is non-dual. Similarly for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. The non-arising of <s>vijñāna</s> is not <s>vijñāna</s>; the non-decay of <s>vijñāna</s> is not <s>vijñāna</s>. Thus non-arising and <s>vijñāna</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. Thus non-decay and <s>vijñāna</s>—this is non-dual and undivided. And when '<s>vijñāna</s>' is spoken of, this designation has been made for what is non-dual.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - tena hi yathāhamāyuṣmataḥ subhūterbhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, tathā bodhisattvo 'pyanutpādaḥ / yadi ca āyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo 'pyanutpādaḥ kiṃ bodhisattvo duṣkaracārikāṃ carati? yāni vā tāni sattvānāṃ kṛtaśo duḥkhānyutsahate pratyanubhavitum? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - nāhamāyuṣman śāriputra icchāmi bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ duṣkaracārikāṃ carantam nāpi sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yo duṣkarasaṃjñayā carati / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi āyuṣman śāriputra duṣkarasaṃjñāṃ janayitvā śakyo 'prameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaḥ kartum / api tu sukhasaṃjñāmeva kṛtvā / sarvasattvānāmantike mātṛsaṃjñāṃ pitṛsaṃjñāṃ putrasaṃjñāṃ duhitṛsaṃjñāṃ kṛtvā strīpuruṣeṣu / evametāḥ saṃjñāḥ kṛtvā bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhisattvacārikāṃ carati / tasmānmātṛsaṃjñā pitṛsaṃjñā putrasaṃjñā duhitṛsaṃjñā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvasattvānāmantike yāvadātmasaṃjñā utpādayitavyā / yathā ātmā sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvaduḥkhebhyo mocayitavyaḥ, evaṃ sarvasattvāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvaduḥkhebhyo mocayitavyā iti / evaṃ ca sarvasattveṣu saṃjñā utpādayitavyā - mayaite sarvasattvā na parityaktavyāḥ / mayaite sarvasattvāḥ parimocayitavyā aparimāṇato duḥkhaskandhāt / na ca mayaiteṣu cittapradoṣa utpādayitavya antaśaḥ śataśo 'pi chidyamāneneti / evaṃ hi bodhisattvena mahāsattvena cittamutpādayitavyam sacedevaṃcitto vihariṣyati, na duṣkarasaṃjñī cariṣyati, na duṣkarasaṃjñī vihariṣyati / punaraparamāyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam - yathā sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvamātmā na vidyate nopalabhyate, evaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvadharmā na saṃvidyante nopalabhyante / evamādhyātmikabāhyeṣu sarvadharmeṣu saṃjñā utpādayitavyā / sacedevaṃcittaścariṣyati, na duṣkarasaṃjñī cariṣyati, na duṣkarasaṃjñī vihariṣyati / yadapyāyuṣman śāriputra evamāha - anutpādo bodhisattvo iti / evametadāyuṣman śāriputra, evam etat / anutpādo bodhisattva iti //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Well then, as I understand the meaning of what the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> has spoken, the <s>bodhisattva</s> too is unproduced. But if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is indeed unproduced, why does the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice the difficult course? Or why does he endure experiencing the sufferings of beings one by one?' Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'I do not wish, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> to practice the difficult course, nor is he a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices with the perception of difficulty. Why is that? For, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having generated the perception of difficulty, it is not possible to accomplish the welfare of immeasurable and innumerable beings. Rather, it is by generating the perception of happiness. Having generated toward all beings the perception of a mother, the perception of a father, the perception of a son, and the perception of a daughter among women and men—having generated these perceptions, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Therefore, the perception of a mother, a father, a son, a daughter, and even the perception of self should be generated by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> toward all beings. Just as one's own self should be liberated entirely, in every way, from all sufferings, so all beings should be liberated entirely, in every way, from all sufferings. And thus, the perception should be generated toward all beings: "These beings are not to be abandoned by me. These beings are to be liberated by me from the immeasurable mass of suffering. And no corruption of mind is to be generated by me toward them, even if I am cut to pieces a hundred times." For thus should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> generate the mind. If he abides with such a mind, he will not practice with the perception of difficulty, he will not abide with the perception of difficulty. Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should generate this mind: "Just as the self is entirely, in every way, not found and not apprehended, so all <s>dharmas</s> are entirely, in every way, not found and not apprehended." Thus should the perception be generated regarding all <s>dharmas</s>, both internal and external. If he practices with such a mind, he will not practice with the perception of difficulty, he will not abide with the perception of difficulty. And as for what you, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, have said—"the <s>bodhisattva</s> is unproduced"—so it is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, so it is. The <s>bodhisattva</s> is unproduced.'

body.text: śāriputra āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattva evānutpādaḥ, utāho bodhisattvadharmā apyanutpādaḥ? subhūtirāha - bodhisattvadharmā api āyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ śāriputra āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvadharmā evānutpādaḥ, utāho sarvajñatāpyanutpādaḥ? subhūtirāha - sarvajñatāpyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ / āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte
body.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is it only the <s>bodhisattva</s> that is unproduced, or are the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> also unproduced?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'The <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> are also unproduced, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are only the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> unproduced, or is <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) also unproduced?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: '<s>Sarvajñatā</s> too is unproduced, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.' He said: 'But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>,

body.text: sarvajñataivānutpādaḥ, utāho sarvajñatādharmā apyanutpādaḥ? āha - sarvajñatādharmā apyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ / āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte sarvajñatādharmā evānutpādaḥ, utāho pṛthagjano 'pyanutpādaḥ? āha - pṛthagjano 'pyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ / āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte pṛthagjana evānutpādaḥ, utāho pṛthagjanadharmā apyanutpādaḥ? āha - pṛthagjanadharmā āpyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ / evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - yadyāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo 'pyanutpādaḥ, bodhisattvadharmā apyanutpādaḥ, sarvajñatāpyanutpādaḥ, sarvajñatādharmā apyanutpādaḥ, pṛthagjano 'pyanutpādaḥ, pṛthagjanadharmā apyanutpādaḥ, nanvāyuṣman subhūte anuprāptaiva ayatnena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvajñatā bhavati / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - nāhamāyuṣman śāriputra anutpannasya dharmasya prāptimicchāmi, nāpyabhisamayam / nāpyanutpannena dharmeṇa anutpannā prāptiḥ prāpyate / āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte anutpannena dharmeṇa anutpannā prāptiḥ prāpyate, utāho utpannena dharmeṇa anutpannā prāptiḥ prāpyate? āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman śāriputra anutpanno dharma utpannaḥ, utāho anutpanna eva dharmo 'nutpannaḥ? āha - kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte utpāda eva dharmo 'nutpādaḥ, utāho anutpādo dharma utpādaḥ? āha - utpādo dharmo 'nutpādo dharma ityāyuṣman śāriputra na pratibhāti jalpitum / āha - anutpādo 'pi te āyuṣman subhūte pratibhāti jalpitum / āha - anutpāda evāyuṣman śāriputra jalpaḥ / anutpāda eva āyuṣmān śāriputra pratibhāti / anutpāda eva āyuṣman śāriputra pratibhānam / evamevāyuṣman śāriputra atyantaṃ pratibhāti //
body.translated_text: is only <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) unproduced, or are the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>sarvajñatā</s> also unproduced?' He said: 'The <s>dharmas</s> of <s>sarvajñatā</s> are also unproduced, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.' He said: 'But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are only the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>sarvajñatā</s> unproduced, or is the <s>pṛthagjana</s> (ordinary person) also unproduced?' He said: 'The <s>pṛthagjana</s> is also unproduced, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.'
