He said: 'But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is only the <s>pṛthagjana</s> unproduced, or are the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>pṛthagjana</s> also unproduced?' He said: 'The <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>pṛthagjana</s> are also unproduced, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.' Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'If, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is unproduced, the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> are unproduced, <s>sarvajñatā</s> is unproduced, the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>sarvajñatā</s> are unproduced, the <s>pṛthagjana</s> is unproduced, and the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>pṛthagjana</s> are unproduced—then surely, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>sarvajñatā</s> is already attained effortlessly by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>!' Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'I do not wish, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, for the attainment of an unproduced <s>dharma</s>, nor for its realization. Nor is unproduced attainment attained by an unproduced <s>dharma</s>.' He said: 'But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is unproduced attainment attained by an unproduced <s>dharma</s>, or is unproduced attainment attained by a produced <s>dharma</s>?' He said: 'But, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is an unproduced <s>dharma</s> produced, or is an unproduced <s>dharma</s> unproduced?' He said: 'But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is production itself the <s>dharma</s> of non-production, or is non-production the <s>dharma</s> of production?' He said: 'It does not occur to me, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, to speak of a <s>dharma</s> of production or a <s>dharma</s> of non-production.' He said: 'Does it not occur to you, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, to speak even of non-production?' He said: 'Non-production itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is speech. Non-production itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, occurs [to me]. Non-production itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is ready eloquence. Even so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it absolutely occurs [to me].'

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - dhārmakathikānāmāyuṣmān subhūtiragratāyāṃ sthāpitavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hyāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthaviro yato yata eva paripraśnīkriyate, tatastata eva niḥsarati, dharmatāyāś ca na calati, tāṃ ca dharmatāṃ na virodhayati / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - dharmataiṣā āyuṣman śāriputra bhagavataḥ śrāvakāṇāmaniśritadharmāṇām / te yato yata eva paripraśnīkriyante, tatastata eva niḥsaranti, dharmatāṃ ca na virodhayanti, dharmatāyāś ca na vyativartante / tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpi nāma aniśritattvātsarvadharmāṇām / evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sādhu sādhu āyuṣman subhūte / katamaiṣā sarvadharmāniśritapāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? subhūtirāha - prajñāpāramitaiva āyuṣman śāriputra sārvayānikī, sarvadharmāniśritatayā sarvadharmāniśritapāramitā ca / iti hi yasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya evaṃ gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāmevaṃ deśyamānāyāmevamupadiśyamānāyāṃ na bhavati cittasya avalīnatvam, na bhavati kāṅkṣāyitatvam, na bhavati dhaṃdhāyitatvam, na bhavati cittasyānyathātvam, veditavyamayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo viharatyanena prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa avirahitaścānena manasikāreṇeti //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> should be placed at the head of <s>Dharma</s> preachers. Why is that? Because the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, from whatever direction he is questioned, emerges from that very direction, does not deviate from <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality), and does not contradict that <s>dharmatā</s>.' Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'This is the <s>dharmatā</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciples whose <s>dharmas</s> are unsupported. From whatever direction they are questioned, from that very direction they emerge, and they do not contradict <s>dharmatā</s>, and they do not deviate from <s>dharmatā</s>. Why is that? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are unsupported.' Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Well done, well done, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>! What is this perfection of the unsupportedness of all <s>dharmas</s> for <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) itself, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, belonging to all vehicles, is the perfection of the unsupportedness of all <s>dharmas</s> through the unsupportedness of all <s>dharmas</s>. Indeed, that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> in whom, when this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken, taught, and instructed, there is no sinking of the mind, no doubt, no hesitation, no alteration of the mind—it should be known that this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abides in this dwelling of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and is not separated from this mental attention.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmataṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kathamāyuṣman subhūte avirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'virahito manasikāreṇa bhavati, yaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa viharati? yadi hyāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'virahito manasikāreṇa bhavati, evaṃ sa virahitaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa bhavati / yadi ca āyuṣman subhūte avirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa bhavati, evaṃ sa virahito manasikāreṇa bhavati / yadi ca āyuṣman subhūte manasikāreṇāvirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, avirahita eva prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa bhavati / evaṃ sati sarvasattvā apyavirahitā bhaviṣyanti prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvasattvā api hyavirahitā manasikāreṇa viharanti //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'How, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not separated from mental attention when he abides in the dwelling of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? For if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not separated from mental attention, then he is separated from the dwelling of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not separated from the dwelling of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, then he is separated from mental attention. And if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not separated from mental attention, he is also not separated from the dwelling of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If so, then all beings too would be not separated from the dwelling of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Why is that? For all beings too abide not separated from mental attention.'

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - sādhu sādhu āyuṣman śāriputra / api tu upālapsye tvā / artha eva tvāyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa bhūtapadābhidhānena parigṛhītaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? sattvāsvabhāvatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā / sattvāsadbhāvatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārāsadbhāvatā veditavyā / sattvaviviktatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā / sattvācintyatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārācintyatā veditavyā / sattvānabhisaṃbodhanatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā / sattvāyathābhūtārthābhisaṃbodhanatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārāyathābhūtārthābhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā / anena āyuṣman śāriputra evaṃrūpeṇa manasikāreṇa icchāmi bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ viharantamanena vihāreṇeti //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Well done, well done, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>! But I shall correct you. The very meaning has been grasped by you, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, through the designation of true words. Why is that? Through the selflessness of beings, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the selflessness of mental attention should be understood. Through the non-existence of beings, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-existence of mental attention should be understood. Through the isolation of beings, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the isolation of mental attention should be understood. Through the inconceivability of beings, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the inconceivability of mental attention should be understood. Through the non-awakening of beings, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-awakening of mental attention should be understood. Through the non-awakening to reality of beings, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-awakening to reality of mental attention should be understood. With this kind of mental attention, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I wish the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> to abide in this dwelling.'

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarvākārajñatācaryāparivarto nāma prathamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the first chapter of the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, called 'The Practice of <s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (Omniscience in All Its Aspects).'

body.text: ASP_2: śakraparivarto dvitīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 2 of the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>: The Chapter on <s>Śakra</s>, the second.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena śakro devānāmindrastasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatitaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt catvāriṃśatā trāyastriṃśatkāyikairdevaputrasahasraiḥ sārdham / catvāraś ca lokapālā viṃśatyā cāturmahārājakāyikairdevaputrasahasraiḥ sārdham / brahmāpi sahāpatirdaśabhirbrahmakāyikairdevaputrasahasraiḥ sārdham / pañca ca śuddhāvāsānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi tasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatitāni saṃniṣaṇṇānyabhūvan / yo 'pi ca devānāṃ svakarmavipākajo 'vabhāsaḥ, so 'pi sarvo buddhānubhāvena buddhatejasā buddhādhiṣṭhānenābhibhūto 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, had assembled and was seated in that very assembly together with forty thousand <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> god-sons, and the four world-protectors (<s>Lokapālas</s>) together with twenty thousand <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> god-sons, and <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> together with ten thousand <s>Brahmakāyika</s> god-sons, and five thousand god-sons of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> heavens had also assembled and were seated in that very assembly. And whatever radiance the gods possessed as a result of their own <s>karma</s>—all of that was overpowered by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the splendor of the <s>Buddha</s>, and the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat - imānyārya subhūte saṃbahulāni devaputrasahasrāṇi asyāṃ parṣadi saṃnipatitāni saṃniṣaṇṇāni āryasya subhūterantikātprajñāpāramitāṃ śrotukāmāni bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmupadeśamavavādānuśāsanīṃ ca / tatkathaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam, kathaṃ śikṣitavyam, kathaṃ yogamāpattavyam? sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha - tena hi kauśika upadekṣyāmi te buddhānubhāvena buddhatejasā buddhādhiṣṭhānena / yairdevaputrairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpāditam, tairutpādayitavyam / ye tvavakrāntāḥ samyaktvaniyāmam, na te bhavyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayitum / tatkasya hetoḥ? baddhasīmāno hi te saṃsārasrotasaḥ / abhavyā hi te punaḥ punaḥ saṃsaraṇāya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayitum / api nu khalu punasteṣāmapyanumode / sacette 'pyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayeran, nāhaṃ kuśalamūlasyāntarāyaṃ karomi / viśiṣṭebhyo hi dharmebhyo viśiṣṭatamā dharmā adhyālambitavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, said to the elder, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'These many thousands of god-sons, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, have assembled and are seated in this assembly, wishing to hear the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> from the noble <s>Subhūti</s>, and the instruction, admonition, and guidance for <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. How should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> stand in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, how should he train, and how should he apply himself to the practice?' The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Well then, <s>Kauśika</s>, I shall instruct you by the power, splendor, and empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>. Those god-sons who have not generated the mind toward supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) should generate it. But those who have entered the certainty of the right path are not capable of generating the mind toward supreme perfect awakening. Why is that? Because they have fixed boundaries in the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For they are incapable of generating the mind toward supreme perfect awakening for the sake of repeated transmigration. Nevertheless, I rejoice even for them. Even if they were to generate minds toward supreme perfect awakening, I would not create an obstacle to their roots of merit. For from superior <s>dharmas</s>, the most superior <s>dharmas</s> should be grasped.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimāmantrayate sma - sādhu sādhu subhūte, sādhu khalu punastvaṃ subhūte, yastvaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmutsāhaṃ dadāsi / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - kṛtajñairasmābhirbhagavan bhagavato bhavitavyaṃ nākṛtajñaiḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? paurvakāṇāṃ hi bhagavaṃstathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantike 'smadarthe bhagavān yathā brahmacaryaṃ bodhāya caran pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūta eva san, yaiḥ śrāvakairavavadito 'nuśiṣṭaś ca pāramitāsu, tatra bhagavatā caratā anuttaraṃ jñānamutpāditam / evaṃ bhagavan asmābhir api bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuparigrahītavyā anuparivārayitavyāśca, saṃparigrahītavyāḥ saṃparivārayitavyāś ca / tatkasya hetoḥ? asmābhir api hi bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuparigṛhītā anuparivāritāśca, saṃparigṛhītāḥ saṃparivāritāś ca kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>! It is excellent indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, that you give encouragement to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>." When this was said, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> replied to the Blessed One: "We should be grateful, O Blessed One, not ungrateful toward the Blessed One. For what reason? Because of the former—"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindramāmantrayate sma - tena hi kauśika śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te yathā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam / śūnyatāyāṃ kauśika tiṣṭhatā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam / tena hi kauśika
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> addressed <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods: "Then, <s>Kauśika</s>, listen well and carefully, and attend closely—I shall explain to you how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should stand in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, O <s>Kauśika</s>, should stand in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> by standing in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). Then, <s>Kauśika</s>—"

body.text: bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhena bhavitavyam / na rūpe sthātavyam / na vedanāyāṃ na saṃjñāyāṃ na saṃskāreṣu / na vijñāne sthātavyam / na cakṣuṣi sthātavyam / na rūpe sthātavyam / na cakṣurvijñāne sthātavyam / na cakṣuḥsaṃsparśe sthātavyam / na cakṣuḥsaṃsparśajāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ sthātavyam / evaṃ na śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaḥsu sthātavyam / na śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmeṣu, na śrotravijñāne, yāvanna manovijñāne / na manaḥsaṃsparśe, na manaḥsaṃsparśajāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ sthātavyam / na pṛthivīdhātau sthātavyam / nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, nākāśadhātau, na vijñānadhātau sthātavyam / na smṛtyupasthāneṣu sthātavyam / na samyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgeṣu, na mārgāṅgeṣu sthātavyam / na srotaāpattiphale sthātavyam / na sakṛdāgāmiphale, na anāgāmiphale, nārhattve sthātavyam / na pratyekabuddhatve sthātavyam / na buddhatve sthātavyam / iti hi rūpamiti na sthātavyam / iti hi vedaneti, saṃjñeti, saṃskārā iti / iti hi vijñānamiti na sthātavyam / iti hi cakṣuriti, yāvanmanaḥsaṃsparśajā vedaneti na sthātavyam / iti hi pṛthivīdhāturiti, yāvadvijñānadhāturiti na sthātavyam / iti hi smṛtyupasthānānīti na sthātavyam / iti hi samyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgānīti, iti hi mārgāṅgānīti na sthātavyam / iti hi srotaāpattiphalamiti na sthātavyam, iti hi sakṛdāgāmiphalamiti, anāgāmiphalamiti, arhattvamiti na sthātavyam / iti hi pratyekabuddhatvamiti na sthātavyam / iti hi buddhatvamiti na sthātavyam / rūpaṃ nityamanityamiti na sthātavyam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ nityamanityamiti na sthātavyam / rūpaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhamiti na sthātavyam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhamiti na sthātavyam / rūpaṃ śūnyamaśūnyamiti na sthātavyam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ śūnyamaśūnyamiti na sthātavyam / rūpamātmānātmeti na sthātavyam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānamātmānātmeti na sthātavyam / rūpaṃ śubhamaśubhamiti na sthātavyam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ śubhamaśubhamiti na sthātavyam / rūpaṃ śūnyamupalabhyate veti na sthātavyam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ śūnyamupalabhyate veti na sthātavyam / srotaāpattiphalamasaṃskṛtaprabhāvitamiti na sthātavyam / evaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalamanāgāmiphalamarhattvamasaṃskṛtaprabhāvitamiti na sthātavyam / pratyekabuddhatvamasaṃskṛtaprabhāvitamiti na sthātavyam / srotaāpanno dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam / srotaāpannāḥ saptakṛto bhavaparamā iti na sthātavyam / sakṛdāgāmī dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam / sakṛdāgāmyapariniṣṭhitattvātsakṛdimaṃ lokamāgamya duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyatīti na sthātavyam / anāgāmī dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam anāgāmī anāgamya imaṃ lokaṃ tatraiva parinirvāsyatīti na sthātavyam / arhan dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam / arhannihaiva anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyatīti na sthātavyam / pratyekabuddho dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam / pratyekabuddho 'tikramya śrāvakabhūmimaprāpya buddhabhūmiṃ parinirvāsyatīti na sthātavyam / buddho dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam / buddho 'tikramya
body.translated_text: a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, girded with the great armor, should not stand in <s>rūpa</s> (form). He should not stand in <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), in <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), in <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). He should not stand in <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). He should not stand in the eye. He should not stand in form. He should not stand in eye-consciousness. He should not stand in eye-contact. He should not stand in the feeling born of eye-contact.

body.text: pṛthagjanabhūmimatikramya śrāvakabhūmimatikramya pratyekabuddhabhūmimaprabheyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ kṛtvā aprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi parinirvāpya aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān sattvān śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamyaksaṃbuddhatvaniyatān kṛtvā buddhabhūmau sthitvā buddhakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau buddhaparinirvāṇena parinirvāsyati ityevamapyanena na sthātavyam //
body.translated_text: having transcended the stage of ordinary beings, having transcended the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple) stage, having transcended the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage, having served the welfare of immeasurable, innumerable beings, having led to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> immeasurable, innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of beings, having established immeasurable, innumerable beings as destined for the awakening of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and Perfectly Awakened Ones, standing on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, performing the <s>Buddha</s>'s work—

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitadabhavat - yadi buddho 'tikramya pṛthagjanabhūmimatikramya śrāvakabhūmimatikramya pratyekabuddhabhūmimaprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ kṛtvā aprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi parinirvāpya aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān sattvān śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamyaksaṃbuddhatvaniyatān kṛtvā buddhabhūmau sthitvā buddhakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau buddhaparinirvāṇena parinirvāsyati ityevamapyanena na sthātavyam, tatkathaṃ punaranena sthātavyaṃ, kathaṃ śikṣitavyamiti? atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase āyuṣman śāriputra kva tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sthitaḥ? āyuṣmān śāriputra āha - na kvacidāyuṣman subhūte tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sthitaḥ / tatkasya heto? apratiṣṭhitamānaso hi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / sa naiva saṃskṛte dhātau sthito nāpyasaṃskṛte dhātau sthito na ca tato vyutthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the following thought occurred to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "If, having transcended the stage of ordinary beings, having transcended the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage, having transcended the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage, having served the welfare of immeasurable, innumerable beings, having led to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> immeasurable, innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of beings, having established immeasurable, innumerable beings as destined for <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and Perfect Awakening—

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - evameva āyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sthātavyam, evaṃ śikṣitavyam - yathā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho na kvacitsthito nāsthito na viṣṭhito nāviṣṭhitaḥ, tathā sthāsyāmītyevamanena śikṣitavyam / yathā tathāgatasthānaṃ tathā sthāsyāmīti, tathā śikṣiṣye iti, yathā tathāgatasthānaṃ tathā sthāsyāmīti, tathā śikṣiṣye iti, yathā tathāgatasthānaṃ tathā sthāsyāmīti susthito 'sthānayogeneti evamatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sthātavyamevaṃ śikṣitavyam / evaṃ hi śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo viharatyanena prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa avirahitaścānena manasikāreṇeti //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Just so, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should stand thus, should train thus: 'Just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, neither stands anywhere nor does not stand, neither abides nor does not abide—so shall I stand.' Thus should he train. As the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s standing is, so—"

body.text: atha khalu tatra parṣadi keṣāṃciddevaputrāṇāmetadabhūt - yāni tāni yakṣāṇāṃ yakṣabhāṣitāni yakṣarutāni yakṣapadāni yakṣamantritāni yakṣapravyāhṛtāni, tāni vijñāyante jalpyamānāni / na punaridaṃ vijñāyate yatsubhūtiḥ sthaviro bhāṣate pravyāharati deśayatyupadiśati / atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāmimamevaṃrūpaṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tān devaputrānāmantrayate sma - na vijñāyate na vijñāyate idaṃ devaputrāḥ / tathā hi nātra kiṃcitsūcyate, nātra kiṃcit śrūyate //
body.translated_text: Then in that assembly, the following thought occurred to certain <s>devaputras</s> (sons of the gods): "The words, utterances, syllables, phrases, and expressions of <s>yakṣas</s>—those are intelligible when spoken. But what the Elder <s>Subhūti</s> speaks, expresses, teaches, and instructs—that is not intelligible." Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s supernatural power—

body.text: atha khalu teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ punarevaitadabhūt - uttānīkariṣyati bata ayamāryasubhūtiḥ / uttānīkariṣyati batāyamāryasubhūtiriti / dūrāddūrataramāryasubhūtiḥ praviśati, sūkṣmātsūkṣmataram / gambhīrādgambhīrataramāryasubhūtiḥ praviśati deśayati bhāṣata iti / atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena punar api teṣāmeva devaputrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tān devaputrānāmantrayate
body.translated_text: Then the following thought again occurred to those <s>devaputras</s>: "The Noble <s>Subhūti</s> will surely make it clear! The Noble <s>Subhūti</s> will surely make it clear! From far, the Noble <s>Subhūti</s> enters into what is even farther; from the subtle, into what is even more subtle. From the profound, the Noble <s>Subhūti</s> enters into, teaches, and expounds what is even more profound." Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s supernatural power—

body.text: sma - tena hi devaputrāḥ yaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptukāmaḥ srotaāpattiphale sthātukāmaḥ, sa nemāṃ kṣāntimanāgamya....peyālam / yaḥ sakṛdāgābhiphalaṃ prāptukāmaḥ, sakṛdāgāmiphale sthātukāmaḥ, yo 'nāgāmiphalaṃ prāptukāmo 'nāgāmiphale sthātukāmaḥ, yo 'rhattvaṃ prāptukāmo 'rhattve sthātukāmaḥ, yaḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptukāmaḥ pratyekabodhau sthātukāmaḥ, sa nemāṃ kṣāntimanāgamya..... / yo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prāptukāmo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau sthātukāmaḥ, sa nemāṃ kṣāntimanāgamya............. //
body.translated_text: said: "Then, O <s>devaputras</s>, one who wishes to attain the fruit of stream-entry, who wishes to stand in the fruit of stream-entry—he cannot do so without having reached this <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance)...and so on in full...one who wishes to attain the fruit of once-returning, who wishes to stand in the fruit of once-returning; one who wishes to attain the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to stand in the fruit of non-returning; one who wishes to attain <s>Arhatship</s>, who wishes to stand in <s>Arhatship</s>; one who wishes to attain <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>—"

body.text: atha khalu punar api teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāmetadabhavat - kiṃrūpā asya āryasubhūterdhārmaśravaṇikā eṣṭavyāḥ? atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tān devaputrānāmantrayate sma - māyānirmitasadṛśā hi devaputrā mama dhārmaśravaṇikā eṣṭavyāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi te naiva śroṣyanti na ca sākṣātkariṣyanti //
body.translated_text: Then again the following thought occurred to those <s>devaputras</s>: "What kind of listeners should be sought for the Noble <s>Subhūti</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-teaching?" Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s supernatural power, having perceived with his mind the mental deliberation of those <s>devaputras</s>, addressed them: "<s>Devaputras</s>, my <s>Dharma</s>-listeners should be sought as being like magical creations. For what reason?—"

body.text: atha khalu te devaputrā āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocan - kiṃ punarārya subhūte māyopamāste sattvā na te māyā? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtistān devaputrānetadavocat - māyopamāste devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ / svapnopamāste devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ / iti hi māyā ca sattvāś ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram, iti hi svapnaś ca sattvāś ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / sarvadharmā api devaputrā māyopamāḥ svapnopamāḥ / srotaāpanno 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ / srotaāpattiphalam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam / evaṃ sakṛdāgāmy api sakṛdāgāmiphalamapi, anāgāmy api anāgāmiphalamapi, arhann api arhattvam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam / pratyekabuddho 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ / pratyekabuddhatvam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam / samyaksaṃbuddho 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ / samyaksaṃbuddhatvam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam / atha khalu devaputrā āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocan - samyaksaṃbuddho 'pyārya subhūte māyopamaḥ svapnopama iti vadasi? samyaksaṃbuddhatv api māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadasi? subhūtirāha - nirvāṇam api devaputrā māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadāmi, kiṃ punaranyaṃ dharmam / te devaputrā āhuḥ - nirvāṇamapyārya subhūte māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadasi? āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - tadyadi devaputrā nirvāṇādapyanyaḥ kaściddharmo viśiṣṭataraḥ syāt, tamapyahaṃ māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadeyam / iti hi devaputrā māyā ca nirvāṇaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram / iti hi svapnaś ca nirvāṇaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāram //
body.translated_text: Then those sons of the gods spoke thus to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'But, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, are those beings like an illusion, or are they not illusions?' When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to those sons of the gods: 'Those beings are like an illusion, O sons of the gods. Those beings are like a dream, O sons of the gods. For indeed, illusion and beings—this is non-dual, without division. For indeed, dream and beings—this is non-dual, without division. All <s>dharmas</s> too, O sons of the gods, are like an illusion, like a dream. A stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>) too is like an illusion, like a dream. The fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) too is like an illusion, like a dream. Likewise, a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) and the fruit of once-returning, a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) and the fruit of non-returning, an <s>Arhat</s> and <s>Arhatship</s> too are like an illusion, like a dream. A <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> too is like an illusion, like a dream. <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s> too is like an illusion, like a dream. A perfectly awakened one (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) too is like an illusion, like a dream. Perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbuddhatva</s>) too is like an illusion, like a dream.' Then the sons of the gods spoke thus to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, do you say that even a perfectly awakened one is like an illusion, like a dream? Do you say that even perfect awakening is like an illusion, like a dream?' <s>Subhūti</s> replied: 'I say, O sons of the gods, that even <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is like an illusion, like a dream—how much more so any other <s>dharma</s>!' The sons of the gods said: 'Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, do you say that even <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is like an illusion, like a dream?' The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> replied: 'Even if, O sons of the gods, there were some <s>dharma</s> more distinguished than <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, I would say that it too is like an illusion, like a dream. For indeed, O sons of the gods, illusion and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>—this is non-dual, without division. For indeed, dream and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>—this is non-dual, without division.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputraḥ, āyuṣmāṃś ca pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputraḥ, āyuṣmāṃś ca mahākoṣṭhilaḥ, āyuṣmāṃś ca mahākātyāyanaḥ, āyuṣmāṃś ca mahākāśapaḥ, anye ca mahāśrāvakā anekairbodhisattvasahasraiḥ sārdhamāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthaviramāmantrayante sma - ke 'syā āyuṣman subhūte prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyāḥ pratyeṣakā bhaviṣyanti? atha khalvāyuṣmānānandastān sthavirānetadavocat - te khalvāyuṣmanto veditavyā avinivartanīyā bodhisattvā
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> <s>Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākoṣṭhila</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, and other great disciples (<s>mahāśrāvakas</s>), together with many thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, addressed the elder, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Who, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, will be the receptive listeners of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> when it is being taught in this way?' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to those elders: 'Those, venerable ones, should be known as irreversible (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) <s>Bodhisattvas</s>

body.text: mahāsattvāḥ, dṛṣṭisaṃpannā vā pudgalāḥ, arhanto vā kṣīṇāsravāḥ, ye 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyāḥ pratyeṣakā bhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, or persons endowed with [right] view, or <s>Arhats</s> whose outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) are exhausted—they will be the receptive listeners of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> when it is being taught in this way.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthavirastān sthavirānetadavocat - nāsyā āyuṣmantaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyāḥ kecitpratyeṣakā bhaviṣyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi - atra na kaściddharmaḥ sūcyate, na kaściddharmaḥ paridīpyate, na kaściddharmaḥ prajñapyate / tadyathaivātra na kaściddharmaḥ sūcyate, na kaściddharmaḥ paridīpyate, na kaściddharmaḥ prajñapyate, tathaivāsyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyā na kaścitpratyeṣako bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then the elder, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, spoke thus to those elders: 'There will be no receptive listeners whatsoever, venerable ones, of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> when it is being taught in this way. What is the reason for that? For herein no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is indicated, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is illuminated, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is designated. Just as herein no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is indicated, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is illuminated, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is designated, so too there will be no receptive listener whatsoever of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> when it is being taught in this way.'

body.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhūt - asya dharmaparyāyasya āryeṇa subhūtinā bhāṣyamāṇasya pūjārthaṃ yannvahaṃ puṣpāṇyabhinirmāya āryaṃ subhūtimabhyavakireyamiti / atha khalu śakro devānāmindrastasyāṃ velāyāṃ puṣpāṇyabhinirmāya āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimabhyavākirat / atha khalvāyuṣmataḥ subhūteḥ sthavirasya śakraṃ devānāmindramanuvyāharaṇāyaitadabhūt - na khalu punarimāni puṣpāṇi mayā trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣu pracaranti dṛṣṭapūrvāṇi, yānīmāni śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa abhyavakīrṇāni / nirmitānyetāni puṣpāṇi / naitāni puṣpāṇi vṛkṣagulmalatānirjātāni, yāni śakreṇa devānāmindreṇābhyavakīrṇāni, manomayānyetāni puṣpāṇīti / atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmataḥ subhūteścetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - anirjātānyetānyārya subhūte puṣpāṇi / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi manonirjātāni kānicitpuṣpāṇi, nāpi vṛkṣagulmalatānirjātāni / atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - yattvaṃ kauśika evaṃ vadasi - anirjātānyetāni puṣpāṇi, naitāni manonirjātāni, nāpi vṛkṣagulmalatānirjātānīti / yatkauśika anirjātaṃ na tatpuṣpam / atha khalu śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhūt - gambhīraprajño batāyamāryaḥ subhūtiḥ / tāṃ ca nāma padaprajñaptiṃ nirdiśati, tāṃ ca na virodhayati, tāṃ cottānīkaroti, tāmeva copadiśati / atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmataṃ subhūtimetadavocat - evametadārya subhūte, evam etat / evaṃ cātra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyaṃ yathā āryasubhūtirupadiśati / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - evametatkauśika, evam etat / evamatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyam / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ kauśika bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na srotaāpattiphale śikṣate, na sakṛdāgāmiphale, na anāgāmiphale, nāhartve śikṣate, na pratyekabuddhatve śikṣate, na buddhatve śikṣate / yo nāsu bhūmiṣu śikṣate, sa buddhatve sarvajñatve vā śikṣate / yo buddhatve sarvajñatve vā śikṣate, so 'prameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhadharmeṣu śikṣate / yo 'prameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhadharmeṣu śikṣate, sa na rūpasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate, na parihāṇāya / evaṃ sa na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / sa na vijñānasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate, na parihāṇāya / yo na rūpasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate na parihāṇāya / evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / yo na vijñānasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate na parihāṇāya, sa na rūpasya parigrahāya śikṣate notsargāya /
body.translated_text: Then it occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'In order to worship this <s>Dharma</s> discourse being spoken by the noble <s>Subhūti</s>, let me create flowers by supernatural power and scatter them over the noble <s>Subhūti</s>.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, at that moment created flowers by supernatural power and scattered them over the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>. Then it occurred to the elder, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, in response to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'These flowers that have been scattered by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, I have never seen before among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. These flowers are magically created. These flowers scattered by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, are not produced from trees, shrubs, or creepers—these flowers are mind-made.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, having known the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>'s thought with his own mind, spoke thus to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'These flowers are unproduced, noble <s>Subhūti</s>. What is the reason? For flowers are neither mind-produced nor produced from trees, shrubs, or creepers.' Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke thus to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'You, <s>Kauśika</s>, say thus: "These flowers are unproduced; they are neither mind-produced nor produced from trees, shrubs, or creepers." But, <s>Kauśika</s>, what is unproduced is not a flower.' Then it occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'The noble <s>Subhūti</s> is truly of profound wisdom! He teaches that very verbal designation, and yet does not contradict it, and makes it clear, and still teaches it.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, spoke thus to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'So it is, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is! And herein a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should train just as the noble <s>Subhūti</s> teaches.' When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke thus to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is! Herein a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should train thus. Training thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not train in the fruit of stream-entry, nor in the fruit of once-returning, nor in the fruit of non-returning, nor does he train in <s>Arhatship</s>, nor in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>, nor in <s>Buddhahood</s>. One who does not train in those stages trains in <s>Buddhahood</s> and omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). One who trains in <s>Buddhahood</s> and omniscience trains in immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. One who trains in immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> does not train for the increase of form (<s>rūpa</s>), nor for its decrease. Likewise, not for feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), nor formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). He does not train for the increase of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), nor for its decrease. One who does not train for the increase of form nor for its decrease—likewise, not for feeling, perception, nor formations—one who does not train for the increase of consciousness nor for its decrease, does not train for the grasping of form nor for its abandoning.

body.text: evaṃ sa na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / sa na vijñānasya parigrahāya śikṣate, notsargāya, nāpi kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate / yo na kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate, sa na sarvajñatāyā api parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate, sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyati //
body.translated_text: Likewise, not for feeling, perception, nor formations. He does not train for the grasping of consciousness, nor for its abandoning, nor does he train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance. One who does not train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance, does not train even for the grasping of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance. Training thus, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in omniscience and will emerge into omniscience.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - ya āyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāsya śikṣate, sa na sarvajñatāyā api parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇa āyuṣmān subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate, sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyati //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> spoke thus to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'That <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, who does not train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance, does not train even for the grasping of omniscience, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance. Training thus, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in omniscience and will emerge into omniscience.'

body.text: āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - evametadāyuṣman śāriputra, evam etat / ya āyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate, sa na sarvajñatāyā api parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate / sarvabuddhadharmāṇām api na parigrahāya śikṣate, notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate / evaṃ cāyuṣman śāriputra śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate, sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyati //
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> replied: 'So it is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, so it is! That <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, who does not train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance, does not train even for the grasping of omniscience, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance. He does not train even for the grasping of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, nor for their arising, nor for their disappearance. And thus, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, training in this way, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in omniscience and will emerge into omniscience.'

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - prajñāpāramitā ārya śāriputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kuto gaveṣitavyāḥ? śāriputra āha - prajñāpāramitā kauśika bodhisattvena mahāsattvena āyuṣmataḥ subhūteḥ parivartādgaveṣitavyā / evamukte śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - kasyaiṣa ārya śāriputra anubhāvo veditavyaḥ? kasyaitadadhiṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadāryasubhūtiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate? āyuṣmān śāriputra āha - tathāgatasyaiṣa kauśika anubhāvo veditavyaḥ / tathāgatasyaitadadhiṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate / atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - yatkauśika evaṃ vadasi - kasyaiṣo 'nubhāvo veditavyaḥ, kasyaitadanuṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadāryasubhūtiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate iti? tathāgatasyaiṣa kauśika anubhāvo veditavyaḥ / tathāgatasyaitadadhiṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadahaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣe / yad api kauśika evaṃ vadasi - prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kuto gaveṣitavyeti? prajñāpāramitā kauśika bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na rūpādgaveṣitavyā nāpyanyatra rūpādgaveṣitavyā / evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārebhyaḥ na vijñānādgaveṣitavyāḥ, nāpyanyatra vijñānādgaveṣitavyā / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi na rūpaṃ prajñāpāramitā, nāpyanyatra rūpātprajñāpāramitā / evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ prajñāpāramitā, nāpyanyatra vijñānātprajñāpāramitā //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Where, noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, should the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> be sought by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>?' <s>Śāriputra</s> replied: 'The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, should be sought by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> from the exposition of the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>.' When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Whose power, noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, should this be understood to be? Whose sustaining force (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) should this be understood to be, that the noble <s>Subhūti</s> speaks the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> replied: 'This should be understood, <s>Kauśika</s>, as the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This should be understood as the sustaining force of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> speaks the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke thus to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'You, <s>Kauśika</s>, say thus: "Whose power should this be understood to be? Whose sustaining force should this be understood to be, that the noble <s>Subhūti</s> speaks the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?" This should be understood, <s>Kauśika</s>, as the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This should be understood as the sustaining force of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that I speak the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And as to your saying, <s>Kauśika</s>: "Where should the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> be sought by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>?" The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, should not be sought by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> in form (<s>rūpa</s>), nor should it be sought apart from form. Likewise, it should not be sought in feeling, perception, formations, nor in consciousness, nor should it be sought apart from consciousness. What is the reason? For form is not the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> apart from form. Likewise, feeling, perception, and formations are not [the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]. Consciousness is not the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> apart from consciousness.'

body.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - mahāpāramiteyamārya subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā / apramāṇapāramiteyamārya subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā / aparimāṇapāramiteyamārya
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, spoke thus to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'This is a great perfection (<s>mahāpāramitā</s>), noble <s>Subhūti</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an immeasurable perfection (<s>apramāṇapāramitā</s>), noble <s>Subhūti</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an incalculable perfection (<s>aparimāṇapāramitā</s>), noble

body.text: subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā / anantapāramiteyamārya subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā / sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha - evametatkauśika, evam etat / mahāpāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā / apramāṇapāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā / aparimāṇapāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā / anantapāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā / tatkasya hetoḥ? rūpamahattayā hi kauśika mahāpāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānamahattayā hi kauśikamahāpāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / rūpāpramāṇatayā kauśika apramāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānāpramāṇatayā kauśika apramāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñapāramitā / rūpāparimāṇatayā kauśika aparimāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānāparimāṇatayā kauśika aparimāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñapāramitā / rūpānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ mahāpāramiteti kauśika nābhiniviśate / evamapramāṇapāramiteti, evamaparimāṇapāramiteti, evamanantapāramiteti nābhiniviśate / tasmātkauśika mahāpāramiteyam, apramāṇapāramiteyam, aparimāṇapāramiteyam, anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an infinite perfection (<s>anantapāramitā</s>), noble <s>Subhūti</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' The elder <s>Subhūti</s> replied: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. This is a great perfection, <s>Kauśika</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an immeasurable perfection, <s>Kauśika</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an incalculable perfection, <s>Kauśika</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an infinite perfection, <s>Kauśika</s>, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. What is the reason? Because of the greatness of form (<s>rūpa</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>, this is a great perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for feeling, perception, and formations. Because of the greatness of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>, this is a great perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Because of the immeasurability of form, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an immeasurable perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for feeling, perception, and formations. Because of the immeasurability of consciousness, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an immeasurable perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Because of the incalculability of form, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an incalculable perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for feeling, perception, and formations. Because of the incalculability of consciousness, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an incalculable perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Because of the infinity of form, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for feeling, perception, and formations. Because of the infinity of consciousness, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus one does not fixate on "great perfection," <s>Kauśika</s>. Thus one does not fixate on "immeasurable perfection," nor on "incalculable perfection," nor on "infinite perfection." Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is a great perfection, an immeasurable perfection, an incalculable perfection, an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: ārambaṇānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / sattvānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / kathaṃ punaḥ kauśika ārambaṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā? sarvadharmāṇāṃ hi kauśika yato nānto na madhyaṃ na paryavasānamupalabhyate, tataḥ kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / anena kauśika paryāyeṇa ārambaṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / punaraparaṃ kauśika yasmātsarvadharmā anantā aparyantāḥ, na teṣāmanto vā madhyaṃ vā paryavasānaṃ vā upalabhyate, tasmātkauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / tatkasya hetoḥ? rūpasya hi kauśika nānto na madhyaṃ na paryavasānamupalabhyate / evaṃ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām / vijñānasya hi kauśika nānto na madhyaṃ na paryavasānamupalabhyate / anenāpi kauśika paryāyeṇa ārambaṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā //
body.translated_text: By the infinitude of its object, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. By the infinitude of beings, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And how is it, <s>Kauśika</s>, that by the infinitude of its object this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? Since, <s>Kauśika</s>, no end, no middle, and no limit of all <s>dharmas</s> is apprehended, therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, by the infinitude of its object, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, since all <s>dharmas</s> are infinite and boundless—no end, no middle, and no limit of them is apprehended—therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Kauśika</s>, no end, no middle, and no limit of form is apprehended. Likewise of feeling, perception, and mental formations. Because, <s>Kauśika</s>, no end, no middle, and no limit of consciousness is apprehended. By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, by the infinitude of its object, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika sattvo 'nanto 'paryantaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi sattvasyānto vā madhyaṃ vā paryavasānaṃ vopalabhyate / tasmātkauśika sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kathamāyuṣman subhūte sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā? sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha - na hi kauśika gaṇanāyogena vā gaṇanābahutvena vā sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a being is infinite and boundless. For what reason? Because no end, no middle, and no limit of a being is apprehended. Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, by the infinitude of beings, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: How, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is this an infinite perfection by the infinitude of beings, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: It is not, <s>Kauśika</s>, by the method of counting or by the multiplicity of counting that by the infinitude of beings this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: śakra āha - kathaṃ tarhīdānīmārya subhūte sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: How then now, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, is this an infinite perfection by the infinitude of beings, namely the

body.text: prajñāpāramitā? sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha - tatkaṃ manyase kauśika katamasyaitaddharmasyādhivacanaṃ yaduta sattvaḥ sattva iti? śakra āha - naitadārya subhūte dharmasyādhivacanaṃ na adharmādhivacanaṃ yaduta sattvaḥ sattva iti / āgantukametannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam / avastukametannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam / anātmīyametannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam / anārambaṇametannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptaṃ yaduta sattvaḥ sattva iti / sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha - tatkiṃ manyase kauśika kācidatra sattvaparidīpanā kṛtā? śakra āha - no hīdamārya subhūte / subhūtirāha - yatra kauśika na kācitsattvaparidīpanā kṛtā, tatra kā sattvānantatā? sacetkauśika tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'nantavijñaptighoṣeṇa gambhīranirghoṣeṇa svareṇa gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān api vitiṣṭhamānaḥ sattvaḥ sattva iti vācaṃ bhāṣeta, api nu tatra kaścitsattva utpanno va utpatsyate vā utpadyate vā, niruddho vā nirotsyate vā nirudhyate vā? śakra āha - no hīdamārya subhūte / tatkasya hetoḥ? ādiśuddhatvādādipariśuddhatvātsattvasya / subhūtirāha - anenāpi kauśika paryāyeṇa evaṃ sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ ca punaḥ kauśika sattvānantatayā prajñāpāramitānantatā veditavyā //
body.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>—of which <s>dharma</s> is this the designation, namely 'being, being'? <s>Śakra</s> said: Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, this is not the designation of a <s>dharma</s> nor the designation of a non-<s>dharma</s>, namely 'being, being.' This is an adventitious name that has been imposed. This is a name without substance that has been imposed. This is a name that belongs to no self that has been imposed. This is a name without a referent that has been imposed, namely 'being, being.' The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>—has any indication of a being been made here? <s>Śakra</s> said: No indeed, noble <s>Subhūti</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Where, <s>Kauśika</s>, no indication of a being has been made, what infinitude of beings is there? If, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, with an infinite-proclamation voice, with a deep-resounding sound, were to remain for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> and utter the words 'being, being'—would any being have arisen, will arise, or is arising, or have ceased, will cease, or is ceasing? <s>Śakra</s> said: No indeed, noble <s>Subhūti</s>. For what reason? Because of the primordial purity, the primordial complete purity, of the being. <s>Subhūti</s> said: By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, by the infinitude of beings, this is an infinite perfection, namely the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, by the infinitude of beings, the infinitude of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.

body.text: atha khalu sendrakā devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ saprajāpatikāḥ sarṣinaranārīgaṇāstrirudānamudānayanti sma - aho dharmaḥ, aho dharmaḥ, aho dharmasya dharmatā / yastathāgatasya prādurbhāvaḥ, sa āryeṇa subhūtinā sthavireṇa subhāṣiteneha sūcyate deśyate prakāśyate prabhāvyate / tathāgataṃ taṃ vayaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamadyāgreṇa dhārayiṣyāmo yo 'nayā prajñāpāramitayā avirahito bhaviṣyati, yo 'pi ca anena bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa vihariṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>devas</s> with <s>Śakra</s>, with <s>Brahmā</s>, with <s>Prajāpati</s>, together with the hosts of sages, men, and women, uttered three exclamations: Oh, the <s>Dharma</s>! Oh, the <s>Dharma</s>! Oh, the true nature of the <s>Dharma</s>! That which is the appearance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>—that is being indicated, taught, illuminated, and made manifest here by the noble elder <s>Subhūti</s> through his excellent speech. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, from today onward we shall uphold that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who shall not be separated from this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and also the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who shall dwell in this abiding of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstān sendrakān sabrahmakān saprajāpatikān sarṣinaranārīgaṇānāmantrayate sma - evametaddevaputrāḥ, evam etat / yadāhaṃ devaputrā dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntike dīpavatyāṃ rājadhānyāmantarāyaṇamadhyagato 'nayā prajñāpāramitayā avirahito 'bhūvam, tadāhaṃ dīpaṃkareṇa tathāgatenārhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhena vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau - bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava anāgate 'dhvani asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpaiḥ śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyānāṃ ca buddho bhagavāniti / atha khalu te devaputrā bhagavantametadavocan - āścaryaṃ bhagavan, paramāścaryaṃ sugata / yāvadiyaṃ prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ sarvajñatāyā āhārikā anuparigrāhikā ceti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed those <s>devas</s> with <s>Śakra</s>, with <s>Brahmā</s>, with <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the hosts of sages, men, and women: Just so, O sons of the gods, just so. When I, O sons of the gods, was in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, in the royal city of <s>Dīpavatī</s>, standing in the middle of a street, and was not separated from this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—then I was predicted by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for unsurpassed perfect awakening: 'You, young man, in the future, after innumerable <s>kalpas</s>, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then those sons of the gods said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: It is wonderful, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! Most wonderful, O <s>Sugata</s>! How this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the bringer and the sustainer of <s>sarvajñatā</s> for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>!

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śakraparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The second chapter, named the Chapter on <s>Śakra</s>, in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: ASP_3: aprameyaguṇadhāraṇapāramitāstūpasatkāraparivartastṛtīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: ASP Chapter 3: The Chapter on the Perfection of Retaining Immeasurable Virtues and the Honoring of <s>Stūpas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān ye tatra devaputrāḥ parṣadi saṃnipatitāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāścābhūvan, yāś ca bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāścābhūvan, tān devaputrān saṃnipatitān saṃniṣaṇṇāṃś ca viditvā, tāś ca sarvāścatasraḥ parṣadaḥ saṃnipatitāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāś ca viditvā, kāmāvacarān rūpāvacarāṃś ca devaputrān brahmakāyikāṃś ca devaputrān ābhāsvarāṃś ca parīttaśubhāṃś ca akaniṣṭhāṃś ca devaputrān sākṣiṇaḥ sthāpayitvā, śakradevendrapramukhān kāmāvacarān devaputrān mahābrahmapramukhāṃś ca brahmakāyikān devaputrānābhāsvarāṃś ca devaputrānāmantrayate sma - yo hi kaściddevaputrāḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati, na tasya māro vā mārakāyikā vā devatā avatāraprekṣiṇyo 'vatāragaveṣiṇyo 'vatāraṃ lapsyante / nāpi tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā avatāraprekṣiṇo 'vatāragaveṣiṇo 'vatāraṃ lapsyante / nāpi sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā viṣamāparihāreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that those sons of the gods who had assembled and were seated in the assembly, and those <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, and <s>upāsikās</s> who had assembled and were seated, and knowing that all four assemblies had assembled and were seated—placing as witnesses the sons of the gods of the realm of desire, the realm of form, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods—addressed the sons of the gods of the realm of desire led by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods led by <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, and the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods: Whoever, O sons of the gods—whether a son or daughter of good family—shall take up, retain, recite, master, and propagate this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, neither <s>Māra</s> nor <s>Māra</s>'s deities, seeking an opportunity, looking for an opening, shall find an opening against them. Nor shall humans or non-humans seeking an opportunity, looking for an opening, find an opening against that son or daughter of good family. Nor shall that son or daughter of good family meet death through any adverse accident.

body.text: punaraparaṃ devaputrāḥ ye devaputrā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāḥ, yaiś ca devaputrairiyaṃ prajñāpāramitā nodgṛhītā na dhāritā na vācitā na paryavāptā na pravartitā, te devaputrāstaṃ kulaputra vā kuladuhitaraṃ vā upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante, tasya ca kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇato dhārayato vācayataḥ paryavāpnuvataḥ pravartayamānasyāntikācchroṣyanti, śrutvā codgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti pravartayiṣyanti / na ca khalu punardevaputrāstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇato dhārayato vācayataḥ paryavāpnuvataḥ pravartayamānasya araṇyagatasya vā vṛkṣamūlagatasya vā śūnyāgāragatasya vā abhyavakāśagatasya vā pathi gatasya vā utpathagatasya vā aṭavīgatasya vā mahāsamudragatasya vā tatra tatropasaṃkrāmato vā caṃkramyamāṇasya vā sthitasya vā niṣaṇṇasya vā vipannasya vā bhayaṃ vā bhaviṣyati, stambhitatvaṃ vā bhaviṣyati, utpatsyate vā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O sons of the gods, those sons of the gods who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening but have not taken up, retained, recited, mastered, or propagated this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—those sons of the gods will think they should visit that son or daughter of good family. And in the presence of that son or daughter of good family who is taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and propagating this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will listen; and having listened, will take it up, retain, recite, master, and propagate it. And furthermore, O sons of the gods, for that son or daughter of good family who is taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and propagating this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—whether gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, to an empty dwelling, to the open air, gone on a road, gone off the road, gone to the wilderness, gone to the great ocean, or going here and there, walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—there shall be no fear, no paralysis, nor shall any arise.

body.text: atha khalu catvāro mahārājāno bhagavantametadavocan - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yadimāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇan dhārayan vācayan paryavāpnuvan pravartayan sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yānatraye sattvān vinayati, na ca sattvasaṃjñāmutpādayati / vayaṃ bhagavaṃstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmaḥ, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then the Four Great Kings said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: It is wonderful, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that this son or daughter of good family, taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and propagating this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, disciplines beings in the three vehicles and yet does not generate the perception of a being. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we shall provide protection, shelter, and guarding for that son or daughter of good family who will take up, retain, recite, master, and propagate this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - aham api bhagavaṃstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmi, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: I too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall provide protection, shelter, and guarding for that son or daughter of good family who will take up, retain, recite, master, and propagate this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: brahmāpi sahāpatiḥ sārdhaṃ brahmakāyikairdevaputrairbhagavantametadavocat - aham api bhagavaṃstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmi, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati //
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> too, together with the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: I too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall provide protection, shelter, and guarding for that son or daughter of good family who will take up, retain, recite, master, and propagate this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yadimāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇan dhārayan vācayan paryavāpnuvan pravartayan sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imān yato dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān pratilabhate parigṛhṇāti, kiṃ punarbhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāmudgṛhītāyāṃ sarvāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitā udgṛhītā bhavanti? evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - evametatkauśika, evam etat / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ kauśika udgṛhītāyāṃ sarvāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitā udgṛhītā bhavanti / punaraparaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāmudgṛhītāyāṃ dhāritāyāṃ vācitāyāṃ paryavāptāyāṃ pravartitāyāṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛhṇāti / tān kauśik sarvān śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti śakro devānāmindro bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavānetadavocat - tatra kauśika ye mama dharmaṃ vigrahītavyaṃ maṃsyante, vivaditavyaṃ maṃsyante, virodhayitavyaṃ maṃsyante, teṣāṃ vigrahītukāmānāṃ vivaditukāmānāṃ virodhayitukāmānāmutpannotpannā vigrahā vivādā virodhāḥ, punarevāntardhāsyanti, na sthāsyanti / teṣāṃ vigrahītukāmānāṃ vivaditukāmānāṃ virodhayitukāmānāṃ na te 'bhiprāyāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? evaṃ hyetatkauśika bhavati - ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati, tasyaivaṃ tānyutpannotpannānyadhikaraṇāni punarevāntardhāsyanti, na sthāsyanti / teṣāṃ vigrahītukāmānāṃ vivaditukāmānāṃ virodhayitukāmānāṃ na te 'bhiprāyāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti / imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇāti dhārayati vācayati paryavāpnoti pravartayati deśayati upadiśati uddiśati svādhyāyati / tadyathāpi nāma kauśika maghī nāmauṣadhī sarvaviṣapraśamanī / tatra āśīviṣeṇa jantunā bubhukṣitena āhārārthinā āhāragaveṣiṇā kaścideva prāṇakajāto janturdṛṣṭo bhavet / sa āśīviṣastaṃ prāṇakajātaṃ gandhenānubadhnīyādanugacchedāhārahetorbhakṣayitukāmaḥ / atha sa prāṇakajāto yena sā madhī nāmauṣadhī tenopasaṃkramet, tenopasaṃkramya tiṣṭhet / atha sa āśīviṣastasyā oṣadhyā gandhenaiva pratyudāvarteta / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tasyā oṣadhyā bhaiṣajyaguṇaḥ sa tādṛśo yastasyāśīviṣasya tadviṣamabhibhavati / evaṃ balavatī hi sā oṣadhī / evameva kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā va imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati, tasya kauśika yāni tānyutpannotpannānyadhikaraṇāni vigrahā vivādā virodhā bhaviṣyanti, te prajñāpāramitāyāstejasā balena sthāmataḥ prajñāpāramitābalādhānena kṣipraṃ tata evoparaṃsyanti upaśamiṣyanti antardhāsyanti na vivardhiṣyante / yato yata evotpatsyante, tatra tatraiva nirotsyante antardhāsyanti, na vivardhiṣyante na sthāsyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? prajñāpāramitā hi rāgādīnāṃ yāvannirvāṇagrāhasyopaśamayitrī, na vivardhiketi / catvāraś ca tasya mahārājānaḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, said to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, O Blessed One, that a son or daughter of good family, by taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and propagating this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, obtains and acquires these qualities visible in this very life. How much more, O Blessed One, when the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been taken up, [will] all six <s>Pāramitās</s>—"

body.text: śakraś ca devānāmindro brahmā ca sahāpatiḥ sarve ca buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvāś ca rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyanti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyatiḥ uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati / ayaṃ tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmiko guṇaḥ parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, and <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, and all the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will provide protection, shelter, and safeguarding for one who will take up, retain, recite, master, propagate, teach, instruct, expound, and study this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. That son of good family or daughter of good family—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati, sa ādeyavacanaś ca bhaviṣyati, mṛduvacanaś ca bhaviṣyati, mitavacanaś ca bhaviṣyati, aprakīrṇavacanaś ca bhaviṣyati, na ca krodhābhibhūto bhaviṣyati, na ca mānābhibhūto bhaviṣyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi taṃ prajñāpāramitā paridamayati, prajñāpāramitā pariṇamayati, na krodhaṃ vardhayati, na mānaṃ vardhayati / sa nopanāhaṃ parigṛhṇāti, na vyāpādaṃ parigṛhṇāti, nānuśayaṃ dhārayati / evaṃ carato 'sya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā smṛtirmaitrī cotpadyate / tasyaivaṃ bhavati - sacedahaṃ vyāpādamutpādayiṣyāmi, tenendriyāṇi me paribhetsyante, mukhavarṇaś ca me dhakṣyate / ayuktaṃ caitanmama yadahamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitaḥ, tatra śikṣitukāmaḥ, krodhasya vaśaṃ gaccheyam / ityevaṃ sa kṣiprameva smṛtiṃ pratilabhate / imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati / evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yatheyaṃ prajñāpāramitā paridamanāya pratyupasthitā anunāmāya bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family will take up, retain, recite, master, propagate, teach, instruct, expound, and study this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—that person will become one whose words are to be heeded, one whose speech is gentle, one whose speech is measured, one whose speech is not scattered,

body.text: bhagavānāha - punaraparaṃ kauśika ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati, sacetkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmevamudgṛhṇan dhārayan vācayan paryavāpnuvan pravartayan deśayan upadiśayan uddiśan svādhyāyan saṃgrāme vartamāne saṃgrāmaśirasi samārūḍhaḥ syāt / tasya saṃgrāmamavatarato vā avatīrṇasya vā atikrāmato vā saṃgrāmamadhyagatasya vā tiṣṭhato vā niṣaṇṇasya vā asthānametatkauśika anavakāśo yattasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ manasi kurvato vā udgṛhṇato vā dhārayato vā vācayato vā paryavāpnuvato vā pravartayato vā deśayato vā upadiśato vā uddiśato vā svādhyāyato vā jīvitāntarāyo vā bhavet / paropakrameṇa jīvitāntarāyaṃ so 'nuprāpnuyāt, naitatsthānaṃ vidyate / sacetpunastasya kaścitkauśika tatra śastraṃ vā daṇḍaṃ vā loṣṭaṃ vā anyadvā kṣipet, naitattasya śarīre nipatet / tatkasya hetoḥ? mahāvidyeyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā / apramāṇeyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā / aparimāṇeyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā / anuttareyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā / asameyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā / asamasameyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā / tatkasya hetoḥ? atra hi kauśika
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family will take up, retain, recite, master, propagate, teach, instruct, expound, and study this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—if that son or daughter of good family, while thus taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, propagating—"

body.text: vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā nātmavyābādhāya cetayate, na paravyābādhāya cetayate, nobhayavyābādhāya cetayate / atra hi kauśika vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate, sarvajñajñānaṃ ca pratilapsyate / tena so 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvasattvānāṃ cittāni vyavalokayiṣyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? atra hi kauśika vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na tatkiṃcidasti, yanna prāptaṃ vā na jñātaṃ vā na sākṣātkṛtaṃ vā syāt / tasmātsarvajñajñānamityucyate / ayam api kauśika tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā dṛṣṭadhārmiko guṇaḥ parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati //
body.translated_text: a son or daughter of good family who is training in this knowledge does not intend harm to oneself, does not intend harm to others, does not intend harm to both. For, <s>Kauśika</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training in this knowledge will attain <s>anuttarā samyaksa��bodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) and will obtain the knowledge of the Omniscient One. Therefore he will attain supreme perfect awakening—"

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yatreyaṃ prajñāpāramitā antaśo likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā pūjāpūrvaṃgamaṃ sthāpayitvā na satkariṣyate, nodgrahīṣyate, na dhārayiṣyate, na vācayiṣyate, na paryavāpsyate, na pravartayiṣyate, na deśayiṣyate, nopadekṣyate, noddekṣyate, na svādhyāsyate, na tatra kauśika sattvānāṃ manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā avatārārthiko 'vatāragaveṣī avatāraṃ lapsyate sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam / imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, wherever this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been written down, made into a book, and placed in a position of honor preceded by worship, even if it is not revered, not taken up, not retained, not recited, not mastered, not propagated, not taught, not instructed, not expounded, not studied—even there, <s>Kauśika</s>, beings' minds will not—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika tadyathāpi nāma ye bodhimaṇḍagatā vā bodhimaṇḍaparisāmantagatā vā bodhimaṇḍābhyantaragatā vā bodhivṛkṣamūlagatā vā manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā, tiryagyonigatānapyupādāya, yāvanna te śakyā manuṣyairvā amanuṣyairvā viheṭhayituṃ vā vyāpādayituṃ vā āveśayituṃ vā sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam / tatkasya hetoḥ? tatra hi atītānāgatapratyutpannāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbhotsyante abhisaṃbudhyante ca, ye sarvasattvānāmabhayamavairamanutrāsaṃ prabhāvayanti prakāśayanti / evameva kauśika yatra kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati, tatra hi kauśika sattvā na śakyā manuṣyairvā amanuṣyairvā viheṭhayituṃ vā vyāpādayituṃ vā āveśayituṃ vā, sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam / tatkasya hetoḥ? anayaiva hi kauśika prajñāpāramitayā pṛthivīpradeśaḥ sattvānāṃ caityabhūtaḥ kṛto vandanīyo mānanīyaḥ pūjanīyo 'rcanīyo 'pacāyanīyaḥ satkaraṇīyo gurukaraṇīyaḥ, trāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ layanaṃ parāyaṇaṃ kṛto bhaviṣyati tatropagatānāṃ sattvānām / imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, just as those beings—whether humans or non-humans, including even animals—who have gone to the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), or who are in the vicinity of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, or who are within the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, or who have gone to the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, cannot be harassed, harmed, or possessed by humans or non-humans—except by the ripening of previous <s>karma</s>—

body.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - yo bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā sthāpayet, enāṃ ca divyābhiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ, bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet, yaś ca
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, said to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, whatever son or daughter of good family, having written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and made it into a book, would place it [in a shrine] and honor it with divine flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, canopies, banners, bells, and pennants, and with rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of worship—"

body.text: tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya śarīrāṇi stūpeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet parigṛhṇīyāt dhārayeddhā, tāṃś ca tathaiva divyābhiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ, samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ, bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet, katarastayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet? evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - tena hi kauśika tvāmevātra pratiprakṣyāmi / yathā te kṣamate, tathā vyākuryāḥ / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika yo 'yaṃ tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sarvajñatātmabhāvo 'bhinirvartitaḥ, sa katamasyāṃ pratipadi śikṣamāṇena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ sarvajñatā pratilabdhā abhisaṃbuddhā? evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - ihaiva bhagavan bhagavatā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ sarvajñatā pratilabdhā abhisaṃbuddhā / bhagavānāha - tasmāttarhi kauśika nānenātmabhāvaśarīrapratilambhena tathāgatastathāgata iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / sarvajñatāyāṃ tu pratilabdhāyāṃ tathāgatastathāgata iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / yeyaṃ kauśika sarvajñatā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya, prajñāpāramitānirjātaiṣā / eṣa ca kauśika tathāgatasyātmabhāvaśarīrapratilambhaḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyanirjātaḥ san sarvajñajñānāśrayabhūto bhavati / enaṃ hyāśrayaṃ niśritya sarvajñajñānasya prabhāvanā bhavati, buddhaśarīraprabhāvanā bhavati, dharmaśarīraprabhāvanā bhavati, saṃghaśarīraprabhāvanā bhavati / ityevaṃ sarvajñajñānahetuko 'yamātmabhāvaśarīrapratilambhaḥ sarvajñajñānāśrayabhūtatvātsarvasattvānāṃ caityabhūto vandanīyaḥ satkaraṇīyo gurukaraṇīyo mānanīyaḥ pūjanīyo 'rcanīyo 'pacāyanīyaḥ saṃvṛtto bhavati / evaṃ ca mama parinirvṛtasyāpi sataḥ eṣāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ pūjā bhaviṣyati / tasmāttarhi kauśika yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ vā kṛtvā sthāpayet, enāṃ ca divyābhiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet, ayameva kauśika tayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvajñajñānasya hi kauśika tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati, yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā iha prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ pustakagatāyāṃ vā satkāraṃ gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ pūjāṃ ca vividhāṃ kuryāt, ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvajñajñānasya hi kauśika tena pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati, yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyai pūjāṃ kariṣyati //
body.translated_text: were to install, collect, and maintain the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in <s>stūpas</s>, and were to honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to those [stūpas] with divine flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, and with rows of lamps all around, and with manifold offerings—which of those two sons of good family or daughters of good family would produce more merit?" When this was said, the Blessed One said to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "Well then, <s>Kauśika</s>, I shall question you about this very matter. As it seems right to you, so you should answer. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>?
