body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: But how, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall that son or daughter of good family know thus: 'Here <s>devas</s>, or <s>nāgas</s>, or <s>yakṣas</s>, or <s>gandharvas</s>, or <s>asuras</s>, or <s>garuḍas</s>, or <s>kinnaras</s>, or <s>mahoragas</s>, or humans, or non-humans are coming to [venerate] this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'?

body.text: kuladuhitrā vā tatra gantavyā - iha devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā gandharvo vā asuro vā garuḍo vā kinnaro vā mahorago vā manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā āgata iti, upasaṃkrānta iti / punaraparaṃ sacetkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatra amānuṣaṃ gandhaṃ ghrāsyatyanāghrātapūrvam, ghrātvā ca tadgandhaṃ niṣṭhā tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tatra gantavyā - iha devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā gandharvo vā asuro vā garuḍo vā kinnaro vā mahorago vā manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā āgata iti, upasaṃkrānta iti //
body.translated_text: the son or daughter of good family should go there [knowing]: 'Here a <s>deva</s>, or a <s>nāga</s>, or a <s>yakṣa</s>, or a <s>gandharva</s>, or an <s>asura</s>, or a <s>garuḍa</s>, or a <s>kinnara</s>, or a <s>mahoraga</s>, or a human, or a non-human has come, has approached.' Furthermore, if, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son or daughter of good family should smell there a non-human fragrance—

body.text: punaraparaṃ sacetkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatra amānuṣaṃ gandhaṃ ghrāsyati anāghrātapūrvam, ghrātvā ca tadgandhaṃ niṣṭhā tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā tatra gantavyāḥ, - iha devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā gandharvo vā asuro vā garuḍo va kinnaro vā mahorago vā manuṣyo vā[amanuṣyo vā]āgata iti, upasaṃkrānta iti / punaraparaṃ sacetkauśika kulaputro va kuladuhitā vā caukṣasamudācāro bhaviṣyati, śucisamudācāro bhaviṣyati, tasya tayā caukṣasamudācāratayā śucisamudācāratayā te devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā āgantavyaṃ maṃsyante / ye ca tatra devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā āgatā bhaviṣyanti, te tasya tayā caukṣasamudācāratayā śucisamudācāratayā āttamanaskāḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā bhaviṣyanti / yāś ca tatra alpaujaskā alpaujaskā devatā adhyuṣitā bhaviṣyanti, tāstato 'pakramitavyaṃ maṃsyante / tatkasya hetoḥ? teṣāmeva hi mahaujaskānāṃ mahaujaskānāṃ devānāṃ nāgāna yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāmasurāṇāṃ garuḍānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ mahoragāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ mamanuṣyāṇāṃ vā śriyaṃ ca tejaś ca gauravaṃ ca asahamānā eva tā alpaujaskā alpaujaskā devatā tato 'pakramitavyaṃ maṃsyante / yathā yathā khalu punaḥ kauśika te mahaujaskā mahaujaskā devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā abhīkṣṇamupasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante, tathā tathā sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prasādabahulo bhaviṣyati / imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigrahīṣyati / tena khalu punaḥ kauśika kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tasya dharmanetrīsthānasya parisāmantake 'śuciracaukṣasamudācāro na pracārayitavyaḥ tasyāṃ gurugauravatāparipūrimupādāya //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son or daughter of good family should smell there a non-human fragrance never smelled before, having smelled that fragrance, the conclusion should be reached by that son or daughter of good family: 'Here a <s>deva</s>, or a <s>nāga</s>, or a <s>yakṣa</s>, or a <s>gandharva</s>, or an <s>asura</s>, or a <s>garuḍa</s>, or a <s>kinnara</s>,

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā na kāyaklamatho na cittaklamatha utpatsyate / sa sukhameva śayyāṃ kalpayiṣyati, sukhaṃ ca prakramiṣyati, suptaś ca san na pāpakān svapnān drakṣati, paśyaṃś ca punastathāgatānevārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān drakṣyati, stūpāneva drakṣyati, bodhisattvāneva drakṣyati, tathāgataśrāvakāneva drakṣyati / śabdāṃś ca śṛṇvan pāramitāśabdāneva śroṣyati, bodhipakṣāneva dharmān drakṣyati, bodhivṛkṣāneva drakṣyati, teṣu ca tathāgatānevārhataḥ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, for that son or daughter of good family, neither bodily fatigue nor mental fatigue shall arise. He shall prepare his bed comfortably, and shall set out comfortably. And when sleeping, he shall not see evil dreams; and what he sees shall be only <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones—

body.text: samyaksaṃbuddhānabhisaṃbudhyamānān drakṣyati / tathā abhisaṃbuddhānāṃ ca dharmacakrapravartanaṃ drakṣyati, bahūṃś ca bodhisattvāneva drakṣyati imāmeva prajñāpāramitāṃ saṃgāyamānān prajñāpāramitāsaṃgītiratān - evaṃ sarvajñatā parigrahītavyā, evaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ viśodhayitavyam, ityupāyakauśalaṃ ca upadiśataḥ / udāraṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmabhisaṃbodhiśabdaṃ śroṣyati - amuṣyāṃ diśi amuṣmin digbhāge amuṣmin lokadhātau amuko 'sau nāmnā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakāṇāṃ śatairbahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakasahasrair bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakaśatasahasrair bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭībhir bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīśatair bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīsahasraiḥ bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīśatasahasrairbahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayatīti / yaś ca khalu punaḥ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imānevaṃrūpān svapnān drakṣyati, sa sukhameva svapsyati, sukhaṃ ca pratibhotsyate, ojaḥprakṣiptaṃ ca kāyaṃ sukhaṃ ca pratisaṃvedayiṣyati, laghu ladhveva ca pratisaṃvedayiṣyati / na cāsya adhimātrayā āhāragṛddhyā cittasaṃtatirutpatsyate / mṛdukā ca asya āhārasaṃjñā bhavati / tadyathāpi nāma kauśika bhikṣoryogācārasya samādhervyutthitasya manasikārapariṣyanditena cittena na balavatyāhāre gṛddhirbhavati, mṛdukā cāsya āhārasaṃjñā bhavati, evameva kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā na balavatyāhāre gṛddhirbhaviṣyati / mṛdukā cāsya āhārasaṃjñā bhaviṣyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? evaṃ hyetatkauśika bhavati - yathāpi nāma prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyogānuyuktatvāttasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā tathā hyasya amanuṣyāḥ kāye oja upasaṃhartavyaṃ maṃsyante / imān api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: he will see Perfectly Awakened Ones in the process of attaining supreme perfect awakening. Likewise, he will see the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) by those who have attained awakening, and he will see many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> reciting this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, delighting in the recitation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: 'Thus should <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) be comprehended, thus the <s>Buddha</s>—'

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā pūjāpūrvaṃgamaṃ sthāpayet pūjayennodgṛhṇīyānna dhārayenna vācayenna paryavāpnuyāt na pravartayenna deśayennopadiśennoddiśenna svādhyāyet, ayameva tataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati / yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmabhiśraddadhadavakalpayannadhimucya prasannacitto bodhāya cittamutpādya adhyāśayataḥ śṛṇuyādudgṛhṇīyāddhārayedvācayetparyavāpnuyātpravartayeddeśayedupadiśeduddiśetsvādhyāyet, parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet, arthamasyā vivṛṇuyāt, manasānvavekṣeta, yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsāmāpadyeta, antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā dhārayetsthāpayetsaddharmacirasthitihetoḥ - mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt, mā saddharmāntardhānam / bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cānugrahopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati netryavaikalyeneti / tāṃ caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayetpūjayedarcayedapacāyetpuṣpairdhūpairgandhairmālyairvile - panaiścūrṇairvastraiśchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ, samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ pūjayet, ayameva tataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati / tasmāttarhi kauśika imān dṛṣṭadhārmikān viśiṣṭān guṇān parigṛhītukāmena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā iyameva prajñāpāramitā abhiśraddhātavyā
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son or daughter of good family, having written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and made it into a book, should place it in a position of honor preceded by worship, and worship it, but should not take it up, retain, recite, master, propagate, teach, instruct, expound, or study it—this very [merit] from that—

body.text: avakalpayitavyā adhibhoktavyā / prasannacittena bodhāya cittamutpādya satkṛtya adhyāśayena śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā deśayitavyā upadeṣṭavyā uddeṣṭavyā svādhyātavyā, parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyā, arthato vivaritavyā, manasānvavekṣitavyā, yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsāmāpadyeta / antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā sthāpayitavyā pūjayitavyā saddharmacirasthitihetoḥ - mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt, mā saddharmāntardhānam / bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cānugrahopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati netryavaikalyeneti / arthikānāṃ ca kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca saṃvibhāgaṃ kariṣyāmi, mama ca pareṣāṃ ca kalyāṇasattvānāṃ buddhanetrīmahācakṣuravaikalyatā bhaviṣyatīti / sadā ca satkartavyā gurukartavyā mānayitavyā pūjayitavyā arcayitavyā apacāyitavyā puṣpairdhūpairgandhairmālyairvilepanaiścūrṇairvastraiśchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ, samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ, bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ pūjayitavyeti //
body.translated_text: should be applied and appropriated. With a clear mind, having generated the thought of awakening, it should be heard with respect and with deep intention, taken up, retained, recited, mastered, propagated, taught, instructed, expounded, studied, and extensively illuminated for others.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmaprameyaguṇadhāraṇapāramitāstūpasatkāraparivarto nāma tṛtīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the Third Chapter, called "The Perfection of Retaining Immeasurable Qualities and the Worship of <s>Stūpas</s>," in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

body.text: ASP_4: guṇaparikīrtanaparivartaścaturthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Four: The Enumeration of Qualities.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindramāmantrayate sma - sacetkauśika ayaṃ te jambūdvīpaḥ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhastathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ dīyeta, iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvopanāmyeta, tata ekatareṇa bhāgena pravāryamāṇo 'nayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayoḥ katamaṃ tvaṃ kauśika bhāgaṃ gṛhṇīyāḥ? śakra āha - sacenme bhagavan ayaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhastathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ dīyeta, iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvopanāmyeta, tata ekatareṇa bhāgena pravāryamāṇo 'nayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorimāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām / tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpi nāma tathāgatanetrīcitrīkāreṇa / etaddhi tathāgatānāṃ bhūtārthikaṃ śarīram / tatkasya hetoḥ? uktaṃ hyetadbhagavatā - dharmakāyā buddhā bhagavantaḥ / mā khalu punarimaṃ bhikṣavaḥ satkāyaṃ kāyaṃ manyadhvam / dharmakāyapariniṣpattito māṃ bhikṣavo drakṣyatha / eṣa ca tathāgatakāyo bhūtakoṭiprabhāvito draṣṭavyo yaduta prajñāpāramitā / na khalu punarme bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣvagauravam / gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu / api tu khalu punarbhagavan itaḥ prajñāpāramitāto nirjātāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante / tasmāttarhi bhagavan anayaiva prajñāpāramitayā pūjitayā teṣām api tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇā pūjā kṛtā bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? prajñāpāramitānirjātattvāttathāgataśarīrāṇām / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāmahaṃ yasmin samaye divye svake āsane niṣaṇṇo bhavāmi, tadā mama devaputrā upasthānāyāgacchanti / yasmin samaye na niṣaṇṇo bhavāmi, atha tasmin samaye yanmamāsanaṃ tatra devaputrā mama gauraveṇa tadāsanaṃ namaskṛtya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punareva prakrāmanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? iha hi kila āsane niṣadya śakro devānāmindro devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayatīti / evameva bhagavan maheśākhyahetupratyayabhūtā prajñāpāramitā / tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sarvajñatāyā āhārikā / sarvajñatāyāś ca tathāgataśarīrāṇyāśrayabhūtāni / na tu tāni pratyayabhūtāni, na kāraṇabhūtāni jñānasyotpādāya / evameva bhagavan sarvajñajñānahetukā tathāgataśarīreṣu pūjā kṛtā bhavati / tasmāttarhi bhagavan anayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorimāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām / na khalu punarme bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣvagauravam / gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu / api tu khalu punarbhagavaṃstāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitatvātpūjāṃ labhante / tiṣṭhatu khalu punarbhagavan ayaṃ jambūdvīpastathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ / tiṣṭhatu cāturmahādvīpako lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ / tiṣṭhatu sāhasro lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ / tiṣṭhatu bhagavan dvisāhasro madhyamo lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ / ayameva bhagavaṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ, eko bhāgaḥ kṛtvā sthāpyeta, iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvā dvitīyo bhāgaḥ sthāpyeta / anayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorekatareṇa bhāgena pravāryamāṇo 'nayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayoryaste bhāgo 'bhipretastamekaṃ bhāgaṃ gṛhāṇeti, tatra imāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām / na khalu
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the Blessed One addressed <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods: "If, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> of yours, completely filled to the brim with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, were offered [to you], and this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having been written, were presented—and if, being required to choose between these two portions,

body.text: punarbhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣvagauravam / gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu / api tu khalu punarbhagavaṃstāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitāni pūjāṃ labhante / tathāgataśarīrāṇi hi sarvajñajñānāśrayabhūtāni / tad api sarvajñajñānaṃ prajñāpāramitānirjātam / tasmāttarhi bhagavan anayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorimāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām / na khalu punar me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣvagauravam / gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu / api tu khalu punarbhagavan itaḥ prajñāpāramitāto nirjātāni tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante yaduta prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitatvāt / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan anarghaṃ maṇiratnamebhirevaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ syāt / tadyathā - tadyatra yatra sthāpyeta, tatra tatra manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā avatāraṃ na labheran / yatra yatra vā amanuṣyagṛhītaḥ kaścidbhavet puruṣo vā strī vā, tatra tatra tasmin maṇiratne praveśitamātre so 'manuṣyastato 'pakrāmet / vātenāpi bādhyamānasya dhamyamāne śarīre tanmaṇiratnaṃ sthāpyeta / tasya taṃ vātaṃ nigṛhṇīyāt, na vivardhayet, upaśamayet / pittenāpi dahyamāne śarīre sthāpyeta / tasya tad api pittaṃ nigṛhṇīyāt, na vivardhayet, upaśamayet / śleṣmaṇāpi parigṛddhe sarvato bādhyamāne śarīre sthāpyeta, tasya tam api śleṣmāṇaṃ nigṛhṇīyāt, na vivardhayet, upaśamayet / sāṃnipātikenāpi vyādhinā duḥkhitasya śarīre sthāpyeta, tasya tam api sāṃnipātikaṃ vyādhiṃ nigṛhṇīyāt, na vivardhayet, upaśamayet / andhakāratamisrāyāṃ ca rātrāvapyavabhāsaṃ kuryāt / uṣṇe cāpi vartamāne yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe sthāpyeta, sa pṛthivīpradeśaḥ śītalo bhavet / śīte cāpi vartamāne yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe sthāpyeta, sa pṛthivīpradeśa uṣṇo bhavet / yasmiṃś ca pṛthivīpradeśe āśīviṣā anuvicareyuḥ, tathā anye 'pi kṣudrajantavaḥ, tatrāpi pṛthivīpradeśe dhāryeta, sthāpitaṃ vā bhavet, te 'pyāśīviṣāste ca kṣudrajantavastato 'pakrāmeyuḥ / sacedbhagavan strī vā puruṣo vā āśīviṣeṇa daṣṭo bhavet, tasya tanmaṇiratnaṃ daśyeta, tasya sahadaṃśanenaiva maṇiratnasya tadviṣaṃ pratihanyeta vigacchet / ebhiścānyaiś ca bhagavan evaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tanmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet / yeṣām api keṣāṃcidbhagavan akṣiṣvarbudaṃ vā timiraṃ vā akṣirogo vā paṭalaṃ vā bhavet, teṣāṃ ca tanmaṇiratnamakṣiṣu sthāpyeta, teṣāṃ sthāpitamātreṇaiva te 'kṣidoṣā nirghātaṃ praśamaṃ gaccheyuḥ / etaiś ca anyaiś ca bhagavan evaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tanmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet / yatra codake sthāpyeta, tadapyudakamekavarṇaṃ kuryātsvakena varṇena / sacetpāṇḍareṇa vastreṇa pariveṣṭya udake prakṣipyeta, tadudakaṃ pāṇḍarīkuryāt / evaṃ sacennīlena pītena lohitena māñjiṣṭhena eteṣāmanyeṣāṃ vā nānāprakārāṇāṃ vastrāṇāmanyatamena vastreṇa tanmaṇiratnaṃ veṣṭayitvā vā baddhvā vā udake prakṣipyeta, tena tena vastrarāgeṇa tattatsvabhāvavarṇaṃ tadudakaṃ kuryāt / yo 'pi tasyodakasya kaluṣabhāvastam api prasādayet / ebhir api bhagavan evaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tanmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet //
body.translated_text: nor do I lack reverence, <s>Bhagavān</s>, toward those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics. I have nothing but reverence, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics. However, <s>Bhagavān</s>, those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics receive worship because they are pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics are the basis of omniscient knowledge. And that omniscient knowledge itself is born from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, between these two portions placed [before me], I would take hold of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Not that I lack reverence, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics. I have nothing but reverence, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics. However, <s>Bhagavān</s>, those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics receive worship precisely because they are born from this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, being pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Just as, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there might be a priceless jewel-gem endowed with such qualities as these: wherever it would be placed, there neither humans nor non-humans could gain entry; wherever a man or woman might be possessed by a non-human, when that jewel-gem is brought near, that non-human would depart from there. If one is afflicted by wind, with the body being blown upon, that jewel-gem placed [on the body] would restrain that wind, not increase it, and pacify it. If the body is burning with bile, placed [on it], it would restrain that bile too, not increase it, and pacify it. If the body is seized by phlegm, afflicted everywhere, placed [on it], it would restrain that phlegm too, not increase it, and pacify it. If one suffers from an illness of combined humors, placed on the body, it would restrain that combined illness too, not increase it, and pacify it. And even in the darkness of night, it would create illumination. And even in hot weather, whatever spot of earth it is placed upon, that spot of earth would become cool. And even in cold weather, whatever spot of earth it is placed upon, that spot of earth would become warm. And in whatever spot of earth venomous serpents and other small creatures wander, if it were held or placed there, those venomous serpents and small creatures would depart from there.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandaḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - kiṃ punaḥ kauśika devaloka
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods: 'But, <s>Kauśika</s>, do such jewel-gems exist only in the heavens

body.text: eva tāni maṇiratnāni santi, uta jāmbūdvīpakānām api manuṣyāṇāṃ tāni maṇiratnāni santi? śakra āha - deveṣvāryānanda tāni maṇiratnāni santi / api tu khalu punarjāmbudvīpakānām api manuṣyāṇāṃ maṇiratnāni santi / tāni tu gurukāṇi alpāni parīttāni guṇavikalāni, na taistathārūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgatāni / tatteṣāṃ divyānāṃ maṇiratnānāṃ śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopayānti, sahasratamīmapi, śatasahasratamīmapi, koṭītamīmapi, koṭīśatatamīmapi, koṭīsahasratamīmapi, koṭīśatasahasratamīmapi, koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīm api kalāṃ nopayānti, saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām api upamām api aupamyam api upanisām api upaniṣadam api na kṣamante nopayānti / yāni khalu punardeveṣu, tāni laghūni sarvākāraguṇaparipūrṇāni / yatra ca karaṇḍake tanmaṇiratnaṃ prakṣiptaṃ bhavati utkṣiptaṃ vā, tata uddhṛte 'pi tasmin maṇiratne karaṇḍakāt spṛhaṇīya eva sa karaṇḍako bhavati / tairmaṇiratnaguṇaiḥ parā tatra karaṇḍake spṛhotpadyate / evameva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyā ete guṇāḥ sarvajñajñānasya ca / yena parinirvṛtasyāpi tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante - sarvajñajñānasyemāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi bhājanabhūtānyabhūvanniti / yathā ca bhagavan sarvalokadhātuṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā prajñāpāramitānirjātatvātpūjyā, evaṃ dharmabhāṇakasya dharmadeśanā prajñāpāramitānirjātatvātpūjyā / yathā ca bhagavan rājapuruṣo rājānubhāvānmahato janakāyasya akutobhayaḥ pūjyaḥ, evaṃ sa dharmabhāṇako dharmakāyānubhāvānmahato janakāyasya akutobhayaḥ pūjyaḥ / yathā ca dharmadeśanā dharmabhāṇakāś ca pūjāṃ labhante, evaṃ tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante / tasmāttarhi bhagavan tiṣṭhatu trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ, ye 'pi bhagavan gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavaḥ, te 'pi sarve tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇāścūlikābaddhā eko bhāgaḥ sthāpyeta, iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvā dvitīyo bhāgaḥ sthāpyeta / tatra cenmāṃ bhagavan kaścideva pravārayedanyatareṇa bhāgena, pravāryamāṇo 'nayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayoḥ - yaste bhāgo 'bhipretaḥ tamekaṃ bhāgaṃ parigṛhṇīṣveti, tatra imāmevāhaṃ bhagavaṃstayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorbhāgaṃ gṛhṇīyāṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitām / na khalu punarbhagavan mama teṣu tathāgataśarīreṣvagauravam / gauravameva bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu / api tu khalu punarbhagavan prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitā sarvajñatā, sarvajñatānirjātā ca tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ pūjā bhavati / tasmāttarhi bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pūjitāyāmatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā kṛtā bhavati //
body.translated_text: , or do the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> also have such jewel-gems?' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Among the gods, noble <s>Ānanda</s>, those jewel-gems exist. But the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> also have jewel-gems. But those are heavy, small, limited, and deficient in qualities—not endowed with such qualities. They do not equal even a hundredth part of those divine jewel-gems, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor a <s>koṭi</s>th, nor a hundred-<s>koṭi</s>th, nor a thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th, nor a hundred-thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th, nor a <s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th part—they do not approach them in number, fraction, calculation, comparison, similarity, or analogy.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan ye 'prameyeṣvasaṃkhyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavanta etarhi tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti, tān dharmatayā draṣṭukāmena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritavyam, prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpattavyam / prajñāpāramitā bhāvayitavyā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a son or daughter of good family who wishes to see the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who presently dwell, abide, and live in immeasurable and innumerable world-systems should practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, should apply themselves to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, should cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - evametatkauśika, evam etat / ye 'pi te kauśika abhūvannatīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ, te 'pi kauśika imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones who in the past fully awakened to supreme perfect awakening—they too, <s>Kauśika</s>, fully awakened to supreme perfect awakening through relying upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: ye 'pi te kauśika bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, te 'pi kauśika imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / ye 'pi te kauśika etarhi aprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti, te 'pi kauśika buddhā bhagavantaḥ imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ / aham api kauśika etarhi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones who will arise in the future—they too, <s>Kauśika</s>, will fully awaken to supreme perfect awakening through relying upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who presently dwell, abide, and live in immeasurable and innumerable world-systems—they too, <s>Kauśika</s>, fully awakened to supreme perfect awakening through relying upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. I too, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one, have fully awakened to supreme perfect awakening through relying upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - mahāpāramiteyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramitā / sarvasattvānāṃ hi bhagavaṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaścittacaritāni samyak prajānāti saṃpaśyati / bhagavānāha - evametatkauśika, evam etat / tathā hi kauśika bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dīrgharātraṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, tena sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaritāni prajñāpāramitāyāṃ samyak prajānāti saṃpaśyati //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This is a great perfection, <s>Bhagavān</s>—namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one truly knows and sees the mental activities of all beings, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. For the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for a long time truly knows and sees the mental activities of all beings through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - kiṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāmeva bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati nānyāsu pāramitāsu? bhagavānāha - sarvāsu kauśika ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati / api tu khalu punaḥ kauśika prajñāpāramitaiva atra pūrvaṃgamā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dānaṃ vā dadataḥ, śīlaṃ vā rakṣataḥ, kṣāntyā vā saṃpādayamānasya, vīryaṃ vā ārabhamāṇasya, dhyānaṃ vā samāpadyamānasya, dharmān vā vipaśyataḥ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitaivātra pūrvaṃgamā / na ca kauśika āsāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāmupāyakauśalyaparigṛhītānāṃ prajñāpāramitāpariṇāmitānāṃ sarvajñatāpariṇāmitānāṃ viśeṣaḥ, na ca nānākaraṇamupalabhyate / tadyathāpi nāma kauśika jambudvīpe nānāvṛkṣā nānāvarṇā nānāsaṃsthānā nānāpatrā nānāpuṣpā nānāphalā nānārohapariṇāhasaṃpannāḥ, na ca teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ chāyāyā viśeṣo vā nānākaraṇaṃ vā prajñāyate, api tu chāyā chāyetyevaṃ saṃkhyāṃ gacchati, evameva kauśika āsāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāmupāyakauśalyaparigṛhītānāṃ prajñāpāramitāpariṇāmitānāṃ sarvajñatāpariṇāmitānāṃ na viśeṣaḥ, na ca nānākaraṇamupalabhyate / evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - mahāguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramitā / aprameyaguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramitā / aparyantaguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramiteti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practice only in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and not in the other <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices in all six <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>. However, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the forerunner for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>—whether giving <s>dāna</s> (generosity), guarding <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), accomplishing <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), undertaking <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), entering into <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), or investigating <s>dharmas</s>—for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the forerunner in all of these. And, <s>Kauśika</s>, without these six <s>pāramitās</s> being embraced by skillful means and directed by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> [they would not lead to full awakening].

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ guṇaparikīrtanaparivarto nāma caturthaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the fourth chapter of the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, called 'The Proclamation of Virtues.'

body.text: ASP_5: puṇyaparyāyaparivartaḥ pañcamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 5 of the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>: The Chapter on the Varieties of Merit, the fifth.

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - yo bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmabhiśraddadhadavakalpayannadhimucya prasannacitto bodhāya cittamutpādya adhyāśayataḥ śṛṇuyādudgṛhṇīyāddhārayedvācayet paryavāpnuyāt pravartayeddeśayedupadiśeduddiśetsvādhyāyet, parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet, arthamasyā vivṛṇuyāt, manasānvavekṣeta, yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsāmāpadyeta, antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā dhārayetsthāpayetsaddharmacirasthitihetoḥ - mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt, mā saddharmāntardhānam / bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ca anugrahopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati netryavaikalyeneti / evamimaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā evaṃmahārthikā bateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā, evaṃmahānuśaṃsā, evaṃmahāphalā, evaṃmahāvipākā bateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā, evaṃ bahuguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā, aparityajanīyā mayā prajñāpāramitā, rakṣitavyā mama prajñāpāramitā, gopāyitavyā mama prajñāpāramitā, paramadurlabhā hīyaṃ prajñāpāramitetyadhimuñcet / svayameva caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayetpūjayedarcayedapacāyetpuṣpairdhūpairgandhairmālyairvilepanaiścūrṇairvastraiśchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ, samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ, bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ yo vā anyaḥ saṃpūjya parasmai cārthikāya chandikāya kulaputrāya kuladuhitre vā yācamānāya dadyādupanāmayenniryātayetparityajet, antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā / katarastayorbhagavan kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet - yo vā parityāgabuddhiryo vā na parityāgabuddhiḥ? evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - tena hi kauśika tvāmevātra pratiprakṣyāmi / yathā te kṣamate vyākuryāḥ / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya śarīraṃ satkṛtya paricareddhārayet satkuryādgurukuryānmānayet pūjayedarcayedapacāyet svayameva / yo vā anyaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgataśarīraṃ svayaṃ ca satkuryādgurukuryānmānayetpūjayedarcayedapacāyet, parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet, dadyāt saṃvibhajet vaistārikī pūjā bhaviṣyatīti sattvānāṃ cānukampāmupādāya / katarastayordvayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet? kiṃ yaḥ svayaṃ ca pūjayet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayeddadyāt saṃvibhajet, kiṃ vā yaḥ svayameva pratyātmaṃ pūjayet? śakra āha - yo bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā svayaṃ ca tathāgataśarīraṃ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayetpūjayedarcayedapacāyet, parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayeddadyātsaṃvibhajet vaistārikī pūjā bhaviṣyatīti sattvānāṃ cānukampāmupādāya, ayamevānayordvayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati / bhagavānāha - evametatkauśika, evam etat / evametatkauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā udgṛhṇīyāddhārayedvācayet paryavāpnuyāt pravartayeddeśayedupadiśeduddiśetsvādhyāyet, parasmai cārthikāya chandikāya kulaputrāya kuladuhitre vā yācamānāya dadyādupanāmayenniryātayetparityajedantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā / ayameva kauśika tayordvayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, a son of good family or daughter of good family who, with faith, without conceptualizing, with conviction, with a clear mind, having generated the mind of awakening, with pure intention, would hear, take up, retain, recite, master, propagate, teach, instruct, expound, and study this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and would illuminate it extensively to others, explain its meaning, examine it with the mind, and investigate it with the most excellent wisdom, and even making it into a book would retain and preserve it for the sake of the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>—[thinking:] 'May there not be the cutting off of the <s>Buddha</s>'s guidance! May there not be the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>! And beneficence and assistance to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> will have been accomplished through the completeness of the guidance'—and having heard this exposition, would resolve: 'How greatly beneficial is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>! How greatly advantageous, how greatly fruitful, how greatly resultful is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>! This <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is endowed with so many virtues! The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> must not be abandoned by me! The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> must be protected by me! The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> must be guarded by me! For this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is supremely rare!'—and would personally honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, flags, rows of lamps all around, and manifold offerings; or another, having worshipped it, would give, offer, transfer, and relinquish it to another son of good family or daughter of good family who desires it and requests it, even making it into a book—which of those two sons of good family or daughters of good family, O Blessed One, would produce more merit: the one with the mind of relinquishing, or the one without the mind of relinquishing?" When this was said, the Blessed One said to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "Well then, <s>Kauśika</s>, I shall question you about this very matter. As it seems right to you, answer. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? A son of good family or daughter of good family who would personally attend to, maintain, honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>—or another son of good family or daughter of good family who would personally honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s relics, and also illuminate them extensively to others, and give and share [them], thinking 'there will be widespread worship,' out of compassion for beings—which of those two sons of good family or daughters of good family would produce more merit? Whether one who personally worships and also extensively illuminates and gives and shares with others, or one who personally worships alone?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "O Blessed One, the son of good family or daughter of good family who would personally honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s relics, and also extensively illuminate and give and share with others, thinking 'there will be widespread worship,' out of compassion for beings—this very one of those two sons of good family or daughters of good family produces more merit." The Blessed One said: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. Thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, the son of good family or daughter of good family who, having copied this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and made it into a book, would take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct in it, expound it, study it, and give, offer, transfer, and relinquish it to another son of good family or daughter of good family who desires it and requests it, even making it into a book—this very one, <s>Kauśika</s>, of those two sons of good family or daughters of good family,

body.text: kuladuhitrorvā parānugrahakaraḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā parityāgabuddhistannidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: the son of good family or daughter of good family who benefits others, with the mind of relinquishing—by that cause produces more merit.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yatra yatra bhājanībhūtāḥ kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā syuḥ asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ, tatra tatra gatvā tebhyaḥ imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ dadyāt saṃvibhāgaṃ kuryāt, ayameva kauśika tataḥ kulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, wherever there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who are suitable vessels for this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, going to each of those places and giving them this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and sharing it—this very one, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce more merit than the other son of good family or daughter of good family.

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā ye jambūdvīpe sattvāstān sarvān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet, tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata / bhagavānāha - ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, yaḥ imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimucyate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt, antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpyakilāsitayā saṃpādayet - udyukto 'muṃ grāhayet saṃdarśayet samādāpayet samuttejayet saṃpraharṣayet, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti / ayaṃ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā parityāgabuddhyā tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika jambūdvīpe sarvasattvāḥ, etena kauśika paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayetpratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ, etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayetpratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ, etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ, etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayetpratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ, etena kauśika paryāyeṇa yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> in the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>kuśala-karmapatha</s>)—what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit thereby?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "Much, O Blessed One; much, O <s>Sugata</s>." The Blessed One said: "Still more merit would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce who, having made this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> into even a book, with faith believes, without conceptualizing refrains from conceptualizing, with conviction is convinced, with a clear mind to one of clear mind, endowed with pure intention to one endowed with pure intention, having generated the mind of awakening to a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the <s>bodhicitta</s>, with [pure] intention would give it, and even for copying or recitation would accomplish it with diligence—zealously would cause them to take it up, would show it, would encourage, would inspire, would delight, would guide by speech, would lead, would illuminate its meaning to them, and would thus purify their minds, would make them free from doubt, and would say to them: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> path! For training here, practicing and striving, you will quickly fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. And having fully awakened, you will lead an immeasurable realm of beings to the unsurpassed extinction of all <s>upadhi</s> (substrates), namely, in the manifestation of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>).' This son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, with the mind of relinquishing, produces more merit than the former son of good family or daughter of good family. But let all the beings in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> stand aside. By this very method, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings in the four-continent world-system in the ten wholesome courses of action—let all the beings in the four-continent world-system stand aside. By this very method, <s>Kauśika</s>, all the beings in the small thousandfold world-system—let all the beings in the small thousandfold world-system stand aside. By this very method, all the beings in the middling two-thousandfold world-system—let all the beings in the middling two-thousandfold world-system stand aside. By this very method, all the beings in the great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system—let all the beings in the great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system stand aside. By this very method, <s>Kauśika</s>, however many beings there are in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, ye 'pi te kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāttyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, ye 'pi te kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, ye 'pi te kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, anena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi kecitkauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan bahu sugata //
body.translated_text: will illuminate it for him, and will thus purify his mind, will remove his doubts, and will say to him thus: 'Come, O son of good family, train in just this <s>bodhisattva</s> path! For training here, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will quickly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimucyate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt, antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati, udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati, saṃdarśayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi, yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even more merit, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family generate—one who has faith in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, even if only written in a book, who has confidence, who does not conceptually construct, who is deeply convinced, who with a clear mind, with a clear—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā svayaṃ ca vācayet, parebhyaś ca likhitvā pūrvavaddadyāt, ayatnataḥ kauśika pūrvakātkulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmarthakuśalo vācayet, parebhyaś ca likhitvā pūrvavaddadyāt, sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet paridīpayet, ayatnataḥ kauśika sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family, having written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, would recite it themselves, and having written it, would give it to others as before—that one, <s>Kauśika</s>, would effortlessly generate more merit than the former son or daughter of good family. Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever—

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - iyam api bhagavan prajñāpāramitā upadeṣṭavyāḥ? evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - iyam api kauśika prajñāpāramitā upadeṣṭavyā abudhyamānasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā / tatkasya hetoḥ? utpatsyate hi kauśika anāgate 'dhvani prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā / tatra abudhyamānaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmo mā praṇaṃkṣīttāṃ prajñāpāramitā prativarṇikāṃ śrutvā //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: Should this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> also be taught, O <s>Bhagavān</s>? When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods: This <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too, <s>Kauśika</s>, should be taught to the son or daughter of good family who does not understand. For what reason?

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan anāgate 'dhvani prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā veditavyā - iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikopadiśyata iti? evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - bhaviṣyanti kauśika anāgate 'dhvani eke bhikṣavaḥ abhāvitakāyā abhāvitaśīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitaprajñā eḍamūkajātīyā prajñāparihīṇāḥ / te prajñāpāramitāmupadekṣyāma iti tasyāḥ prativarṇikāmupadekṣyanti / kathaṃ ca kauśika prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikāmupadekṣyanti? rūpavināśo rūpānityatetyupadekṣyanti / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / vijñānavināśo vijñānānityatetyupadekṣyanti / evaṃ copadekṣyanti - ya evaṃ gaveṣayiṣyati, sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ cariṣyatīti / iyaṃ sā kauśika prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā veditavyā / na khalu punaḥ kauśika rūpavināśo rūpānityatā draṣṭavyā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / na khalu punaḥ kauśika vijñānavināśo vijñānānityatā draṣṭavyā / sacedevaṃ paśyati, prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikāyāṃ carati / tasmāttarhi kauśika kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā prajñāpāramitāyā artha upadeṣṭavyaḥ / prajñāpāramitāyā arthamupadiśan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in the future be recognized—'This is being taught as a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'? When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, the Lord of the Gods: There will be, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the future—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ, tān sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata / bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimuñcate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya, adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt, antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati, udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati, saṃdarśayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if someone, whether a son or daughter of good family, were to establish all the beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>)—what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit from that cause? <s>Śakra</s> said: Much, O <s>Bhagavān</s>!

body.text: samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase, abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti / evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta - eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti / ayameva kauśika tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? ato hi kauśika srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvyate //
body.translated_text: he will encourage, uplift, and delight him; he will lead, guide, and further guide him by speech; he will illuminate the meaning for him, and will purify his mind thus and make it free from doubt, and will say to him: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> path!'

body.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jāmbūdvīpakān sarvasattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet //
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation of establishing all beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the fruit of stream-entry. As many beings as there are in the four-continent world-system, <s>Kauśika</s>—if some son or daughter of good family were to establish them all in the fruit of stream-entry—

body.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet //
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation of establishing all beings of the four-continent world-system in the fruit of stream-entry. As many beings as there are in the small chiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s>—if some son or daughter of good family were to establish them all in the fruit of stream-entry—

body.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet //
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation of establishing all beings of the small chiliocosm in the fruit of stream-entry. As many beings as there are in the medium dichiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s>—if some son or daughter of good family were to establish them all in the fruit of stream-entry—

body.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet //
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation of establishing all beings of the medium dichiliocosm in the fruit of stream-entry. As many beings as there are in the great trichiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s>—if some son or daughter of good family were to establish them all in the fruit of stream-entry—

body.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro va kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata //
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation of establishing all beings of the great trichiliocosm in the fruit of stream-entry. As many beings as there are in trichiliocosms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>—if some son or daughter of good family were to establish them all in the fruit of stream-entry—

body.text: bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimuñcate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya, adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt, antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati, udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati, saṃdarśayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Even so, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son or daughter of good family would produce far greater merit who, having made this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> even just into a book, has faith in it, applies it, is devoted to it, and with a clear mind—"

body.text: cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti / evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta - eteṣām api tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti / ayameva kauśika tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? ato hi kauśika srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvyate //
body.translated_text: and will say to him: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> path! For training here, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will swiftly attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). And having awakened, you will guide an unlimited realm of beings to the supreme destruction of the substrates [of suffering]—'

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yo hi kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ, tān sarvān sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata / bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimuñcate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya, adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāyādhyaśayena dadyāt, antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati, udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati, saṃdarśayiṣyati samadāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti / evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta - eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti / ayameva kauśika tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? ato hi kauśika sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvyate / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jāmbūdvīpakān sarvasattvān sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasatvān sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyabhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if some son or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the fruit of once-returning—what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family on that account produce much merit?" <s>Śakra</s> replied: "Much, O Blessed One—"

body.text: sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvān sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhātu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvān sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvān sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata //
body.translated_text: if some son or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings in the fruit of once-returning. Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation of establishing all beings of the small chiliocosm in the fruit of once-returning. As many beings as there are in the medium dichiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s>—

body.translated_text: you will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. And having awakened, you shall lead an immeasurable realm of beings into the unsurpassed exhaustion of the substrata of existence, namely into the realization of the ultimate limit of reality'—and should utter these words: 'O son of good family, obtain these very <s>dharmas</s>, namely those connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' This one generates much more merit than the former.

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even more merit, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family generate from that cause—one who has faith in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, even if only written in a book, who has confidence, who does not conceptually construct, who is deeply convinced, who with a clear mind [teaches it] to one with a clear mind, endowed with deep aspiration [teaches it] to one endowed with deep aspiration—

Much, O <s>Sugata</s>! The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even more merit would that

body.translated_text: beings in the three-thousand great-thousand world-systems—if someone, whether a son or daughter of good family, were to establish all of them in <s>arhatship</s>—what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit from that cause? <s>Śakra</s> said: Much, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! Much, O <s>Sugata</s>! The aggregate of merit, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, of that—

body.text: bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimuñcate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya, adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt, antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati, udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati, samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti / evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta - eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava, yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti / ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? ato hi kauśika arhattvaṃ prabhāvyate / evaṃ ca asyotsāhaṃ vardhayiṣyati - yathā yathā hi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyase, tathā tathā tvamanupūrveṇa buddhadharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyasi, āsannaś ca bhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, anāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, arhattvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, pratyekabuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, samyaksaṃbuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi / iti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even more merit, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family generate—one who has faith in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, even if only written in a book, who has confidence, who does not conceptually construct, who is deeply convinced, who with a clear mind [teaches it] to one with a clear mind, endowed with deep aspiration [teaches it] to one endowed with deep aspiration—

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugataḥ / bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimuñcate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya, adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt, antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati, udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati, saṃdarśayiṣyati
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if someone, whether a son or daughter of good family, were to establish all beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the state of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one)—what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit from that cause? <s>Śakra</s> said: Much, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! Much, O <s>Sugata</s>! The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even more would that—

body.text: samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti / evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta - eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti / ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? ato hi kauśika pratyekabuddhatvaṃ prabhāvyate / evaṃ cāsyotsāhaṃ vardhayiṣyati - yathā yathā hi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyase, tathā tathā tvamanupūrveṇa buddhadharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyasi, āsannaś ca bhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣiprameva srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, anāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, arhattvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, pratyekabuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyati, samyaksaṃbuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasīti / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jambūdvīpakān sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake loakadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, ye 'pi kecitkauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ, tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata //
body.translated_text: ...will encourage, inspire, and delight [him]; will lead, guide, and direct [him] by speech; will illuminate the meaning of this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] for him; will thus purify his mind and make it free from doubt; and will say to him thus: 'Come, O son of good family, train in this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> path! For training herein, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will quickly attain supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And having awakened, you will guide an immeasurable realm of beings to the supreme extinction of the bases [of suffering], namely to the realization of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>).' And he should speak these words: 'O son of good family, become a recipient of these very <s>dharmas</s> connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' This one would produce even more merit than that. What is the reason? For from this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>], <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s> is brought about. And thus he will increase his enthusiasm: 'In proportion as you, O son of good family, will train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, in that proportion you will gradually become a recipient of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and will draw near to supreme perfect awakening. For training in this training, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will quickly bring about the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, <s>Arhatship</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>, and perfect <s>Buddhahood</s>.' But set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation from establishing all beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the four-continent world-system—some son or daughter of good family might establish all of them too in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. But set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation from establishing all beings in the four-continent world-system in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the small thousand world-system—some son or daughter of good family might establish all of them too in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. But set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation from establishing all beings in the small thousand world-system in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the middle two-thousand world-system—some son or daughter of good family might establish all of them too in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. But set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation from establishing all beings in the middle two-thousand world-system in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the great three-thousand-fold world-system—some son or daughter of good family might establish all of them too in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. But set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation from establishing all beings in the great three-thousand-fold world-system in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in three-thousand-fold great world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>—some son or daughter of good family might establish all of them too in <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>—would that son or daughter of good family produce much merit on account of that?' <s>Śakra</s> replied: 'Much, Blessed One! Much, <s>Sugata</s>!'

body.text: bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate, avakalpayannavakalpayate, adhimuñcannadhimuñcate, prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya, adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāyādhyāśayena dadyāt,
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Even more merit than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family produce who, having made this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> into a book at least, having faith places faith in it, not discriminating does not discriminate, resolving resolves, with a serene mind, for one with a serene mind, endowed with superior intention, for one endowed with superior intention, having generated the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), would give it with superior intention to a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the <s>bodhicitta</s>,

body.text: antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati, adyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati, saṃdarśayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati, vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati, arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati, nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati, evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva - atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti / evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta - eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti / ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? ato hi kauśika pratyekabuddhatvaṃ prabhāvyate / evaṃ cāsya utsāhaṃ vardhayiṣyasi - yathā yathā hi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyase, tathā tathā tvamanupūrveṇa buddhadharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyasi, āsannaś ca bhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / atra hi tvaṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, anāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, arhattvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi, samyaksaṃbuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasīti //
body.translated_text: and would accomplish even at least the writing or reciting [of it] with unflagging effort; and being intent, would cause that one to learn it; would show, encourage, inspire, and delight [him]; would lead, guide, and direct [him] by speech; would illuminate the meaning of this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] for him; and would thus purify his mind and make it free from doubt. And would say to him thus: "Come, O son of good family, train in this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> path! For training herein, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will quickly attain supreme perfect awakening. And having awakened, you will guide an immeasurable realm of beings to the supreme extinction of the bases [of suffering], namely to the realization of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>)." And he should speak these words: "O son of good family, become a recipient of these very <s>dharmas</s> connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>." This one would produce even more merit than that. What is the reason? For from this, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s> is brought about. And thus he will increase his enthusiasm: "In proportion as you, O son of good family, will train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, in that proportion you will gradually become a recipient of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and will draw near to supreme perfect awakening. For training in this training, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will quickly bring about the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, <s>Arhatship</s>, and perfect <s>Buddhahood</s>."'

body.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ samutpādayet, yaścānyaḥ kaścitkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā teṣāṃ sarveṣāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya tebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā dadyāt / yo vā kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā avinivartanīyāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya enāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā upanāmayet, atraiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyate, yogamāpatsyate / atraiva prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayan vṛddhiṃ virūḍhiṃ vipulatāṃ gataḥ paripūrayiṣyati buddhadharmāniti / ayaṃ tasmātpaurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? niyatameṣo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sattvānāṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyatīti / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jāmbūdvīpakānāṃ sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ, teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ, teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ, teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, teṣām api sarveṣāṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, however many beings there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>—some son or daughter of good family might generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening in all of them. And some other son or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, having generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening in all of them for supreme perfect awakening, might give them this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having written it. Or, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son or daughter of good family might offer this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having written it, to an irreversible (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, [who] will train in this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and apply himself in yoga. Cultivating this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having reached growth, development, and expansiveness, he will fulfill the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. This one would produce even more merit than that former son or daughter of good family. What is the reason? For this one will certainly, having attained supreme perfect awakening, make an end of suffering for beings. But set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation from generating the mind of supreme perfect awakening in all beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the four-continent world-system—some son or daughter of good family might generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening in all of them. But set aside that. However many beings there are in the small thousand world-system—some son or daughter of good family might generate the mind in all of them. But set aside that. However many beings there are in the middle two-thousand world-system—some son or daughter of good family might generate the mind in all of them. But set aside that. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the great three-thousand-fold world-system—in all of them too,

body.text: kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet / tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ, teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet / yaścānyaḥ kaścitkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā teṣāṃ sarveṣāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya tebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā dadyāt / yo vā kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā avinivartanīyāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya enāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā dadyāt, upanāmayet, atraiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyate, yogamāpatsyate / evamasyeyaṃ prajñāpāramitā bhūyasyā mātrayā bhāvanāṃ vṛddhiṃ virūḍhiṃ vipulatāṃ paripūriṃ gamiṣyatīti / ayaṃ kauśiaka tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? niyatameṣo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sattvānāṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: some son or daughter of good family might generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening. But set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meritorious formation from generating the mind of supreme perfect awakening in all beings of the great three-thousand-fold world-system. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in three-thousand-fold great world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>—in all of them too, some son or daughter of good family might generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening. And some other son or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, having generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening in all of them for supreme perfect awakening, might give them this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having written it. Or, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son or daughter of good family might give and offer this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having written it, to an irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>; and [that one] will train in this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and apply himself in yoga. Thus this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for him will reach greater cultivation, growth, development, expansiveness, and fulfillment. This one, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce even more merit than that former son or daughter of good family. What is the reason? For this one will certainly, having attained supreme perfect awakening, make an end of suffering for beings.'
