sacetkhalu punarevam api bhāṣyamāṇe evaṃ nirdiśyamāne bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya cittaṃ na kṣubhyati na calati, ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ / sacedbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya cittaṃ parataḥ śrutvaivaṃ vivekapadāni dharmatāyā na parihīyate, na pratyudāvartate 'sya mānasam, na cānyathābhāvaścittasya bhavati, tāni ca sarvāṇi mārakarmāṇi tathā saṃjānāti - asthānaṃ subhūte anavakāśaḥ, yatsa bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathā caran pāramitāsu na sarvajñatāmanuprāpnuyāt -
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 165)

body.text: asthānametadanavakāśo yattathā caratastathā śikṣamāṇasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya yathā tathāgatairākhyātaṃ tayā caryayā avirahitasya ebhiḥ pāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairviharato māraḥ pāpīyānnāvatāraṃ lapsyate / sacedbodhisattvo mahāsattvo mārakarmāṇi budhyate, parataś ca śrutvā vivekapadāni na parihīyate, na pratyudāvartate 'sya mānasam, na cāsya cittamanyathā bhavati, tāni ca mārakarmāṇi tathā saṃjānāti / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, an irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not pursue the ten paths of unwholesome action. He guards the ten paths of wholesome action. For what reason? Because he has well undertaken the precepts of training—

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na rūpasaṃjñāmabhisaṃskāroti, na rūpasaṃjñāmutpādayati / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāṃ na saṃjñāsaṃjñāṃ na saṃskārasaṃjñām / na vijñānasaṃjñāmabhisaṃskaroti, na vijñānasaṃjñāmutpādayati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi avinivartanīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svalakṣaṇaśūnyairdharmairbodhisattvanyāmāvakrāntaḥ / tam api dharmaṃ nopalabhate nābhisaṃskāroti notpādayati / tata ucyate anutpādajñānakṣāntiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīya iti / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, an irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>'s bed, seat, robes, and alms-bowl are clean, pure, and not defiled—

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān bhikṣuveṣeṇopasaṃkramya bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamevaṃ vicchandayiṣyati - ākāśasamaiṣā yaduta sarvajñatā / asanneṣa dharmo yaduta sarvajñatā / asaṃvidyamāna eṣa dharmo yaduta sarvajñatā / ko 'trājñāsyati, ko 'trābhisaṃbhotsyate? naitena kaścinniryāsyati - yaścābhisaṃbudhyeta, yaccābhisaṃboddhavyam, yaś ca ājānīyāt, yacca ājñātavyam / sarvatra te dharmā ākāśasamāḥ / nirarthakaṃ tvaṃ vihanyase / mārakarmairvaitatparidīpitaṃ yaduta anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃboddhavyeti, naitadbuddhabhāṣitamiti / tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā evaṃ jñātavyamevaṃ samanvāhartavyamevaṃ veditavyam - mārakarmaivaitat, yeyaṃ vivecanatā / evaṃ cintayitvā tatra dṛḍhacittena bhavitavyam, aprakampyacittenāsaṃhāryacittena bhavitavyam / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, an irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> is not harassed by <s>Māra</s> or <s>Māra</s>'s retinue. He is not attacked by the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>)—

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūminirvṛttaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ pravṛtto bhavati / sa ākāṅkṣan prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate / tathā dvitīyaṃ tathā tṛtīyaṃ tathā caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate / sa ebhiścaturbhirdhyānairviharati, dhyānaparijayaṃ ca karoti, dhyānāni ca samāpadyate, na ca dhyānavaśenopapadyate / sa punareva kāmāvacarān dharmānadhyālambate / idam api subhūte avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya avinivartanīyalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, an irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> has gone beyond the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stages and is established in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). If he wishes, he enters the first <s>dhyāna</s>; likewise the second, likewise the third—

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na nāmaguruko bhavati, na kīrtiśabdaślokaguruko bhavati, na nāmni sajjate / so 'saṃkṣubhitacitto bhavati, sarvasattveṣu
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, an irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not attach importance to name, does not attach importance to fame, reputation, and renown, and does not cling to name. His mind is unperturbed, [with compassion] toward all beings—

body.text: hitacittaś ca bhavati / so 'bhikrāman vā pratikrāman vā abhrāntacitto 'bhikrāmati, abhrāntacittaḥ pratikrāmati / smṛtimānevābhikrāmati, smṛtimāneva pratikrāmati / sacetso 'gāramadhyāvasati, nāsya bhavatyadhimātraḥ kāmeṣu kāmābhiṣvaṅgo vā abhiprāyo vā / sa nirvitsaṃjñyeva kāmān paribhuṅkte / sa utrastasaṃjñyeva kāmān paribhuṅkte / tadyathāpi subhūte caurakāntāramadhyagataḥ puruṣaḥ āhārakṛtyaṃ kurvannutrastasaṃjñyevāhāraṃ kuryāt, gamanasaṃjñyevāhāraṃ kuryāt, kadā nu khalu nāma ahamitaścaurakāntārādatikrānto bhaviṣyāmītyevaṃsaṃjñī aviśrabdhamāhāramāharati / evameva subhūte avinivartanīyā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā agāramadhyāvasanto yān yāneva kāmān paribhuñjate, tāṃstānanarthikā eva agṛddhā eva asaktā eva kāmān paribhuñjate / anarthikā eva ca te bhavanti priyarūpasātarūpaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ / te 'gāramadhyāvasanto na samaviṣameṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayanti / dharmeṇaiva jīvikāṃ kalpayanti nādharmeṇāpi / maraṇamupagacchanti na tveva pareṣāmapamardanaṃ kurvanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi taiḥ satpuruṣairmahāpuruṣairatipuruṣaiḥ puruṣapravaraiḥ puruṣaśobhanaiḥ puruṣarṣabhaiḥ puruṣodāraiḥ puruṣaśauṭīraiḥ puruṣapuṃgavaiḥ puruṣadhuryaiḥ puruṣapadmaiḥ puruṣapuṇḍarīkaiḥ puruṣājāneyaiḥ puruṣanāgaiḥ puruṣasiṃhaiḥ puruṣadamyasārathibhiḥ sarvasattvāḥ paramasukhe niyojayitavyāḥ / evaṃ hi subhūte agāramadhyāvasanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvā yathāpi nāma prajñāpāramitābalādhānaprāptatvāt / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā avinivartanīyā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: he has a mind of benevolence. Whether going forward or going back, he goes forward with an unconfused mind, he goes back with an unconfused mind. He goes forward with mindfulness, he goes back with mindfulness. And if he dwells as a householder, there does not arise in him excessive desire for or attachment to sensual pleasures. He enjoys sensual pleasures with a perception of disgust. He enjoys sensual pleasures with a perception of terror. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a man who has entered into the midst of a wilderness infested with thieves, when taking his meal, would take his food with a perception of terror, would take his food with the perception of departing — 'When indeed shall I have passed beyond this wilderness of thieves?' — with such a perception he eats his food without ease. In exactly the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, irreversible <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>, while dwelling as householders, whatever sensual pleasures they enjoy, they enjoy those pleasures without desire for them, without greed, without attachment. They are without desire for the five strands of sensual pleasure that are lovely and agreeable. While dwelling as householders, they do not sustain their livelihood by unequal means. They sustain their livelihood by <s>Dharma</s> alone, not by <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness). They would accept death rather than cause harm to others. For what reason? For indeed those true men, great men, supreme men, foremost of men, splendid men, bulls among men, noble men, heroic men, chief among men, yoke-leaders of men, lotuses among men, white lotuses among men, thoroughbreds among men, elephants among men, lions among men, tamers and charioteers of men — they must establish all beings in the highest happiness. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, do <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> dwell as householders, inasmuch as they have attained the empowerment of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). By these signs, these marks, these indications too, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed with them should be recognized as irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya vajrapāṇirmahāyakṣo nityānubaddho bhavati / sa durdharṣo bhavati, anatikramaṇīyaś ca bhavati manuṣyairvā amanuṣyairvā, durāsadaḥ sarvasattvānām / sa na vikṣiptacitto bhavati, na vikalendriyo bhavati, paripūrṇaindriyaś ca bhavati nāparipūrṇendriyaḥ / puruṣavṛṣabhendriyasamanvāgataś ca bhavati nāsatpuruṣaḥ / sa yānīmāni strīṇāṃ vaśīkaraṇāni mantrajāpyauṣadhividyābhaiṣajyādīni, tāni sarvāṇi sarveṇa sarvaṃ na prayojayati / śuddhājīvaś ca bhavati na mithyājīvaḥ / na vigrahavivādaśīlaḥ / ṛjudṛṣṭikaś ca bhavati / nātmotkarṣī na parapaṃsakaḥ / sa ebhiścānyaiś ca guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / sa na striyaṃ na ca puruṣaṃ vyākaroti - putro vā te bhaviṣyati, duhitā vā te bhaviṣyatīti / tasyaivamādikā evaṃrūpā ādeyatādoṣā na bhavanti / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>yakṣa</s> (nature spirit), is the constant companion of an irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. He becomes invincible, and cannot be overpowered by humans or non-humans, and is unapproachable by all beings. He is not distracted in mind, nor deficient in his faculties, but is complete in his faculties, not incomplete. He is endowed with the faculties of a bull among men, and is not an untrue person. As for the various means of bewitching women — spells, incantations, herbs, magical knowledge, medicines, and the like — he does not employ any of them whatsoever. He is pure in livelihood, not of wrong livelihood. He is not given to quarrels and disputes. He is of right views. He does not exalt himself nor disparage others. He is endowed with these and other virtues. He does not make predictions for women or men — 'You will have a son,' or 'You will have a daughter.' Such faults of credulity do not arise in him. By these signs, these marks, these indications too, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed with them should be recognized as irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ye ākārā yāni liṅgāni yāni nimittāni yairākārairyairliṅgairyairnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo veditavyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, tānākārāṃstāni liṅgāni tāni nimittāni deśayiṣyāmi / te punaḥ katame? tadyathā - na te skandhāyatanadhātupratītyasamutpādayogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na saṃgaṇikārāmakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na rājakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na caurakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na senākathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, I shall teach the signs, the marks, the indications of an irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> — those signs, those marks, those indications by which a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed with them should be known as irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. And what are they? Namely — they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination); they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about socializing and amusement; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about kings; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about thieves; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about armies

body.text: viharanti, na yuddhakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīkathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, nātmakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, nāmātyamahāmātrakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na strīpuruṣanapuṃsakakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na yānodyānavihāraprāsādahradasarastaḍāgapuṣkariṇīvanārāmaśailakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na yakṣarākṣasapretapiśācakaṭapūtanakumbhāṇḍakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, nānnapānavastrābharaṇagandhamālyavilepanakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na vīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakaviśikhāpaṇaśibikākuṭumbakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na gītanṛtyākhyāyikānaṭanartakacāraṇakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na sāgaranadīdvīpakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na dharmaviruddhakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, na pṛthagjanaratikathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti, api tu prajñāpāramitākathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti / avirahitāś ca bhavanti sarvajñatāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ / na ca te kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti / dharmakāmā eva ca te bhavanti, nādharmakāmāḥ / abhedavarṇavādinaś ca te bhavanti, na bhedavarṇavādinaḥ / mitrakāmāś ca te bhavanti, nāmitrakāmāḥ / dharmavādinaś ca te bhavanti, nādharmavādinaḥ / te tathāgatadarśanamevākāṅkṣanta ākāṅkṣanti anyeṣu lokadhātuṣu ye tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti, teṣāmantike upapattaye cittamutpādayanti / te ākāṅkṣantastatropapadyante / evaṃ te avirahitā bhavanti tathāgatadarśanena tathāgataparyupāsanena tathāgataparyupasthānena ca //
body.translated_text: they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about warfare; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and capital cities; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about the self; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about ministers and great officials; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about women, men, and eunuchs; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about carriages, gardens, monasteries, palaces, lakes, pools, ponds, lotus ponds, forests, parks, and mountains; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> (stinking spirits), and <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd spirits); they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about food, drink, clothing, ornaments, fragrances, garlands, and ointments; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about streets, squares, crossroads, lanes, shops, palanquins, and families; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about songs, dances, tales, actors, dancers, and performers; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about oceans, rivers, and islands; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk contrary to <s>Dharma</s>; they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about the pleasures of ordinary beings; but rather they dwell engaged in the practice of talk about the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And they are never separated from mental activities connected with omniscience. And they do not dwell engaged in the practice of talk about quarrels, disputes, conflicts, and altercations. They are lovers of <s>Dharma</s>, not lovers of <s>adharma</s>. They are speakers of harmony, not speakers of discord. They are lovers of friendship, not lovers of enmity. They are speakers of <s>Dharma</s>, not speakers of <s>adharma</s>. When they wish for the sight of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, they generate the aspiration for rebirth in the presence of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones who abide, continue, and sustain in other world-systems. And wishing thus, they are reborn there. Thus they are never separated from the sight of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, from attending upon <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and from serving <s>Tathāgatas</s>. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kāmāvacarebhyo devebhyaścyutā rūpāvacarebhya ārūpyāvacarebhyo vā devebhyaścyutāḥ santaḥ ihaiva madhyadeśe jambūdvīpe pratyājāyante / yatra sattvāḥ kalāsu kovidāḥ, kāvyeṣu kovidāḥ, mantreṣu kovidāḥ, vidyāsu kovidāḥ, śāstreṣu kovidāḥ, nimitteṣu kovidāḥ, dharmārthakovidāḥ / alpakāḥ pratyantajanapadeṣu pratyājāyante, yadbhūyastvena madhyadeśe pratyājāyante / ye 'pi pratyanteṣu janapadeṣu pratyājāyante, te 'pi mahānagareṣu pratyājāyante / ete 'pi teṣāṃ guṇāḥ saṃvidyante / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, irreversible <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>, having fallen from the <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm) gods, or having fallen from the <s>Rūpāvacara</s> (form realm) or <s>Ārūpyāvacara</s> (formless realm) gods, are reborn right here in the central region of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — where beings are skilled in the arts, skilled in poetry, skilled in sacred formulas, skilled in sciences, skilled in treatises, skilled in reading signs, and skilled in the meaning of <s>Dharma</s>. Rarely are they reborn in outlying regions; for the most part they are reborn in the central region. And even those who are reborn in outlying regions are reborn in great cities. These virtues too are found in them. By these signs, these marks, these indications too, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed with them should be recognized as irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya naivaṃ bhavati - avinivartanīyo vāham, na vāhamavinivartanīya iti / nāsyaivaṃ vicikitsotpadyate, na cāsya saṃśayo bhavati, svasyāṃ bhūmau nāpyasya saṃsīdanā bhavati / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte srotaāpannaḥ srotaāpattiphale svakāyāṃ bhūmau na kāṅkṣati na vicikitsati / na cāsya saṃśayo bhavati / svasyāṃ bhūmau nāpyasya saṃsīdanā bhavati / utpannotpannāni ca mārakarmāṇi kṣipramevābudhyate / na cotpannotpannānāṃ mārakarmaṇāṃ vaśena gacchati / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte puruṣa ānantaryakārī ānantaryacittena avirahito bhavati, yāvanmaraṇāvasthāyām, na taccittaṃ śaknoti prativinodayituṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, in an irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> there does not arise the thought — 'I am irreversible,' or 'I am not irreversible.' No such doubt arises in him, nor does he have any uncertainty, nor does he waver in his own stage. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) does not doubt or waver regarding the fruit of stream-entry, regarding his own stage. Nor does he have any uncertainty, nor does he waver in his own stage. And he quickly recognizes each and every <s>mārakarmāṇi</s> (deed of <s>Māra</s>) as they arise. And he does not fall under the power of those deeds of <s>Māra</s> as they arise. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a man who has committed an <s>ānantarya</s> (deed of immediate retribution) is never separated from the consciousness of that deed of immediate retribution until the moment of death, and cannot dispel that consciousness

body.text: vā viṣkambhayituṃ vā / anuvartata evāsya taccittaṃ yāvanmaraṇakālasamaye 'pi / evameva subhūte avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya avinivartanīyacittaṃ sthitaṃ bhavati, svakāyāmavinivartanīyāyāṃ bhūmāvavikampyaṃ bhavati / sadevamānuṣāsureṇāpi lokena na śakyaṃ cālayituṃ vā kampayituṃ vā / utpannotpannāni ca mārakarmāṇyeva budhyate / na cotpannotpannānāṃ mārakarmaṇāṃ vaśena gacchati / tasya svasyāṃ bhūmau niṣkāṅkṣasya nirvicikitsasya jātivyativṛttasyāpi na śrāvakacittaṃ na pratyekabuddhacittaṃ votpadyate / jātivyativṛttasyāpyevaṃ bhavatināhaṃ nābhisaṃbhotsye / abhisaṃbhotsye evāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ svasyāṃ bhūmau sthitaḥ / aparapraṇeyo bhavati, anavamardanīyaś ca bhavati svasyāṃ bhūmau / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi sa sthito 'saṃhāryeṇa cittena asaṃhāryeṇa jñānena samanvāgato bhavati / sacetkhalu punarmāraḥ pāpīyān buddhaveṣeṇopasaṃkrāmet, tamupasaṃkramyaivaṃ vadet - ihaiva tvamarhattvaṃ sākṣātkuru / na tvaṃ vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / na tava te ākārāstāni liṅgāni tāni nimittāni vā saṃvidyante, yairākārairyairliṅgairyairnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / kiṃ vātra tvaṃ carasīti? sacetpunarbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anyathā cittaṃ bhavati, veditavyametatsubhūte nāyaṃ bodhisattvo vyākṛtaḥ paurvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti / sacetpunarevaṃ samanvāharati - māro batāyaṃ pāpīyān buddhaveṣamabhinirmāyopasaṃkrāntaḥ, mārādhiṣṭhito vā māranirmito veti, nāyaṃ tathāgataḥ / yathoktaṃ tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena tathā tannānyathā / sacedevaṃ pratyavekṣate, evaṃ samanvāharati - māro batāyaṃ pāpīyān buddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtvā māṃ vivecayitukāmo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhita iti / sacenmāraḥ pratyudāvartate, veditavyametatsubhūte vyākṛto 'yaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paurvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ / sthito 'yaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau / sacetsubhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ime ākārā imāni liṅgāni imāni nimittāni saṃvidyante, veditavyametatsubhūte yathā asyeme guṇāḥ / addhā batāyaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vyākṛtaḥ paurvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ / sthito 'yaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hyasya te ākārāstāni liṅgāni tāni nimittāni saṃvidyante, yāni avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: or suppress it. That consciousness follows him even until the moment of death. In exactly the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the irreversible consciousness of an irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> remains fixed; in his own irreversible stage it is unshakeable. Even by the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> (titans), it cannot be moved or shaken. And he recognizes each and every deed of <s>Māra</s> as they arise. And he does not fall under the power of those deeds of <s>Māra</s> as they arise. In him who is without doubt, without uncertainty in his own stage, even when he has passed beyond birth, there does not arise the thought of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple) or the thought of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one). Even when he has passed beyond birth, he thinks thus — 'It is not the case that I shall not awaken. I shall certainly awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, established in my own stage.' He becomes one who cannot be led astray by others, and one who cannot be crushed in his own stage. For what reason? For indeed he stands endowed with an irreducible consciousness and irreducible knowledge. And if <s>Māra</s> the Evil One were to approach in the guise of a <s>Buddha</s>, and having approached were to say — 'Realize <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) right here and now! You have not been predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Those signs, those marks, those indications are not found in you, by which signs, marks, and indications a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Why do you practice here?' — and if thereupon the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s mind becomes otherwise, it should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, that this <s>bodhisattva</s> has not been predicted by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, for unsurpassed perfect awakening. But if he reflects thus — 'This is indeed <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, who has fashioned the guise of a <s>Buddha</s> and approached, or one who is controlled by <s>Māra</s> or created by <s>Māra</s>; this is not a <s>Tathāgata</s>. What was spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, is thus and not otherwise' — if he examines thus, if he reflects thus — 'This is indeed <s>Māra</s> the Evil One who, having assumed the authority of a <s>Buddha</s>, wishes to divert me from unsurpassed perfect awakening' — and if thereupon <s>Māra</s> turns back, it should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, that this <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> has been predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones. This <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is established in the irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> stage. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, these signs, these marks, these indications are found in a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, it should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, that these are his virtues. Surely this <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> has been predicted by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones. This <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is established in the irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> stage. For what reason? For indeed those signs, those marks, those indications are found in him that belong to an irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. By these signs, these marks, these indications too, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> endowed with them should be recognized as irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saddharmaparigrahasya kṛtaśaḥ ātmaparityāgam api karoti, jīvitaparityāgam api karoti / tasmādbodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyaḥ saddharmaparigrahāya paramudyogamāpadyate atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ premṇā ca gauraveṇa ca / dharmakāyā buddhā bhagavanta iti dharme prema ca gauravaṃ copādāya
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, an irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, for the sake of preserving the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>), even undertakes the sacrifice of his own self, even undertakes the sacrifice of his own life. Therefore, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> who is irreversible exerts the utmost effort for the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s>, out of love and reverence for the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavats</s> (Blessed Ones) of the past, future, and present. Since the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavats</s> have the <s>Dharma</s> as their body (<s>dharmakāya</s>), it is out of love and reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> that

body.text: saddharmaparigrahaṃ karoti / nāyaṃ kevalamatītānāmeva buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saddharmaparigrahaḥ, pratyutpannānām api buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmeṣa eva saddharmaparigrahaḥ, anāgatānām api buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmeṣa eva saddharmaparigrahaḥ - aham api tatra teṣāmanāgatānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saṃkhyāṃ gaṇanāṃ praviṣṭa iti, aham api tatra vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, mamāpyeṣa eva saddharmaparigraha iti / sa imamapyarthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyan saddharmaparigrahasya kṛtaśa ātmaparityāgam api karoti, jīvitaparityāgam api karoti / na ca tatra saṃsīdati, na ca kausīdyamāpadyate / ebhir api subhūte ākārairebhirliṅgairebhirnimittaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: he upholds the true <s>Dharma</s>. And this is not only the upholding of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones of the past; it is also the upholding of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones of the present; and it is also the upholding of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones of the future—'I too am included in the number of those future <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones; I too have been predicted for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening); for me too this is the upholding of the true <s>Dharma</s>.' Seeing this purpose too, he makes even the sacrifice of self for the sake of upholding the true <s>Dharma</s>; he makes even the sacrifice of life. And in that he does not sink down, nor does he fall into indolence. By these aspects, marks, and signs too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> be recognized as irreversible from <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte avinivartanīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya dharmaṃ deśayato na kāṅkṣati, na vicikitsati / subhūtirāha - kiṃ tathāgatasyaiva bhagavan dharmaṃ deśayato na kāṅkṣati na vicikitsati, na śrāvakasya? bhagavānāha - śrāvakasyāpi subhūte dharmaṃ deśayato na kāṅkṣati na vicikitsati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiḥ pratilabdhā / tena sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmatāmaviruddhāṃ śṛṇoti / śṛṇvaṃś ca na kāṅkṣati, na vicikitsati / ebhiḥ subhūte guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vinivartanīyo bhavati / imāny api subhūte avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ākāraliṅganimittāni veditavyānyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheriti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not doubt or waver when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Does he not doubt or waver only when the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, Blessed One, or also when a <s>Śrāvaka</s> teaches?' The Blessed One said: 'He does not doubt or waver when a <s>Śrāvaka</s> too teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>. What is the reason? For that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> has obtained <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore he hears the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>dharmas</s> without contradiction. And hearing it, he does not doubt or waver. By these qualities, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> is irreversible. These too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as the aspects, marks, and signs of the irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> from <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.'

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmavinivartanīyākāraliṅganimittaparivarto nāma saptadaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the seventeenth chapter, called 'The Chapter on the Aspects, Marks, and Signs of the Irreversible,' in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: ASP_18: śūnyatāparivarto 'ṣṭādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Eighteen of the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>: The Eighteenth Chapter on Emptiness.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan mahāguṇasamanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / apramāṇaguṇasamanvāgato bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / aparimitaguṇasamanvāgato bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / tatkasya hetoḥ? avinivartanīyena hi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anantamaparyantaṃ jñānaṃ pratilabdhamasaṃhāryaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'It is wonderful, Blessed One, how the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> is endowed with great qualities! Endowed with immeasurable qualities, Blessed One, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>! Endowed with unlimited qualities, Blessed One, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>!' When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. What is the reason? For the irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, has obtained infinite, boundless knowledge that cannot be shaken by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>.'

body.text: subhūtirāha - pratibalo bhagavan avinivartanīyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpānākārān liṅgāni nimittāni nirdeṣṭum / ata eva bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya gambhīrāṇi gambhīrāṇi sthānāni prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni sūcayitavyāni / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sādhu sādhu subhūte yastvaṃ gambhīrāṇi gambhīrāṇi sthānānyārabhya nigamayitukāmaḥ / gambhīramiti subhūte śūnyatāyā etadadhivacanam / ānimittasya apraṇihitasya anabhisaṃskārasya anutpādasya ajāterabhāvasya virāgasya nirodhasya nirvāṇasya vigamasyaitatsubhūte adhivacanaṃ yaduta gambhīramiti //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'One would be able, Blessed One, to set forth the aspects, marks, and signs of the irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. For this very reason, Blessed One, the profound, deeply profound stations connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> are to be indicated.' When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>! You who wish to bring to a conclusion the profound, deeply profound stations. "Profound," <s>Subhūti</s>, is a designation for <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). It is a designation for the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>), the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>), the unconditioned (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>), the non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>), the unborn (<s>ajāti</s>), non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, and departure (<s>vigama</s>)—this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is what "profound" designates.'

body.text: subhūtirāha - eteṣāmeva bhagavan kevalametaddharmāṇāmadhivacanaṃ na punaḥ sarvadharmāṇām? bhagavānāha - sarvadharmāṇāmapyetatsubhūte adhivacanaṃ yaduta gambhīramiti / tatkasya hetoḥ? rūpaṃ hi subhūte gambhīram / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ hi subhūte gambhīram / kathaṃ ca subhūte rūpaṃ gambhīram? kathaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ? kathaṃ ca subhūte vijñānaṃ gambhīram? yathā subhūte tathatā, tathā gambhīraṃ rūpam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / yathā subhūte tathatā, tathā gambhīraṃ vijñānam / tatra subhūte yathā rūpatathatā, tathā gambhīraṃ rūpam / yathā vedanātathatā saṃjñātathatā saṃskāratathatā / tatra subhūte yathā vijñānatathatā, tathā gambhīraṃ vijñānam / yatra subhūte na rūpam, iyaṃ rūpasya gambhīratā / yatra subhūte na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārā na vijñānam, iyaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāṇām, iyaṃ vijñānasya gambhīratā //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Is this a designation for just these <s>dharmas</s> alone, Blessed One, and not for all <s>dharmas</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'It is a designation for all <s>dharmas</s> too, <s>Subhūti</s>, namely "profound." What is the reason? For form, <s>Subhūti</s>, is profound. Likewise feeling, perception, and formations. For consciousness, <s>Subhūti</s>, is profound. And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, is form profound? How are feeling, perception, and formations? And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, is consciousness profound? Just as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>Subhūti</s>, so is form profound. Likewise feeling, perception, and formations. Just as <s>tathatā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, so is consciousness profound. Now, <s>Subhūti</s>, just as the <s>tathatā</s> of form, so is form profound. Just as the <s>tathatā</s> of feeling, the <s>tathatā</s> of perception, the <s>tathatā</s> of formations. Now, <s>Subhūti</s>, just as the <s>tathatā</s> of consciousness, so is consciousness profound. Where, <s>Subhūti</s>, there is no form—this is the profundity of form. Where, <s>Subhūti</s>, there is no feeling, no perception, no formations, no consciousness—this is the profundity of feeling, perception, and formations; this is the profundity of consciousness.'

body.text: subhūtirāha - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvatsūkṣmeṇopāyena rūpataś ca nivārito nirvāṇaṃ ca sucitam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / yāvatsūkṣmeṇopāyena vijñānataś ca nivārito nirvāṇaṃ ca sūcitam / bhagavānāha - imāni subhūte gambhīrāṇi gambhīrāṇi sthānāni prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni yaścintayiṣyanti tulayiṣyati upanidhyāsyati - evaṃ mayā sthātavyaṃ yathā prajñāpāramitāyāmājñaptam / evaṃ mayā śikṣitavyaṃ yathā prajñāpāramitāyāmākhyātam / evaṃ mayā pratipattavyaṃ yathā prajñāpāramitāyāmupadiṣṭam / tathā saṃpādayamānastathopanidhyāyaṃstathopaparīkṣamāṇastathā prayujyamānastathā ghaṭamānastathā vyāyacchamāna ekadivasamapyatra yogamāpadyate / ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvastenaikadivasena kiyatkarma karoti? tadyathāpi nāma subhūte kaścideva puruṣo rāgacarito vitarkacaritaḥ / tasya puruṣasya rāgacaritasya vitarkacaritasya striyā abhirūpayā prāsādikayā darśanīyayā saha saṃketaḥ kṛto bhavet / sā khalu punaḥ strī
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'It is wonderful, Blessed One, how by such a subtle means one is turned away from form and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is indicated! Likewise feeling, perception, and formations. By such a subtle means one is turned away from consciousness and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is indicated!' The Blessed One said: 'These profound, deeply profound stations connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>—whoever will reflect upon, weigh, and contemplate them, thinking: "Thus should I stand as has been enjoined in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus should I train as has been declared in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus should I practice as has been taught in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>." Thus accomplishing, thus contemplating, thus investigating, thus striving, thus exerting, thus making effort—if he applies himself to this practice even for a single day, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, by that single day, how much <s>karma</s> does he accomplish? Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, suppose there were a man given to passion, given to discursive thought. And that man, given to passion, given to discursive thought, had made an assignation with a beautiful, pleasing, attractive woman. But that woman

body.text: paraparigṛhītā bhavet / na vaśayedātmānamagārānniṣkramitum / tatkiṃ manyase subhūte kiṃpratisaṃyuktāstasya puruṣasya vitarkāḥ pravarteran? subhūtirāha - strīpratisaṃyuktā eva bhagavaṃstasya puruṣasya vitarkāḥ pravarteran - iyamāgacchati, iyamāgatā / tayā sārdhamevaṃ kariṣyāmi, evaṃ ramiṣyāmi, evaṃ krīḍiṣyāmi, evaṃ pravicārayiṣyāmīti / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte divasasyātyayena tasya puruṣasya kiyanto vitarkā utpadyeran? subhūtirāha - bahavo bhagavan divasasyātyayena tasya puruṣasya vitarkā utpadyeran / bhagavānāha - yāvantaḥ subhūte tasya puruṣasya divasasyātyayena vitarkā utpadyeran, iyataḥ subhūte kalpān bodhisattvo mahāsattvaśchorayati vipṛṣṭhīkaroti saṃsārādvyantīkaroti, ya iha prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yathājñaptaṃ yathākhyātaṃ yathopadiṣṭaṃ yathoddiṣṭaṃ yathānirdiṣṭaṃ tiṣṭhati śikṣate pratipadyate upanidhyāyati yogamāpadyate, tāṃś ca doṣān vivarjayati, yairdoṣairbodhisattvo mahāsattvo vivartate 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / evaṃ hi subhūte yaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyogamanuyuktaḥ, anena vihāreṇa viharan yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ, ekadivasena tāvatkarma karoti / yaś ca prajñāpāramitāvirahito bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan dānaṃ dadyāt, ayameva tato viśiṣyate yo 'yaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva evamekadivasam api prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyate //
body.translated_text: belonged to another man, and she could not get herself to leave the house. What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—what kind of thoughts would arise in that man?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Thoughts connected with the woman would arise in that man, Blessed One: "She is coming, she has come! With her I shall do thus, with her I shall take pleasure thus, with her I shall play thus, with her I shall engage thus."' The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—at the end of the day, how many thoughts would arise in that man?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Many thoughts, Blessed One, would arise in that man at the end of the day.' The Blessed One said: 'However many thoughts, <s>Subhūti</s>, would arise in that man at the end of the day—that many <s>kalpas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> cut short, turn away from, and make an end of in <s>saṃsāra</s>, who stands, trains, practices, contemplates, and applies himself here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as enjoined, as declared, as taught, as pointed out, as expounded, and who avoids those faults by which a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> turns back from <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who is devoted to the practice of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, dwelling in this abiding, namely in mental attentions connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, accomplishes that much <s>karma</s> in a single day. And a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, standing for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were to give gifts—this very one surpasses him, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who applies himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> even for a single day.'

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte yaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan srotaāpannebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, pratiṣṭhāpayet, evaṃ sakṛdāgāmiṣvanāgāmiṣvarhatsu dānaṃ dadyāt, pratiṣṭhāpayet / pratyekabuddheṣu dānaṃ dadyāt pratiṣṭhāpayet / tathāgateṣvarhatsu samyaksaṃbuddheṣu dānaṃ dadyāt pratiṣṭhāpayet, virahitaś ca prajñāpāramitāyā / yaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yathopadiṣṭaṃ yathoddiṣṭaṃ yathānirdiṣṭaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ tathaiva yogamāpadyeta ekadivasam api / ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvastataḥ paurvakādbodhisattvadbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, standing for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were to give gifts to <s>Srotaāpannas</s> (stream-enterers), were to establish them—likewise were to give gifts to <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s> (once-returners), <s>Anāgāmins</s> (non-returners), and <s>Arhats</s>, were to establish them; were to give gifts to <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, were to establish them; were to give gifts to <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, were to establish them—and yet were devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; and if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, just as taught, just as pointed out, just as expounded, were to apply himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> even for a single day—this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> produces far more merit than that former <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte yo bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan srotaāpanneṣu yāvatsamyaksaṃbuddheṣu dānaṃ dadyāt pratiṣṭhāpayet, śīleṣu ca paripūrṇakārī bhavet, virahitaś ca prajñāpāramitayā bhavet / yaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihārī tato manasikārādvyutthāya dharmaṃ deśayet, ayameva subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastataḥ paurvakādbodhisattvādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, standing for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were to give gifts to <s>Srotaāpannas</s> up to Perfectly Awakened Ones, were to establish them, and were to be one who fully fulfills the moral precepts, yet were devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; and if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, dwelling in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, rising from that mental attention, were to teach the <s>Dharma</s>—this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, produces far more merit than that former <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte yo bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan srotaāpanneṣu yāvatsamyaksaṃbuddheṣu dānaṃ dadyāt pratiṣṭhāpayet, śīleṣu ca paripūrṇakārī bhavet, kṣāntyā ca samanvāgato bhavet, virahitaś ca prajñāpāramitayā / yaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihārī tato manasikāradvyutthāya dharmadānaṃ dadyāt, ayameva subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāsattvastataḥ paurvakādbodhisattvādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, standing for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were to give gifts to <s>Srotaāpannas</s> up to Perfectly Awakened Ones, were to establish them, were to be one who fully fulfills the moral precepts, and were endowed with patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), yet were devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; and if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, dwelling in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, rising from that mental attention, were to give the gift of <s>Dharma</s>—this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, produces far more merit than that former <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan srotaāpanneṣu yāvatsamyaksaṃbuddheṣu dānaṃ dadyāt pratiṣṭhāpayet, śīleṣu paripūrṇakārī kṣāntyā ca samanvāgataḥ, ārabdhavīryaḥ san dhyāneṣu bodhipakṣeṣu ca dharmeṣu yogamāpadyeta, virahitaś ca prajñāpāramitayā / yaś ca khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathā dharmadānaṃ datvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayet, ayameva subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastataḥ paurvakādbodhisattvādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, standing for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were to give gifts to <s>Srotaāpannas</s> up to Perfectly Awakened Ones, were to establish them, fully fulfilling the moral precepts, endowed with patience, with vigorous effort aroused, were to apply himself to the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and to the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), yet were devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; and if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, having thus given the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, were to dedicate it to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>—this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, produces far more merit than that former <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathā dharmadānaṃ datvā prajñāpāramitoktena pariṇāmena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayet, ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who, having thus given the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, were to dedicate it to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> with the dedication taught by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—this one produces far more merit.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathā dharmadānaṃ datvā prajñāpāramitoktena pariṇāmena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayet, pariṇāmya ca pratisaṃlāne na punareva yogamāpadyeta / yaś ca khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathā dharmadānameva dadyāt, na punaḥ pratisaṃlāne yogamāpadyeta, sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na tāvatpuṇyaṃ prasavati, yāvadya evaṃ dharmadānaṃ dadad bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pratisaṃlāne ca punareva yogamāpadyamānaḥ prajñāpāramitayā ca parigṛhītastatpratisaṃlānamavirahitaṃ karoti prajñāpāramitayā, ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who, having thus given the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, were to dedicate it to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> with the dedication taught by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having dedicated it, were not to apply himself further to meditative seclusion (<s>pratisaṃlāna</s>); and another <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who were to give just such a gift of <s>Dharma</s> but were not to apply himself to meditative seclusion—that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not produce as much merit as this one who, giving the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, and again applying himself to meditative seclusion, embraced by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, makes that meditative seclusion not devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> produces far more merit.

body.text: subhūtirāha - yadā bhagavan abhisaṃskāro vikalpa ityuktaṃ bhagavatā, tadā kathaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavatītyucyate? bhagavānāha - so 'pīdānīṃ subhūte puṇyābhisaṃskāro bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ śūnyaka ityevākhyāyate, riktaka ityevākhyāyate, tucchaka ityevākhyāyate, asāraka ityevākhyāyate / yathā yathā khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ sarvadharmān pratyavekṣate, tathā tathā subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'virahito bhavati prajñāpāramitayā / yathā yathā ca subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'virahito bhavati prajñāpāramitayā, tathā tathā aprameyamasaṃkhyeyaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> asked: "When, O Blessed One, the Blessed One has said that formations are conceptual elaboration, how can it be said that [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] produces greater merit?" The Blessed One replied: "Even that meritorious formation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>—"

body.text: subhūtirāha - aprameyasya ca bhagavan asaṃkhyeyasya ca kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ vā, kaḥ prativiśeṣo vā? bhagavānāha - aprameyamiti subhūte yatra pramāṇānyuparamante / asaṃkhyeyamiti subhūte yanna śakyaṃ saṃkhyayāpi kṣapayitum //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> asked: "O Blessed One, what is the difference between 'immeasurable' and 'innumerable,' or what is the distinction?" The Blessed One replied: "'Immeasurable,' <s>Subhūti</s>, means that where measures cease. 'Innumerable,' <s>Subhūti</s>, means that which cannot be counted—"

body.text: subhūtirāha - syādbhagavan paryāyo yadrūpamaprameyaṃ bhavet, evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / syādbhagavan paryāyo yadvijñānamaprameyaṃ bhavet? bhagavānāha - yatsubhūtirevamāha - syādbhagavan paryāyo yadrūpamaprameyaṃ bhavet, evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / syādbhagavan paryāyo yadvijñānamaprameyaṃ bhavediti / syātsubhūte paryāyo yena rūpamevāprameyaṃ bhavet, evaṃ vedanaiva saṃjñaiva saṃskārā eva / syātsubhūte paryāyo yena vijñānamevāprameyaṃ bhavet / subhūtirāha - kasya punarbhagavan etadadhivacanamaprameyamiti? bhagavānāha - śūnyatāyāḥ subhūte etadadhivacanamaprameyamiti / ānimittasyaitadadhivacanam / apraṇihitasya subhūte etadadhivacanamaprameyamiti //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> asked: "Might there be a way, O Blessed One, in which <s>rūpa</s> (form) could be immeasurable, and likewise <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations)? Might there be a way, O Blessed One, in which <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) could be immeasurable?" The Blessed One replied: "That which you say, <s>Subhūti</s>—'Might there be a way—'"

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—are <s>rūpa</s> and space different?" <s>Subhūti</s> replied: "No, O Blessed One. <s>Rūpa</s> is not different from space; space is not different from <s>rūpa</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> itself is space; space itself is <s>rūpa</s>—"

body.text: subhūtirāha - kiṃ śūnyatāyā eva bhagavan kevalametadadhivacanamaprameyamiti, ānimittasyaiva apraṇihitasyaiva bhagavan kevalametadadhivacanamaprameyamiti, nānyeṣāṃ dharmāṇām? bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte nanu mayā sarvadharmāḥ śūnyā ityākhyātāḥ? subhūtirāha - śūnyā eva bhagavan sarvadharmāstathāgatenākhyātāḥ / bhagavānāha - ye ca subhūte śūnyāḥ, akṣayā api te / yā ca śūnyatā, aprameyatāpi sā / tasmāttarhi subhūte eṣāṃ dharmāṇāmarthato viśeṣo vā nānākaraṇaṃ vā nopalabhyate / abhilāpā ete subhūte tathāgatenākhyātāḥ abhilapitāḥ - aprameyamiti vā, asaṃkhyeyamiti vā, akṣayamiti vā, śūnyamiti vā, ānimittamiti vā, apraṇihitamiti vā, anabhisaṃskāra iti vā, anutpāda iti vā, ajātiriti vā abhāva iti vā, virāga iti vā, nirodha iti vā, nirvāṇamiti vā / deśanābhinirhāranirdeśa eṣa subhūte tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhenākhyātaḥ //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "If, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>rūpa</s> is not different from space and space is not different from <s>rūpa</s>, then <s>rūpa</s> itself is space and space itself is <s>rūpa</s>. Likewise, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>—<s>vijñāna</s> is not different from space; space is not different from <s>vijñāna</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> itself is space; space itself is <s>vijñāna</s>—"

body.text: subhūtirāha - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvadyadiyaṃ tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmatā deśitā, sā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmatā anabhilāpyā / yathāhaṃ bhagavan bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, tathā sarvadharmā api bhagavan anabhilāpyāḥ / bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / sarvadharmā api subhūte anabhilāpyāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yā ca subhūte sarvadharmāṇāṃ śūnyatā, na sā śakyā abhilapitum / subhūtirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan anabhilapyasyārthasya vṛddhirvāsti, parihāṇirvā vidyate? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / subhūtirāhasacedbhagavan anabhilapyasyārthasya na vṛddhirna parihāṇiḥ, dānapāramitāyā api bhagavan na vṛddhirna parihāṇirbhaviṣyati / evaṃ śīlapāramitāyā api, kṣāntipāramitāyā api, vīryapāramitāyā api, dhyānapāramitāyā api, prajñāpāramitāyā api bhagavan na vṛddhirna parihāṇirbhaviṣyati / sacedbhagavan āsāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ na vṛddhirna parihāṇiḥ, kathaṃ bhagavan vivardhamānānāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ balena bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate? kathaṃ ca anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherabhyāsannībhavati? na ca bhagavan apratipūrayan pāramitāṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhyāsannībhavatyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / na khalu punaḥ subhūte pāramitārthasya kācidvṛddhirvāsti parihāṇirvā vidyate / api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayata upāyakuśalasya naivaṃ bhavati - iyaṃ dānapāramitā vivardhate, iyaṃ dānapāramitā parihīyate iti / api tu khalu punarasyaivaṃ bhavati - nāmadheyamātrametadyaduta dānapāramiteti / sa dānaṃ dadat tān manasikārāṃstāṃścittotpādāṃstāni kuśalamūlāni anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati / yathā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhistathā pariṇāmayati //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> asked: "If, O Blessed One, <s>rūpa</s> and space are not different, and space and <s>rūpa</s> are not different—O Blessed One, if the five <s>skandhas</s> are space, then how will a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, training in space, fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>?"

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayataḥ upāyakuśalasya naivaṃ bhavati - iyaṃ śīlapāramitā vivardhate, iyaṃ śīlapāramitā
body.translated_text: The Blessed One replied: "<s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not stand in the notion 'form is space' or 'space is form'—"

body.text: parihīyate iti / api tu khalu punarasyaivaṃ bhavati - nāmadheyamātrametadyaduta śīlapāramiteti / sa śīlaṃ samādāya vartamānastān manasikārāṃstāṃścittotpādāṃstāni kuśalamūlāni anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati / yathā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhistathā pariṇāmayati //
body.translated_text: For, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not stand in <s>rūpa</s>, does not stand in <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>. He does not stand in the impermanence of <s>rūpa</s>, nor in the impermanence of <s>vedanā</s>—"

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayataḥ upāyakuśalasya naivaṃ bhavati - iyaṃ kṣāntipāramitā vivardhate, iyaṃ kṣāntipāramitā parihīyate iti / api tu khalu punarasyaivaṃ bhavati - nāmadheyamātrametadyaduta kṣāntipāramiteti / sa kṣāntyā saṃpādayaṃstān manasikārāṃstāṃścittotpādāṃstāni ca kuśalamūlāni anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati / yathā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhistathā pariṇāmayati //
body.translated_text: "Nor does he stand in the suffering of <s>rūpa</s>, nor in the emptiness, nor in the selflessness of <s>rūpa</s>. Likewise for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>—"

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayata upāyakuśalasya naivaṃ bhavati - iyaṃ vīryapāramitā vivardhate, iyaṃ vīryapāramitā parihīyate iti / api tu khalu punarasyaivaṃ bhavati - nāmadheyamātrametadyaduta vīryapāramiteti / sa vīryamārabhamāṇastān manasikārāṃstāṃścittotpādāṃstāni ca kuśalamūlāni anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmayati / yathā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhistathā pariṇāmayati //
body.translated_text: "Not standing in any <s>dharma</s>, he trains in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). Thus training, he fully awakens to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Having fully awakened, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings—"

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayataḥ upāyakuśalasya naivaṃ bhavati - iyaṃ dhyānapāramitā vivardhate, iyaṃ dhyānapāramitā parihīyate iti / api tu khalu punarasyaivaṃ bhavati - nāmadheyamātrametadyaduta dhyānapāramiteti / sa dhyānāni samāpadyamānastān manasikārāṃstāṃścittotpādāṃstāni ca kuśalamūlāni anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati / yathā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhistathā pariṇāmayati //
body.translated_text: (Vaidya 177)

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayataḥ upāyakuśalasya naivaṃ bhavati - iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā vivardhate, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā parihīyate iti / api tu khalu punarasyaivaṃ bhavati - nāmadheyamātrametadyaduta prajñāpāramiteti / sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayaṃstān manasikārāṃstāṃścittotpādāṃstāni ca kuśalamūlāni anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati / yathā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhistathā pariṇāmayati //
body.translated_text: "He teaches through various <s>Dharma</s>-doors suitable to the inclinations of beings. Having taught thus, he establishes immeasurable, innumerable beings in the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, <s>Arhatship</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>, and <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>—"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - kā punareṣā bhagavan anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ? bhagavānāha - tathataiṣā subhūte anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ / na ca subhūte tathatā vivardhate, vā, parihīyate vā / sacedbodhisattvo mahāsattvastatpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairabhīkṣṇaṃ bahūlaṃ viharati, evaṃ sa āsannībhavatyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, taiś ca manasikārairna parihīyate / evaṃ khalu subhūte anabhilapyasyārthasya na vṛddhirna parihāṇirbhavati / evaṃ pāramitānāṃ na vṛddhirna parihāṇirbhavati / evaṃ sarvadharmāṇām api subhūte na vṛddhirna parihāṇirbhavati / evaṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva ebhirevaṃrūpairmanasikārairviharan āsannībhavatyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheriti //
body.translated_text: "Yet, <s>Subhūti</s>, no being has been established anywhere by anyone. For what reason? Because of the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things) of those <s>dharmas</s>—"

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śūnyatāparivarto nāmāṣṭādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the Eighteenth Chapter, called "The Chapter on Emptiness," in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

body.text: ASP_19: gaṅgadevībhaginīparivarta ekonaviṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Nineteen: The Chapter on the Goddess <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s Sister.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - kiṃ punarbhagavan prathamacittotpādena bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, utāho paścimacittotpādena bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate? paurvako bhagavaṃścittotpādaḥ paścimakena cittotpādena asamavahitaḥ, paścimakaścittotpādaḥ paurvakeṇa cittotpādena asamavahitaḥ / kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kuśalamūlānāmupacayo bhavati? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte tailapradyotasya jvalato 'rciṣā prathamābhinipātena sā vartirdagdhā, utāho paścimābhinipātenārciṣā sā vartirdagdhā? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / na hi bhagavan arciṣā prathamābhinipātena sā vartirdagdhā / na ca prathamābhinipātamanāgamya arciṣā sā vartirdagdhā / na ca bhagavan paścimābhinipātenārciṣā sā vartirdagdhā, na ca paścimābhinipātamanāgamya arciṣā sā vartirdagdhā / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sā vartirdagdhā? subhūtirāha - dagdhā bhagavan, dagdhā sugata / bhagavānāha - evameva subhūte na ca prathamacittotpādena bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, na ca prathamacittotpādamanāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / na ca paścimacittotpādena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, na ca paścimacittotpādamanāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / na ca taiścittopādairna cānyatra tebhyaścittotpādebhyo 'bhisaṃbudhyate / abhisaṃbudhyate ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: "Does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, O Blessed One, awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> with the first arising of the mind, or does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> with the last arising of the mind—"

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - gambhīro 'yaṃ bhagavan pratītyasamutpādaḥ / na ca nāma bhagavan prathamacittotpādenaiva bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, na ca nāma prathamacittotpādamanāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / na ca nāma paścimacittotpādenaiva bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, na ca nāma paścimacittotpādamanāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, na ca nāma taiścittotpādairna cānyatra tebhyaścittotpādebhyo 'bhisaṃbudhyate / abhisaṃbudhyate ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Profound, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does not awaken to supreme perfect awakening by the first arising of the mind alone, nor does he awaken to supreme perfect awakening without having reached the first arising of the mind. A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not awaken to supreme perfect awakening by the last arising of the mind alone, nor does he awaken to supreme perfect awakening without having reached the last arising of the mind. He does not awaken by those arisings of the mind, nor apart from those arisings of the mind does he awaken. And yet the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does awaken to supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yaccittaṃ niruddham, api nu tatpunarutpatsyate? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yaccittamanutpannam, api nu tannirodhadharmi? āha - nirodhadharmi bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yannirodhadharmi, api nu tannirotsyate? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yaccittamanutpannam, api nu tannirodhadharmi? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yannirodhadharmi, api nu tannirotsyate? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yaccittamanutpādānirodhadharmi,
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—a mind that has ceased, will it arise again?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—a mind that has not arisen, is it subject to cessation?' He said: 'It is subject to cessation, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—that which is subject to cessation, will it cease?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—a mind that has not arisen, is it subject to cessation?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—that which is subject to cessation, will it cease?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—a mind that is of the nature of neither arising nor cessation,

body.text: api nu tannirotsyate? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yo dharmaḥ prakṛtyā svabhāvaniruddha eva, sa dharmo nirotsyate? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yā dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā sā nirotsyate? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte tathaiva sthāsyati yathā tathatā? āha - tathaiva bhagavan sthāsyati yathā tathatā / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yadi tathaiva sthāsyati yathā tathatā, tadā mā kuṭasthā bhūt? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte gambhīrā tathatā? āha - gambhīrā bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase tathatāyāṃ cittam? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte cittaṃ tathatā? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte anyattathatāyāścittam? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - samanupaśyasi tvaṃ subhūte tathatām? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ya evaṃ carati sa gambhīre carati? āha - yo bhagavan evaṃ carati, sa na kvaciccarati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hyasya te samudācārā na pravartante, na samudācaranti / bhagavānāha - yaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ carati, sa kva carati? āha - carati bhagavan paramārthe / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ paramārthe carati, sa nimitte carati? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu tasya nimittamavibhāvitam? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato nimittaṃ vibhāvitaṃ bhavati? subhūtirāha - na sa bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ prayujyate - kathamahaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ carannihaiva nimittaprahāṇamanuprāpnuyāmiti / sacetpunaranuprāpnuyāt, apratipūrṇaiḥ sarvabuddhadharmaiḥ śrāvako bhavet / etattadbhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyopāyakauśalyaṃ yat, tacca nimittaṃ jānāti, yallakṣaṇaṃ yannimittamānimitte ca parijayaṃ karoti //
body.translated_text: will it cease?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—a <s>dharma</s> that is by its very nature, by its own nature, already ceased—will that <s>dharma</s> cease?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—the <s>dharmatā</s> (essential nature) of <s>dharmas</s>, will it cease?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—will it remain just as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is?' He said: 'It will remain just as <s>tathatā</s> is, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—if it will remain just as <s>tathatā</s> is, would it not then be immutable?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—is <s>tathatā</s> profound?' He said: 'It is profound, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think—is the mind in <s>tathatā</s>?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—is the mind <s>tathatā</s>?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—is the mind other than <s>tathatā</s>?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you perceive <s>tathatā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—one who practices thus, does he practice in the profound?' He said: 'One who practices thus, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does not practice anywhere. Why is that? For those mental activities do not operate, do not function for him.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>—where does he practice?' He said: 'He practices in ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices in ultimate reality, does he practice in signs?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—has the sign not been cultivated by him?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> cultivate the sign?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'That <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does not exert himself thinking: "How shall I, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> course, attain the abandonment of signs right here?" For if he were to attain it, he would become a <s>śrāvaka</s> with <s>Buddha</s> qualities unfulfilled. This, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>: that he knows that sign, knows what characteristic and what sign [it has], and yet gains familiarity with the signless.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - ya āyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svapnāntaragatastrīṇi vimokṣamukhāni bhāvayati - śūnyatāmānimittamapraṇihitaṃ ca, api nu tasya prajñāpāramitā vivardhate? subhūtirāha - sacedāyuṣman śāriputra divasabhāvanayā vivardhate, evaṃ svapnāntaragatasyāpi vivardhate / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpo hi āyuṣman śāriputra svapnaś ca divasaścokto bhagavatā / sacedāyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitālābhī divase divase prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, tato 'sya prajñāpāramitābhyāsataḥ svapnāntaragatasyāpi bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāvaipulyena bhavitavyam / śāriputra āha - yatpunarāyuṣman subhūte strī vā puruṣo vā svapnāntaragataḥ karma śubhamaśubhaṃ vā karoti, kiṃ bhavati tasya karmaṇa ācayo vā upacayo vā? subhūtirāha - yathā svapnopamāḥ sarvadharmā uktā bhagavatā, tathā na tasya karmaṇo bhavatyācayo vā upacayo vā / atha punarāyuṣman śāriputra sa puruṣaḥ prativibuddhaḥ san vikalpayan hatasaṃjñāmutpādayati,
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> within a dream cultivates the three gates of liberation—<s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness), and <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness)—does his <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> increase?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'If, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it increases through daytime cultivation, then it also increases for one within a dream. Why is that? For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared that dream and daytime are without distinction. If, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has attained the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> day after day, then through his familiarity with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, even within a dream the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should have the fullness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, when a man or woman within a dream performs wholesome or unwholesome <s>karma</s>, is there accumulation or increase of that <s>karma</s>?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Just as all <s>dharmas</s> have been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be dream-like, so there is neither accumulation nor increase of that <s>karma</s>. But if, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that person, having awakened, conceptualizes and generates the perception of killing,

body.text: bhavati tasya karmaṇa ācayo vā upacayo vā / kathaṃ ca āyuṣman śāriputra vikalpayan hatasaṃjñāmutpādayati? sacetsvapnāntaragataḥ prāṇātipātaṃ kṛtvā prativibuddhaḥ sannevaṃ vikalpayati - aho hataḥ, sādhu hataḥ, suṣṭhu hataḥ, mayā hataḥ, ityevaṃ vikalpayan hatasaṃjñāmutpādayati / śāriputra āha - sacedāyuṣman subhūte sa puruṣaḥ prativibuddhaḥ san vikalpayan hatasaṃjñāmutpādayati - aho hataḥ, sādhu hataḥ, suṣṭhu hataḥ, mayā hata iti, bhavati tasya karmaṇa ācayo vā upacayo vā? buddho bhagavān api vikalpayan kṣayasaṃjñāmutpādayati / tasyāpi karmaṇa ācayo vā upacayo vā bhavet? subhūtirāha - no hīdamāyuṣman śāriputra / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvakalpavikalpaprahīṇo hi tathāgataḥ / tadyathāpi nāma ākāśameva āyuṣman śāriputra nānārambaṇaṃ karmotpadyate, nānārambaṇaṃ cittamutpadyate / tasmāttarhyāyuṣman śāriputra sārambaṇameva karmotpadyate, na anārambaṇam / sārambaṇameva cittamutpadyate, na anārambaṇam / dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāteṣvāyuṣman śāriputra dharmeṣu buddhiḥ pravartate / tatra kācidbuddhiḥ saṃkleśaṃ parigṛhṇāti, kācidbuddhirvyavadānaṃ parigṛhṇāti / tasmāttarhi āyuṣman śāriputra sārambaṇaiva cetanotpadyate na anārambaṇā, sārambaṇameva karmotpadyate na anārambaṇam / śāriputra āha - yadāyuṣman subhūte sarvārambaṇāni viviktāni ākhyātāni bhagavatā, tadā kasmādāyuṣman subhūte sārambaṇaiva cetanotpadyate na anārambaṇā? subhūtirāha - nimittīkṛtya āyuṣman śāriputra vidyamānamevārambaṇamārambaṇīkṛtya sārambaṇaiva cetanotpadyate, na anārambaṇā / cetanāpyāyuṣman śāriputra viviktā, nimittam api viviktam / evamavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā api viviktāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānamapi, yāvajjātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇam api viviktam / evameva āyuṣman śāriputra sarvārambaṇāni viviktāni / nimittena viviktā cetanā lokavyavahāramupādāyotpadyata iti //
body.translated_text: there is accumulation and increase of that <s>karma</s>. And how, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, does one generate the perception of killing through conceptualizing? If, having taken life within a dream, one awakens and conceptualizes thus: "Ah, killed! Well killed! Properly killed! Killed by me!"—conceptualizing thus, one generates the perception of killing.' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'If, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, that person, having awakened, conceptualizes and generates the perception of killing—"Ah, killed! Well killed! Properly killed! Killed by me!"—is there accumulation and increase of that <s>karma</s>? Does the awakened <s>Bhagavān</s> too, conceptualizing, generate the perception of destruction? Would there also be accumulation and increase of that <s>karma</s>?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. Why is that? For the <s>Tathāgata</s> has abandoned all conceptualization and discrimination. Just as, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in space itself no <s>karma</s> arises with reference to various objects, and no mind arises with reference to various objects—therefore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>karma</s> arises only with a support, not without a support; mind arises only with a support, not without a support. In things seen, heard, thought, and known, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, cognition operates. Some cognition grasps defilement, and some cognition grasps purification. Therefore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, volition arises only with a support, not without a support; <s>karma</s> arises only with a support, not without a support.' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, when all supports have been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be isolated [empty], then why, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does volition arise only with a support and not without a support?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Having made a sign, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having taken an existing support as a support, volition arises only with a support, not without a support. Volition too, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is isolated, and the sign too is isolated. Likewise, formations conditioned by ignorance are also isolated; consciousness conditioned by formations is also [isolated]; up to aging and death conditioned by birth is also isolated. Thus indeed, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all supports are isolated. Volition, isolated from the sign, arises based on worldly convention.'

body.text: śāriputra āha - yadāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svapnāntaragato dānaṃ dadyāt, tacca dānamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati / pariṇāmitaṃ kiṃ taddānaṃ vaktavyam? subhūtirāha - ayamāyuṣman śāriputra maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saṃmukhībhūtaḥ / eṣa tathāgatena vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / eṣo 'trārthe kāyasākṣī / eṣa praṣṭavyaḥ / eṣa enamarthaṃ visarjayiṣyati / atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - ayamāyuṣman maitreya subhūtiḥ sthavira evamāha - mayaṃ maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / eṣa enamarthaṃ visarjayiṣyatīti / visarjaya āyuṣmannajita enamartham / atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattva āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - yadāyuṣmān subhūtirevamāha - ayaṃ maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / eṣa enamarthaṃ visarjayiṣyatīti / kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte yadetannāmadheyaṃ maitreya iti? etadenamarthaṃ visarjayiṣyati, uta rūpaṃ visarjayiṣyati, uta vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ, atha vijñānaṃ visarjayiṣyati, utāho varṇo visarjayiṣyati, atha saṃsthānaṃ visarjayiṣyati, utāho yā rūpasya śūnyatā, sā visarjayiṣyati? evaṃ yā vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām,
body.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> within a dream gives a gift, and dedicates that gift to supreme perfect awakening—is that gift to be called dedicated?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'This <s>Maitreya</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, is present here. He has been given a prophecy by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for supreme perfect awakening. He is an eyewitness in this matter. He should be asked. He will resolve this question.' Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>: 'Venerable <s>Maitreya</s>, the elder <s>Subhūti</s> here speaks thus: "<s>Maitreya</s> is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. He will resolve this question." Resolve, venerable <s>Ajita</s>, this question.' Then <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, you speak thus: "This is <s>Maitreya</s> the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. He will resolve this question." But what is this name "<s>Maitreya</s>"? Will this [name] resolve the question, or will form resolve it, or feeling, perception, formations, or will consciousness resolve it, or will color resolve it, or will shape resolve it, or will the emptiness of form resolve it? Likewise, the [emptiness] of feeling, perception, formations,

body.text: yā vijñānasya śūnyatā, sā visarjayiṣyati? yā khalu punarāyuṣman subhūte rūpasya śūnyatā, na sā pratibalā visarjayitum / evaṃ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām / yā khalu punarāyuṣman subhūte vijñānasya śūnyatā, na sā pratibalā visarjayitum / tamapyahamāyuṣman subhūte dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi, yo dharmo visarjayet / tamapyahaṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi, yo dharmo visarjayitavyaḥ / tamapyahaṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi, yena dharmeṇa visarjayet / tamapyahaṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi, yo dharmo vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau //
body.translated_text: will the emptiness of consciousness resolve it? But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the emptiness of form is not capable of resolving [it]. Likewise of feeling, perception, and formations. And, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the emptiness of consciousness is not capable of resolving [it]. I do not perceive, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, any <s>dharma</s> that would resolve [it]. I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> that should be resolved. I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> by which one would resolve [it]. I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> that has been given a prophecy for supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - kaccitpunarāyuṣman maitreya tvayā ete dharmā evaṃ sākṣātkṛtāḥ, yathainān vācā bhāṣase? maitreya āha - na mayā āyuṣman śāriputra ete dharmā evaṃ sākṣātkṛtāḥ, yathainān vācā bhāṣe / evamapyahamenānāyuṣman śāriputra dharmānna vedmi, nopalabhe, na samanupaśyāmi, yathā vācā bhāṣe, cittena vā cintayāmi / api tu khalu punarāyuṣman śāriputra na kāyena spṛśyeta, na vācā bhāṣyeta, na manasā samanvāhriyeta / evaṃsvabhāvāḥ sarve dharmā asvabhāvatvāt / atha khalvāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitadabhūt - gambhīraprajño batāyaṃ maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, yathāpi nāma dīrgharātraṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritāvī nirdiśati //
