yathā mayā nāmadheyamanuvartitamanuvitarkitamanuvicāritam, aho bata me 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya sataḥ idaṃ nāmadheyaṃ bhavediti, tathā tena bhikṣuṇā nirdiṣṭamiti / sa evaṃ yacca nāmadheyaṃ svayamanuvicintitam, yacca tena māreṇa pāpīyasā mārakāyikābhirvā devatābhirabhinirmitena mārādhiṣṭhitena vā bhikṣuṇā nāmadheyamudīritam, tadubhayaṃ tulayitvā yathā ca mama cittotpāda utpannaḥ, yathā ca anena bhikṣuṇā nirdiṣṭaṃ mama nāmadheyaṃ sameti nāmnā, nāmavyākṛto 'haṃ taiḥ paurvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti maṃsyate / yāni ca mayā subhūte avinivartanīyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmākārā liṅgāni nimittāni ākhyātāni, tāni tasya na bhaviṣyanti / sa tairvirahito 'nena nāmāpadeśena nāmavyākaraṇena manyanāmutpādayiṣyati / sa manyanāmutpādya tato 'nyān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānavamaṃsyate - ahaṃ vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, naite vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti / evaṃ sa tena mānena atimānena mānātimānena abhimānena mithyāmānena ca tadanyān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānavamanyamāno dūrīkariṣyati sarvajñatām, dūrīkariṣyati buddhajñānam / tasya prajñāpāramitayā aparigṛhītasya upāyakauśalyavirahitasya kalyāṇamitravirahitasya pāpamitraparigṛhītasya dvayorbhūmyoranyatarā bhūmiḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyā - śrāvakabhūmirvā pratyekabuddhabhūmirvā / sacetpunaściraṃ suciraṃ saṃdhāvya saṃsṛtya enāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmo bhavet, yadi cāsāvupasarpet kalyāṇamitrāṇi, abhīkṣṇaṃ ca tānyupasaṃkramiṣyati, tenaiva cātmabhāvapratilambhena tāvatpūrvakāṃścittotpādān vigarhiṣyati, vāntīkariṣyati, jugupsiṣyati, pratiniḥ - srakṣyati, pratideśayiṣyati, tathāpi buddhabhūmistasya durlabhā bhaviṣyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tāvadgurutaraṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mananāpattisthānam / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte bhikṣoḥ śrāvakayānikasya śrāvakabhūmau catasro mūlāpattayo gurvyo bhavanti, yato 'nyatarānyatarā māpattimadhyāpadya abhikṣurbhavatyaśramaṇo 'śākyaputrīyaḥ, iyameva tābhyaścatasṛbhya āpattibhyo gurutarā āpattiḥ, yo 'yaṃ mānacittotpādaḥ, yaduta nāmāpadeśena bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyāvamānanayā mahānakuśalaścittotpāda utpannaḥ / ayaṃ tābhyaścatasṛbhya āpattibhyo gurutaraścittotpādo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should understand prediction by name-designation as a deed of <s>Māra</s>. And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> understand prediction by name-designation as a deed of <s>Māra</s>? Here—

body.text: tiṣṭhantu subhūte catasro gurvyo mūlāpattayaḥ / pañcabhyo 'pi subhūte ānantaryebhyaḥ
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Subhūti</s>, the four grave root transgressions. Even the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) [deeds], <s>Subhūti</s>—

body.text: karmabhyo gurutaro 'yaṃ cittotpādaḥ, yo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmāpadeśena mānasahagataścittotpāda utpannaḥ / ayaṃ tebhyaḥ pañcabhya ānantaryebhyaḥ karmabhyo gurutaraścittotpādo veditavyaḥ / iti hi subhūte anenāpi nāmāpadeśena sūkṣmasūkṣmāṇi mārakarmāṇyutpatsyante / tāni bodhisattvena mahāsattvena boddhavyāni / anyebhyaścāvabodhayitavyāni, buddhvā ca vivarjayitavyāni //
body.translated_text: more weighty than those <s>karmas</s> is this arising of the mind—this mental arising accompanied by mere designation that has arisen for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. This arising of the mind should be known as more weighty than those five acts of immediate retribution (<s>ānantarya</s>). Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, even by this mere designation, the subtlest of <s>Māra</s>'s deeds will arise. Those should be recognized by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, and he should make others recognize them too; having recognized them, he should abandon them.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān vivekaguṇena bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamupasaṃkramya codayiṣyati smārayiṣyati / kathaṃ ca subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān vivekaguṇena bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamupasaṃkramya codayiṣyati smārayiṣyati? iha subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamupasaṃkramiṣyati, upasaṃkramyaivaṃ vakṣyati - vivekasya tathāgato varṇavādī araṇyavanaprasthagiriguhāśmaśānapalālapuñjādiṣu vihartavyamiti / na cāhaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya evaṃvidhaṃ vivekaṃ vadāmi, yaduta āraṇyakāni prāntāni śayanāsanāni vijanapadāni viviktāni, vividhāni vanaprasthagiriguhāśmaśānapalālapuñjādīni //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one will approach the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> under the guise of the virtue of seclusion, and will urge and remind him. And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, will <s>Māra</s> the evil one approach the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> under the guise of the virtue of seclusion, and urge and remind him? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one will approach the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> and, having approached, will speak thus: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> praises seclusion—one should dwell in forests, groves, mountain caves, charnel grounds, heaps of straw, and such places.' But I, <s>Subhūti</s>, do not speak of such seclusion for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>—namely, forest retreats, remote lodgings, uninhabited places, secluded spots, various groves, mountain caves, charnel grounds, heaps of straw, and the like.

body.text: subhūtirāha - katamaḥ punaḥ sa bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anyo viveko yadi vā āraṇyakāni prāntāni śayanāsanāni vijanapadāni viviktāni vividhāni vanaprasthagiriguhāśmaśānapalālapuñjādīni? yadi tāni nādhyāvasati, kiyadrūpaḥ punarbhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyānyo vivekaḥ? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sacetsubhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vivikto bhavati śrāvakapratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ, vivikto bhavati pratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ, evaṃ sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vivikto viharati / grāmānte 'pi hi viharan prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaparigṛhītaḥ sarvasattvamaitrīmahākaruṇāvihāreṇa viharet / anena vihāreṇa viharan vivikta eva sa viharati / ayaṃ khalu punaḥ subhūte mayā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya śrāvakapratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktamanasikāraviveko 'nujñātaḥ / anena vivekena viharan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo rātriṃdivānyatināmayati, vivikto viharati / sacedbodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'raṇyavanaprasthagiriguhāśmaśānaprāntaśayanāsaneṣvanena vihāreṇa viharati, vivikto bodhisattvo mahāsattvo viharati / yaṃ punaḥ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān vivekamupadekṣyati araṇyavanaprasthagiriguhāśmaśānaprāntaśayanāsanavihārān, sa tena vivekena śrāvakapratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ saṃkīrṇa eva san prajñāpāramitāyāmanabhiyujyamāno na sarvajñajñānaṃ paripūrayati / evaṃ sa saṃkīrṇavihāreṇa viharan so 'pariśuddhena manasikāreṇa viharan apariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmāntaḥ eva bhaviṣyati / apariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmānta eva saṃstato 'nyān api bodhisattvān mahāsattvān grāmāntavihāriṇo 'saṃkīrṇān śrāvakapratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ prajñopāyamahākaruṇāvihāravihāriṇo 'vamaṃsyate / araṇye 'pi viharan so 'pariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmāntaḥ san saṃkīrṇavihāryeva bhavati, na viviktavihārī / sa prajñopāyamahākaruṇāvihāravihāriṇo
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'What then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the other seclusion for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, if it is not forest retreats, remote lodgings, uninhabited places, secluded spots, various groves, mountain caves, charnel grounds, heaps of straw, and the like? If he does not resort to those, what manner of seclusion, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the other seclusion for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is secluded from mental activities connected with the <s>śrāvakas</s>, secluded from mental activities connected with the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>—thus that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells in seclusion. For even dwelling at the edge of a village, sustained by <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), he would dwell in the dwelling of great loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward all beings. Dwelling in this manner, he indeed dwells in seclusion. And this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the seclusion I have prescribed for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>: seclusion from mental activities connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Dwelling in this seclusion, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> passes his days and nights in seclusion. If the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells in forest, grove, mountain cave, charnel ground, or remote lodgings with this manner of dwelling, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells in seclusion. But the seclusion that <s>Māra</s> the evil one will teach—dwelling in forest, grove, mountain cave, charnel ground, or remote lodgings—by that seclusion, being mingled with mental activities connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, not applying himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he will not fulfill the knowledge of omniscience (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>). Thus, dwelling in a mingled manner, dwelling with impure mental activity, he will have impure conduct of body, speech, and mind. Having impure conduct of body, speech, and mind, he will disparage other <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who dwell at the edge of villages, who are unmingled with mental activities connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, who dwell in the dwelling of wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion. Even dwelling in the forest, having impure conduct of body, speech, and mind, he is one who dwells in a mingled manner, not one who dwells in seclusion. He, [disparaging] those who dwell at the edge of villages in the dwelling of wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion,

body.text: grāmānte viharataḥ pariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmasamudācārān śrāvakapratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktamanasikāraviviktānasaṃkīrṇān śrāvakapratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraistāṃstāvatso 'vamanyamāno na dhyānasamādhisamāpattivimokṣābhijñānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati / na cāsya tāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi so 'nupāyakuśalo bhavati //
body.translated_text: who are of pure conduct of body, speech, and mind, who are secluded from mental activities connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, unmingled with mental activities connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>—disparaging those, he will not obtain <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), or <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). Nor will those reach fulfillment for him. Why is that? For such a person is unskilled in means (<s>anupāyakuśala</s>).'

body.text: kiṃcāpi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yojanaśatikeṣvaṭavīkāntāreṣu viharedapagatavyālamṛgapakṣisaṃgheṣu apagatakṣudramṛgavyālayakṣarākṣasānuvicariteṣu apagatacaurakāntārabhayabhairavopadraveṣu saṃtiṣṭhet, varṣaṃ vā varṣaśataṃ vā varṣasahasraṃ vā varṣaśatasahasraṃ vā varṣakoṭīṃ vā varṣakoṭīśataṃ vā varṣakoṭīsahasraṃ vā varṣakoṭīśatasahasraṃ vā varṣakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraṃ vā, tato vā upari / imaṃ ca vivekaṃ mayopadiṣṭaṃ na jānīyāt, yena vivekena bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'dhyāśayasaṃprasthito 'dhyāśayasaṃpanno viharati / taṃ so 'nupāyakuśalo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'jānannaraṇyaparamo viharati / tatra ca viveke niśritaḥ ālīno 'dhyavasito 'dhyavasāyamāpannaḥ / naiva me subhūte etāvatā sa bodhisattvaścittamārādhayati / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaḥ subhūte viveko bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mayā ākhyātaḥ, tena vivekena viharannasmin viveke na saṃdṛśyate / tamenaṃ māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃkramya uparyantarīkṣe vihāyasi sthitvā evaṃ vakṣyati - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, eṣa bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ tathāgatena viveka ākhyātaḥ / anenaiva tvaṃ kulaputra vivekena vihara / evaṃ tvaṃ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase / sa tato vivekātpunareva araṇyādgrāmāntamavatīrya tadanyān bodhisattvān mahāsattvān peśalān bhikṣūn sabrahmacāriṇaḥ kalyāṇadharmaṇo 'saṃkīrṇān śrāvakapratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ pariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmāntān jīvānavamaṃsyate / sa evaṃ vakṣyati - saṃkīrṇavihāreṇa bateme āyuṣmanto viharanti, na viviktavihāreṇa / ākīrṇavihāreṇa bateme āyuṣmanto viharanti, na viviktavihāreṇa viharantīti / ye te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā viviktavihāreṇa viharanti, tān saṃkīrṇavihāreṇa codayiṣyati, ākīrṇavihāreṇa codayiṣyati / ye ca te saṃkīrṇavihāreṇa viharanti, tān sa viviktavihāreṇa samudācariṣyati, tatra gauravamutpādayiṣyati / yatra ca gauravamutpādayitavyam, tatra mānamutpādayiṣyati / tatkasya hetoḥ? ahamamanuṣyaiścodye, ahamamanuṣyaiḥ smārye / eṣa subhūte vihāro yenāhaṃ vihāreṇa viharāmi / kaṃ grāmāntavihāriṇamamanuṣyāścodayiṣyanti, kaṃ grāmāntare viharantamamanuṣyāḥ smārayiṣyanti, ityevaṃ hi bodhisattvayānikān pudgalānavamaṃsyate / ayaṃ subhūte bodhisattvacaṇḍālo veditavyaḥ, bodhisattvadūṣī veditavyaḥ, bodhisattvapratirūpako veditavyaḥ, bodhisattvaprativarṇiko veditavyaḥ, bodhisattvakāraṇḍavako veditavyaḥ, cauraḥ śramaṇaveṣeṇa, cauro bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pudgalānām, cauraḥ sadevakasya lokasya / tajjātīyaḥ khaluḥ punaḥ subhūte pudgalo na sevitavyo na bhaktavyo na paryupāsitavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? abhimānapatitā hi te tathārūpāḥ pudgalā veditavyāḥ / anyeṣām api tathārūpāṇāmalpa
body.translated_text: 'Even if, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> were to dwell in wilderness tracts extending for hundreds of <s>yojanas</s>, devoid of herds of wild beasts and birds, free from small animals, serpents, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> roaming about, free from the dangers, terrors, and calamities of robber-infested wilds—for a year, a hundred years, a thousand years, a hundred thousand years, a <s>koṭī</s> of years, a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of years, a thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of years, a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of years, a <s>niyuta</s> hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of years, or even longer—yet if he does not know this seclusion that I have taught, the seclusion by which a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has set out with deep aspiration and who is endowed with deep aspiration dwells—that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, unskilled in means, not knowing [true seclusion], dwells as one devoted to the forest. And in that seclusion he is dependent, withdrawn, settled, and stuck in his resolve. Such a <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, does not satisfy my mind. Why is that? The seclusion that I have declared for <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>—dwelling in that seclusion, he is not seen in this [false] seclusion. Then <s>Māra</s> the evil one will approach him and, standing above in the sky, will speak thus: "Well done, well done, son of good family! This is the seclusion that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared for <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. Dwell, son of good family, in just this seclusion. Thus you will quickly awaken to supreme perfect awakening." He then, coming down from that seclusion, from the forest to the edge of the village, will disparage other <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, gentle monks, fellow practitioners of the holy life, of virtuous character, unmingled with mental activities connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, of pure conduct of body, speech, and mind. He will speak thus: "These venerable ones dwell in a mingled manner, not in seclusion. These venerable ones dwell in a crowded manner, not in seclusion." Those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who dwell in seclusion, he will accuse of dwelling in a mingled manner, will accuse of dwelling in a crowded manner. And those who dwell in a mingled manner, he will declare to be dwelling in seclusion and will generate reverence there. Where reverence should be generated, he will generate pride. Why is that? [He will think:] "I am urged by non-human beings, I am reminded by non-human beings. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the manner in which I dwell. What village-dweller will non-human beings urge? What person dwelling at the village edge will non-human beings remind?" Thus he will disparage persons of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle. This one, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as a <s>bodhisattva</s>-outcaste, should be known as a <s>bodhisattva</s>-corrupter, should be known as a counterfeit <s>bodhisattva</s>, should be known as a sham <s>bodhisattva</s>, should be known as a <s>bodhisattva</s>-rubbish heap, a thief in the guise of a renunciant, a thief among persons of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, a thief of the world with its gods. Such a person, <s>Subhūti</s>, should not be associated with, not served, not attended upon. Why is that? For such persons should be known as fallen into conceit. Even of others of weak

body.text: sthāmānācirayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ saṃdūṣaṇaṃ kuryuḥ / aviśuddhadharmāṇo hi te tathārūpāḥ pudgalāḥ veditavyāḥ / anāryā hi te tathārūpāḥ pudgalā veditavyāḥ / anāryadharmāṇo hi te tathārūpāḥ pudgalā veditavyāḥ / yasya khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya aparityaktāḥ sarvasattvāḥ, aparityaktā sarvajñatā, aparityaktā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ, tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena adhyāśayena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena sarvasattvānāmarthaṃ kartukāmena tajjātīyāḥ pudgalā na sevitavyāḥ, na bhaktavyāḥ, na paryupāsitavyāḥ / api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte sarvasattvānāmarthāya abhyutthitena eteṣāṃ ca anyeṣāṃ ca mārakarmaṇāmavabodhāya nityamevodvignacittena bhavitavyaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ mārgamapratilabhamānānāmupadeṣṭumutrastamānasena asaṃsṛṣṭena traidhātukena / tatrāpi tāvanmaitrāyamāṇena karuṇāyamānena mahākaruṇāmutpādya anukampāmupādāya samyakpratipanneṣu sattveṣu muditacittenānupalabdhidharmatayā dharmāṇāmupekṣakeṇa evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam - tathā kariṣyāmi yathā sarve mārakarmadoṣāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvatra sarvadā ca na bhaviṣyanti, notpatsyante / sacedutpatsyante, kṣiprameva pratigamiṣyanti, evaṃ śikṣiṣye iti / ayam api bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ svayamabhijñāya parākramo veditavyaḥ / idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena vivekaguṇena mārakarma veditavyamiti //
body.translated_text: strength who have recently set out in the vehicle, they would cause corruption. For such persons should be known as of impure qualities. Such persons should be known as ignoble. Such persons should be known as of ignoble qualities. But, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has not abandoned all beings, has not abandoned <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), has not abandoned supreme perfect awakening—that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, with deep aspiration, wishing to awaken to supreme perfect awakening, wishing to act for the welfare of all beings, should not associate with, not serve, not attend upon such persons. But rather, <s>Subhūti</s>, one who has risen up for the welfare of all beings, in order to recognize these and other deeds of <s>Māra</s>, should always be of agitated mind, eager to instruct all beings who have not found the path, unmingled with the three realms. Therein, cultivating loving-kindness and compassion, having generated great compassion, having taken up sympathy, with a joyful mind toward beings who are rightly practicing, observing <s>dharmas</s> through their nature of non-apprehension with equanimity, one should generate this mind: "I shall act in such a way that all faults of <s>Māra</s>'s deeds will in every way, everywhere, at all times, not come to be and not arise. If they arise, they will quickly retreat. Thus shall I train." This too should be known as the valorous effort of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> based on their own superknowledge. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a deed of <s>Māra</s> under the guise of the virtue of seclusion.'

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ mārakarmaparivarto nāma ekaviṃśatitamaḥ //

body.text: ASP_22: kalyāṇamitraparivarto dvāviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 22 of the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>: The Chapter on the Spiritual Friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), the twenty-second.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapyāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimāmantrayate sma - iha subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena adhyāśayasaṃprasthitena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena ādita evaṃ kalyāṇamitrāṇi sevitavyāni bhaktavyāni paryupāsitavyāni / subhūtirāha - katamāni tāni punarbhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kalyāṇamitrāṇi veditavyāni, yāni bodhisattvena mahāsattvena adhyāśayasaṃprasthitena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena ādita eva kalyāṇamitrāṇi sevitavyāni bhaktavyāni paryupāsitavyāni? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - buddhā eva subhūte bhagavantaḥ, ye ca te 'vinivartanīyā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bodhisattvacaryākuśalāḥ, ya enaṃ pāramitāsvavavadanti anuśāsati, ye 'smai prajñāpāramitāṃ deśayantyupadiśanti / imāni tāni subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kalyāṇamitrāṇi veditavyāni / prajñāpāramitaiva subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kalyāṇamitraṃ veditavyam / sarvā eva ca subhūte ṣaṭ pāramitā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kalyāṇamitrāṇi veditavyāni / ṣaḍeva pāramitāḥ śāstā, ṣaṭ pāramitā mārgaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitā ālokaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitā ulkā, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ avabhāsaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitāstrāṇam, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ śaraṇam, ṣaṭ pāramitā layanam, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ parāyaṇam, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ dvīpaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitā mātā, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ pitā, ṣaṭ pāramitā jñānāya bodhāya anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye saṃvartante / tatkasya hetoḥ? atra hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā pariniṣṭhitā bhavati yaduta ṣaṭpāramitāsu / ye 'pi te subhūte atīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya parinirvṛtāḥ, teṣām api buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmitonirjātaiva sarvajñatā, yaduta ṣaḍbhyaḥ pāramitābhyaḥ / ye 'pi te subhūte bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante, teṣām api buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmitonirjātaiva sarvajñatā, yaduta ṣaḍbhyaḥ pāramitābhyaḥ / ye 'pi te subhūte aprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣvaparimāṇeṣvacintyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā etarhyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāstiṣṭhanti, dhriyante, yāpayanti, dharmaṃ ca deśayanti, teṣām api buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmitonirjātaiva sarvajñatā, yaduta ṣaḍbhyaḥ pāramitābhyaḥ / aham api subhūte tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha etarhyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / mamāpi hi subhūte itonirjātaiva sarvajñatā, yaduta ṣaḍbhyaḥ pāramitābhyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? āsu hi subhūte ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣā dharmā antargatāḥ, catvāro brahmavihārāḥ, catvāri saṃgrahavastūni / yāvāṃś ca kaścidbuddhadharmo buddhajñānaṃ svayaṃbhūjñānamacintyajñānamatulyajñānamaprameyajñānamasaṃkhyeyajñānamasamajñānamasamasamajñānaṃ sarvajñajñānam, sarvaṃ tat ṣaṭsu pāramitāsvantargatam / tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya ṣaṭ pāramitā eva kalyāṇamitrāṇi veditavyāni, ṣaḍeva pāramitāḥ śāstā, ṣaṭ pāramitā mārgaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitā ālokaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitā ulkā, ṣaṭ pāramitā avabhāsaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitāstrāṇam, ṣaṭ
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who has set out with deep resolve, wishing to fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, should from the very beginning attend upon, serve, and follow spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitras</s>)." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Who, O Blessed One, should be understood as the spiritual friends of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>—those whom a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who has set out with deep resolve, wishing to fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, should from the very beginning attend upon, serve, and follow?" When this was said, the Blessed One said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "The <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> themselves, <s>Subhūti</s>, and those irreversible (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who are skilled in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice, who instruct and advise him in the <s>pāramitās</s>, who teach and explain the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to him—these should be understood as the spiritual friends of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as the spiritual friend of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. And all six <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as the spiritual friends of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. The six <s>pāramitās</s> are the teacher; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the path; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the light; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the torch; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the illumination; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the protection; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the refuge; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the shelter; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the final resort; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the island; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the mother; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the father; the six <s>pāramitās</s> conduce to knowledge, to awakening, to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> comes to completion in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past who fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>—their <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) too arose from here, namely from the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who will fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in the future—their <s>sarvajñatā</s> too will arise from here, namely from the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who at present, in immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, inconceivable world-systems, have fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, abide, continue, sustain, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>—their <s>sarvajñatā</s> too arose from here, namely from the six <s>pāramitās</s>. I too, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, have at present fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. My <s>sarvajñatā</s> too, <s>Subhūti</s>, arose from here, namely from the six <s>pāramitās</s>. For what reason? Because within these six <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, the thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>) are included, the four divine abodes (<s>brahmavihāras</s>), the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastus</s>). And whatever <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>, <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, self-arising knowledge, inconceivable knowledge, incomparable knowledge, immeasurable knowledge, innumerable knowledge, unequalled knowledge, supremely unequalled knowledge, omniscient knowledge there is—all of that is included in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the six <s>pāramitās</s> alone should be understood as the spiritual friends of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>; the six <s>pāramitās</s> alone are the teacher; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the path; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the light; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the torch; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the illumination; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the protection; the six

body.text: pāramitāḥ śaraṇam, ṣaṭ pāramitā layanam, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ parāyaṇam, ṣaṭ pāramitā dvīpaḥ, ṣaṭ pāramitā mātā, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ pitā, ṣaṭ pāramitā jñānāya bodhāya sarvajñatāyai anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhiprāptaye saṃvartante / sarvasattvānāmapratyupakāriṇām api upakāribhūto bhavati, yadā bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ṣaṭpāramitāsu śikṣate //
body.translated_text: <s>pāramitās</s> are the refuge; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the shelter; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the final resort; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the island; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the mother; the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the father; the six <s>pāramitās</s> conduce to knowledge, to awakening, to <s>sarvajñatā</s>, to the attainment of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. He becomes a benefactor even to all beings who do not reciprocate, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in the six <s>pāramitās</s>."

body.text: āsu khalu punaḥ subhūte ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu śikṣitukāmena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena iyameva prajñāpāramitā śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā deśayitavyā upadeṣṭavyā uddeṣṭavyā svādhyātavyā, arthataś ca dharmataś ca nayataścopaparīkṣitavyā upanidhyātavyā paripraṣṭavyā paripraśnayitavyā / tatkasya hetoḥ? eṣā hi prajñāpāramitā ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ pūrvaṃgamā nāyikā pariṇāyikā saṃdarśikā avadarśikā janayitrī dhatrī / tatkasya hetoḥ? prajñāpāramitāvirahitā hi pañca pāramitā na prajñāyante, nāpi pāramitānāmadheyaṃ labhante / tasmāttarhi subhūte aparapraṇeyatāṃ gantukāmena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena aparapraṇeyatāyāṃ sthātukāmena ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam //
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> wishing to train in these six <s>pāramitās</s> should hear, take up, retain, recite, master, propagate, teach, explain, expound, study this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and should examine, investigate, and inquire into it in terms of its meaning, its <s>dharma</s>, and its method. For what reason? Because this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the forerunner, the guide, the leader, the shower, the revealer, the generator, and the nurse of the six <s>pāramitās</s>. For what reason? Because the five <s>pāramitās</s> without the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> are not recognized, nor do they receive the designation '<s>pāramitā</s>.' Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> wishing to reach the state of not being led by others and wishing to stand in that state of not being led by others should train right here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>."

body.text: subhūtirāha - kiṃlakṣaṇā bhagavan prajñāpāramitā? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - asaṅgalakṣaṇā subhūte prajñāpāramitā / subhūtirāha - syādbhagavan paryāyo yena paryāyeṇa yenaivāsaṅgalakṣaṇena prajñāpāramitā saṃvidyate, tenaiva asaṅgalakṣaṇena sarvadharmāḥ saṃvidyeran? bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / syātsubhūte paryāyo yena paryāyeṇa yenaiva asaṅgalakṣaṇena prajñāpāramitā saṃvidyate, tenaiva asaṅgalakṣaṇena sarvadharmāḥ saṃvidyante / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvadharmā hi subhūte viviktāḥ / sarvadharmā hi subhūte śūnyāḥ / tasmāttarhi subhūte yenaiva asaṅgalakṣaṇena prajñāpāramitā viviktā śūnyā, tenaiva asaṅgalakṣaṇena sarvadharmā viviktāḥ śūnyāḥ / subhūtirāha - yadi bhagavan sarvadharmā viviktāḥ, sarvadharmāḥ śūnyāḥ, kathaṃ bhagavan sattvānāṃ saṃkleśaḥ prajñāyate, kathaṃ bhagavan sattvānāṃ vyavadānaṃ prajñāyate? na ca bhagavan viviktaṃ saṃkliśyate, na bhagavan viviktaṃ vyavadāyati / na ca bhagavan śūnyaṃ saṃkliśyate, na ca bhagavan śūnyaṃ vyavadāyati / na ca bhagavan viviktaṃ vā śūnyaṃ vā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / anyatrāpi bhagavan śūnyatāyāḥ sarvadharmo nopalabhyate, yo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho vā, abhisaṃbhotsyate vā, abhisaṃbudhyate vā / kathaṃ vā vayaṃ bhagavan asya bhāṣitasyārthamājānīmaḥ? deśayatu bhagavan, deśayatu sugata / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase dīrgharātraṃ sattvā ahaṃkāre mamakāre caranti? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata / dīrgharātraṃ sattvā ahaṃkāre mamakāre caranti / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu ahaṃkāramamakārau śūnyau? subhūtirāha - śūnyau bhagavan, śūnyau sugata / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ahaṃkāreṇa mamakāreṇa ca sattvāḥ saṃsāre saṃsaranti? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata / ahaṃkāreṇa mamakāreṇa ca sattvāḥ saṃsāre saṃsaranti / bhagavānāha - evaṃ khalu subhūte sattvānāṃ saṃkleśaḥ prajñāyate / yathā sattvānāmudgraho 'bhiniveśaḥ, tathā saṃkleśaḥ / na cātra
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "What is the characteristic of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, O Blessed One?" When this was said, the Blessed One said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, has the characteristic of non-attachment (<s>asaṅga</s>)." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Could it be, O Blessed One, that by the very same characteristic of non-attachment by which the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> exists, by that very characteristic of non-attachment all <s>dharmas</s> also exist?" The Blessed One said: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. It could be, <s>Subhūti</s>, that by the very same characteristic of non-attachment by which the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> exists, by that very characteristic of non-attachment all <s>dharmas</s> also exist. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, are isolated. All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, are empty. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the very same characteristic of non-attachment by which the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is isolated and empty, by that very characteristic of non-attachment all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated and empty." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "If, O Blessed One, all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated, all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, how, O Blessed One, is the defilement of beings recognized? How, O Blessed One, is the purification of beings recognized? For, O Blessed One, what is isolated is not defiled; what is isolated, O Blessed One, is not purified. What is empty, O Blessed One, is not defiled; what is empty, O Blessed One, is not purified. Nor does what is isolated or empty fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Apart from <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), O Blessed One, no <s>dharma</s> is apprehended that has fully awakened, will fully awaken, or is fully awakening to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. How then are we to understand the meaning of this statement? May the Blessed One teach! May the <s>Sugata</s> teach!" When this was said, the Blessed One said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "What do you think—for a long time beings have been dwelling in ego-clinging (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, O Blessed One. So it is, O <s>Sugata</s>. For a long time beings have been dwelling in ego-clinging and possessiveness." The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—are ego-clinging and possessiveness empty?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "They are empty, O Blessed One. They are empty, O <s>Sugata</s>." The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—do beings wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> through ego-clinging and possessiveness?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, O Blessed One. So it is, O <s>Sugata</s>. Beings wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> through ego-clinging and possessiveness." The Blessed One said: "Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the defilement of beings is recognized. According to how beings grasp and cling, so is their defilement. Yet herein

body.text: kaścitsaṃkliśyate / yathā ca subhūte anudgaho 'nabhiniveśaḥ, tathā nāhaṃkāramamakārau prajñāyete / evaṃ khalu subhūte sarvasattvānāṃ vyavadānaṃ prajñāyate / yathā sattvānāmanudgraho 'nabhiniveśaḥ, tathā vyavadānam / na cātra kaścidvyavadāyati / evaṃ khalu subhūte caran bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām / evaṃ khalu subhūte sarvadharmeṣu vivikteṣu sarvadharmeṣu śūnyeṣu sattvānāṃ saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ ca prajñāyate / subhūtirāha - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvadyadidaṃ sarvadharmeṣu vivikteṣu sarvadharmeṣu śūnyeṣu sattvānāṃ saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ ca prajñāyate / evaṃ ca bhagavaṃścaran bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām / evaṃ hi caran bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na rūpe carati, na vedanāyāṃ na saṃjñāyāṃ na saṃskāreṣu, na vijñāne carati / evaṃ caran bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'navamardanīyo bhavati sadevamānuṣāsureṇa lokena / evaṃ caran bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarveṣāṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ pratyekabuddhayānikānāṃ ca pudgalānāṃ caryāmabhibhavati, anabhibhūtaṃ ca sthānaṃ pratilabhate / tatkasya hetoḥ? anabhibhūtaṃ hi bhagavan buddhatvaṃ tathāgatatvaṃ svayaṃbhūtvaṃ sarvajñatvam / anenāpi bhagavan manasikāreṇa prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktena vihāreṇa viharan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo rātriṃdinānyatināmayet, āsannaḥ syādanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeta / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / evaṃ caran subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām / evaṃ hi caran subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na rūpe carati, na vedanāyāṃ na saṃjñāyāṃ na saṃskāreṣu, na vijñāne carati / evaṃ caran subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'navamardanīyo bhavati sadevamānuṣāsureṇa lokena / evaṃ caran subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarveṣāṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ pratyekabuddhayānikānāṃ ca pudgalānāṃ caryāmabhibhavati, anabhibhūtaṃ ca sthānaṃ pratilabhate / tatkasya hetoḥ? anabhibhūtaṃ hi subhūte buddhatvaṃ tathāgatatvaṃ svayaṃbhūtvaṃ sarvajñatvam / anenāpi subhūte manasikāreṇa prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktena vihāreṇa viharan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo rātriṃdinānyatināmayet, āsannaḥ syādanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, kṣipraṃ ca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeta //
body.translated_text: no one is defiled. And, <s>Subhūti</s>, according to how there is non-grasping and non-clinging, so ego-clinging and possessiveness are not recognized. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the purification of all beings is recognized. According to how beings have non-grasping and non-clinging, so is their purification. Yet herein no one is purified. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, practicing in this way, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, while all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated and all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, the defilement and purification of beings is recognized." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "It is wonderful, O Blessed One, how, while all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated and all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, the defilement and purification of beings is recognized! Thus practicing, O Blessed One, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For one practicing thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not dwell in <s>rūpa</s> (form), not in <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), not in <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), not in <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), not in <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Practicing thus, O Blessed One, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> becomes invincible by the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Practicing thus, O Blessed One, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> surpasses the practice of all persons following the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, and attains the unconquered station. For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, <s>Buddha</s>-hood, <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood, self-arising nature, and <s>sarvajñatā</s> are unconquered. By this very attention (<s>manasikāra</s>), O Blessed One, dwelling in the abiding connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> would pass his days and nights, would be near to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, and would quickly fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>." When this was said, the Blessed One said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. Practicing thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For one practicing thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not dwell in <s>rūpa</s>, not in <s>vedanā</s>, not in <s>saṃjñā</s>, not in <s>saṃskāras</s>, not in <s>vijñāna</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> becomes invincible by the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> surpasses the practice of all persons following the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, and attains the unconquered station. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Buddha</s>-hood, <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood, self-arising nature, and <s>sarvajñatā</s> are unconquered. By this very attention, <s>Subhūti</s>, dwelling in the abiding connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> would pass his days and nights, would be near to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, and would quickly fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>."

body.text: sacetkhalu punaḥ subhūte ye jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ, te sarve 'pūrvācaramaṃ mānuṣyakamātmabhāvaṃ pratilabheran, mānuṣyakamātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayeran, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya yāvajjīvaṃ tiṣṭheyuḥ, yāvajjīvaṃ tiṣṭhanto yāvajjīvaṃ sarvatathāgatān satkuryurgurukuryurmānayeyuḥ pūjayeyurarcayeyurapacāyeyuḥ, evaṃ sarvasattvebhyo 'pi dānaṃ dadyuḥ, tacca dānamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayeyuḥ / tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasaveyuḥ? subhūtirāha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata / bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ subhūte sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati, yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'ntataḥ ekadivasam api prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairviharati /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, if all the beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> were for the first time to obtain a human existence, and having obtained a human existence were to generate the mind directed toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, and having generated that mind were to remain for their entire lifetime, and remaining for their entire lifetime were to honor, respect, esteem, worship, revere, and venerate all <s>Tathāgatas</s> for their whole lives, and were likewise to give gifts to all beings, and were to dedicate that gift in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>—what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, would those <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> generate much merit from that?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Much, O Blessed One! Much, O <s>Sugata</s>!" The Blessed One said: "Yet, <s>Subhūti</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family generates even more merit—that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who dwells in attentions connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for even a single day.

body.text: tatkasya hetoḥ? yathā yathā hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārai rātriṃdivaṃ viharati, tathā tathā sarvasattvānāṃ dakṣiṇīyatāṃ gacchati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi subhūte nāsti tadanyeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tādṛśaṃ maitrīsahagataṃ cittam, yathā tasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya, sthāpayitvā buddhān bhagavataḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? apratipudgalā hi subhūte tathāgatāḥ / nirupamā hi subhūte tathāgatāḥ / acintyadharmasamanvāgatā hi subhūte tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ //
body.translated_text: For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, in whatever way a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> dwells day and night with mental activities connected to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, in that very way he becomes worthy of offerings from all beings. For what reason? Because in that way—

body.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tāvattatpuṇyamabhinirharati? tādṛśyā subhūte prajñayā samanvāgataḥ sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhavati, yādṛśyā prajñayā samanvāgato vadhyagatāniva sarvasattvān paśyati / tena tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahākaruṇāparigṛhīto bhavati / sa divyena cakṣuṣā vyavalokayan aprameyānasaṃkhyeyānaparimeyānaparimāṇān sattvānānantaryakarmasamanvāgatān paśyati, akṣaṇaprāptāṃś ca vihanyamānāṃś ca dṛṣṭijālapraticchannāṃś ca mārgamapratilabhamānān / aparāṃś ca kṣaṇaprāptān paśyati, kṣaṇāṃś ca virāgayataḥ paśyati / tasya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahān saṃvega utpadyate / te cāsya sarvasattvāstayā mahāmaitryā tayā ca mahākaruṇayā sphāritvā manasikṛtā bhavanti - ahameteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ nātho bhaviṣyāmi, ahamenān sarvasattvān sarvaduḥkhebhyo mocayiṣyāmīti / na ca tena vā anyena vā nimittena sārdhaṃ saṃvasati / ayam api subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahān prajñāloko 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / anena hi subhūte vihāreṇa viharanto bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvalokasya dakṣiṇīyatāṃ parigṛhṇanti, na ca vivartante 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / yeṣāṃ ca dāyakānāṃ dānapatīnāṃ ca paribhuñjate cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān, asyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sūpasthitacittāḥ, teṣāṃ dāyakānāṃ dānapatīnāṃ ca dānadakṣiṇāṃ viśodhayanti / sarvajñatā caiṣāmāsannībhavati / tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena amoghaṃ rāṣṭraṃ piṇḍaṃ paribhoktukāmena sarvasattvānāṃ mārgamupadeṣṭukāmena vipulamavabhāsaṃ kartukāmena saṃsāragatān sattvān saṃsārātparimocayitukāmena sarvasattvānāṃ cakṣurviśodhayitukāmena anena prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktena manasikāreṇa vihartavyam / sacedanena manasikāreṇa vihartumicchati, tena prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktā manasikārāḥ samanvāhartavyāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yo hyenān samanvāhartavyān maṃsyate, sa evāsya manasikāro bhaviṣyati / tato 'nyeṣāṃ manasikārāṇāṃ prajñāpāramitāvirahitānāmavakāśo na dātavyaḥ / tathā ca kartavyaṃ yathāyaṃ prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārai rātriṃdivāni kṣapayet / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte kenacideva puruṣeṇa maṇiratnajñāne vartamānena maṇiratnajātijñena apratilabdhapūrvaṃ mahāmaṇiratnaṃ pratilabdhaṃ bhavet / sa tanmahāmaṇiratnaṃ pratilabhya mahatodāreṇa prītiprāmodyena samanvāgato bhavet / tasya tanmahāmaṇiratnaṃ punareva praṇaśyet / sa tatonidānaṃ mahatā duḥkhadaurmanasyena saṃyujyeta / tasya satatasamitaṃ tanmahāmaṇiratnaṃ prati saṃyuktā eva manasikārāḥ pravarteran - aho batāhaṃ tena
body.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does that son or daughter of good family produce that much merit? That <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is endowed with such wisdom that, with this wisdom, he [regards] all beings as if they were being led to execution—

body.text: mahāmaṇiratnena viprayukta iti hi sa puruṣastasya mahāmaṇiratnasya na vismaret yāvat tadvā anyadvā tadguṇaṃ tajjātikaṃ tena mahāmaṇiratnaṃ pratilabdhaṃ bhavet / evameva subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāmahāmaṇiratnaparibhraṣṭena mahāmaṇiratnaparibhraṣṭeneva mahāmaṇiratnena ratnasaṃjñinā prajñāpāramitāmanasikārāviprayuktena prajñāpāramitāmanasikārāvirahitasarvajñatācittena tāvadanveṣṭavyā, yāvatsā vā anyā vā pratilabdhā bhavati / tāvattena prajñāpāramitāmahāmaṇiratnapratilambhapratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ sarvajñatāmahāmaṇiratnapratilambhapratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairavirahitena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: "Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a man who loves his life, being led to the place of execution, has only one thought: 'How may I be freed? How may I be released?'—his mind goes nowhere else—

body.text: subhūtirāha - yatpunarbhagavan sarvadharmāḥ sarvamanasikārāḥ svabhāvena virahitāḥ śūnyā uktā bhagavatā, tatkathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ sarvajñatāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairavirahito bhavati? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sacetsubhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ manasi karoti - sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvena viviktāḥ, sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvena śūnyā iti, evametanmanasi kurvan prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ sarvajñatāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairavirahito bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? prajñāpāramitā hi subhūte śūnyā / sā naiva vivardhate, na ca parihīyate / subhūtirāha - sacedbhagavan prajñāpāramitā śūnyā, sā naiva vivardhate na ca parihīyate, kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'vivardhamānayā prajñāpāramitayā bodhaye samudāgacchati, kathaṃ ca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - na khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran vivardhate vā parihīyate vā / yathaiva subhūte prajñāpāramitā śūnyā, sā naiva vivardhate na ca parihīyate, evameva subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śūnyaḥ / sa naiva vivardhate, na ca parihīyate / yataḥ subhūte yathaiva prajñāpāramitā śūnyā, sā naiva vivardhate na ca parihīyate, evameva subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śūnyaḥ / sa naiva vivardhate, na ca parihīyate / tato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhaye samudāgacchati, evaṃ ca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / sacetsubhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ evaṃ bhāṣyamāṇe notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate na saṃsīdati, veditavyametatsubhūte caratyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāmiti //
body.translated_text: "So too, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, seeing beings burning in the fire of <s>saṃsāra</s>, thinks: 'How may these beings be liberated from this great suffering?'—his mind is settled only in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)—

body.text: subhūtirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan prajñāpāramitā carati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāhano hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan yā prajñāpāramitāyāḥ śūnyatā, sā carati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan anyatra prajñāpāramitāśūnyatāyāḥ sa kaściddharma upalabhyate, yaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan śūnyatā carati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan śūnyatāyāṃ sa kaściddharma upalabhyate yaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan śūnyatā carati śūnyatāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan rūpaṃ carati prajñāpāramitāyām?
body.translated_text: "Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who is a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend) of beings should be understood as the mother and father of all beings. Through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he generates great compassion—"

body.text: bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ, kiṃ punarbhagavan vijñānaṃ carati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan anyatra rūpātsa dharmaḥ kaścidupalabhyate, yaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / āha - kiṃ punarbhagavan anyatra vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārebhyaḥ, anyatra vijñānātsa dharmaḥ kaścidupalabhyate, yaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / subhūtirāha - kathaṃ punarbhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām? evamukte - bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kiṃ punaḥ subhūte samanupaśyasi tvaṃ taṃ dharmaṃ yaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - samanupaśyasi tvaṃ subhūte tāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ yatra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yo dharmo 'nupalambhaḥ, taṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyasi? api nu sa eva dharma utpanno vā utpatsyate vā utpadyate vā, niruddho vā nirotsyate vā nirudhyate vā? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - evaṃ khalu subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntirevaṃrūpā bhavati / evaṃrūpayā ca subhūte kṣāntyā samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vyākriyate 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / iyaṃ subhūte tathāgatasya vaiśāradyapratipad yāṃ pratipadyamāno bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ evaṃ caran evaṃ ghaṭamānaḥ evaṃ vyāyacchamāno 'nuttaraṃ buddhajñānaṃ sarvajñajñānaṃ mahāsārthavāhajñānaṃ nānuprāpsyatīti naitatsthānaṃ vidyate //
body.translated_text: "A <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> thinking: 'I am the refuge of all beings. I am the protector of all beings. I am the island of all beings. I am the leader of all beings. I am the caravan-guide of all beings. I am the resort of all beings'—"

body.text: subhūtirāha - yā bhagavan sarvadharmāṇāmanutpattikadharmatā, sā vyākriyate 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? bhagavānāha - no hīdaṃ subhūte / subhūtirāha - kathamasyedānīṃ bhagavan dharmasya vyākaraṇaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? bhagavānāha - kiṃ punaḥ subhūte samanupaśyasi tvaṃ taṃ dharmaṃ yasya dharmasya vyākaraṇaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / nāhaṃ bhagavaṃstaṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi yo dharmo vyākṛto vyākariṣyate vyākriyate vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tamapyahaṃ bhagavan dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi, yo dharmo 'bhisaṃbudhyate, yo dharmo 'bhisaṃboddhavyaḥ, yena vā dharmeṇābhisaṃbudhyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvadharmeṣu bhagavan anupalabhyamāneṣu na me evaṃ bhavati - ayaṃ dharmo 'bhisaṃbudhyate, ayaṃ dharmo 'bhisaṃboddhavyaḥ, anena vā dharmeṇābhisaṃbudhyate iti //
body.translated_text: "Thinking: 'I shall lead all beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Yet I do not lead them to a <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in which the <s>dharma</s>-element is destroyed.' Thus training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> becomes worthy of the offerings of all the world with its gods—"

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ kalyāṇamitraparivarto nāma dvāviṃśatitamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the Twenty-Second Chapter, called "The Chapter on Spiritual Friends," in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

body.text: ASP_23: śakraparivartastrayoviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Twenty-Three: The Chapter on <s>Śakra</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena śakro devānāmindrastasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatitaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt / atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - gambhīreyaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitā / durddaśā duranubodhā bateyaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitā / evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - evametatkauśika, evam etat / gambhīreyaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitā / durdṛśā duranubodhā bateyaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitā / ākāśagambhīratayā gambhīreyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / viviktatvāddurdṛśā / śūnyatvādduranubodheyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - na te bhagavan sattvā avarakeṇa kuśalamūlena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti ya imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyanti / śrutvā ca udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti pravartayiṣyanti deśayiṣyantyupadekṣyantyuddekṣyanti svādhyāsyanti likhiṣyanti / evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - evametatkauśika, evam etat / na te kauśika sattvā avarakeṇa kuśalamūlena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti, ya imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyanti / śrutvā codgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti pravartayiṣyanti deśayiṣyantyupadekṣyantyuddekṣyanti svādhyāsyanti likhiṣyanti / yāvantaḥ kauśika jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ, te sarve daśakuśalakarmapathasamanvāgatā bhaveyuḥ, tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu te sattvāstatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasaveyuḥ? śakra āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata / bhagavānāha - ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyati / śrutvā ca udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyatyupadekṣyatyuddekṣyati svādhyāsyati likhiṣyati / asya kauśika puṇyaskandhasya asau paurvakāṇāṃ jāmbūdvīpakānāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ śīlamayaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti / sahasratamīm api śatasahasratamīm api koṭītamīm api koṭīśatatamīm api koṭīsahasratamīm api koṭīśatasahasratamīm api koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti / saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām api upamām api aupamyam api upanisām api upaniṣadam api na kṣamate, yena kuśalamūlena sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā samanvāgato bhavati, ya imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyati / śrutvā codgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyatyupadekṣatyuddekṣyati svādhyāsyati likhiṣyati //
body.translated_text: Now at that time, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, had assembled and was seated in that very assembly. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: 'Profound, Blessed One, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. How difficult to see, how difficult to comprehend, Blessed One, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>!' When this was said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. Profound, <s>Kauśika</s>, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. How difficult to see, how difficult to comprehend, <s>Kauśika</s>, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. It is profound by the profundity of space. It is difficult to see because of its seclusion. It is difficult to comprehend because of its emptiness.' When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: 'Those beings, Blessed One, will not be endowed with inferior wholesome roots who will hear this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct in it, expound it, study it, and write it.' When this was said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. Those beings, <s>Kauśika</s>, will not be endowed with inferior wholesome roots who will hear this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct in it, expound it, study it, and write it. However many beings there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>—suppose they were all endowed with the ten wholesome courses of action. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would those beings thereby produce much merit?' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Yet that son or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, produces far more merit who will hear this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct in it, expound it, study it, and write it. The aggregate of merit based on morality of all those former beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, does not approach even a hundredth part of this aggregate of merit—not a thousandth, not a hundred-thousandth, not a <s>koṭi</s>th, not a hundred-<s>koṭi</s>th, not a thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th, not a hundred-thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th, not a <s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th part does it approach. It cannot bear comparison, fraction, calculation, analogy, illustration, simile, or elucidation—the wholesome root with which that son or daughter of good family is endowed who will hear this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct in it, expound it, study it, and write it.'

body.text: atha khalvanyataro bhikṣuḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - abhibhūto 'si kauśika tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā ya imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyati / śrutvā codgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyatyupadekṣyatyuddekṣyati svādhyāsyati likhiṣyati / evamukte śakro devānāmindrastaṃ bhikṣumetadavocat - ekacittotpādenaiva ahamārya tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā abhibhūtaḥ / kaḥ punarvādo ya imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyati / śrutvā ca udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati
body.translated_text: Then a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'You are surpassed, <s>Kauśika</s>, by that son or daughter of good family who will hear this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct in it, expound it, study it, and write it.' When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to that <s>bhikṣu</s>: 'By even a single production of the thought [of awakening], noble one, I am surpassed by that son or daughter of good family. How much more so by one who will hear this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it,

body.text: deśayiṣyatyupadekṣyatyuddekṣyati svādhyāsyati likhiṣyati / kaḥ punarvādo ye śrutvā udgṛhya dhārayitvā vācayitvā paryavāpya pravartya deśayitvopadiśyoddiśya svādhyāyya likhitvā tathatvāya śikṣiṣyante, tathatvāya pratipatsyante, tathatvāya yogamāpatsyante / te sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokamabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / na kevalaṃ te sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokamabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti, ye 'pi te srotaāpannāḥ sakṛdāgāmino 'nāgāmino 'rhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, tān api te sarvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / na kevalaṃ srotaāpannān sakṛdāgāmino 'nāgāmino 'rhataḥ pratyekabuddhānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti, ye 'pi te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahādānapatayaḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyavirahitāḥ, tān api te sarvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / na kevalaṃ tān mahādānapatīn bodhisattvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti, ye 'pi te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā pariśuddhaśīlā akhaṇḍena śīlaskandhenācchidreṇākalmaṣeṇa paripūrṇena pariśuddhena aśabalena śīlaskandhena samanvāgatāḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyavirahitāḥ, tān api te sarvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / na kevalamakhaṇḍenācchidreṇākalmaṣeṇa paripūrṇena pariśuddhena aśabalena śīlaskandhena samanvāgatān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti, ye 'pi te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kṣāntisaṃpannā upaśamasaṃpannā apratihatacittā antato dagdhasthūṇāyāmapyāghātacittaṃ notpādayanti prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyavirahitāḥ, tān api te sarvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / na kevalaṃ kṣāntisaṃpannānupaśamasaṃpannānapratihatacittān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti, ye 'pi te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ārabdhavīryā anikṣiptadhurā akusīdā anavalīnakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmāntāḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyavirahitāḥ, tān api te sarvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / na kevalamārabdhavīryānanikṣiptadhurānakusīdānanavalīnakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmāntān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti, ye 'pi te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā dhyānārāmā dhyānaratā dhyānabalino dhyānabalavanto dhyānapratiṣṭhitā dhyānavaśinaḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyavirahitāḥ, tān api te sarvānabhibhavanto gamiṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / yathānirdiṣṭāyāṃ hi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sadevamānuṣāsuralokaṃ sarvān śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikānanupāyakuśalāṃś ca bodhisattvān mahāsattvānabhibhavati, teṣāṃ cānabhibhūto bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? yo hi bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yathānirdiṣṭāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, prajñāpāramitāmanuvartate, ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñavaṃśasyānupacchedāya sthito bhavati / ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatān na dūrīkariṣyati / ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ pratipadyamāno nacirādgamiṣyati bodhimaṇḍam / ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ sattvān kleśapaṅke saṃsīdamānānuddhariṣyati / ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvaśikṣāyāṃ śikṣate, na śrāvakaśikṣāyāṃ śikṣate, na pratyekabuddhaśikṣāyāṃ śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaṃ ca prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ
body.translated_text: teach it, instruct in it, expound it, study it, and write it. How much more so those who, having heard, taken up, retained, recited, mastered, propagated, taught, instructed, expounded, studied, and written it, will train for suchness, will practice for suchness, will strive for suchness! Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> will go surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Not only will they go surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>—those <s>Srotaāpannas</s>, <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s>, <s>Anāgāmins</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, and Perfectly Awakened Ones too, all of them will they go surpassing, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Not only will they go surpassing the <s>Srotaāpannas</s>, <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s>, <s>Anāgāmins</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>—those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who are great lords of giving but are devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, all of them too will they go surpassing, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Not only will they go surpassing those great lords of giving among the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who are of purified morality, endowed with an unbroken, unblemished, unstained, complete, purified, unspotted aggregate of moral conduct, yet are devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, all of them too will they go surpassing, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Not only will they go surpassing the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> endowed with an unbroken, unblemished, unstained, complete, purified, unspotted aggregate of moral conduct—those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who are accomplished in patience, accomplished in tranquility, with unhindered mind, who do not produce a thought of hostility even toward a burnt stump, yet are devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, all of them too will they go surpassing, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Not only will they go surpassing the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> accomplished in patience, accomplished in tranquility, with unhindered mind—those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who have aroused vigor, who have not laid down their burden, who are not indolent, whose bodily, verbal, and mental actions are not withdrawn, yet are devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, all of them too will they go surpassing, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Not only will they go surpassing the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who have aroused vigor, who have not laid down their burden, who are not indolent, whose bodily, verbal, and mental actions are not withdrawn—those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who delight in <s>dhyāna</s>, who take pleasure in <s>dhyāna</s>, who have the power of <s>dhyāna</s>, who possess the strength of <s>dhyāna</s>, who are established in <s>dhyāna</s>, who have mastery over <s>dhyāna</s>, yet are devoid of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, all of them too will they go surpassing, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who practices in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as expounded surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, all those of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who are unskilled in means—and is unsurpassed by them. What is the reason? For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who practices in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as expounded, who follows the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> stands for the uninterrupted continuity of the lineage of the omniscient ones. This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> will not be far from the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, practicing thus, will before long go to the seat of awakening (<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>). This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, training thus, will lift up beings sinking in the mire of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, training thus, trains in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training, not in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> training, not in the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> training. And a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training thus in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,

body.text: catvāro lokapālā mahārājāna upasaṃkramyaivaṃ vakṣyanti - kṣipraṃ tvaṃ kulaputra asyāṃ bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ śikṣasva, laghu śikṣasva / imāni te catvāri pātrāṇi yāni tvayā bodhimaṇḍe niṣadya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhena pratigrahītavyānīti / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ yathānirdiṣṭāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ na kevalaṃ catvāro lokapālā mahārājāna upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante, aham api bhagavaṃstaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamupasaṃkramiṣyāmi, kaḥ punarvādastadanye devaputrāḥ / tathāgatair api so 'rhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairnityameva samanvāhṛto bhaviṣyati bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / evaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya yāni kānicillaukikāni duḥkhāni paropakramikāṇi vā anyāni vā utpadyeran, tānyasya sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ notpatsyante / ayam api bhagavan dṛṣṭadhārmiko guṇastasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato bhavati //
body.translated_text: the four world-protectors, the great kings (<s>Lokapāla Mahārāja</s>), will approach and say: 'Quickly, son of good family, train in this <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct! Train swiftly! These are your four bowls which, having sat at the seat of awakening and having awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, you are to accept.' And not only will the four world-protectors, the great kings, consider the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training thus in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as expounded worthy of approach—I too, Blessed One, will approach that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>; how much more so other <s>devaputras</s>! And that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> will always be watched over by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones too. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practicing thus in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, whatever worldly sufferings might arise—whether from the aggression of others or from any other cause—will absolutely not arise at all. This too, Blessed One, is a benefit visible in this very life for that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmata ānandasyaitadabhavat - kimayaṃ śakro devānāmindraḥ svakena pratibhānena bhāṣate, utāho buddhānubhāveneti? atha khalu buddhānubhāvena śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmata ānandasya cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya āyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - buddhānubhāvo 'yamāryānanda veditavyaḥ, buddhādhiṣṭhānamidam api āryānanda veditavyam, apratibalo hyahamāryānanda bodhisattvān mahāsattvānārabhya vyāhartum / atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma - evametadānanda, evam etat yathā śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa bhāṣitam / tathāgatasyaiṣo 'nubhāvaḥ, tathāgatasyaitadadhiṣṭhānam, yacchakreṇa devānāmindreṇa bhāṣitamiti //
body.translated_text: Then it occurred to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Does this <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, speak through his own eloquence, or through the <s>Buddha</s>'s power?' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s power, having known with his mind the thought in the mind of the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'This should be known, noble <s>Ānanda</s>, as the <s>Buddha</s>'s power. This too, noble <s>Ānanda</s>, should be known as the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment. For I am not able, noble <s>Ānanda</s>, to speak with reference to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> [on my own].' Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is, just as <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, has spoken. This is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s power; this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment, that <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, has spoken thus.'

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śakraparivarto nāma trayoviṃśatitamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the twenty-third chapter, called 'The Chapter on <s>Śakra</s>,' in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: ASP_24: abhimānaparivartaścaturviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Twenty-four of the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>: The Twenty-fourth Chapter on Conceit.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapyāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma - yasmin khalu punarānanda samaye bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣate, prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyate, prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati, tasmin ānanda samaye ye trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau mārāḥ pāpīyāṃsaḥ, te sarve saṃśayitā bhavanti - kimayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'ntarā bhūtakoṭiṃ sākṣātkariṣyati śrāvakabhūmau vā pratyekabuddhabhūmau vā, utāho anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate iti / punaraparamānanda tasmin samaye mārāḥ pāpīyāṃsaḥ śokaśalyaviddhā bhavanti yasmin samaye bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa viharati / punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyate, prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati, tasmin samaye mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya viheṭhāmupasaṃharanti, bhayaṃ saṃjanayanti, ulkāpātān diśi diśyutsṛjanti, digdāhānupadarśayanti - apyeva nāma ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'valīyeta vā romaharṣo vā asya bhavet, yenāsyaikacittotpādo 'pi kṣīyeta anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodheriti / tatra ānanda na sarvasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃkrāmati viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ, api tu kasyacidupasaṃkrāmati, kasyacinnopasaṃkrāmati //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'At whatever time, <s>Ānanda</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, applies himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivates the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—at that time, <s>Ānanda</s>, all the evil <s>Māras</s> in the three-thousand-fold great world-system are filled with doubt: "Will this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> prematurely realize the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) on the <s>Śrāvaka</s> level or the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> level, or will he awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>?" Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at that time the evil <s>Māras</s> are pierced by the dart of sorrow whenever the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> dwells in the abiding of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at whatever time the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, applies himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivates the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—at that time the evil <s>Māras</s> bring harassment upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, generate fear, hurl meteor showers in every direction, display conflagrations in every quarter—thinking: 'Perhaps this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> will shrink back, or his hair will stand on end, so that even a single production of thought toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> might be destroyed in him!' But there, <s>Ānanda</s>, the evil <s>Māra</s> does not approach every <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> with the intention of harassment; rather, he approaches some and does not approach others.

body.text: ānanda āha - kiyadrūpasya bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya upasaṃkrāmati māraḥ pāpīyān viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ? bhagavānāha - yena ānanda bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pūrvāntataḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāmadhimukticittaṃ notpāditaṃ bhavati, asya ānanda bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃkrāmati viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ, avatāraṃ cāsya labhate //
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said: What kind of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does <s>Māra</s> the Evil One approach with the intention to harass? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: That <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, who in former times has not generated the mind of conviction when <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> was being taught—<s>Māra</s> the Evil One approaches this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, with the intention to harass, and he finds an opening against him.

body.text: punaraparamānanda yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ saṃśayaprāpto bhavati, vimatimutpādayati - syādveyaṃ prajñāpāramitā, evaṃ na vā syāditi, asyāpyānanda bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃkrāmati viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ, avatāraṃ cāsya labhate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, when the profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being taught, becomes seized by doubt and generates uncertainty—'Could this be <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, or could it not be so?'—<s>Māra</s> the Evil One also approaches this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, with the intention to harass, and he finds an opening against him.

body.text: punaraparamānanda yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kalyāṇamitravirahito bhavati, pāpamitraparigṛhītaś ca bhavati, sa gambhīrāṇi gambhīrāṇi sthānāni prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ na śṛṇoti, aśṛṇvanna jānāti, ajānanna paripṛcchati - kathaṃ prajñāpāramitā bhāvayitavyeti, asyāpyānanda bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃkrāmati viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ, avatāraṃ cāsya labhate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is devoid of a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend) and is under the influence of evil friends—he does not hear the profound, very profound passages when <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being taught; not hearing, he does not understand; not understanding, he does not inquire: 'How should <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> be cultivated?'—<s>Māra</s> the Evil One also approaches this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, with the intention to harass, and he finds an opening against him.

body.text: punaraparamānanda yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'saddharmaparigrāhakamālīno bhavati - eṣa mama sahāyakaḥ, sarvārtheṣu māṃ na parityajati, bahavo 'pi bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mamānye 'pi sahāyakāḥ santi / na ca punaste mamābhiprāyaṃ paripūrayanti / ayaṃ tu mayā pratirūpaḥ sahāyo labdhaḥ / ayaṃ mamābhiprāyaṃ paripūrayiṣyati / asyāpyānanda bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃkrāmati viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ, avatāraṃ cāsya labhate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> becomes attached to one who upholds the false <s>Dharma</s>, thinking: 'This one is my companion; he does not abandon me in any matter. Although there are many other <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are my companions, they do not fulfill my intentions. But I have found a suitable companion in this one. This one will fulfill my intentions.'—<s>Māra</s> the Evil One also approaches this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, with the intention to harass, and he finds an opening against him.

body.text: punaraparamānanda yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'syāṃ gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāmanyaṃ bodhisattvamevaṃ vadet - gambhīrā bateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / kiṃ tavainayā śrutayā? na hyevamatra yujyamānamanyeṣu sūtrānteṣu yathā tathāgatena bhāṣitam / ahamapyasyāmagādhamāsvādaṃ na labhe / kiṃ tavainayā śrutayā likhitayā veti? evamanyān api bodhisattvān mahāsattvān vivecayate / asyāpyānanda bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃkrāmati viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ, avatāraṃ cāsya labhate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, when this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being taught, says to another <s>bodhisattva</s>: 'This <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is indeed profound! What use is hearing it for you? For what is presented here does not accord with what the <s>Tathāgata</s> has taught in other <s>sūtras</s>. Even I cannot fathom its depth. What use is hearing or writing it for you?'—thus he also alienates other <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. <s>Māra</s> the Evil One also approaches this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, with the intention to harass, and he finds an opening against him.

body.text: punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nyān bodhisattvānavamanyate - ahaṃ vivekavihāreṇa viharāmi, nānye vivekavihāreṇa viharanti, nānyeṣāṃ vivekavihārāḥ saṃvidyante iti / tasminnānanda samaye māraḥ pāpīyāṃstuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhavati, saṃharṣajāto harṣitacittaḥ prītiprāmodyajāto bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? dūrīkarotyeṣo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimiti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> looks down upon other <s>bodhisattvas</s>, thinking: 'I dwell in solitary practice, others do not dwell in solitary practice; solitary practices are not found among others'—at that time, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One becomes pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, filled with happiness and gladness, filled with delight and exhilaration. Why is that? Because this one is distancing himself from unsurpassed perfect awakening.
