body.text: punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmagrahaṇaṃ vā gotragrahaṇaṃ vā dhutaguṇaparikīrtanaṃ vā bhavati, evaṃ sa tāvanmātrakeṇa tato 'nyān bodhisattvān mahāsattvān peśalān kalyāṇadharmaṇo 'vamanyate / te ca tasya guṇā na saṃvidyante, ye 'vinivartanīyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratāṃ guṇāḥ, te ākārāstāni liṅgāni tāni nimittāni tasya na saṃvidyante / so 'saṃvidyamāneṣvavinivartanīyaguṇeṣu kleśamutpādayati, yaduta ātmānamutkrośayati, parān paṃsayati - na khalvete teṣu dharmeṣu saṃdṛśyante, yatrāhaṃ saṃdṛśya iti / tatra mārāṇāṃ pāpīyasāmevaṃ bhavati - na śūnyāni mārabhavanāni bhaviṣyanti, utsadāni bhaviṣyanti / mahānirayāstiryañcaḥ pretaviṣayā āsurāś ca kāyā utsadā bhaviṣyantīti / tathā ca māraḥ pāpīyānadhiṣṭhāsyati, yathā te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā evaṃ pravṛttā adhyākrāntā lābhasatkāreṇa bhaviṣyanti, ādeyavacanāś ca bhaviṣyanti / te tayā ādeyavacanatayā bahujanaṃ grāhayiṣyanti / teṣāṃ ca sa mahājanaḥ śrotavyaṃ śraddhātavyaṃ maṃsyate / te dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca teṣāmanukṛtimāpatsyante / te dṛṣṭaśrutānukṛtimāpadyamānā na tathatvāya śikṣiṣyante, na tathatvāya pratipatsyante, na tathatvāya yogamāpatsyante / evaṃ te na tathatāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā na tathatāyāṃ pratipadyamānā na tathatāyāṃ yogamāpadyamānāḥ saṃkleśaṃ vivardhayiṣyanti / evaṃ te viparyastayā cittasaṃtatyā yadyadeva karma ārapsyante kāyena vā vācā vā manasā vā, tatsarvamanirdiṣṭatvāya akāntatvāya apriyatvāya amanaāpatvāya saṃvartsyate / evaṃ te mahānirayā utsadā bhaviṣyanti, tiryañcaḥ pretaviṣayā āsurāś ca kāyāḥ, mārabhavanāni cotsadāni bhaviṣyanti / imamapyānanda arthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyan māraḥ pāpīyāṃstuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is praised by name, by lineage, or by proclamation of his <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities), and by just that much he looks down upon other <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are gentle and of wholesome character—and he does not possess those qualities that belong to irreversible <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; those aspects, those marks, those signs are not found in him—and lacking those qualities of irreversibility, he generates <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), namely, he exalts himself and disparages others, saying: 'Surely these others are not seen in those <s>dharmas</s> in which I am seen.' Thereupon the Evil <s>Māras</s> think thus: 'The abodes of <s>Māra</s> will not be empty; they will be full. The great hells, the animal realms, the hungry ghost realms, and the <s>asura</s> hosts will be full.' And <s>Māra</s> the Evil One will so influence them that those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, thus disposed, will be overwhelmed by gain and honor, and their words will be accepted. Through that acceptance of their words, they will lead many people. And those many people will consider their words worthy of hearing and believing. Seeing and hearing them, they will follow their example. Following the example of what they have seen and heard, they will not train in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), will not practice in accordance with <s>tathatā</s>, will not apply themselves to <s>tathatā</s>. Thus, not training in <s>tathatā</s>, not practicing in accordance with <s>tathatā</s>, not applying themselves to <s>tathatā</s>, they will increase defilement. Thus, with a perverted stream of mind, whatever action they undertake with body, speech, or mind, all of it will conduce to what is undetermined, undesirable, displeasing, and disagreeable. Thus the great hells will be full, the animal realms, the hungry ghost realms, the <s>asura</s> hosts, and the abodes of <s>Māra</s> will be full. Seeing this advantage too, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One becomes pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with happiness and gladness.

body.text: punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śrāvakayānikena pudgalena sārdhaṃ kalahāyati vivadati vigṛhṇīte ākrośet paribhāṣeta vyāpadyeta doṣamutpādayati, tasmin
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> quarrels, disputes, argues, reviles, abuses, becomes hostile toward, and generates ill-will against a person of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle—at that time—

body.text: samaye mārasya pāpīyasa evaṃ bhavati - dūrīkariṣyati batāyaṃ kulaputraḥ sarvajñatām, atidūre sthāsyati sarvajñatāyāḥ sacetpunarbodhisattvayānikaḥ pudgalo 'nyena bodhisattvayānikena pudgalena sārdhaṃ kalahāyati vivadati vigṛhṇīte ākrośati paribhāṣate vyāpadyate doṣamutpādayati, tatra māraḥ pāpīyān bhūyasyā mātrayā tuṣṭo bhavati, udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhavati / evaṃ cāsya bhavati - ubhāvapyetau bodhisattvau dūre sthāsyataḥ sarvajñatāyā iti //
body.translated_text: —<s>Māra</s> the Evil One thinks thus: 'This son of good family will distance himself from <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience); he will stand far from <s>sarvajñatā</s>.' And if a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle quarrels, disputes, argues, reviles, abuses, becomes hostile toward, and generates ill-will against another person of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One becomes even more pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with happiness and gladness. And he thinks thus: 'Both these <s>bodhisattvas</s> will stand far from <s>sarvajñatā</s>.'

body.text: punaraparamānanda yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vyākṛto 'vyākṛtena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sārdhaṃ kalahāyet vivadet vigṛhṇīyāt ākrośet paribhāṣeta vyāpadyeta doṣamutpādayet, cittaṃ cāghātayet, tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena cittotpāde tāvata eva kalpān saṃnāhaḥ saṃnāhyaḥ, sacedasyāparityaktā sarvajñatā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, if a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has been predicted quarrels, disputes, argues, reviles, abuses, becomes hostile toward, and generates ill-will against an unpredicted <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, and vexes his mind—that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> must don the armor for as many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) as the number of those mind-moments, if his <s>sarvajñatā</s> has not been abandoned.

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - asti bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ cittotpādānāṃ kiṃcinniḥsaraṇam, utāho tāvata eva kalpānavaśyaṃ tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena saṃnāhaḥ saṃnahyaḥ? bhagavānāha - saniḥsaraṇamānanda mayā dharmo deśitaḥ śrāvakayānikānāṃ pratyekabuddhayānikānāṃ bodhisattvayānikānāṃ ca pudgalānām / tatra ānanda yo 'yaṃ bodhisattvayānikaḥ pudgalo bodhisattvayānikena pudgalena sārdhaṃ kalahāyitvā vivaditvā vigṛhya ākruśya paribhāṣya vyāpadya doṣamutpādya na pratideśayati, nāyatyāṃ saṃbarāya pratipadyate, anuśayaṃ vahati, anuśayabaddho viharati, nāhamānanda tasya pudgalasya niḥsaraṇaṃ vadāmi / avaśyaṃ tena ānanda pudgalena punareva tāvata eva kalpān saṃnāhaḥ saṃnahyaḥ / yaḥ punarānanda bodhisattvayānikaḥ pudgalo bodhisattvayānikena pudgalena sārdhaṃ kalahāyitvā vivaditvā vigṛhya ākruśya paribhāṣya vyāpadya doṣamutpādya pratideśayati, pratideśya āyatyāṃ saṃvarāya pratipadyate, evaṃ ca cittamutpādayati - yena mayā sarvasattvānāṃ vigrahā vivādā virodhā utsārayitavyā nidhyāpayitavyāḥ praśamayitavyāḥ, so 'haṃ nāma svayameva vivadāmi / lābhā me durlabdhā na sulabdhāḥ, yo 'haṃ jalpite pratijalpāmi / yena mayā sarvasattvānāṃ saṃkramabhūtena bhavitavyam, so 'haṃ pareṣu tvamity api vācaṃ bhāṣe, paruṣaṃ vā karkaśaṃ vā prativaco dadāmi / idam api mayā naiva vaktavyam / jaḍasadṛśena eḍamūkasamena mayā kalahavigrahavivādeṣu bhavitavyam, parato duruktāni durāgatāni durbhāṣitāni bhāṣyamāṇāni śṛṇvatā cittaṃ nāghātayitavyam / pareṣāmantike na mamaitatsādhu, na caitanmamāṃ pratirūpam, yo 'haṃ parasya doṣāntaraṃ saṃjāne / etad api me na pratirūpam, yadahaṃ pareṣa doṣāntaram api śrotavyaṃ manye / tatkasya hetoḥ? na mayā adhyāśayo vikopayitavyaḥ, yena mayā sarvasattvāḥ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sukhayitavyāḥ, parinirvāpayitavyāś ca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya, sa nāmāhaṃ vyāpadye / na ca mayā svaparāddheṣv api pareṣu vyāpattavyam / sa nāmāhaṃ kṣobhaṃ gacchāmi / idaṃ mayā na karaṇīyam / dṛḍhaparākramatayā parākrāntavyam / na ca mayā jīvitāntarāye 'pi kriyamāṇe kṣobhaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, na bhrukuṭirmukhe utpādayitavyeti / asyāhamānanda
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is there any escape from those mind-moments, or must that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> necessarily don the armor for that many <s>kalpas</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: I have taught the <s>Dharma</s> as having an escape, <s>Ānanda</s>, for persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle. In that regard, <s>Ānanda</s>, if a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, having quarreled, disputed, argued, reviled, abused, become hostile toward, and generated ill-will against a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, does not confess it, does not undertake restraint for the future, carries resentment, and dwells bound by resentment—I do not speak of an escape for that person, <s>Ānanda</s>. That person, <s>Ānanda</s>, must necessarily don the armor again for that many <s>kalpas</s>. But, <s>Ānanda</s>, if a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, having quarreled, disputed, argued, reviled, abused, become hostile toward, and generated ill-will against a person of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, confesses it, and having confessed, undertakes restraint for the future, and generates this thought: 'I who should remove, pacify, and settle the quarrels, disputes, and conflicts of all beings—I myself now quarrel! My gains are ill-gained, not well-gained, that I talk back when spoken to. I who should become a bridge for all beings—I even speak the word "you" to others, or give harsh and rough replies! I should not even say this. I should be like one who is dull, like one who is mute, in quarrels, conflicts, and disputes; when hearing ill-spoken, ill-approached, ill-expressed words from others, I should not vex my mind. It is not good for me before others, nor is it fitting for me, that I should recognize a fault in another. This too is not fitting for me, that I should think another's fault is even worth hearing about. Why is that? I should not corrupt my resolve. I who should make all beings happy with all provisions of happiness, and who should lead them to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening—I become hostile! I should not even become hostile toward others who are at fault. I who get agitated—this I should not do. I should exert myself with firm effort. Even when my life is being endangered, I should not become agitated, nor should I produce a frown on my face.' For this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>—

body.text: bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya niḥsaraṇaṃ vadāmi / evaṃ cānanda bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śrāvakayānikānām api pudgalānāmantike sthātavyam, yathā na kasyacitsattvasyāntike kṣubhyeta, evameva ca sarvasattvānāmantike sthātavyam / kathaṃ cānanda bodhisattvena mahāsattvena apareṣāṃ bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pudgalānāmantike sthātavyam? tadyathāpi nāma ānanda śāstari / ete mama bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ śāstāra ityevaṃ sthātavyam / ekayānasamārūḍhā bateme mama bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, ekamārgasamārūḍhā bateme mama bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, samānābhiprāyā bateme mama bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, samayānasaṃprasthitā bateme mama bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ / yatraibhiḥ śikṣitavyam, tatra mayā śikṣitavyam / yathaiva caibhiḥ śikṣitavyam, tathaiva mayā śikṣitavyam / sacetpunareṣāṃ kaścidvyavakīrṇavihāreṇa vihariṣyati, na mayā vyavakīrṇavihāreṇa vihartavyam / sacetpunarete 'vyavakīrṇavihāreṇa vihariṣyanti sarvajñatāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ, mayāpyevaṃ śikṣitavyam / evaṃ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya ānanda bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya antarāyo na bhavatyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, kṣipraṃ ca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate iti //
body.translated_text: —I speak of an escape. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should conduct himself even toward persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle so that he is not disturbed toward any being whatsoever, and he should conduct himself just so toward all beings. And how, <s>Ānanda</s>, should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> conduct himself toward other persons of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle? Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, toward a teacher. He should regard them thus: 'These <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> are my teachers. These <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> have mounted the same vehicle as I. These <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> have set out on the same path as I. These <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> share the same aspiration as I. These <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> have set forth on the same journey as I. Where they must train, there I must train. Just as they must train, so must I train. If any among them dwells in undisciplined conduct, I should not dwell in undisciplined conduct. If they dwell in disciplined conduct with mental applications connected to <s>sarvajñatā</s>, I too should train in this way.' For a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> training thus in <s>sarvajñatā</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is no obstacle to unsurpassed perfect awakening, and he quickly attains unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmabhimānaparivarto nāma caturviṃśatitamaḥ //
body.translated_text: The twenty-fourth chapter, named the Chapter on Conceit, in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: ASP_25: śikṣāparivartaḥ pañcaviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: ASP Chapter 25: The Twenty-fifth Chapter on Training.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - kva punarbhagavan śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate? bhagavānāha - sacetsubhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣaye śikṣate, sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate / evamanutpāde 'nirodhe 'jātau abhāve viveke virāge ākāśe dharmadhātau / sacetsubhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo nirvāṇe śikṣate, sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate / subhūtirāha - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣaye śikṣamāṇaḥ śikṣate sarvajñatāyām, evamanutpāde 'nirodhe 'jātau abhāve viveke virāge ākāśe dharmadhātau nirvāṇe śikṣamāṇaḥ śikṣate sarvajñatāyām? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - yatsubhūte evaṃ vadasi - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣaye śikṣamāṇaḥ śikṣate sarvajñatāyām / evamanutpāde 'nirodhe 'jātau abhāve viveke virāge ākāśe dharmadhātau nirvāṇe śikṣamāṇaḥ śikṣate sarvajñatāyāmiti? tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yā tathāgatasya tathatā yayā tathatayā tathāgatastathāgata iti prabhāvyate, api nu sā kṣīyate? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi bhagavan kṣayaḥ kṣīyate / akṣayo hi bhagavan kṣayaḥ / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yā tathāgatasya tathatā yayā tathatayā tathāgatastathāgata iti prabhāvyate, api nu sā utpadyate vā nirudhyate vā jāyate vā bhavati vā vibhavati vā vivicyate vā rajyate vā virajyate vā ākāśībhavati vā dharmībhavati vā? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yā tathāgatasya tathatā yayā tathatayā tathāgatastathāgata iti prabhāvyate, api nu sā nirvāti? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tasmāttarhi subhūte evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ na tathatā kṣīyate ityevaṃ śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śikṣate sarvajñatāyām / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śikṣate prajñāpāramitāyām, śikṣate buddhabhūmau, śikṣate baleṣu, śikṣate vaiśāradyeṣu, śikṣate sarvabuddhadharmeṣu, śikṣate sarvajñajñāne / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvaśikṣāpāramitāmanuprāpsyati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na śakyo māreṇa vā māraparṣadā vā mārakāyikābhirvā devatābhirabhimarditum / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣipramavinivartanīyadharmatāmanuprāpsyati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣipraṃ bodhimaṇḍe niṣatsyati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svake gocare carati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śikṣate nāthakarakeṣu dharmeṣu, śikṣate mahāmaitryām, mahākaruṇāyāṃ śikṣate, mahāmuditāyāṃ śikṣate, mahopekṣāyāṃ śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śikṣate triparivartasya dvādaśākārasya dharmacakrasya pravartanāya / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvadhātuṃ nonīkariṣyāmīti śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatavaṃśasyānupacchedāya śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'mṛtadhātudvāraṃ vivariṣyāmīti śikṣate / neyaṃ subhūte udārā
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Training in what, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> train in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains in cessation, he trains in <s>sarvajñatā</s>. Likewise in non-arising, non-cessation, the unborn, non-existence, seclusion, dispassion, space, and <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of reality). If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, he trains in <s>sarvajñatā</s>.' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'For what reason, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> training in cessation train in <s>sarvajñatā</s>—likewise training in non-arising, non-cessation, the unborn, non-existence, seclusion, dispassion, space, <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'As to your question, <s>Subhūti</s>—"for what reason does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> training in cessation train in <s>sarvajñatā</s>, likewise training in non-arising, non-cessation, the unborn, non-existence, seclusion, dispassion, space, <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>?"—what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>: the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by which <s>tathatā</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s> is proclaimed as "<s>Tathāgata</s>"—does it undergo cessation?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. Why is that? For cessation does not undergo cessation, <s>Bhagavān</s>. Cessation is indeed inexhaustible, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>: the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by which <s>tathatā</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s> is proclaimed as "<s>Tathāgata</s>"—does it arise, or cease, or be born, or come into being, or perish, or become secluded, or become passionate, or become dispassionate, or become space, or become <s>dharma</s>?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>: the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by which <s>tathatā</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s> is proclaimed as "<s>Tathāgata</s>"—does it attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>?' He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, training thus, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains [knowing] that <s>tathatā</s> does not undergo cessation. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains in <s>sarvajñatā</s>. Training thus, he trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, trains in the <s>Buddha</s> stage, trains in the powers (<s>bala</s>), trains in the confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), trains in all <s>Buddha</s> qualities, trains in the knowledge of omniscience (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>). Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> will attain the perfection of all trainings. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> cannot be crushed by <s>Māra</s>, by <s>Māra</s>'s assembly, or by <s>Māra</s>'s host of deities. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> will quickly attain the state of irreversibility. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> will quickly sit at the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening). Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> moves in his own domain. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains in qualities that provide refuge, trains in great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), trains in great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), trains in great joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), trains in great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>). Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains for the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (wheel of <s>Dharma</s>) with three turnings and twelve aspects. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains [thinking]: "I shall empty all realms." Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains for the uninterrupted continuation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lineage. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains [thinking]: "I shall open the gate of the deathless element (<s>amṛtadhātu</s>)." This exalted

śikṣā śakyā hīnasattvena śikṣitum / na hi alpasthāmnā śakyamasyāṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣitum / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvasattvasārā hi te subhūte, sarvasattvanāthakāmā hi te subhūte, ye 'syāṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣante / sarvasattvābhyudgatatāṃ te 'nuprāptukāmāḥ, ya iha śikṣante / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na nirayeṣūpapadyate, na tiryagyoniṣūpapadyate, na pretaviṣayeṣūpapadyate, nāsureṣu kāyeṣūpapadyate, na pratyantajanapadeṣūpapadyate, na caṇḍālakuleṣūpapadyate, na śākunikakuleṣūpapadyate, na niṣādadhīvaraurabhrikakuleṣūpapadyate, nāpyanyeṣvevaṃrūpeṣu hīnajātikeṣu hīnakarmaseviṣu vā kuleṣūpapadyate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo nāndho bhavati, na badhiro bhavati, na kāṇo bhavati, na kuṇṭho bhavati, na kubjo bhavati, na kuṇirbhavati, na laṅgo bhavati, na khañjo bhavati, na jaḍo bhavati, na lolo bhavati, na lollo bhavati, na kallo bhavati, na hīnāṅgo bhavati, na vikalāṅgo bhavati, na vikṛtāṅgo bhavati, na durbalo bhavati, na durvarṇo bhavati, na duḥsaṃsthāno bhavati, na hīnendriyo bhavati, na vikalendriyo bhavati / sarvākāraparipūrṇendriyo bhavati, svarasaṃpanno bhavati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na prāṇātipātī bhavati, nādattādāyī bhavati, na kāmamithyācārī bhavati, na mṛṣāvādī bhavati, na piśunavāgbhavati, na paruṣavāgbhavati, na saṃbhinnapralāpī bhavati, nābhidhyālurbhavati, na vyāpannacitto bhavati, na mithyādṛṣṭiko bhavati, na mithyājīvena jīvikāṃ kalpayati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na dīrghāyuṣkeṣu deveṣūpapadyate, na duḥśīlaparigrāhako bhavati, nābhūtadharmaparigrāhako bhavati, na dhyānasamāpattivaśenopapadyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? asti hi tasyopāyakauśalyaṃ yenopāyakauśalyena samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na dīrghāyuṣkeṣu deveṣūpapadyate / tatpunaḥ subhūte upāyakauśalyaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya katamat? yaduta iyameva prajñāpāramitā / tathā ca atropāyakauśalye yogamāpadyate, yathā anyenopāyakauśalyena samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dhyānāni ca samāpadyate, na ca dhyānavaśenopapadyate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo balapariśuddhiṃ nigacchati, vaiśāradyapariśuddhiṃ nigacchati,
sarvabuddhadharmapariśuddhiṃ nigacchati, tāmanuprāpnoti //
body.translated_text: training, <s>Subhūti</s>, cannot be trained in by an inferior being. For one of little strength cannot train in this training. Why is that? For those, <s>Subhūti</s>, who train in this training are the essence of all beings; those, <s>Subhūti</s>, wish to be the protector of all beings. Those who train here wish to attain the state of surpassing all beings. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not reborn in hells, is not reborn in animal realms, is not reborn in the domain of hungry ghosts, is not reborn in <s>asura</s> bodies, is not reborn in border regions, is not reborn in outcaste families, is not reborn in fowler families, is not reborn in families of hunters, fishermen, or butchers, nor is he reborn in other such families of low birth or engaged in low occupations. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not blind, not deaf, not one-eyed, not lame, not hunchbacked, not crippled-handed, not limping, not halting, not dull, not unsteady, not stammering, not mute, not deficient in limbs, not deformed in limbs, not misshapen in limbs, not weak, not ill-colored, not ill-formed, not deficient in faculties, not impaired in faculties. He is complete in all faculties, endowed with a beautiful voice. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not kill living beings, does not take what is not given, does not engage in sexual misconduct, does not speak falsehood, does not speak divisively, does not speak harshly, does not engage in idle chatter, is not covetous, is not malicious in mind, does not hold wrong views, does not sustain livelihood by wrong livelihood. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not reborn among the long-lived gods, does not embrace immoral conduct, does not embrace false <s>dharmas</s>, and is not reborn through the power of <s>dhyāna</s> and attainment. Why is that? For he possesses skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) by which the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, endowed with skillful means, is not reborn among the long-lived gods. And what, <s>Subhūti</s>, is that skillful means of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>? It is this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And he applies himself to this skillful means such that, endowed with another [level of] skillful means, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> enters the <s>dhyānas</s> yet is not reborn through the power of <s>dhyāna</s>. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> attains purification of the powers, attains purification of the confidences, attains purification of all <s>Buddha</s> qualities, and reaches them.

body.text: āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - yadā bhagavan sarvadharmā evaṃ prakṛtipariśuddhāḥ, tatkatamasya bhagavan dharmasya bodhisattvo mahāsattvo balapariśuddhiṃ nigacchati, vaiśāradyapariśuddhiṃ nigacchati, sarvabuddhadharmapariśuddhiṃ nigacchati, tāmanuprāpnoti? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvadharmā hi subhūte prakṛtyaiva pariśuddhāḥ / evaṃ subhūte prakṛtipariśuddheṣu sarvadharmeṣu bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya yā asaṃsīdanatā anavalīnatā, iyaṃ sā subhūte prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ subhūte bālapṛthagjanā enān dharmānajānanto 'paśyanto dharmāṇāṃ dharmatāṃ na jānanti, na paśyanti / teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'When, <s>Bhagavān</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are thus pure by nature, then of what <s>dharma</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> attain purification of the powers, purification of the confidences, purification of all <s>Buddha</s> qualities, and reach them?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. Why is that? For all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, are indeed pure by their very nature. When all <s>dharmas</s> are thus pure by nature, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s not sinking and not shrinking while training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—that, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, childish ordinary beings, not knowing and not seeing these <s>dharmas</s>, do not know and do not see the <s>dharmatā</s> (essential nature) of <s>dharmas</s>. For the sake of those beings,

body.text: kṛtaśaḥ subhūte bodhisattvā mahāsattvā vyāyacchante, vīryamārabhante - vayamevamajānakān sattvān jānayiṣyāmaḥ, vayamevamapaśyakān sattvān paśyayiṣyāmaḥ ityatra śikṣāyāṃ śikṣante / atra śikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā balānyanuprāpnuvanti, vaiśāradyānyanuprāpnuvanti / sarvabuddhadharmānanuprāpnuvanti / evaṃ śikṣamāṇāḥ subhūte bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ cittacaritavispanditāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānanti / yathābhūtaṃ prajānantaḥ paracittacaritajñatāyāḥ pāraṃ gacchanti / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte alpakāste mahāpṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpradeśāḥ ye 'pagatapāṣāṇāḥ, yatra suvarṇaṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā rajataṃ votpadyate / atha khalu punarbahutarakāste mahāpṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpradeśāḥ, ya ūṣarā ujjaṅgalā vividhatṛṇakāṇḍakaṇṭakādhānāḥ / evameva subhūte alpakāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye 'syāṃ sarvajñatāśikṣāyāṃ śikṣante yaduta prajñāpāramitāśikṣāyām / atha khalu bahutarakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye śrāvakapratyekabuddhaśikṣāyāṃ śikṣante //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> exert themselves and undertake vigor [thinking]: "We shall make these unknowing beings know; we shall make these unseeing beings see"—in this training they train. Training in this training, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> attain the powers, attain the confidences, attain all <s>Buddha</s> qualities. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> know as it truly is the mental conduct, activities, and inclinations of other beings and other persons. Knowing as it truly is, they reach the perfection of knowledge of the mental conduct of others. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, few are those regions of the great earth that are free of stones, where gold, fine gold, or silver is produced; but many indeed are those regions of the great earth that are barren, saline, covered with various grasses, reeds, and thorns—even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, few are those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> found among the multitude of beings who train in this training in <s>sarvajñatā</s>, namely the training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But many indeed are those beings found among the multitude of beings who train in the training of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tadyathāpi nāma alpakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye cakravartirājyasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma samādāya vartante / atha khalu bahutarakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye koṭṭarājyasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma samādāya vartante / evameva subhūte alpakāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye imaṃ mārgamārūḍhā yaduta prajñāpāramitāmārgam, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyāmahe iti / atha khalu bahutarakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye śrāvakapratyekabuddhamārgamārūḍhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, just as few are those beings found among the multitude of beings who undertake <s>karma</s> leading to universal sovereignty (<s>cakravartin</s> kingship), but many indeed are those beings found among the multitude of beings who undertake <s>karma</s> leading to minor kingship—even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, few are those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> found among the multitude of beings who have ascended this path, namely the path of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> [thinking]: "We shall awaken to supreme perfect awakening." But many indeed are those beings found among the multitude of beings who have ascended the path of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tadyathāpi nāma alpakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye śakrasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma samādāya vartante / atha khalu bahutarakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye devalokasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma samādāya vartante / evameva subhūte alpakāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye 'syāṃ prajñāpāramitāśikṣāyāṃ śikṣante / atha khalu bahutarakāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye śrāvakapratyekabuddhaśikṣāyāṃ śikṣante //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, just as few are those beings found among the multitude of beings who undertake <s>karma</s> leading to [the position of] <s>Śakra</s>, but many indeed are those beings found among the multitude of beings who undertake <s>karma</s> leading to the divine realms—even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, few are those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> found among the multitude of beings who train in this training of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But many indeed are those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> found among the multitude of beings who train in the training of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tadyathāpi nāma alpakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye brahmasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma samādāya vartante / atha khalu bahutarakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye brahmapārṣadyasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma samādāya vartante / evameva subhūte alpakāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye 'vinivartanīyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / atha khalu bahutarakāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye vivartante 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / tasmāttarhi subhūte alpakāste sattvāḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyante, ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāḥ / tebhyo 'pi subhūte alpebhyo 'lpatarakāste sattvāḥ, ye tathatvāya pratipadyante /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, just as few are those beings found among the multitude of beings who undertake <s>karma</s> leading to [the position of] <s>Brahmā</s>, but many indeed are those beings found among the multitude of beings who undertake <s>karma</s> leading to [the position of] members of <s>Brahmā</s>'s retinue—even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, few are those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> found among the multitude of beings who are irreversible from supreme perfect awakening. But many indeed are those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> found among the multitude of beings who fall back from supreme perfect awakening. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, few are those beings found among the multitude of beings who have set out for supreme perfect awakening. Even among those few, <s>Subhūti</s>, fewer still are those who practice for suchness (<s>tathatva</s>).

body.text: tebhyo 'pi subhūte alpatarakebhyastathatvāya pratipadyamānebhyo 'lpatamāste ye prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyante / tebhyo 'pi subhūte alpatamebhyaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyamānebhyo 'lpatamāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, ye 'vinivartanīyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ya ete 'lpatamebhyo 'lpatamā avinivartanīyā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, teṣu gaṇanāṃ gantukāmena ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam, yogamāpattavyam //
body.translated_text: Even fewer, <s>Subhūti</s>, than those fewer ones who practice for suchness, are those who apply themselves to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Even fewer, <s>Subhūti</s>, than those fewest ones who apply themselves to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, are the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are irreversible from supreme perfect awakening. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to be counted among those fewest of the fewest—the irreversible <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>—should train right here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and should apply himself to it.'

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya evaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya na khilasahagataṃ cittamutpadyate, na vicikitsāsahagataṃ cittamutpadyate, nerṣyāmātsaryasahagataṃ cittamutpadyate, na dauḥśīlyasahagataṃ cittamutpadyate, na vyāpādasahagataṃ cittamutpadyate, na kausīdyasahagataṃ cittamutpadyate, na vikṣepasahagataṃ cittamutpadyate, na dauṣprajñasahagataṃ cittamutpadyate / evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvāḥ pāramitā saṃgṛhītā bhavanti, sarvāḥ pāramitā udgṛhītā bhavanti, sarvāḥ pāramitā anugatā bhavanti / sarvāḥ pāramitā antargatā bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte satkāyadṛṣṭau dvāṣaṣṭidṛṣṭigatānyantargatāni bhavanti, evameva subhūte prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tasyāṃ sarvāḥ pāramitā antargatā bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte puruṣasya jīvitendriye pravartamāne sarvāṇīndriyāṇyantargatāni bhavanti, evameva subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya sarvakuśalā dharmā antargatā bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte puruṣasya jīvitendriye niruddhe sarvāṇīndriyāṇi niruddhāni bhavanti, evameva subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya ajñāne niruddhe sarve 'kuśalā dharmā niruddhā bhavanti, sarvāś ca tadanyāḥ pāramitā antargatāḥ parigṛhītā bhavanti / tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvāḥ pāramitāḥ parigrahītukāmena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvasattvānāmagratāyāṃ śikṣate / tatkasya hetoḥ? puṇyāgratvāt / tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yāvantastrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ sattvasaṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhyamāṇāḥ, api nu te bahavo bhavanti? subhūtirāha - jāmbūdvīpakā eva tāvadbhagavan bahavaḥ sattvā bhavanti, kaḥ punarvādo ye trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ / bhagavānāha - yaḥ subhūte eko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yāvajjīvaṃ tiṣṭhaṃstān sarvasattvān cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānaiścopatiṣṭhet, tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvastatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati? subhūtirāha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata / bhagavānāha - ataḥ sa subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvastatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśo 'cchaṭāsaṃghātamātrakam api bhāvayet / tatkasya hetoḥ? evaṃ mahārthikā hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherāhārikā / tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena sarvasattvānāmanuttaratāṃ gantukāmena sarvasattvānāmanāthānāṃ nāthena bhavitukāmena
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> thus training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, no thought accompanied by rigidity arises, no thought accompanied by doubt arises, no thought accompanied by jealousy and miserliness arises, no thought accompanied by immorality arises, no thought accompanied by ill-will arises, no thought accompanied by laziness arises, no thought accompanied by distraction arises, no thought accompanied by poor wisdom arises. For, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all <s>pāramitās</s> are collected, all <s>pāramitās</s> are taken up, all <s>pāramitās</s> are followed, all <s>pāramitās</s> are included. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the sixty-two wrong views are included within the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all <s>pāramitās</s> are included within it. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, when a person's life faculty is functioning, all faculties are included within it, just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are included. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, when a person's life faculty ceases, all faculties cease, just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, when ignorance ceases, all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> cease, and all other <s>pāramitās</s> are included and encompassed. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> wishing to encompass all <s>pāramitās</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> trains in the foremost position among all beings. For what reason? Because of the supremacy of merit. What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—are all the beings in the great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system, when counted by the count of beings, many?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Even the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> alone, O Blessed One, are many—how much more so the beings in the great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system!" The Blessed One said: "If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a single <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, remaining for his entire lifetime, were to provide all those beings with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines and provisions for the sick, and with all comforts—what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, would that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> generate much merit from that?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Much, O Blessed One! Much, O <s>Sugata</s>!" The Blessed One said: "Yet that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, generates even more merit from this: one who cultivates this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for even so brief a time as a finger-snap. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is of such great benefit for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, bringing <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> wishing to fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, wishing to attain the supreme position among all beings, wishing to become the protector of all unprotected beings,

body.text: buddhaviṣayamanuprāptukāmena buddhavṛṣabhitāmanugantukāmena buddhavikrīḍitaṃ vikrīḍitukāmena buddhasiṃhanādaṃ naditukāmena buddhasaṃpattimanuprāptukāmena trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau dharmasāṃkathyaṃ kartukāmena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ subhūte śikṣamāṇasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāhaṃ tāṃ saṃpattiṃ samanupaśyāmi, yā tena na śikṣitā bhavati / subhūtirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan śrāvakasaṃpattir api tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitā bhavati? bhagavānāha - śrāvakasaṃpattir api subhūte tena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitā bhavati / na khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śrāvakasaṃpatyāṃ sthāsyāmīti śikṣate, śrāvakasaṃpattirvā me bhaviṣyatīti naivaṃ śikṣate / ye 'pi te subhūte śrāvakagaṇāḥ, tān api sa jānāti, na ca tatrāvatiṣṭhate / evaṃ ca vyavacārayati, na ca prativahati - mayāpyete śrāvakaguṇā deśayitavyāḥ prakāśayitavyā iti śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasya dakṣiṇīyatāṃ gacchati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvāṃstato 'nyān dakṣiṇīyān śrāvakapratisaṃyuktān pratyekabuddhapratisaṃyuktāṃścābhibhavati, sarvajñatā cāsya āsannībhavati / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na riñcati, prajñāpāramitāṃ carati prajñāpāramitāyāmavirahitaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa / evaṃ caran subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'parihāṇadharmā aparihāṇadharmeti veditavyaḥ / sarvajñatāyā dūrīkaroti śrāvakabhūmim, pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ ca, āsannībhavatyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / sacetpunarasyaivaṃ bhavati - iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitā imāṃ sarvajñatāmāhariṣyati, ityevaṃ saṃjānīte, carati prajñāpāramitām / atha tām api prajñāpāramitāṃ na saṃjānīte - iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitā, asya vā prajñāpāramitā sarvajñatāmāhariṣyatīti vā, evam api subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na saṃjānīte, na samanupaśyati / sacedevaṃ carati bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, carati prajñāpāramitāyāmiti //
body.translated_text: wishing to reach the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to follow the bull-like power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to sport in the sport of the <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to roar the lion's roar of the <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to attain the accomplishment of the <s>Buddhas</s>, wishing to give a <s>Dharma</s> discourse in the great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system—should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. I do not see, <s>Subhūti</s>, any accomplishment that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has not trained in." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Does even the accomplishment of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, O Blessed One, become trained in by that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>?" The Blessed One said: "Even the accomplishment of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is trained in by that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. However, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not train thinking 'I will remain in the accomplishment of <s>Śrāvakas</s>' or 'The accomplishment of <s>Śrāvakas</s> will be mine'—he does not train thus. Although, <s>Subhūti</s>, he knows the assemblies of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, he does not remain there. He discerns thus and does not take them upon himself: 'I too must teach and illuminate these qualities of <s>Śrāvakas</s>'—thus he trains. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> becomes worthy of offerings from the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> surpasses all other recipients of offerings connected with <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and his <s>sarvajñatā</s> draws near. Training thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not fall short; he practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, unseparated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, dwelling in the abiding of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should be known as one of non-declining nature. He distances himself from the <s>Śrāvaka</s> level and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> level for the sake of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, and draws near to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. But if it occurs to him: 'This <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will bring about this <s>sarvajñatā</s>'—if he perceives thus and practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—then he also does not perceive or recognize that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: 'This is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' or 'This <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will bring about <s>sarvajñatā</s>.' Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not perceive or recognize it. If he practices thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>."

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣāparivarto nāma pañcaviṃśatitamaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the twenty-fifth chapter, called the Chapter on Training.

body.text: ASP_26: māyopamaparivartaḥ ṣaḍviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Twenty-Six of the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>: the Chapter on Illusion-Like, the twenty-sixth.

body.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhūt - caranneva tāvadayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvasattvānabhibhavati, kaḥ punarvādo yadā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati / lābhāsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sulabdhāḥ, sujīvitaṃ ca te sattvā jīvanti, yeṣāṃ sarvajñatāyāṃ cittaṃ krāmati / kaḥ punarvādo yairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / spṛhaṇīyāste sattvā ye sattvasārā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante //
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "Even while still practicing, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> surpasses all beings—how much more so when he will have fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>! Those beings have gained well, well-gained, and those beings live a good life, whose minds proceed toward <s>sarvajñatā</s>. How much more so those who have generated the mind directed toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>! Enviable are those beings, the essence of beings, who will fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>!"

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro māndāravāṇi puṣpāṇyabhinirmāya puṣpāṇāmañjaliṃ kṛtvā tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamabhyavākirat, evaṃ ca vācamabhāṣata - yairbodhisattvayānikaiḥ pudgalairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam - anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyāmahe, abhisaṃbudhya sarvasattvān mahatā saṃsārārṇavenohyamānān same pārime tīre pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāma iti, samṛdhyantāṃ teṣāmabhīpsitāḥ paricintitāḥ, parigṛhītāścittotpādāḥ eteṣāmeva buddhadharmāṇāṃ paripūraṇāya bhavantu, eteṣāmeva sarvajñatāpratisaṃyuktānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ paripūraṇāya bhavantu, eteṣāmeva svayaṃbhūdharmāṇāṃ paripūraṇāya bhavantu, eteṣāmeva asaṃhāryadharmāṇāṃ paripūraṇāya bhavantu / na me bhagavan ekacittotpādo 'pyutpadyate, yatte bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahākaruṇayā samanvāgatā vivarteran anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheriti / na me bhagavan ekacittotpādo 'pyutpadyate yatte bodhisattvayānikāḥ pudgalā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhuṃ saṃprasthitāḥ, tato vivarteran / iti yadbhūyasyā mātrayā praṇidhiṃ janayiṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau imāni saṃsārāvacarāṇi duḥkhāni sattvānāṃ saṃpaśyantaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? tayā mahākaruṇayā arthakāmā hitakāmā hi te sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasyānukampakāḥ, ye imairevaṃrūpaiścittotpādaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ kimiti vayaṃ tīrṇāḥ sattvāṃstārayema, muktā mocayema, āśvastā āśvāsayema, parinirvṛtāḥ parinirvāpayema, ityetaiścittotpādairviharanti / yasteṣāṃ bhagavan prathamayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cittotpādānanumodate, avinivartanīyānāmapyavinivartanīyadharmatāmanumodate, ekajātipratibaddhānām api bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmekajātipratibaddhadharmatāmanumodate, kiyatsa bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati? evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - syātkhalu punaḥ kauśika śakyeta sumeroḥ parvatarājasya palāgreṇa tulyamānasya pramāṇaṃ grahītum, na tveva kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyānumodanāsahagatasya cittotpādasya puṇyapramāṇaṃ grahītum / syātkhalu punaḥ kauśika śakyeta cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau palāgreṇa tulyamāne pramāṇaṃ grahītum, na tveva kauśika tasyānumodanāsahagasya cittotpādasya puṇyapramāṇaṃ grahītum / syātkhalu punaḥ kauśika śakyeta sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau tulyamāne palāgreṇa pramāṇaṃ grahītum, na tveva kauśika tasyānumodanāsahagatasya cittotpādasya puṇyapramāṇaṃ grahītum / syātkhalu punaḥ kauśika śakyeta
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, having magically created <s>Māndārava</s> flowers and making a handful of flowers, showered them upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and spoke these words: "May the aspirations, thoughts, and intentions of those persons following the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle who have generated the mind directed toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>—'We shall fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, and having awakened, we shall establish all beings, who are being swept away by the great flood of <s>saṃsāra</s>, on the even, farther shore'—may those be fulfilled, for the completion of these very <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, for the completion of these very <s>dharmas</s> connected with <s>sarvajñatā</s>, for the completion of these very self-arising <s>dharmas</s>, for the completion of these very irreversible <s>dharmas</s>! Not even a single thought arises in me, O Blessed One, that those <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> endowed with great compassion might turn back from <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Not even a single thought arises in me, O Blessed One, that those persons following the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle who have set out to fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> might turn back from it. Even more so, they will generate the aspiration for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, seeing the sufferings of beings caught in <s>saṃsāra</s>. For what reason? Because with that great compassion, desiring their welfare and benefit, they have compassion for the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>—those who are endowed with such thoughts: 'Having crossed over, may we ferry beings across; being liberated, may we liberate; being consoled, may we console; having attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, may we cause others to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>'—with these thoughts they abide. One who, O Blessed One, rejoices in the mind-generations of those <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who have first set out, and also rejoices in the nature of irreversibility of those who are irreversible, and also rejoices in the nature of one-more-birth of those <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who are bound by one more birth—how much merit, O Blessed One, does that son of good family or daughter of good family generate?" When this was said, the Blessed One said to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "It might be possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, when weighed on a scale with a blade of grass, but it is not possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the merit of that mind-generation accompanied by rejoicing of that son of good family or daughter of good family, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. It might be possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the world-system of four great continents when weighed on a scale with a blade of grass, but it is not possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the merit of that mind-generation accompanied by rejoicing. It might be possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the thousandfold minor world-system when weighed on a scale with a blade of grass, but it is not possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the merit of that mind-generation accompanied by rejoicing. It might be possible, <s>Kauśika</s>,

body.text: dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau palāgreṇa tulyamāne pramāṇaṃ grahītum, na tveva kauśika tasyānumodanāsahagatasya cittotpādasya puṇyapramāṇaṃ grahītum / syātkhalu punaḥ kauśika śakyeta trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau tulyamāne palāgreṇa pramāṇaṃ grahītum, na tveva kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyānumodanāsahagatasya cittotpādasya puṇyapramāṇaṃ grahītum //
body.translated_text: to determine the measure of the twice-thousandfold intermediate world-system when weighed on a scale with a blade of grass, but it is not possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the merit of that mind-generation accompanied by rejoicing. It might be possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system when weighed on a scale with a blade of grass, but it is not possible, <s>Kauśika</s>, to determine the measure of the merit of that mind-generation accompanied by rejoicing of that son of good family or daughter of good family, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>."

body.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - mārādhiṣṭhitāste bhagavan sattvā veditavyāḥ, ye bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhānāmevamaprameyamanumodanāsahagatasya cittotpādasya puṇyamiti na śṛṇvanti, na jānanti, na paśyanti, tāmanumodanāṃ na samanvāharanti / mārapakṣikā bhagavaṃste sattvā bhaviṣyanti, ye bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmimāṃścittotpādānnānumodiṣyante / mārabhavanebhyaś ca te bhagavan sattvāścyutā bhaviṣyanti, ya imāṃścittotpādāṃsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ nānumodiṣyante / tatkasya hetoḥ? mārabhavanavidhvaṃsanakarā hi tairbhagavan ime cittotpādā abhinirhṛtāḥ, yairamī cittotpādā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmitāḥ, anumoditā vā amī cittopādāḥ / anumoditavyā bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmamī cittotpādāḥ, yairbodhisattvairmahāsattvairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / yeṣāṃ bhagavaṃstathāgato 'parityaktaḥ, dharmo 'parityaktaḥ, saṃgho 'parityaktaḥ, taiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhiśceme cittotpādā anumoditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One: "Those beings, O Blessed One, should be understood as controlled by <s>Māra</s>, who do not hear, do not know, do not see, and do not practice that rejoicing regarding the immeasurable merit of the mind-generation accompanied by rejoicing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, from their first generation of the mind up to their full awakening to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Those beings, O Blessed One, will be on <s>Māra</s>'s side, who will not rejoice in these mind-generations of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Those beings, O Blessed One, will have fallen from <s>Māra</s>'s realms, who will not rejoice in these mind-generations of these <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, these mind-generations that have been produced by them destroy <s>Māra</s>'s realms—by those who have dedicated these mind-generations in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, or who have rejoiced in these mind-generations. These mind-generations of those <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> should be rejoiced in, O Blessed One—of those <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who have generated the mind directed toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Those sons of good family and daughters of good family who have not abandoned the <s>Tathāgata</s>, have not abandoned the <s>Dharma</s>, have not abandoned the <s>Saṅgha</s>—by them should these mind-generations be rejoiced in."

body.text: evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - evametatkauśika, evam etat / yeṣāṃ kauśika tathāgato 'parityaktaḥ, dharmo 'parityaktaḥ, saṃgho 'parityaktaḥ, taiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhiśceme cittotpādā anumoditavyāḥ / yaiḥ kauśika kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhiśceme cittopādā anumoditā bodhisattvayānikairvā pratyekabuddhayānikairvā śrāvakayānikairvā, te kṣipraṃ tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānārāgayiṣyanti, na virāgayiṣyanti / evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata / yaiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhiśceme cittotpādā anumoditā bodhisattvayānikairvā pratyekabuddhayānikairvā śrāvakayānikairvā, te kṣipraṃ tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānārāgayiṣyanti, na virāgayiṣyanti / evaṃ tairanumodanāsahagataiścittotpādakuśalamūlairyatra yatropapatsyante, tatra tatra satkṛtāś ca bhaviṣyanti, gurukṛtāś ca bhaviṣyanti, mānitāś ca bhaviṣyanti, pūjitāś ca bhaviṣyanti, arcitāś ca bhaviṣyanti, apacāyitāś ca bhaviṣyanti / na ca te amanaāpāni rūpāṇi drakṣyanti [NOTE: Conze translates "nor hear any unpleasant sounds"] / na ca te amanaāpān gandhān ghrāsyanti / na ca te amanaāpān rasān paribhokṣyante / na ca te amanaāpāni spraṣṭavyāni sprakṣyanti / na ca teṣāmapāyeṣūpapattiḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyā / svargopapattisteṣāṃ pratikāṅkṣitavyā / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi taiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhirvā sarvasattvasukhāvahānyaprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlānyanumoditāni yair api bhagavaṃśchandamutpādya bodhaye bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ te cittotpādā anumoditāḥ, teṣāṃ te cittotpādā
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the Gods: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. Those sons and daughters of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, who have not abandoned the <s>Tathāgata</s>, have not abandoned the <s>Dharma</s>, have not abandoned the <s>Saṃgha</s>—by them should these mental aspirations be rejoiced in. Those sons and daughters of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, who have rejoiced in these mental aspirations directed toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [path]—"

body.text: vivardhamānā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherāhārakā bhaviṣyanti / te 'pyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān sattvān parinirvāpayiṣyanti / bhagavānāha - evametatkauśikaḥ, evametat, yathā tvayā vāgbhāṣitā tathāgatasyaivānubhāvena / yena kauśika kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ te cittotpādā anumoditāḥ, anena kauśika paryāyeṇa tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ tāṃścittotpādānanumodya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlānyanumoditāni bhavanti, avaropitāni abhinirhṛtāni ca bhavanti //
body.translated_text: "—growing ever greater, [these aspirations] will become the nourishment for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). They too, having fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, will lead immeasurable, incalculable beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>." The Blessed One said: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. As these words have been spoken by you, it is through the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s power alone. By whichever son or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Bodhi</s>—"

body.text: subhūtirāha - kathaṃ ca bhagavan māyopamaṃ cittamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte samanupaśyasi tvaṃ māyopamaṃ cittam? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte samanupaśyasi tvaṃ māyām? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / nāhaṃ bhagavan māyopamaṃ cittaṃ nāpi māyāṃ samanupaśyāmi / bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yanna māyāṃ nāpi māyopamaṃ cittaṃ samanupaśyasi, tatkiṃ tvamanyatra māyāyā māyopamādvā cittāt taṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyasi yo dharmo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / nāhaṃ bhagavan anyatra māyāyā māyopamādvā cittāt taṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi, yo dharmo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / so 'haṃ bhagavan anyatra māyāyā māyopamādvā cittāt taṃ dharmasamanuśyan katamaṃ dharmamupadekṣyāmi astīti vā nāstīti vā? yaś ca atyantavivikto dharmaḥ, na so 'stīti vā nāstīti vā upaiti / yo 'pi dharmo 'tyantatayā viviktaḥ, nāsāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi bhagavan asaṃvidyamāno dharmo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / tasmāttarhi bhagavan atyantaviviktā prajñāpāramitā / yaś ca dharmo 'tyantaviviktaḥ, nāsau dharmo bhāvayitavyaḥ / nāpyasau kasyaciddharmasyāvāhako vā nirvāhako vā / kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'tyantaviviktāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate? anuttarāpi nāma bhagavan samyaksaṃbodhiratyantaviviktā / yadā bhagavan prajñāpāramitāpyatyantaviviktā, anuttarāpi samyaksaṃbodhiratyantaviviktā, tadā kathaṃ bhagavan viviktena viviktamabhisaṃbuddhaṃ bhavati? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sādhu sādhu subhūte / evametatsubhūte, evam etat / atyantaviviktā subhūte prajñāpāramitā, atyantaviviktaiva anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ / yata eva subhūte atyantaviviktā prajñāpāramitā, ata eva atyantaviviktā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbudhyate / sacetsubhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāmatyantaviviktāmiti saṃjānīte, na sā prajñāpāramitā syāt / evaṃ khalu subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, nāpi subhūte prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / na ca vivekena vivekamabhisaṃbudhyate, abhisaṃbudhyate ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim / na ca prajñāpāramitāmanāgamyābhisaṃbudhyate //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "How, Blessed One, does an illusion-like mind fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>?" When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, do you perceive an illusion-like mind?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, do you perceive an illusion?" He said—

body.text: subhūtirāha - yathāhaṃ bhagavan bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, tathā gambhīre bhagavan arthe carati bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / gambhīre 'rthe subhūte carati bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / duṣkarakārakaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, yo gambhīre 'rthe carati, taṃ cārthaṃ na sākṣātkaroti yaduta śrāvakabhūmau vā pratyekabuddhabhūmau vā //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "As I understand the meaning of the Blessed One's teaching, Blessed One, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices in a profound sense." The Blessed One said: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, practices in a profound sense. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is one who does what is difficult, for he practices in the profound sense—"

body.text: subhūtirāha - yathāhaṃ bhagavan bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, tathā na kaścidduṣkarakārako bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan sa eva dharmo nopalabhyate yaḥ sākṣātkuryāt, so 'pi dharmo nopalabhyate yaḥ sākṣātkriyate, so 'pi dharmo nopalabhyate yena sākṣātkriyeta / sacedbhagavan evaṃ bhāṣyamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na saṃsīdati, nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate, na vipṛṣṭhībhavati, notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate, carati prajñāpāramitāyām / saceccarāmīti na samanupaśyati, carati prajñāpāramitāyām / āsannā me 'nuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti sacedevamati na samanupaśyati, carati prajñāpāramitāyām / dūrīkṛtā me śrāvakabhūmiḥ pratyekabuddhabhūmirveti sacedasyaivam api na bhavati, carati prajñāpāramitāyām / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan ākāśasya naivaṃ bhavati - kasyacidahamāsannaḥ, kasyacidvā dūra iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādbhagavan ākāśasya / evameva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya naivaṃ bhavati - anuttarāṃ samyaksabodhirmamāsannā, śrāvakabhūmiḥ pratyekabuddhabhūmiś ca mama dūra iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? nirvikalpatvādbhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan māyāpuruṣasya naivaṃ bhavati - māyākāro mamāsannaḥ, yaḥ punaranyo janakāyaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ sa mama dūra iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādbhagavan māyāpuruṣasya / evameva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya naivaṃ bhavati - anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirmamāsannā, śrāvakabhūmiḥ pratyekabuddhabhūmiś ca mama dūra iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādbhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan pratibhāsasya naivaṃ bhavati - yenārambaṇena pratibhāsa utpadyate tanmamāsanne, ye tu khalu punaratra nopasaṃkrāntā ādarśe vā udakapātre vā te mama dūra iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādbhagavan pratibhāsasya / evameva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya naivaṃ bhavati - anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirmamāsannā, śrāvakabhūmiḥ pratyekabuddhabhūmiś ca mama dūra iti / tat kasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādbhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavaṃstathāgatasya kaścitpriyo vā apriyo vā na saṃvidyate, tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvakalpavikalpaprahīṇatvāttathāgatasya, evameva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na kaścitpriyo vā apriyo vā saṃvidyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādbhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / yathaiva hi bhagavan sarvakalpavikalpaprahīṇastathāgataḥ, tathaiva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāpi sarvakalpavikalpaprahīṇā / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavaṃstathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena yo nirmitako nirmitaḥ, na tasyaivaṃ bhavati - śrāvakabhūmiḥ pratyekabuddhabhūmiś ca mama dūre, anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirmamāsanneti / tatkasya
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "As I understand the meaning of the Blessed One's teaching, Blessed One, no <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does what is difficult. For what reason? Because, Blessed One, that very <s>dharma</s> which would be directly realized is not apprehended; that <s>dharma</s> which is directly realized is also not apprehended; that <s>dharma</s> by which it would be directly realized is also not apprehended. If—"

body.text: hetoḥ? avikalpatvādbhagavannirmitasya / evameva bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāṃ carato naivaṃ bhavati - śrāvakabhūmiḥ pratyekabuddhabhūmiś ca mama dūre, anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirmamāsanneti / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādeva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan sa nirmitako yasya kṛtyasya kṛtaśo nirmitaḥ, tatkṛtyaṃ karoti / sa ca nirmitako 'vikalpaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādeva nirmitasya / evameva bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yasya kṛtyasya kṛtaśa imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati, tacca kṛtyaṃ karoti, sā ca prajñāpāramitā avikalpā / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādeva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan dakṣeṇa palagaṇḍena vā palagaṇḍāntevāsinā vā dārumayī strī vā puruṣo vā yantrayuktaḥ kṛto bhavet / sa yasya kṛtyasyārthāya kṛtaḥ, tacca kṛtyaṃ karoti / sa ca dārusaṃghāto 'vikalpaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādeva bhagavan dārusaṃghātasya / evameva bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yasya kṛtyasya kṛtaśa imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati, tacca kṛtyaṃ karoti, sā ca prajñāpāramitā avikalpā / tatkasya hetoḥ? avikalpatvādeva bhagavan asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā iti //
body.translated_text: "For what reason? Because, Blessed One, an emanation is without conceptual discrimination. Just so, Blessed One, when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, there is no thought: 'The <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage are far from me; <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> is near to me.' For what reason? Because, Blessed One, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself is without conceptual discrimination. Just as, Blessed One—"

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ māyopamaparivarto nāma ṣaḍviṃśatitamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the Twenty-Sixth Chapter, called "The Chapter on Illusion," in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

body.text: ASP_27: sāraparivartaḥ saptaviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Chapter on Essence.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sāre batāyamāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati, yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - sāre batāyamāyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati, yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Indeed, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> practices in the essence. When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: Indeed, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> practices in the essence.

body.text: atha khalu saṃbahulānāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devaputrasahasrāṇāmetadabhavat - namaskartavyāste sattvāḥ, yairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni abhinirhṛtāni / ye ceha gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranti, tathā caranto bhūtakoṭiṃ na sākṣātkurvanti, yaduta śrāvakabhūmau vā pratyakabuddhabhūmau vā / anenāpi paryāyeṇa duṣkarakārakā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā veditavyāḥ, ye dharmāṇāṃ dharmatāyāṃ caranti, na ca tāṃ dharmatāṃ sākṣātkurvanti / atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtisteṣāṃ saṃbahulānāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devaputrasahasrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tāni saṃbahulāni kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇyāmantrayante sma - nedaṃ devaputrāsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ duṣkaram, yatte tāṃ bhūtakoṭiṃ na sākṣātkurvanti / idaṃ tu devaputrāsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ duṣkaraṃ caiva paramaduṣkaraṃ caiva, yadaprameyānasaṃkhyeyānapramāṇān sattvān parinirvāpayiṣyāma iti saṃnāhaṃ saṃnahyante / te ca sattvā atyantatayā na saṃvidyante, asaṃvidyamānā nopalabhyante, sattvaviviktatvāt / evaṃ vainayikā atyantatayā na saṃvidyante / evaṃ ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhuṃ saṃprasthitāḥ sattvān vineṣyāma iti, ākāśaṃ sa devaputrā vinetavyaṃ manyeta yaḥ sattvān vinetavyān manyeta / tatkasya hetoḥ? ākāśaviviktatayā hi devaputrāḥ sattvaviviktatā veditavyā / anena devaputrāḥ paryāyeṇa duṣkarakārakā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, ye 'saṃvidyamānānāmanupalabhyamānānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṛtaśaḥ saṃnāhaṃ saṃnahyante / ākāśena na sa devaputrāḥ sārdhaṃ veditavyaṃ manyeta, yaḥ sattvānāṃ kṛtaśaḥ saṃnāhaṃ saṃnaddhavyaṃ manyeta / ayaṃ ca saṃnāho bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sattvānāṃ kṛtaśaḥ saṃnaddhaḥ / sarvātyantatayā sattvānupalabdhiruktā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena / sā ca sattvaviviktatayaiva veditavyā, vainayikavivaktatayā ca sattvaviviktatā veditavyā / sacedatraivaṃ bhāṣyamāṇe bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na saṃsīdati, veditavyametaddevaputrāḥ - caratyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyām / tatkasya hetoḥ? sattvaviviktatayā hi rūpaviviktatā veditavyā / evaṃ sattvaviviktatayā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāraviviktatā veditavyā / sattvaviviktatayā vijñānaviviktatā veditavyā / evaṃ yāvatsattvaviviktatayā sarvadharmaviviktatā veditavyā / evaṃ devaputrāḥ sarvadharmaviviktatā draṣṭavyā / evaṃ devaputrāḥ sarvadharmaviviktatāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na saṃsīdati / yato na saṃsīdati, tataścarati prajñāpāramitāyām //
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to many thousands of <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) of the desire realm: Those beings are to be honored who have generated and brought forth the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening, and who practice in this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and while so practicing do not realize <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the ultimate point of reality) at the <s>śrāvaka</s> stage or the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> stage. By this method too, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> should be known as doers of what is difficult to do—they who practice in the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of <s>dharmas</s>, yet do not realize that <s>dharmatā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, knowing the mental reflections of those many thousands of <s>devaputras</s> of the desire realm with his own mind, addressed those many thousands of <s>devaputras</s> of the desire realm: O <s>devaputras</s>, it is not this that is difficult for those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>—that they do not realize that <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>. Rather, O <s>devaputras</s>, this is what is difficult, supremely difficult, for those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>: that they don the armor thinking 'We shall lead immeasurable, incalculable, unlimited beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>'—yet those beings are ultimately not found; being unfound, they are not apprehended, because of the emptiness of beings. Likewise, those to be disciplined are ultimately not found. And yet <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, having set forth to attain unsurpassed perfect awakening, think 'We shall discipline beings.' O <s>devaputras</s>, whoever thinks that beings are to be disciplined might as well think that space is to be disciplined. Why is that? For, O <s>devaputras</s>, the emptiness of beings should be understood through the emptiness of space. By this method, O <s>devaputras</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> are doers of what is difficult to do—they who don the armor for the sake of beings who are not found and not apprehended. O <s>devaputras</s>, one should not think that the armor is to be donned for the sake of beings together with space—whoever might think that the armor is to be donned for the sake of beings. And yet this armor has been donned by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> for the sake of beings. The complete non-apprehension of beings has been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One in terms of their ultimate nature. And that should be understood through the emptiness of beings, and the emptiness of beings should be understood through the emptiness of those to be disciplined. If, when this is being taught, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not sink down—then, O <s>devaputras</s>, it should be known: 'This <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Why is that? For through the emptiness of beings, the emptiness of form should be understood. Likewise, through the emptiness of beings, the emptiness of feeling, perception, and mental formations should be understood. Through the emptiness of beings, the emptiness of consciousness should be understood. Thus, through the emptiness of beings, the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. Thus, O <s>devaputras</s>, the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> should be seen. Thus, O <s>devaputras</s>, when the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> is being taught, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not sink down. Because he does not sink down, he practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān jānanneva āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ sarvadharmaviviktatāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ na saṃsīdati? subhūtirāha -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing full well, said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: For what reason, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not sink down when the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> is being taught? <s>Subhūti</s> said—

body.text: viviktatvādbhagavanna saṃsīdati / anena bhagavan kāranena bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvadharmaviviktatāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ na saṃsīdati / nāpi bhagavan kaściddharmaḥ saṃsīdati / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi bhagavan kaściddharma upalabhyate, yaḥ saṃsīdet / so 'pi bhagavan dharmo nopalabhyeta, yena dharmeṇa yo dharmaḥ saṃsīdet / bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evam etat / api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte sacedevaṃ bhāṣyamāṇe deśyamāne nirdiśyamāne evamupadiśyamāne bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na saṃsīdati na viṣīdati na viṣādamāpadyate, nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate, na vipṛṣṭhīkaroti mānasam, na bhagnapṛṣṭhīkaroti, notrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate, carati prajñāpāramitāyām / subhutirāha - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata / sacedbhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ carati, carati prajñāpāramitāyām / evaṃ carantaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ sendrakā devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ saprajāpatikāḥ seśānāḥ sarṣinaranārīgaṇā ārātprāñjalībhūtā namasyanti / bhagavānāha - na kevalaṃ subhūte evaṃ carantaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ sendrakā devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ saprajāpatikāḥ seśānāḥ sarṣinaranārīgaṇā ārātprāñjalībhūtā namasyanti, ye 'pi te subhūte brahmakāyikā devā brahmapurohitā brahmapārṣadyā mahābrahmāṇaḥ parīttābhā apramāṇābhā ābhāsvarāḥ parīttaśubhā apramāṇaśubhāḥ śubhakṛtsnā anabhrakāḥ puṇyaprasavā bṛhatphalā asaṃjñisattvā abṛhā atapāḥ sudṛśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhāś ca devāḥ, te 'pi subhūte taṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ evaṃ carantaṃ namasyanti / ye 'pi te subhūte aprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā etarhi tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti, te 'pi buddhā bhagavantaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāmevaṃ carantaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ buddhacakṣuṣā paśyanti / te ca subhūte bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carantamanugṛhṇanti, samanvāharanti / ye ca khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carantastathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairanugṛhyante samanvāhriyante, te te subhūte bodhisattvā mahāsattvā avinivartanīyā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherdhārayitavyāḥ / na ca teṣāmantarāyā utpatsyante mārato vā anyato vā / tatkasya hetoḥ? ye subhūte trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, te sarve mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso bhaveyuḥ / ekaikaś ca māraḥ pāpīyāṃstāvatīreva mārasenā abhinirmimīte / te 'pi subhūte mārāḥ pāpīyāṃsastasya buddhasamanvāhṛtasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato na pratibalā antarāyaṃ kartumanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ subhūte trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvā mārāḥ pāpīyāṃsaḥ, yāvanta subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ, te 'pi sarve mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso bhaveyuḥ, ekaikaś ca māraḥ pāpīyāṃstāvatīreva mārasenā abhinirmimīte, te 'pi subhūte mārāḥ pāpīyāṃsastasya buddhasamanvāhṛtasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato na pratibalā antarāyaṃ kartumanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / dvābhyāṃ subhūte dharmābhyāṃ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasmin samaye durdharṣo bhavati māraiḥ pāpīyobhirmārakāyikābhirvā devatābhiḥ / katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām? yaduta sarvasattvāścāsya aparityaktā bhavanti, sarvadharmāś ca anena śūnyatāto vyavalokitā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: —Because of emptiness, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, he does not sink down. For this reason, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not sink down when the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> is being taught. Nor, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does any <s>dharma</s> sink down. Why is that? For no <s>dharma</s> is apprehended, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that could sink down. Nor, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is that <s>dharma</s> apprehended by which a <s>dharma</s> could sink down. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, just so. But furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if, when this is being taught, declared, expounded, and thus instructed, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not sink down, does not despair, does not fall into despondency, does not shrink back, does not withdraw, does not turn his mind away, does not become broken-backed, does not become frightened, does not become terrified, does not fall into terror—he practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: So it is, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, so it is, O <s>Sugata</s>. If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices thus, he practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The <s>devas</s> together with <s>Indra</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, together with <s>Prajāpati</s>, together with <s>Īśāna</s>, together with the hosts of <s>ṛṣis</s>, men, and women, pay homage from afar with palms joined to such a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices thus.
