The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from [the understanding that] all <s>dharmas</s> are expressed merely by name, merely by convention. And convention is nowhere, from nowhere, and no convention at all. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from [the understanding that] all <s>dharmas</s> are beyond convention, beyond expression, unconvened, unexpressed. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the immeasurability of all <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the immeasurability of <s>rūpa</s> (form). Likewise from the immeasurability of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the immeasurability of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the signlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the penetration of all <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the natural purity of all <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the inexpressibility of all <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the non-cessation of all <s>dharmas</s>, by the equality of abandonment. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> of all <s>dharmas</s>, by the equality of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). All <s>dharmas</s> do not come and do not go, are unknowing, unborn, and ultimately unborn—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the seeing through of self and other. All <s>dharmas</s> are noble <s>Arhats</s>, naturally pure—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. All <s>dharmas</s> have laid down the burden, by not placing any burden—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the placelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? Because <s>rūpa</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is without place and without locality by its own-nature. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is without place and without locality by its own-nature. Because of the refreshment of the cessation of all <s>dharmas</s>—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from non-delight and non-aversion. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from non-attachment and non-detachment. For what reason? Because <s>rūpa</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, by its true nature and own-nature, is neither attached nor detached. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, by its true nature and own-nature, is neither attached nor detached, because of its natural purity—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. All <s>dharmas</s> are unattached, free from attachment and non-attachment—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. Awakening: all <s>dharmas</s> are [understood] by the awakening through <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed by the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. All <s>dharmas</s> have medicine and <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) as their forerunner—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. All <s>dharmas</s> abide in <s>maitrī</s>, abide in <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), abide in <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), abide in <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity)—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. All <s>dharmas</s> are <s>Brahma</s>-like, by the non-production of faults, by the non-production of all faults—thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed from the wishlessness and unobstructedness of all <s>dharmas</s>. By the boundlessness of the ocean, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of the sky, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the variegation of <s>Meru</s>, the variegation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of <s>rūpa</s>, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>

body.text: anugantavyā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / sūryaraśmimaṇḍalāparyantāvabhāsanatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / sarvaśabdāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / sarvabuddhadharmasamudāgamāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / sarvasattvadhātupuṇyajñānasaṃbhārāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / pṛthivīdhātvaparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / evamabdhātutejodhātuvāyudhātvākāśadhātuvijñānadhātvaparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / kuśalākuśaladharmasaṃcayāpramāṇatayā prajñāpāramitāpramāṇatā anugantavyā / sarvadharmasaṃcayāpramāṇatayā prajñāpāramitāpramāṇatā anugantavyā / sarvadharmasamādhyaparyantatāpratilambhitayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / sarvabuddhadharmāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / sarvadharmāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / śūnyatāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / cittacaitasikāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / cittacaritāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / kuśalākuśaladharmāparimāṇatayā prajñāpāramitāparimāṇatā anugantavyā / siṃhanādanadanatayā prajñāpāramitānadanatā anugantavyā / sarvadharmākopyatayā prajñāpāramitākopyatā anugantavyā / tatkasya hetoḥ ? rūpaṃ hi subhūte samudrasamam / evaṃ vedanāṃ saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ hi subhūte samudrasamam / rūpaṃ hi gaganasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ gaganasamam / rūpaṃ vicitramerūsamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ vicitramerusamam / rūpamaparyantasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānamaparyantasamam / rūpaṃ sūryamaṇḍalaraśmyutpādasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sūryamaṇḍalaraśmyutpādasamam / rūpaṃ sarvaśabdāparyantasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sarvaśabdāparyantasamam / rūpaṃ sarvasattvadhātvaparyantasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sarvasattvadhātvaparyantasamam / rūpaṃ sarvabuddhadharmasamudāgamāparyantasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sarvabuddhadharmasamudāgamāparyantasamam / rūpaṃ sarvasattvadhātupuṇyajñānasaṃbhārāparyantasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sarvasattvadhātupuṇyajñānasaṃbhārāparyantasamam / rūpaṃ pṛthivīsamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ pṛthivīsamam / rūpamapsamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānamapsamam / rūpaṃ tejaḥsamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ tejaḥsamam / rūpaṃ vāyusamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ vāyusamam / rūpamākāśasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānamākāśasamam / rūpaṃ vijñānasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ vijñānasamam / rūpaṃ kuśalākuśaladharmasaṃcayavigatam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ kuśalākuśaladharmasaṃcayavigatam / rūpaṃ sarvadharmasaṃcayavigatam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sarvadharmasaṃcayavigatam / rūpaṃ sarvadharmasamādhyaparyantatāsamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sarvadharmasamādhyaparyantatāsamam / rūpaṃ vigamaḥ, rūpasvabhāvo rūpatathatā buddhadharmāḥ / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ vigamaḥ,
body.translated_text: should be followed. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. By the boundlessness of <s>vijñāna</s>, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundless illumination of the orb of the sun's rays, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of all sounds, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of the accomplishment of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of the accumulation of merit and knowledge of all sentient realms, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of the earth element, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. Likewise, by the boundlessness of the water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the immeasurability of the accumulation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the immeasurability of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the immeasurability of the accumulation of all <s>dharmas</s>, the immeasurability of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the non-attainment of the boundlessness of <s>samādhi</s> regarding all <s>dharmas</s>, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of mind and mental factors, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the boundlessness of the conduct of mind, the boundlessness of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the immeasurability of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the immeasurability of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the roaring of the lion's roar, the roaring of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. By the unshakeability of all <s>dharmas</s>, the unshakeability of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed. For what reason? Because <s>rūpa</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is equal to the ocean. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is equal to the ocean. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the sky. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the sky. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to variegated <s>Meru</s>. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to variegated <s>Meru</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the boundless. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the boundless. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the arising of the rays of the sun's orb. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the arising of the rays of the sun's orb. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the boundlessness of all sounds. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the boundlessness of all sounds. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the boundlessness of all sentient realms. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the boundlessness of all sentient realms. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the boundlessness of the accomplishment of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the boundlessness of the accomplishment of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the boundlessness of the accumulation of merit and knowledge of all sentient realms. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the boundlessness of the accumulation of merit and knowledge of all sentient realms. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the earth. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the earth. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to water. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to water. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to fire. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to fire. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to wind. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to wind. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to space. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to space. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to consciousness. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to consciousness. <s>Rūpa</s> is devoid of the accumulation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is devoid of the accumulation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> is devoid of the accumulation of all <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is devoid of the accumulation of all <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the boundlessness of <s>samādhi</s> regarding all <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the boundlessness of <s>samādhi</s> regarding all <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> is passing away; the own-nature of <s>rūpa</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>rūpa</s>, are <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is passing away;

body.text: vijñānasvabhāvo vijñānatathatā buddhadharmāḥ / rūpaṃ sarvadharmāparyantadharmatā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ sarvadharmāparyantadharmatā / rūpaṃ śūnyamaparyantadharmatā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ śūnyamaparyantadharmatā / rūpaṃ cittacaitasikāparyantatā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ cittacaitasikāparyantatā / rūpaṃ cittacaritotpattiḥ / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ cittacaritotpattiḥ / rūpaṃ kuśalamakuśalam, yāvadanupalabdhiḥ / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ kuśalamakuśalam, yāvadanupalabdhiḥ / rūpaṃ siṃhanādasamam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānaṃ siṃhanādasamam / rūpamakopyam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānamakopyam / evaṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitā anugantavyā //
body.translated_text: the own-nature of <s>vijñāna</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>vijñāna</s>, are <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> has the nature of the boundlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> has the nature of the boundlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Rūpa</s> is empty, having the nature of boundlessness. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is empty, having the nature of boundlessness. <s>Rūpa</s> has the boundlessness of mind and mental factors. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> has the boundlessness of mind and mental factors. <s>Rūpa</s> is the arising of the conduct of mind. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is the arising of the conduct of mind. <s>Rūpa</s> is wholesome and unwholesome, yet ultimately non-apprehensible. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is wholesome and unwholesome, yet ultimately non-apprehensible. <s>Rūpa</s> is equal to the lion's roar. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is equal to the lion's roar. <s>Rūpa</s> is unshakeable. Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is unshakeable. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be followed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>."

body.text: yadāyaṃ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattva evamenāṃ prajñāpāramitāmanugamiṣyati, vyavacārayiṣyati avatariṣyati avabhotsyate cintayiṣyati tulayiṣyati upaparīkṣiṣyate bhāvayiṣyati sarvamāyāśāṭhyavivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, sarvamanyanāvivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, ātmotkarṣaṇavivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, sarvakausīdyavivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, parapaṃsanāvivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, ātmasaṃjñāvivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, sattvasaṃjñāvivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, lābhasatkāraślokavivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, pañcanīvaraṇavivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, īrṣyāmātsaryavivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, sarveñjanāvivarjitairmanasikāraiḥ, tadā nāsya durlabhā bhaviṣyati sarvaguṇānāṃ paripūriḥ, buddhakṣetrasyānuttarāṇāṃ ca buddhadharmāṇāṃ paripūririti //
body.translated_text: "When, <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> thus follows, discerns, enters into, awakens to, reflects upon, weighs, examines, and cultivates this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—with attentions free from all deceit and dishonesty, with attentions free from all pride, with attentions free from self-exaltation, with attentions free from all laziness, with attentions free from disparaging others, with attentions free from the perception of self, with attentions free from the perception of a being, with attentions free from gain, honor, and fame, with attentions free from the five hindrances, with attentions free from jealousy and miserliness, with attentions free from all trickery—then the fulfillment of all qualities, the fulfillment of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), and the fulfillment of the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> will not be difficult for him to attain."

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmanugamaparivarto nāmaikonatriṃśattamaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the twenty-ninth chapter, called the Chapter on Following.

body.text: ASP_30: sadāpraruditaparivartastriṃśattamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Thirty of the <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>: the Chapter on <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping), the thirtieth.

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tatheyaṃ prajñāpāramitā paryeṣṭavyā, yathā sadāpraruditena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena paryeṣitā, ya etarhi bhīṣmagarjitanirghoṣasvarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ carati / evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan sadāpraruditena bodhisattvena mahāsattveneyaṃ prajñāpāramitā paryeṣitā? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sadāpraruditena subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pūrvaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ paryeṣamāṇena kāye 'narthikena jīvitanirapekṣeṇa lābhasatkāraślokeṣvaniśritena paryeṣamāṇena paryeṣitā / tena prajñāpāramitāṃ paryeṣamāṇena araṇyagatena antarīkṣānnirghoṣaḥ śruto 'bhūt - gaccha tvaṃ kulaputra pūrvasyāṃ diśi / tataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyasi / tathā ca gaccha, yathā na kāyaklamathamanasikāramutpādayasi, na styānamiddhamanasikāramutpādayasi, na bhojanamanasikāramutpādayasi, na pānīyamanasikāramutpādayasi, na rātrimanasikāramutpādayasi, na divasamanasikāramutpādayasi, na śītamanasikāramutpādayasi, noṣṇamanasikāramutpādayasi / mā ca kvaciccittaṃ praṇidhāḥ adhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā / mā ca kulaputra vāmenālokayan gāḥ, mā dakṣiṇena, mā pūrveṇa, mā paścimena, mottareṇa, mordhvam, mādhaḥ, mā ca anuvidiśamavalokayan gāḥ / tathā ca kulaputra gaccha, yathā nātmato na satkāyataścalasi / yathā na rūpataścalasi, yathā na vedanāto na saṃjñāto na saṃskārataḥ, yathā na vijñānataścalasi / yo hyataścalati, sa vitiṣṭhate / kuto vitiṣṭhate? buddhadharmebhyo vitiṣṭhate / yo buddhadharmebhyo vitiṣṭhate, sa saṃsāre carati / yaḥ saṃsāre carati, sa na carati prajñāpāramitāyām / sa prajñāpāramitāṃ nānuprāpnotīti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be sought just as it was sought by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping), who now practices the holy life in the presence of <s>Bhīṣmagarjitanirghoṣasvara</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, did the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> seek this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, formerly sought <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> without regard for his body, without concern for his life, without relying on gain, honor, or fame. While seeking <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having gone to the wilderness, he heard a voice from the sky: 'Go, O son of good family, to the eastern direction. There you will hear <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And go in such a way that you do not generate attention to bodily fatigue, do not generate attention to torpor and drowsiness, do not generate attention to food, do not generate attention to drink, do not generate attention to night, do not generate attention to day, do not generate attention to cold, do not generate attention to heat. And do not fix your mind anywhere, internally or externally. And, O son of good family, do not go looking to the left, nor to the right, nor to the front, nor behind, nor upward, nor above, nor below, nor looking to the intermediate directions. And, O son of good family, go in such a way that you do not waver from self or from the body-aggregate; that you do not waver from form, that you do not waver from feeling, perception, or mental formations, that you do not waver from consciousness. For whoever wavers from these deviates. From what does he deviate? He deviates from the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. Whoever deviates from the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Whoever wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s> does not practice <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. He does not attain <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: evamukte sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastaṃ nirghoṣametadavocat - evaṃ vai kariṣyāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ? ahaṃ hi sarvasattvānāmālokaṃ kartukāmo buddhadharmān samudānetukāma iti / evamukte sa nirghoṣaḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra sadāprarudita //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said this to that voice: 'I shall do just so. Why is that? For I wish to create light for all beings, I wish to gather the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>.' When this was said, that voice said this to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family <s>Sadāprarudita</s>!'

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punar api śabdamaśrauṣīt / evaṃ cāśrauṣīt - śūnyatānimittāpraṇihiteṣu ca tvayā kulaputra sarvadharmeṣvadhimuktimutpādya prajñāpāramitā paryeṣṭavyā / nimittaparivarjitena bhāvaparivarjitena sattvadṛṣṭiparivarjitena ca tvayā bhavitavyam / pāpamitrāṇi ca tvayā kulaputra parivarjayitavyāni / kalyāṇamitrāṇi ca tvayā sevitavyāni bhaktavyāni paryupāsitavyāni, yāni ca śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānutpādājātāniruddhābhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti dharmaṃ deśayanti / evaṃ tvaṃ kulaputra pratipadyamāno nacireṇa prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyasi pustakagatāṃ vā dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣoḥ kāyagatām / yasya ca tvaṃ kulaputra antikātprajñāpāramitāṃ śṛṇuyāḥ śāstṛsaṃjñā tvayā tatrotpādayitavyā / kṛtajñena ca tvayā bhavitavyaṃ kṛtavedinā ca - eṣa mama kalyāṇamitraṃ yasyemāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantikācchṛṇomi / yāmahaṃ śṛṇvan
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> heard yet another sound. And he heard thus: 'You, O son of good family, having generated conviction in all <s>dharmas</s> as empty, signless, and wishless, should seek <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. You should be free from signs, free from existence-views, and free from the view of beings. And, O son of good family, you should avoid evil friends. And you should attend upon, serve, and wait upon spiritual friends—those who teach the <s>Dharma</s> that all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, signless, wishless, unborn, unarisen, unceased, and without inherent existence. Thus practicing, O son of good family, before long you will hear <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, whether in a written text or embodied in a <s>Dharma</s>-preaching <s>bhikṣu</s>. And, O son of good family, toward the one from whom you hear <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, you should generate the perception of a teacher. And you should be grateful and appreciative, thinking: "This is my spiritual friend, from whom I hear this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Hearing it—"

body.text: kṣiprameva avinivartanīyo bhaviṣyāmyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, āsannaś ca bhaviṣyāmi tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām / tathāgatāvirahiteṣu buddhakṣetreṣūpapatsye / akṣaṇāṃś ca vivarjayiṣyāmi / kṣaṇasaṃpadaṃ ca ārāgayiṣyāmīti / imāstvayā kulaputra anuśaṃsāḥ paritulayamānena dharmabhāṇake bhikṣau śāstṛsaṃjñotpādayitavyā / na ca tvayā kulaputra lokāmiṣapratisaṃyuktayā cittasaṃtatyā dharmabhāṇako bhikṣuranubaddhavyaḥ / dharmārthikena ca tvayā dharmagauraveṇa dharmabhāṇako bhikṣuranubaddhavyaḥ / mārakarmāṇi ca tvayā avaboddhavyāni / asti hi kulaputra māraḥ pāpīyān dharmabhāṇakasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya rūpaśabdagandharasasparśānupasaṃharati sevituṃ bhaktuṃ paryupāsitum / tāṃścāsāvabhibhūya upāyakauśalyena parisevate bhajate paryupāste / tatra ca tvayā kulaputra dharmabhāṇake bhikṣau nāprasādacittamutpādayitavyam / api tvevaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam - nāhaṃ tadupāyakauśalyaṃ jāne, yadeṣa upāyakauśalyaṃ prajānāti / eṣa sattvavinayena sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlaparigrahamupādāya enān dharmān pratisevate bhajate paryupāste / na hi kvacidbodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ saṅgo vā ārambaṇaṃ vā saṃvidyate / tatkṣaṇaṃ ca tvayā kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ bhūtanayaḥ pratyavekṣitavyaḥ / katamaś ca kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ bhūtanayaḥ? yaduta sarvadharmā asaṃkleśā avyavadānāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvadharmā hi svabhāvena śūnyāḥ / sarvadharmā hi niḥsattvā nirjīvā niṣpoṣā niṣpuruṣā niṣpudgalā māyopamāḥ svapnopamāḥ pratiśrutkopamāḥ pratibhāsopamāḥ / evaṃ tvaṃ kulaputra sarvadharmāṇāṃ bhūtanayaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇo dharmabhāṇakamanubadhnan nacireṇa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ niryāsyasi / aparam api tvaṃ kulaputra mārakarma samanvāhareḥ / sacetkulaputra dharmabhāṇakaḥ prajñāpāramitārthikaṃ kulaputramavasādayati, na samanvāharati, tatra tvayā kulaputra na prativāṇiḥ kartavyā / api tu dharmārthikenaiva dharmagauraveṇaiva anirviṇṇamānasena dharmabhāṇako bhikṣuranubaddhavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "—I shall quickly become irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening, and I shall be near to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. I shall be reborn in <s>buddha-kṣetras</s> not bereft of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I shall avoid the unfavorable states. And I shall obtain the good fortune of favorable conditions." Weighing these benefits, O son of good family, you should generate the perception of a teacher toward the <s>Dharma</s>-preaching <s>bhikṣu</s>. And, O son of good family, you should not follow the <s>Dharma</s>-preaching <s>bhikṣu</s> with a mental disposition connected to worldly gains. Rather, desiring the <s>Dharma</s>, with reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, you should follow the <s>Dharma</s>-preaching <s>bhikṣu</s>. And you should recognize the deeds of <s>Māra</s>. For, O son of good family, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One presents forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles to the <s>Dharma</s>-preaching <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> for him to attend upon, serve, and wait upon. But he, overcoming these through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), attends upon, serves, and waits upon the teacher. And, O son of good family, you should not generate a mind of displeasure toward the <s>Dharma</s>-preaching <s>bhikṣu</s>. Rather, you should generate this thought: "I do not know the <s>upāyakauśalya</s> that he knows. He, for the purpose of disciplining beings and gathering their wholesome roots, resorts to, serves, and attends upon these <s>dharmas</s>. For nowhere is there attachment or hindrance for <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>." And at that very moment, O son of good family, you should contemplate the true method of <s>dharmas</s>. And what, O son of good family, is the true method of <s>dharmas</s>? Namely, all <s>dharmas</s> are undefiled and unpurified. Why is that? For all <s>dharmas</s> are empty by their own nature. All <s>dharmas</s> are without a being, without a life-force, without a soul, without a person, without an individual—they are like illusions, like dreams, like echoes, like reflections. Thus, O son of good family, contemplating the true method of all <s>dharmas</s> while following the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, before long you will succeed in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And further, O son of good family, you should be aware of another deed of <s>Māra</s>: if, O son of good family, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher dismisses the son of good family who seeks <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and does not support him, then, O son of good family, you should not turn back. Rather, desiring the <s>Dharma</s>, with reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, with an unwearied mind, you should follow the <s>Dharma</s>-preaching <s>bhikṣu</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasya nirghoṣasyāntikādimāmanuśāsanīṃ pratigṛhya yena pūrvā dik tena pratikrāmati sma / aciraprakrāntasya cāsyaitadabhūt - na mayā sa nirghoṣaḥ paripṛṣṭaḥ - kiyaddūraṃ mayā gantavyamiti / sa tatraiva pṛthivīpradeśe sthito 'bhūt / tatra rudan krandan śocan paridevamānaḥ evaṃ cintayati sma - asminneva pṛthivīpradeśe ekaṃ vā rātriṃdivamatināmayiṣyāmi, dve vā, trīṇi vā, catvāri vā, pañca vā, ṣaḍ vā, sapta vā rātriṃdivānyatināmayiṣyāmi / na kāyaklamathamanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi / na styānamiddhamanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi / na bhojanamanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi / na pānīyamanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi / na rātrimanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi / na divasamanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi / na śītamanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi / noṣṇamanasikāramutpādayiṣyāmi, yāvanna prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyāmīti / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte kaścideva puruṣaḥ ekaputrake kālagate mahatā duḥkhadaurmanasyena samanvāgato 'bhavat, tasya putraśokena nānyaḥ kaścinmanasikāraḥ pravartate, api tvekaputrakamanasikāra eva pravartate / evameva subhūte sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tasmin
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, having received this instruction from that voice, set out toward the eastern direction. And shortly after setting out, this thought occurred to him: 'I did not ask that voice: "How far must I go?"' He stood right there on that spot of earth. There, weeping, wailing, lamenting, and grieving, he thought thus: 'On this very spot of earth I shall spend one night and day, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven nights and days. I shall not generate attention to bodily fatigue. I shall not generate attention to torpor and drowsiness. I shall not generate attention to food. I shall not generate attention to drink. I shall not generate attention to night. I shall not generate attention to day. I shall not generate attention to cold. I shall not generate attention to heat—until I hear <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, when a certain man's only son has died, he is overcome with great grief and sorrow, and no other mental attention arises in him except attention to his only son—just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> at that—

body.text: samaye nānyaḥ kaścinmanasikāraḥ pravartate sma, api tu kadā nāmāhaṃ tāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyāmīti //
body.translated_text: —time, no other mental attention arose, but only: 'When shall I hear that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?'

body.text: atha khalu subhūte sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tathotkaṇṭhitasya tathāgatavigrahaḥ purataḥ sthitvā sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamenāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣase / evaṃ hi kulaputra paurvakair api tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caradbhiḥ prajñāpāramitā paryeṣitā, yathā tvametarhi paryeṣase / tena hi tvaṃ kulaputra etenaiva vīryeṇa etenaivotsāhenaṃ etayaivārthikatayā etayaiva cchandikatayā anubadhya pūrvāmeva diśaṃ gaccha / asti kulaputra itaḥ pañcabhiryojanaśatairgandhavatī nāma nagarī saptaratnamayī, saptabhiḥ prākārairanuparikṣiptā, saptabhiḥ parikhābhiḥ saptabhistālapaṅktibhiranuparikṣiptā, dvādaśa yojanāni āyāmena, dvādaśa yojanāni vistāreṇa, ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca pañcabhirantarāpaṇavīthiśatairālekhyavicitrasadṛśairdarśanīyairnirviddhā asamasamairanutpīḍajanayugyayānasaṃkramaṇasthānasthāpitaiḥ sumāpitā / samantataḥ prākārāś ca tasyā nagaryāḥ saptaratnamayāḥ / teṣāṃ ca saptaratnamayānāṃ prākārāṇāṃ jāmbūnadasya suvarṇasya khoḍakaśīrṣāṇi pramāṇavantyupodgatāni / sarvasmiṃś ca khoḍakaśīrṣe saptaratnamayo vṛkṣo jāto nānāvicitrai ratnamayaiḥ phalaiḥ phalavān / sarvataś ca khoḍakavṛkṣādratnamayaṃ sūtraṃ dvitīyaṃ khoḍakavṛkṣāntaramavasaktam / sarvāvatī ca sā nagarī sauvarṇena kiṅkiṇījālena praticchannā / tasya ca kiṅkiṇījālasya vāteneritasya valgurmanojño rañjanīyaḥ śabdo niścarati / tadyathāpi nāma pañcāṅgikasya tūryasya sametya saṃgītyāṃ kuśalairgandharvaiḥ saṃpravāditasya valgurmanojño rañjanīyo nirghoṣo niścarati, evameva tasya kiṅkiṇījālasya vāteritasya valgurmanojño rañjanīyo nirghoṣo niścarati / tena ca śabdena te sattvāḥ krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti / samantācca tasyā nagaryāḥ parikhā vāriparipūrṇā anusārivārivāhinyo vāriṇo nātiśītasya nātyuṣṇasya pūrṇāḥ / tasmiṃś ca vāriṇi nāvaḥ saptānāṃ ratnānāṃ vicitrā darśanīyāsteṣāmeva sattvānāṃ pūrvakarmavipākenābhinirvṛttāḥ, yāsu te sattvā abhiruhya krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti / sarvaṃ ca tadvāri utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchāditam, anyaiś ca abhijātābhijātaiḥ sugandhagandhibhiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃchāditam / nāsti sā kācittrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau puṣpajātiryā tatra nāsti / samantācca tasyā nagaryāḥ pañcodyānaśatāni / sarvāṇi tāni saptaratnamayāni vicitrāṇi darśanīyāni / ekaikasmiṃścodyāne pañca pañca puṣkariṇīśatāni / krośaḥ krośaḥ pramāṇaṃ samantāttatpuṣkariṇīnām / sarvāsu tāsu puṣkariṇīṣu saptaratnamayāni vicitrāṇi darśanīyāni utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāṇi jātāni, yaistadudakaṃ saṃchāditam / sarvāṇi ca tānyutpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāni śakaṭacakrapramāṇapariṇāhāni sugandhāni nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanidarśanāni nīlanirbhāsāni, pītāni pītavarṇāni pītanidarśanāni pītanirbhāsāni, lohitāni lohitavarṇāni lohitanidarśanāni lohitanirbhāsāni, avadātāni avadātavarṇānyavadātanidarśanānyavadātanirbhāsāni / sarvāś ca tāḥ puṣkariṇyo haṃsasārasakāraṇḍavakrauñcacakravākopanikūjitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Subhūti</s>, before the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, who was thus longing, a form of the <s>Tathāgata</s> appeared standing before him and gave its approval: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! Just so did the former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, when formerly practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> course, seek <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, just as you now seek it. Therefore, O son of good family, with just this vigor, just this zeal, just this desire, just this aspiration, continue to go to the eastern direction. There is, O son of good family, five hundred <s>yojanas</s> from here, a city named <s>Gandhavatī</s>, made of the seven precious substances, surrounded by seven walls, seven moats, and seven rows of <s>tāla</s> (palm) trees, twelve <s>yojanas</s> in length and twelve <s>yojanas</s> in breadth, prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, traversed by five hundred market streets that are beautiful as paintings and lovely to behold, with even and unobstructed spaces for people, yoked animals, and vehicles to pass. All around the walls of that city are made of the seven precious substances. On those walls of the seven precious substances are pinnacles of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, proportionate and rising high. On each pinnacle grows a tree of the seven precious substances, bearing fruit of various wonderful jewels. And from each pinnacle-tree, a string of jewels hangs to the next pinnacle-tree. And that entire city is covered with a net of golden bells. When that net of bells is stirred by the wind, it produces a sweet, pleasant, and delightful sound—just as when a five-part musical ensemble is played by skilled <s>gandharvas</s> in concert, a sweet, pleasant, and delightful melody issues forth—just so, when that net of bells is stirred by the wind, a sweet, pleasant, and delightful melody issues forth. And with that sound those beings sport, enjoy themselves, and take pleasure. All around that city, the moats are filled with water, with flowing streams, filled with water that is neither too cold nor too hot. In that water there are boats, ornamented with the seven precious substances, beautiful to behold, produced by the ripening of the former deeds of those very beings, in which those beings climb aboard and sport, enjoy themselves, and take pleasure. And all that water is covered with <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses), <s>padmas</s> (lotuses), <s>kumudas</s> (white water-lilies), and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> (white lotuses), and covered with other noble and fragrant flowers. There is no species of flower in the trichiliocosm that is not found there. All around that city are five hundred parks, all made of the seven precious substances, variegated and beautiful to behold. In each park there are five hundred lotus ponds, each a <s>krośa</s> in extent on every side. In all those lotus ponds, <s>utpalas</s>, <s>padmas</s>, <s>kumudas</s>, and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> made of the seven precious substances, variegated and beautiful to behold, have grown, covering the water. All those <s>utpalas</s>, <s>padmas</s>, <s>kumudas</s>, and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> are as large in circumference as a cart-wheel, fragrant, blue with blue color, blue in appearance, and blue in radiance; yellow with yellow color, yellow in appearance, and yellow in radiance; red with red color, red in appearance, and red in radiance; white with white color, white in appearance, and white in radiance. And all those lotus ponds resound with the calls of <s>haṃsas</s> (swans), <s>sārasas</s> (cranes), <s>kāraṇḍavas</s> (ducks), <s>krauñcas</s> (herons), and <s>cakravākas</s> (ruddy geese)—

body.text:
sarvāni ca tānyudyānāni amamānyaparigrahāṇi, teṣāmeva sattvānāṃ pūrvakarmavipākenābhinirvṛttāni, yathāpi nāma dīrgharātraṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritavatāṃ buddhanetrīcitrīkārānugatasugataśrutacittānāṃ sattvānāṃ dīrgharātraṃ gambhīreṣu dharmeṣvadhimuktānām / tatra ca kulaputra gandhavatyāṃ nagaryāṃ madhyeśṛṅgāṭakasya dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya gṛhaṃ yojanaṃ samantāt / saptānāṃ ratnānāṃ citraṃ darśanīyam / saptabhiḥ prākāraiḥ saptabhistālapaṅktibhiranuparikṣiptam / tasmiṃś ca gṛhe catvāryudyānāni gṛhaparibhogopabhogaparibhogāya / nityapramuditaṃ ca nāmodyānam / aśokaṃ ca nāma śokavigataṃ ca nāma puṣpacitraṃ ca nāmodyānam / ekaikasmiṃścodyāne 'ṣṭāvaṣṭau puṣkariṇyo yaduta bhadrā ca nāma, bhadrottamā ca nāma, nandā ca nāma, nandottamā ca nāma, kṣamā ca nāma, kṣamottamā ca nāma, niyatā ca nāma, avivāhā ca nāma / tāsāṃ ca khalu puṣkariṇīnāmekaṃ pārśvaṃ sauvarṇamayaṃ dvitīyaṃ pārśvaṃ rūpyamayaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pārśvaṃ vaidūryamayaṃ caturthaṃ pārśvaṃ sphaṭikamayam / adhobhūmiḥ karketanamayī, suvarṇavālukāstīrṇā / ekaikasyāṃ ca puṣkariṇyāmaṣṭāvaṣṭau sopānāni nānāvicitrai ratnamayaiḥ sopānaphalakaiḥ pratimaṇḍitāni / sarvasmiṃś ca sopānaphalakavivarāntare jāmbūnadasya suvarṇasya kadalīvṛkṣo jātaḥ / sarvāś ca tāḥ puṣkariṇyo nānotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchāditasalilā haṃsasārasakāraṇḍavakrauñcacakravākopakūjitāḥ / samantācca tāsāṃ puṣkariṇīnāṃ nānācitrāḥ puṣpavṛkṣā jātāḥ / teṣāṃ puṣpavṛkṣāṇāṃ vāteneritāni puṣpāṇi puṣkariṇīṣu patanti / sarvāsu ca tāsu puṣkariṇīṣu candanagandhikaṃ vāri, varṇopetaṃ rasopetaṃ sparśopetam / tatra ca dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saparivāro 'ṣṭaṣaṣṭayā strīsahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūtaḥ krīḍati ramate paricārayati / ye 'pi
tatra nagare anye sattvā vāstavyāḥ, striyaś ca puruṣāśca, te 'pi sarve nityapramuditā udyāneṣu puṣkariṇīṣu ca pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitāḥ samanvaṅgībhūtāḥ krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti / sa khalu punardharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sārdhaṃ parivāreṇa tāvatkālaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati, tatastrikālaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ deśayati / ye 'pi te sattvāstatra gandhavatyāṃ nagaryāṃ vāstavyāḥ te 'pi madhyenagaraśṛṅgāṭakasya dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya āsanaṃ prajñapayanti, suvarṇapādakaṃ vā rūpyapādakaṃ vā vaiḍūryapādakaṃ vā sphaṭikapādakaṃ vā, tūlikāstīrṇaṃ vā, goṇikāstīrṇaṃ vā, uparigarbholikaṃ vā, kāśikavastrapratyāstaraṇaṃ vā ardhakrośamuccaistvena / upariṣṭāccāntarīkṣe cailavitānaṃ muktāvicitritaṃ samaṃ sahitā niratāḥ kimayaṃ saṃsthita iti susaṃsthitavicitravipākatayā dhārayanti / samantācca taṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ pañcavarṇikaiḥ kusumairabhyavakiranti saṃpravikiranti / nānāgandhadhūpadhūpitaṃ ca taṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ kurvanti, yathāpīdaṃ dharmāśayaviśuddhyā tasya dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dharmagauraveṇa ca / tatra dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo niṣaṇṇaḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ deśayati / evaṃrūpeṇa kulaputra dharmagauraveṇa dharmāṇāṃ saṃniśrayatayā
body.translated_text: —and all those parks are ownerless and without possessions, brought into existence by the ripening of the former deeds of those very beings—just as for beings who have long practiced the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, whose minds have followed the guidance of the Buddha-eye and the adornment of the <s>Sugata</s>'s teaching, who have long had faith in the profound <s>dharmas</s>. And in that city of <s>Gandhavatī</s>—

body.text: śraddheyaśraddadhānatayā śraddhotpādanena te sattvā dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyāntikātprajñāpāramitāṃ śṛṇvanti / tatra ca bahūni prāṇiśatāni bahūni prāṇisahasrāṇi bahūni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni devamanuṣyāṇāṃ śṛṇvanti / tato 'nye keciduddiśanti, kecitsvādhyāyanti, kecillikhanti, kecidyoniśomanasikāreṇānugacchanti / sarvaṃ ca te sattvā avinipātadharmāṇo 'vinivartanīyā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / tasya tvaṃ kulaputra dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyāntikaṃ gaccha / tataḥ śroṣyasi prajñāpāramitām / sa hi tava kulaputra dīrgharātraṃ kalyāṇamitraṃ saṃdarśakaḥ samādāpakaḥ samuttejakaḥ saṃpraharṣako 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / tenāpi kulaputra pūrvamevaṃ prajñāpāramitā paryeṣitā, yathā tvametarhi paryeṣase / gaccha tvaṃ kulaputra rātriṃdivamadhiṣṭhitamanasikāramutpādayamāno nacireṇa prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyasi //
body.translated_text: —through the trustworthiness of their faith and the arising of their confidence, those beings hear the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. And there, many hundreds of living beings, many thousands of living beings, many hundreds of thousands of living beings, both gods and humans, have gathered and listen. And among them, some recite, some study, some write—

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ idaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanaskaḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'bhūt / tadyathāpi nāma puruṣaḥ saviṣeṇa śalyena viddho nānyaṃ manasikāramutpādayati, api tu kadā nāmāhaṃ śalyahartāraṃ vaidyaṃ lapsye yo mamedaṃ śalyamuddhariṣyati, yo māmito duḥkhānmocayiṣyatīti / evameva sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasmin samaye nānyaṃ kaṃciddharmaṃ manasi karoti, api tu kadā nāmāhaṃ taṃ kulaputraṃ drakṣyāmi yo māṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śrāvayiṣyati, yanmama dharmaṃ śrutvā upalambhamanasikārāḥ prahāsyanta iti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, having heard this, became pleased, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with rapture and happiness. Just as a man pierced by a poisoned arrow produces no other thought than: 'When shall I obtain a physician, a remover of arrows, who will extract this arrow from me, who will release me from this suffering?'—

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasminneva pṛthivīpradeśe sthitaḥ tasya dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāṃ deśayataḥ śṛṇoti sma / śṛṇvaṃś ca sarvadharmeṣvaniśritasaṃjñāmutpādayati sma / tasyānekāni samādhimukhānyāmukhībhūtānyabhūvan / tadyathāsarvadharmasvabhāvavyavalokano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmasvabhāvānupalabdhirnāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmasvabhāvajñānanirgamo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmanirnānātvo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmanirvikāradarśī nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmāvabhāsakaro nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmatamopagato nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmajñānavidhvaṃsano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmavidhūnano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmānupalabdhirnāma samādhiḥ / kusumābhikīrṇo nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmātmabhāvābhinirhāro nāma samādhiḥ / māyāvivarjito nāma samādhiḥ / ādarśamaṇḍalapratibhāsanirhāro nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvarutanirhāro nāma samādhiḥ / rajopagato nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvābhipramodano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvarutakauśalyānugato nāma samādhiḥ / nānārutapadavyañjanābhinirhāro nāma samādhiḥ / astambhito nāma samādhiḥ / prakṛtyavyavahāro nāma samādhiḥ / anāvaraṇavimokṣaprāpto nāma samādhiḥ / rājopagato nāma samādhiḥ / nāmaniruktipadavyañjano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmavipaśyano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmaviṣayāpagato nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmānāvaraṇakoṭirnāma samādhiḥ / gaganakalpo nāma samādhiḥ / vajropamo nāma samādhiḥ / āsannarūparājo nāma samādhiḥ / asapatnarājo nāma samādhiḥ / jayalabdho nāma samādhiḥ / avivartyacakṣurnāma samādhiḥ / dharmadhātuniyato nāma samādhiḥ / dharmadhātunirgato nāma samādhiḥ / āśvāsadātā nāma samādhiḥ / siṃhābhigarjito
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, standing in that very spot of earth, heard the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> teaching the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And while listening, he produced the perception of non-reliance regarding all <s>dharmas</s>. Many doors of <s>samādhi</s> opened before him, namely: the <s>samādhi</s> called 'own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>'—

body.text: nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasattvābhibhavano nāma samādhiḥ / vigatarajo nāma samādhiḥ / asaṃkliṣṭo nāma samādhiḥ / padmavyūho nāma samādhiḥ / kāṅkṣocchedano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasārānugato nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmābhyudgato nāma samādhiḥ / abhijñābalavaiśāradyaprāpto nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmanirvedhako nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmavibhavamudrā nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmavibhavasamudro nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmanirviśeṣadarśī nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadṛṣṭikṛtagahanavivarjito nāma samādhiḥ / tamopagato nāma samādhiḥ / sarvadharmanimittāpagato nāma samādhiḥ / sarvasaṅgavimukto nāma samādhiḥ / sarvakausīdyāpagato nāma samādhiḥ / gambhīradharmaprabhākaro nāma samādhiḥ / merukalpo nāma samādhiḥ / asaṃhāryo nāma samādhiḥ / māramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsanakaro nāma samādhiḥ / trailokyānabhiniviṣṭo nāma samādhiḥ / raśminirhāro nāma samādhiḥ / tathāgatadarśano nāma samādhiḥ / sarvatathāgatadarśī nāma samādhiḥ / sa eṣu samādhiṣu sthitaḥ san daśadiśi loke buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyati sma aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān imāmeva prajñāpāramitāṃ prakāśayato bodhisattvebhyo mahāsattvebhyaḥ / te ca tathāgatāḥ sādhukāraṃ dadati sma, svāsanaṃ cāsya kurvanti sma / evaṃ cāvocan - asmābhir api kulaputra pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caradbhirevameva prajñāpāramitā parigaveṣitā / parigaveṣamāṇaiś ca ete eva samādhayaḥ pratilabdhāḥ, ye tvayaitarhi pratilabdhāḥ / enāṃś ca samādhīn pratilabhya gatiṃgatāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, prajñāpāramitāyāmavinivartanīyeṣu buddhadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhitāḥ / te vayameteṣāmeva samādhīnāṃ prakṛtiṃ svabhāvaṃ vyavalokayantastaṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmo yaḥ samāpadyate vā vyuttiṣṭhate vā, yo bodhāya caret, yo vā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeta / iyaṃ sā kulaputra prajñāpāramitā, yā na kenaciddharmeṇa manyamānatā / amanyamānatāsthitairasmābhiriyamevaṃrūpā kāyasya suvarṇavarṇatā pratilabdhā / dvātriṃśacca mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni / aśītiścānuvyañjanāni / vyāmaprabhatā ca / acintyaṃ ca anuttaraṃ buddhajñānaṃ buddhaprajñā, anuttaraś ca buddhasamādhiḥ, sarvabuddhadharmaguṇapāramitā ca anuprāptā yasyā guṇapāramitāyā na śakyaṃ tathāgataireva tāvatpramāṇaṃ grahītuṃ paryanto vā nidarśayitum, kiṃ punaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ? tasmāttarhi kulaputra eteṣveva tvayā dharmeṣu gauravamutpādayitavyaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā arthikatayā chandikatayā ca / arthikasya hi kulaputra chandikasya ca na durlabhā bhavatyanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ / kalyāṇamitreṣu ca tvayā kulaputra tīvraṃ gauravamutpādayitavyam, prema ca karaṇīyam, prasādaś ca karaṇīyaḥ / kalyāṇamitraparigṛhītā hi bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kṣiprameva anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante //
body.translated_text: —the <s>samādhi</s> called 'overcoming all beings'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'free from defilement'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'unafflicted'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'lotus array'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'cutting off doubt'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'penetrating all essences'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'surpassing all <s>dharmas</s>'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'attaining superknowledges, powers, and fearlessnesses'; the <s>samādhi</s> called 'penetrating all <s>dharmas</s>'—

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāṃstathāgatānetadavocat - ko 'smākaṃ kalyāṇamitramiti? ta enametadavocan - dīrgharātraṃ tvaṃ kulaputra dharmodgatena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripācitaḥ parigṛhītaś ca / prajñāpāramitāyāmupāyakauśalye buddhadharmeṣu ca śikṣāpitaḥ / sa tava kulaputra parigrāhakaḥ kalyāṇamitraṃ ca / tattvayā kṛtajñatayā kṛtaveditayā ca satkṛtya tatkṛtaṃ dhārayitavyam / sacettvaṃ kulaputra dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> spoke thus to those <s>Tathāgatas</s>: "Who is our spiritual friend?" They spoke thus to him: "For a long time, son of good family, you have been matured and taken care of by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> regarding <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. He has instructed you in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, in <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), and in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>—"

body.text: mahāsattvamekaṃ vā kalpaṃ dvau vā kalpau trīn vā kalpān kalpaśataṃ vā kalpasahasraṃ vā kalpaśatasahasraṃ vā tato vā uttare cailoṇḍukamiva śirasā parikarṣeḥ, sarvasattvasukhopasthānaṃ cāsyopasthāpayeḥ, yāvantastrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau rūpaśabdagandharasasparśāḥ, tān sarvānupanāmayeḥ / evam api tvayā kulaputra tasya kulaputrasya naiva kṛtasya pratikṛtaṃ bhavet / tatkasya hetoḥ? tasya hi kulaputra kulaputrasya anubhāvena tavaiṣāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ samādhīnāṃ pratilambhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaśravaś ca prajñāpāramitāpratilambhaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ //
body.translated_text: the <s>Mahāsattva</s> for one <s>kalpa</s>, or two <s>kalpas</s>, or three <s>kalpas</s>, or a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, or a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, or a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, or even more, carrying him on your head like a ball of mud, and were to attend him with all comforts for all beings, and were to present to him all the forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangible objects in the three-thousand-fold great world-system—even so, son of good family, you would not have repaid what was done for you by that son of good family. What is the reason? For it is through the power of that son of good family that your attainment of such <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) has come about, and your hearing of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, and your attainment of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, have come about.

body.text: atha khalu te tathāgatāḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ samāśvāsya antarhitā abhūvan / sa ca kulaputrastebhyaḥ samādhibhyo vyudasthāt / vyutthitasya cāsya etadabhūt - kutaste tathāgatāḥ, kva vā te tathāgatā iti / sa tāṃstathāgatānapaśyan mahatīmutkaṇṭhāṃ paritasanaṃ cāpannaḥ / tasyaitadabhūt - āryo dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dhāraṇīpratilabdhaḥ pañcābhijñaḥ pūrvajinakṛtādhikāraḥ mama saṃparigrāhakaḥ kalyāṇamitraṃ ca / dīrgharātraṃ ca mama tenārthaḥ kṛtaḥ / yannvahametamarthaṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamabhigamyopasaṃkramya paripṛccheyam - kutaste tathāgatā āgatāḥ, kva vā te tathāgatā gatā iti //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having consoled the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping), disappeared. And that son of good family arose from those <s>samādhis</s>. And having arisen, this thought occurred to him: 'Where have those <s>Tathāgatas</s> gone? Where are those <s>Tathāgatas</s>?' Not seeing those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, he fell into great longing and distress. This thought occurred to him: 'The noble <s>Dharmodgata</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, who has obtained <s>dhāraṇī</s>, who possesses the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), who has served former Conquerors, is my supporter and spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). For a long time he has done me great service. Let me approach and go to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> about this matter and ask: "From where have those <s>Tathāgatas</s> come? Where have those <s>Tathāgatas</s> gone?"'

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmodgate bodhisattve mahāsattve prema ca prasādaṃ ca citrīkāraṃ ca gauravaṃ ca upasthāpayati / upasthāpya evaṃ prācintayat - kiyadrūpayā nu khalvahaṃ satkriyayā taṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamupasaṃkrāmeyam? daridraścāsmi / na ca me kiṃcittathārūpaṃ vastraṃ vā ratnaṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā maṇayo vā muktā vā vaidūryaṃ vā śaṅkhaśilā vā pravālaṃ vā rajataṃ vā puṣpaṃ vā dhūpo vā gandho vā mālyaṃ vā vilepanaṃ vā cūrṇaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā chatraṃ vā dhvajaṃ vā ghaṇṭā vā patākā vā saṃvidyate / kenāhaṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkuryāṃ gurukuryām? na ca mamaitatpratirūpaṃ bhavet, yadahamevameva dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamupasaṃkrāmeyam / daridraścāsmi / na ca me prītirvā prāmodhaṃ votpadyate //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> generated affection, faith, reverence, and respect for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. Having generated them, he reflected: 'With what kind of honor should I approach the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>? I am poor. I have nothing of the kind—no garments, no jewels, no gold, no gems, no pearls, no <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), no conch-stone, no coral, no silver, no flowers, no incense, no perfume, no garlands, no ointments, no powder, no robes, no parasols, no banners, no bells, no flags. With what shall I honor the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>? It would not be fitting for me to approach the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> just like this. I am poor, and neither joy nor gladness arises in me.'

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃrūpairguṇairgauravamanasikārairgacchan anupūrveṇa anyataraṃ nagaramanuprāpto 'bhūt / tatra tasyāntarāpaṇamadhyagatasya etadabhūt - yannvahamimamātmabhāvaṃ vikrīya tena mūlyena dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya satkāraṃ kuryām / dīrgharātraṃ hi mamātmabhāvasahasrāṇi bhagnāni kṣīṇāni niruddhāni vikrītāni / punaḥ punaraparimāṇe saṃsāre aparimāṇāni ca nirayaduḥkhāni mayā kāmahetoḥ kāmanidānamanubhūtāni / na punarevaṃrūpāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kṛtaśa evaṃrūpāṇāṃ vā sattvānāṃ satkārāyeti / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvontarāpaṇamadhyagataḥ śabdamanuśrāvayāmāsa, ghoṣamudīrayati sma - kaḥ puruṣeṇārthikaḥ, kaḥ puruṣeṇārthikaḥ, kaḥ puruṣaṃ kretumicchatīti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, going with such qualities and thoughts of respect, in due course arrived at a certain city. There, having gone into the midst of the marketplace, this thought occurred to him: 'Let me sell this body and with the price make an offering to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. For a long time thousands of my bodies have been destroyed, exhausted, perished, and wasted. Again and again in immeasurable <s>saṃsāra</s>, immeasurable sufferings of the hells have been experienced by me for the sake of desire, caused by desire. But never before for the sake of such <s>dharmas</s> or for the honor of such beings.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, having gone into the midst of the marketplace, raised his voice and proclaimed: 'Who needs a man? Who needs a man? Who wishes to buy a man?'

body.text: atha khalu mārasya pāpīyasa etadabhūt - ayaṃ sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmakāmatayā yadyātmānaṃ vikrīya dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya satkāraṃ kariṣyati,
body.translated_text: Then the evil <s>Māra</s> thought: 'If this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, out of desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, sells himself and makes an offering to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>,

body.text: prajñāpāramitāmupāyakauśalyaṃ ca pariprakṣyati - kathaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran kṣipramanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariniṣpatsyate iti, tadā śrutasāgaratāṃ cānuprāpsyati, adhṛṣyaś ca bhaviṣyati māreṇa vā mārakāyikābhirvā devatābhiḥ, sarvaguṇapāramitāṃ cānuprāpsyati / tatra ca bahūnāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ kariṣyati / tāṃś ca mama viṣayādatikrāmayiṣyati anyāṃś ca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya / yannvahamasyāntarāyaṃ kuryāmiti //
body.translated_text: and asks about the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means—"How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> quickly reach fulfillment in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>?"—then he will attain an ocean of learning (<s>śrutasāgara</s>), and he will become invincible by <s>Māra</s> or by the deities of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, and he will attain the perfection of all qualities. And he will be of benefit to many beings, and he will lead them beyond my domain, and others too, by awakening to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Let me create an obstacle for him!'

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyāṃstān brāhmaṇagṛhapatikāṃstathā pratyutthāpayāmāsa, yathā te taṃ ghoṣaṃ nāśrauṣuḥ sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya - kaḥ puruṣeṇārthikaḥ, kaḥ puruṣeṇārthikaḥ, kaḥ puruṣaṃ kretumicchatīti / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yadā ātmanaḥ krāyakaṃ na labhate, tadā ekāntaṃ gatvā prārodīt, aśrūṇi prāvartayat / evaṃ cāvocat - aho batāsmākaṃ durlabdhā lābhāḥ, ye vayamātmabhāvasyāpi krāyakaṃ na labhāmahe - yadvayamātmabhāvaṃ vikrīya dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkuryāmeti //
body.translated_text: Then the evil <s>Māra</s> influenced those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders in such a way that they did not hear the cry of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'Who needs a man? Who needs a man? Who wishes to buy a man?' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, when he did not find a buyer for himself, went to a secluded place and wept, shedding tears. And he said: 'Alas, how unlucky we are! We cannot even find a buyer for our own body—that we might sell our body and honor the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>!'

body.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhūt - yannvahaṃ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ tulayeyam - kiṃ nvayaṃ sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'dhyāśayapratipanna ātmabhāvaparityāgaṃ prati dharmakāmatayā, uta neti / atha khalu śakro devānāmindro māṇavakaveṣamabhinirmāya yena sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāmati sma / upasaṃkramya sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - kiṃ tvaṃ kulaputra dīnadīnamanā utkaṇṭhitamānaso 'śrūṇi pravartayamānaḥ sthitaḥ? sadāpraruditastamevamāha - ahaṃ māṇavaka ātmānaṃ vikretukāmaḥ / asya cātmabhāvasya krāyakaṃ na labhe / taṃ māṇavakarūpī śakra āha - kasya punastvaṃ kulaputra arthāya ātmānaṃ vikretukāmaḥ? sadāpraruditastamāha - ahaṃ māṇavaka dharmakāmatayā imamātmānaṃ vikrīya dharmapūjāṃ kartukāmaḥ, āryaṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkartukāmaḥ / so 'hamasyātmabhāvasya krāyakaṃ na labhe / tasya me etadabhūt - aho batāhamatyalpapuṇyaḥ, yo 'hamasyātmabhāvasyāpi krāyakaṃ na labhe, yena taṃ vikrīya prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjāṃ kuryām, āryaṃ ca dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkuryāmiti / atha khalu māṇavakaḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - na khalu mama kulaputra puruṣeṇa kṛtyam / api tu khalu punaḥ piturbhe yajño yaṣṭavyaḥ / tatra me puruṣasya hṛdayena kṛtyam, lohitena ca asthimajjayā ca / taddāsyasi tvaṃ krayeṇa? atha khalu sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaitadabhūt - lābhā me paramasulabdhāḥ, pariniṣpannaṃ cātmabhāvaṃ jāne prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalye buddhadharmeṣu ca, yanmayāyaṃ māṇavakaḥ krāyako labdhaḥ hṛdayasya rudhirasya ca asthimajjāyāśceti / sa hṛṣṭacittaḥ kalyacittaḥ pramuditacittastaṃ māṇavakametadavocat - dāsyāmi māṇavaka yena yenaiva te iti ātmabhāvādarthaḥ / sa tametadavocat - kiṃ te kulaputra mūlyaṃ dadāmi? sa tametadavocat - yatte māṇavaka parityaktam, taddehīti / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ viddhvā lohitaṃ niḥsrāvayati sma / dakṣiṇaṃ coruṃ viddhvā nirmāṃsaṃ kṛtvā asthi bhettuṃ kuḍyamūlamupasaṃkrāmati sma /
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'Let me test the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: Is this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> truly established in his resolve regarding the sacrifice of his body for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>, or not?' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, manifesting himself in the form of a young <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'Why, son of good family, do you stand here wretched and miserable in mind, full of longing, shedding tears?' <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said this to him: 'I, young man, wish to sell myself. But I cannot find a buyer for this body.' The young man who was <s>Śakra</s> in disguise said to him: 'For what purpose, son of good family, do you wish to sell yourself?' <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said to him: 'I, young man, out of desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, wish to sell this body to make a <s>Dharma</s>-offering, to honor the noble <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. But I cannot find a buyer for this body. And this thought occurred to me: "Alas, how small my merit is, that I cannot find a buyer even for this body, that I might sell it and make an offering to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and honor the noble <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>."' Then the young man said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'I do not actually need a man, son of good family. But my father has a sacrifice to perform. For that I need a man's heart, blood, and bone-marrow. Will you sell those?' Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'My gains are supremely well gained! I know my body to be perfected for the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, skill in means, and the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, since I have found this young man as a buyer for my heart, blood, and bone-marrow!' Joyful, glad, and delighted in mind, he said this to the young man: 'I shall give you, young man, whatever you need from my body.' He said to him: 'What price shall I give you, son of good family?' He said to him: 'Whatever you are willing to give, young man, give that.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, taking a sharp weapon, pierced his right arm and let the blood flow out; and piercing his right thigh, having stripped it of flesh, he approached a wall-base to split the bone.

body.text: atha khalu anyatarā śreṣṭhidārakā upariṣṭātprāsādatalagatābhūt / sā adrākṣītsadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ bāhuṃ viddhvā rudhiraṃ niḥsrāvya ūruṃ nirmāṃsaṃ kṛtvā asthi bhettuṃ kuḍyamūlamupasaṃkrāntam / tasyā etadabhūt - kiṃ nu khalvayaṃ kulaputra ātmanaivātmanaḥ īdṛśīṃ kāraṇāṃ kārayati? yannvahamenaṃ kulaputramupasaṃkramya paripṛccheyam / atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā yena sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastenopasaṃkrāntā / upasaṃkramya sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - kiṃ nu khalu tvaṃ kulaputra evaṃrūpāmātmanaḥ prāṇahāriṇīṃ kāraṇāṃ kārayasi? kiṃ cānena rudhireṇa kariṣyasi tvamasthimajjābhyāṃ ca? sadāprarudita āha - asya dārike māṇavakasyāntike idaṃ vikrīya prajñāpāramitāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi, āryaṃ ca dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkariṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: Then a certain merchant's daughter was on the upper terrace of a mansion. She saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, who had pierced his arm, let the blood flow, stripped the thigh of flesh, and approached a wall-base to split the bone. This thought occurred to her: 'Why is this son of good family inflicting such suffering upon himself? Let me approach and ask this son of good family.' Then that merchant's daughter approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>. Having approached, she said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'Why, son of good family, are you inflicting such life-threatening suffering upon yourself? What will you do with this blood, these bones and marrow?' <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said: 'By selling these to this young man, maiden, I shall make an offering to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and honor the noble <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvatadavocat - kā punaste kulaputra tato guṇajātirniṣpatsyate guṇaviśeṣo vā, yattvamātmano hṛdayaṃ rudhiraṃ cāsthimajjānaṃ ca vikrīya taṃ kulaputraṃ satkartukāmaḥ? sa tāṃ dārikāmetadavocat - sa dārike kulaputro 'smākaṃ prajñāpāramitāmupāyakauśalyaṃ copadekṣyati / tatra ca vayaṃ śikṣiṣyāmahe / tatra vayaṃ śikṣamāṇāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyāmaḥ / anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya suvarṇavarṇaṃ ca kāyaṃ pratilapsyāmahe / dvātriṃśacca mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni aśītiṃ cānuvyañjanāni vyāmaprabhatāṃ ca anantaraśmitāṃ ca mahāmaitrī ca mahākaruṇāṃ ca mahāmuditāṃ ca mahopekṣāṃ ca / catvāri vaiśāradyāni pratilapsyāmahe, catasraś ca pratisaṃvidaḥ pratilapsyāmahe, aṣṭādaśa ca āveṇikabuddhadharmān pratilapsyāmahe, pañca ca abhijñāḥ, acintyāṃ ca śīlaviśuddhim, acintyāṃ ca samādhiviśuddhim, acintyāṃ ca prajñāviśuddhim, daśa ca tathāgatabalāni pratilapsyāmahe / anuttaraṃ ca buddhajñānamabhisaṃbhotsyāmahe / anuttaraṃ ca dharmaratnaṃ pratilapsyāmahe, yena ca sarvasattvānāṃ saṃvibhāgaṃ kariṣyāma iti //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'What kind of excellent qualities or special virtues will result from that, son of good family, that you wish to sell your heart, blood, bones, and marrow to honor that son of good family?' He said this to that maiden: 'That son of good family, maiden, will teach us the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means. Therein we shall train. Training therein, we shall become a refuge for all beings. Having awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, we shall obtain a body of golden color, and the thirty-two marks of a great man, and the eighty minor marks, and a fathom-wide radiance, and infinite rays of light, and great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), and great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>). We shall obtain the four confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and we shall obtain the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), and we shall obtain the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), and inconceivable purity of morality, and inconceivable purity of concentration, and inconceivable purity of wisdom, and we shall obtain the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>daśabala</s>). And we shall awaken to the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. And we shall obtain the supreme jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>, which we shall share with all beings.'

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - āścaryaṃ kulaputra yāvadudārāḥ praṇītāścāmī tvayā dharmāḥ parikīrtitāḥ / ekaikasyāpi tāvatkulaputra evaṃrūpasya dharmasyārthāya gaṅgānadīvālukopamān api kalpānātmabhāvāḥ parityaktavyā bhaveyuḥ, prāgeva bahūnāmarthāya ekaḥ / tathodārāḥ praṇītāścāmī tvayā dharmāḥ parikīrtitāḥ, yathā mamāpyete rocante kṣamante ca / api nu khalu punaḥ kulaputra yena yenaivārthena te kṛtyam, tattatte dāsyāmi suvarṇaṃ vā maṇīn vā muktāṃ vā rajataṃ vā vaidūryaṃ vā musāragalvaṃ vā lohitārkaṃ vā sphāṭikaṃ vā puṣpaṃ vā dhūpaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā mālyaṃ va vilepanaṃ vā cūrṇaṃ vā vastraṃ vā chatraṃ vā dhvajaṃ vā ghaṇṭāṃ vā patākāṃ vā dīpaṃ vā / tena tvaṃ taṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkariṣyasi / mā ca ātmana imāmevaṃrūpāṃ kāraṇāṃ kārṣīḥ / vayam api tvayaiva sārdhaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ, yenāryo dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / vayam api tvayaiva sārdhaṃ kuśalamūlānyavaropayiṣyāmaḥ, yaduta eṣāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratilambhāyeti //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'It is wonderful, son of good family, how lofty and eminent are these <s>dharmas</s> that you have proclaimed! For the sake of even one such <s>dharma</s>, son of good family, bodies should be sacrificed for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>—how much more for the sake of many, just one body! So lofty and eminent are these <s>dharmas</s> that you have proclaimed that they please and satisfy even me. Son of good family, whatever you need for your purpose, I shall give you that—whether gold, gems, pearls, silver, <s>vaidūrya</s>, <s>musāragalva</s> (a precious stone), red gold, crystal, flowers, incense, perfume, garlands, ointments, powder, garments, parasols, banners, bells, flags, or lamps. With those you shall honor the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. And do not inflict such suffering upon yourself! We too shall go with you to the noble <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. We too shall plant wholesome roots along with you, for the attainment of such <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro māṇavakaveṣamantardhāpayitvā svakenātmabhāvena sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya purato 'sthāt, idaṃ cāvocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yasya te iyamevaṃrūpā dṛḍhasamādānatā / evaṃrūpayā ca dharmārthikatayā pūrvakair api tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caradbhiḥ prajñāpāramitāmupāyakauśalyaṃ ca paripṛcchadbhiranuttarā ca samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā, dharmaratnaṃ ca pratilabdham / tanna mama kulaputra hṛdayena kāryam, na rudhireṇa, nāsthimajjābhyām, api tu khalu punarahaṃ tvāmeva mīmāṃsitukāma ihāgataḥ / vṛṇīṣva kulaputra varam / kiyadrūpaṃ te varaṃ dāsyāmīti? sa tāmāha - anuttarān me śakra buddhadharmān dehīti / devendra āha - na mamātra kulaputra viṣaye viṣayitā / buddhānāṃ punarbhagavatāmatra viṣaye viṣayitā / anyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti / sadāprarudita āha - alpotsukastvaṃ devendra bhava atra sthāne mamātmabhāvaparipūrimupādāya / svayamevāhamatra devendra satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kariṣyāmi / yenāhaṃ satyena avinivartanīyo 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhervyākṛtastathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ, jñātaścāsmyaśāṭhyenādhyāśayena, tena devendra satyena satyavacanena mama yathāpaurāṇo 'yamātmabhāvo bhavatu / atha khalu tatkṣaṇaṃ tallavaṃ tanmuhūrtaṃ sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya buddhānubhāvena āśayapariśuddhyā ca yathāpaurāṇo 'sya kāyaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt, arogo nirupadravaś ca / atha khalu śakro devānāmindro māraś ca pāpīyān niṣpratibhānaḥ sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyottare pratibhānamapratipadyamānastatraivāntarhito 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, made the form of the young man disappear and stood in his own form before <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, and spoke thus: 'Well done, well done, son of good family! Such is your firm resolution. By just such eagerness for the <s>Dharma</s>, former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, when previously practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> course and inquiring about the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), awakened to supreme perfect awakening and obtained the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>. I had no need, son of good family, for your heart, blood, bones, or marrow; rather, I came here wishing only to test you. Choose a boon, son of good family. What manner of boon shall I give you?' He said to him: 'Give me, <s>Śakra</s>, the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s> qualities.' <s>Devendra</s> said: 'That, son of good family, is not within my domain. It is within the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>. Choose another boon.' <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said: 'Be at ease, <s>Devendra</s>, regarding the restoration of my body in this matter. I myself, <s>Devendra</s>, shall make a truth-declaration (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>) here. By that truth by which I have been declared irreversible from supreme perfect awakening by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, and by which I am known for my sincere aspiration without deceit—by that truth, <s>Devendra</s>, by that truthful speech, may my body become as it was before.' Then at that very instant, at that very moment, through the power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and the purity of his aspiration, the body of <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, became restored as it had been before—healthy and free from affliction. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, and <s>Māra</s> the evil one, unable to find any response, unable to counter the reply of <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, disappeared right there.

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - ehi tvaṃ kulaputra / yenāsmākaṃ niveśanam, tenopasaṃkrāma / ahaṃ te mātāpitṝṇāmantikāttaddhanaṃ dāpayiṣyāmi, yena tvaṃ tāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pūjayiṣyasi, taṃ cāryaṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkariṣyasi, yaduta dharmakāmatayā / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sārdhaṃ tayā śreṣṭhadārikayā yenāsyāḥ svakaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmati sma / upasaṃkramya dvāramūle 'sthāt //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter said to <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>: 'Come, son of good family. Approach our dwelling. I shall have that wealth given to you from my parents, with which you will honor the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and pay homage to the noble <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>—out of love for the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, together with that merchant's daughter, approached her dwelling. Having approached, he stood at the entrance.

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā svakaṃ niveśanaṃ praviśya svāṃ mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caitadavocat - amba tāta daddhvaṃ hiraṇyaṃ suvarṇaṃ ratnāni maṇīn vastrāṇi puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākāḥ / nānāvidhāś ca divyā vādyaprakṛtīrutsṛjata, mām api sārdhamebhiḥ pañcabhirdārikāśatairyā mamopasthāyikā yuṣmabhireva dattāḥ / gamiṣyāmyaham api sadāpraruditena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sārdhaṃ dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyāntikaṃ tasya pūjārthaṃ ca / so 'smākaṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati / tena vayaṃ buddhadharmān pratilapsyāmahe / atha khalu tau tasyā dārikāyā mātāpitarau tāṃ dārikāmetadavocatām - kaḥ punareṣa dārike sadāprarudito nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, kva vā sa etarhi tiṣṭhati? dārikā āha - eṣa kulaputro 'smākameva niveśanadvāramūle 'vasthitaḥ / eṣa ca kulaputro 'dhyāśayena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhuṃ saṃprasthitaḥ, yaduta sarvasattvānaparimāṇataḥ saṃsāraduḥkhānmocayitukāmaḥ, sarvadharmakāmatayātmānaṃ
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter entered her own dwelling and said to her mother and father: 'Mother, father, give me gold, silver, jewels, gems, garments, flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and pennants. Release various kinds of divine musical instruments. Let me go, together with these five hundred maidens who are my attendants and were given by you. I shall go together with <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, to the presence of <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, for the purpose of honoring him. He will teach us the <s>Dharma</s>. Through that, we shall obtain the <s>Buddha</s> qualities.' Then the parents of that girl said to her: 'Who, daughter, is this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, and where does he presently abide?' The girl said: 'This son of good family stands at the very entrance of our dwelling. This son of good family has set out with deep aspiration to awaken to supreme perfect awakening—wishing to liberate immeasurable beings from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and wishing, out of love for all <s>dharmas</s>, to sell himself

body.text: vikrīya prajñāpāramitāṃ pūjayitukāmaḥ, āryaṃ ca dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkartukāmaḥ / tasya cātmabhāvasya kaṃcitkrāyakaṃ na labhate / alabhamānaḥ san duḥkhito durmanāḥ pradhyāyan dīnamanā aśrūṇi pravartayamānaḥ sthitaḥ / sa śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa māṇavakarūpamabhinirmāyoktaḥ - kiṃ tvaṃ kulaputra duḥkhī durmanāḥ pradhyāyan dīnamānaso 'śrūṇi pravartayamānaḥ sthita iti? sa tamāha - ātmānaṃ vikretukāmo 'ham / tasya ca krāyakaṃ na labhe / māṇavakarūpī śakrastamāha - kasya punastvaṃ kulaputra arthāyātmānaṃ vikretukāmaḥ? sadāpraruditenoktaḥ - prajñāpāramitāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi, āryaṃ ca dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkariṣyāmi yaduta dharmakāmatayā / tatra pratibaddhāś ca me buddhadharmā iti / māṇavakarūpī śakrastamāha - na mama kulaputra tvayārthaḥ / api tu khalu punaḥ piturme yajño bhaviṣyati / tatra me puruṣasya hṛdayena rūdhireṇa asthimajjābhyāṃ ca kṛtyamiti / tata eṣa kulaputro 'viṣaṇṇamānasa āha - dāsyāmīti / sa tīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā ātmano bāhuṃ viddhvā lohitaṃ niḥsrāvya ūruṃ ca nirmāṃsaṃ kṛtvā asthi bhettuṃ kuḍyamūlamupasaṃkrāntaḥ ekānte sthitvā asthi bhittvā majjānaṃ ca dāsyāmīti / ahaṃ cainaṃ kulaputramupariṣṭātprāsādatalagatā kṣaradrudhiramadrākṣam / tasyā mamaitadabhūt - kiṃ nu khalvayaṃ puruṣa ātmanaivātmana evaṃrūpāṃ kāraṇāṃ kārayatīti? tamenamahamupasaṃkramyaivamavocam - kimarthaṃ tvayā kulaputra ātmanaivātmana evaṃ kṣaradrūdhiraṃ śarīraṃ vikṛtaṃ kṛtam? tata eṣa māmevamāha - asya dārike māṇavakasya lohitaṃ hṛdayamasthi majjānaṃ ca dāsyāmīti / tatkasya hetoḥ? na mamānyatkiṃciddhanaṃ saṃvidyate / daridro 'smīti / tamenamahamevamavocam - kiṃ punastvaṃ tena dhanena kariṣyasīti? sa eṣa māmetadavocat - prajñāpāramitāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi, taṃ cāryaṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkariṣyāmi yaduta dharmakāmatayeti / tamenamahamevamavocam - kā punaste kulaputra tato guṇajātirbhaviṣyati guṇaviśeṣo veti? tataḥ so 'cintyān me buddhaguṇān varṇayati saṃprakāśayati, aprameyāṃś ca buddhadharmān - eṣāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ me tata āgamo bhaviṣyatīti / tasya me mahattaraṃ prītiprāmodyamutpannaṃ tānacintyān buddhaguṇān śrutvā / evaṃ ca me 'bhūt - āścaryaṃ yāvadduṣkarakārakaścāyaṃ kulaputro 'tīva dharmakāmaśca, yo 'yamevaṃrūpamātmanaḥ śarīrasya pīḍāsthānamutsahate / ayaṃ hi nāma kulaputro dharmakāmatayā ātmānaṃ parityajati / kasmādasmābhirdharmo na pūjayitavyaḥ? evaṃrūpeṣu ca sthāneṣu praṇidhānaṃ na kartavyaṃ syāt, yeṣāmasmākaṃ prabhūtā vipulāś ca bhogāḥ saṃvidyante iti / sāhamenaṃ kulaputrametadavocam - mā mā tvaṃ kulaputra imāmevaṃrūpāmātmanaḥ prāṇahāriṇīṃ kāraṇāṃ kārṣīḥ / ahaṃ te prabhūtaprabhūtaṃ dhanamanupradāpayiṣyāmi yena tavārthaḥ / tena tvaṃ tamāryaṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkariṣyasi gurukariṣyasi / aham api tvayaiva sārdhaṃ yena dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tenopasaṃkramiṣyāmi / aham api tasya kulaputrasya pūjāṃ kariṣyāmi / vayamapyevaṃrūpān dharmānniṣpādayiṣyāmo yaduta anuttarān buddhadharmān ye tvayā parikīrtitā iti / tanmāmamba tāta anujānīta / prabhūtaprabhūtaṃ ca me dhanaskandhaṃ daddhvam, yenāhametenaiva kulaputreṇa sārdhaṃ gatvā āryaṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: in order to honor the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and to pay homage to the noble <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. And he cannot find any buyer for his own body. Unable to find one, he stands sorrowful, dejected, brooding, downcast, shedding tears.
