He was approached by <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, who had magically created the form of a young man, and was asked: "Why do you stand, son of good family, sorrowful, dejected, brooding, downcast, shedding tears?" He said to him: "I wish to sell myself, but I cannot find a buyer." <s>Śakra</s> in the form of a young man said to him: "For whose benefit, son of good family, do you wish to sell yourself?" <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said: "I shall honor the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and pay homage to the noble <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, out of love for the <s>Dharma</s>. And the <s>Buddha</s> qualities are bound up for me in that." <s>Śakra</s> in the form of a young man said to him: "I have no need of you, son of good family. But my father will have a sacrifice, and for that I need a man's heart, blood, bones, and marrow." Then this son of good family, with undismayed mind, said: "I shall give them." Taking a sharp blade, he pierced his own arm, let the blood flow out, and having stripped the flesh from his thigh, approached the foot of a wall to break the bone, standing to one side, [thinking]: "I shall break the bone and give the marrow." And I, from atop a palace terrace, saw this son of good family with blood flowing. This thought occurred to me: "Why indeed does this man inflict such torment upon himself by himself?" Having approached him, I spoke thus: "For what reason, son of good family, have you by yourself made your own body disfigured with flowing blood?" Then he said to me: "I shall give this young man my blood, heart, bones, and marrow. Why is that? I have no other wealth. I am poor." I then said to him: "What will you do with that wealth?" He said to me: "I shall honor the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and pay homage to the noble <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, out of love for the <s>Dharma</s>." I then said to him: "What kind of qualities and distinction will come to you from that?" Then he described and illuminated to me inconceivable <s>Buddha</s> qualities and immeasurable <s>Buddha</s> qualities: "From that, such <s>Buddha</s> qualities will come to me." Great joy and delight arose in me upon hearing those inconceivable <s>Buddha</s> qualities. And this thought occurred to me: "It is wonderful how this son of good family performs a difficult task and is exceedingly fond of the <s>Dharma</s>, that he endures such a place of suffering for his own body. This son of good family abandons himself out of love for the <s>Dharma</s>. Why should we not honor the <s>Dharma</s>? And should we not make aspirations in such matters, we who possess abundant and vast wealth?" So I said to this son of good family: "Do not, do not, son of good family, inflict upon yourself this torment that threatens your life. I shall have abundant wealth given to you, with which you will accomplish your purpose. With it you shall pay homage to and revere the noble <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. I too, together with you, shall approach <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. I too shall make an offering to that son of good family. We too shall accomplish such <s>dharmas</s>—namely, the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s> qualities that you have proclaimed." Therefore, mother, father, grant me permission. And give me abundant stores of wealth, with which I, going together with this very son of good family, shall honor the noble <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu tau tasyā dārikāyā mātāpitarau tāṃ dārikāmetadavocatām - āścaryaṃ yāvadduṣkaraṃ ca tvametasya kulaputrasya sthānamācakṣe / ekāṃśenaiva te dharmā acintyāḥ, sarvalokaviśiṣṭāḥ sarvasattvasukhāvahāśca, yeṣāmeṣa kṛtaśaḥ kulaputro duṣkaraṃ sthānamevamutsahate / anujānīva āvāṃ tvāṃ dārike / āvayorapyavakāśaṃ kuru, yadāvām api gacchāvastvayaiva sārdhaṃ taṃ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ draṣṭuṃ vandituṃ paryupāsituṃ pūjayituṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Then the parents of that girl said to her: 'It is wonderful how difficult a station you describe of this son of good family. Without doubt, those <s>dharmas</s> are inconceivable, surpassing the whole world and bringing happiness to all beings, for whose sake this son of good family endures such a difficult station. We grant you permission, daughter. Allow us too an opportunity, that we too may go together with you to see, venerate, attend upon, and honor <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pūjārthaṃ satkārārthaṃ ca prasthitāṃ svāṃ mātaraṃ pitaraṃ ca viditvā etadavocat - amba tāta evaṃ kuruta, yathā vadata / nāhaṃ kasyacitkuśalapakṣasyāntarāyaṃ karomi / ityuktvā evaṃ sā śreṣṭhidārikā dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pūjārthaṃ satkārārthaṃ ca prasthitā babhūva //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter, learning that her mother and father had set out for the purpose of honoring and paying homage to <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, said: 'Mother, father, do as you say. I shall not create an obstacle to any wholesome endeavor.' Having spoken thus, that merchant's daughter set out for the purpose of honoring and paying homage to <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā pañca rathaśatānyalaṃkārayāmāsa / tāni ca pañca dārikāśatānyalaṃkārayāmāsa / alaṃkṛtya nānāvarṇāni vicitrāṇi puṣpāṇi gṛhītvā nānāraṅgāṇi vastrāṇi puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākāś ca gṛhītvā nānāratnāni ca vicitrāṇi nānāratnamayāni ca vicitrāṇi puṣpāṇi gṛhītvā prabhūtaprabhūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ svādanīyaṃ ca gṛhītvā ekaṃ rathaṃ sadāpraruditena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sārdhamabhiruhya taiḥ pañcabhī rathaśataiḥ pañcadārikāśatābhirūḍhaiḥ parivṛttā puraskṛtā mahatā ca parivāreṇa mātāpitṛpūrvaṃgamā yena pūrvā dik tena prakrāntā / anupūrveṇa ca gacchan sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'drākṣīddūrādeva tāṃ gandhavatīṃ nagarīṃ saptānāṃ ratnānāṃ citrāṃ darśanīyāṃ saptabhiḥ prākāraiḥ saptaratnamayairanuparikṣiptāṃ saptabhistoraṇaiḥ saptabhiḥ parikhābhiḥ saptabhistālapaṅktibhiranuparikṣiptāṃ dvādaśa yojanāni vistāreṇa dvādaśa yojanānyāyāmena ṛddhāṃ sphītāṃ ca kṣemāṃ ca subhikṣāṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṃ ca pañcabhirantarāpaṇavīthīśatairālekhyavicitracitrasadṛśairdarśanīyairnirviddhāṃ samasamairanutpīḍajanayugyayānasaṃkramaṇasthānasthāpitaiḥ sumāpitāṃ ca / madhye ca nagaraśṛṅgāṭakasya adrākṣīddharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ dharmāsanagatamanekaśatayā parṣadā anekasahasrayā anekaśatasahasrayā parṣadā parivṛttaṃ puraskṛtaṃ dharmaṃ deśayantam / sahadarśanenaiva ca tasya evaṃrūpaṃ sukhaṃ saṃpratilabhate sma tadyathāpi nāma prathamadhyānasamāpanno bhikṣurekāgreṇa manasikāreṇa / dṛṣṭvā cāsya etadabhūt - na mama pratirūpametadbhavet, yadahaṃ rathagata eva dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamupasaṃkrāmeyam / yannvahaṃ rathādavatareyam / sa tato rathādavātarat / tāny api pañca dārikāśatāni śreṣṭhidārikayā saha rathebhyo 'vateruḥ / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śreṣṭhidārikāpūrvaṃgamaiḥ pañcabhirdārikāśataiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto 'parimāṇapūjāvyūhena yena dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tenopasaṃkrāmati sma //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter adorned five hundred chariots and adorned those five hundred maidens. Having adorned them, she took flowers of various colors and varieties, garments of various hues, flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and pennants, as well as various jewels and various jewel-flowers of many kinds, and abundant food, drink, and delicacies. Mounting one chariot together with <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, surrounded and attended by those five hundred chariots mounted by the five hundred maidens, with a great retinue, preceded by her parents, she set forth toward the eastern direction. And as he traveled, <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, saw from afar that city of <s>Gandhavatī</s>—beautiful with the seven precious substances, lovely to behold, encircled by seven ramparts made of the seven jewels, with seven gateways, seven moats, and seven rows of <s>tāla</s> trees; twelve <s>yojanas</s> in breadth and twelve <s>yojanas</s> in length; prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and thronging with many people; traversed by five hundred market streets, beautiful as painted pictures, lovely to behold; well-constructed with spaces for the passage of people, oxen, carriages, and travelers, all level and even. And in the center, at the crossroads of the city, he saw <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, seated on a <s>Dharma</s>-seat, surrounded and attended by an assembly of many hundreds, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. At the very moment of seeing him, he experienced such happiness as a monk who has entered the first <s>dhyāna</s> with one-pointed attention. And this thought occurred to him: 'It would not be fitting for me to approach <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while mounted on a chariot. Let me descend from the chariot.' He descended from that chariot. Those five hundred maidens too, together with the merchant's daughter, descended from their chariots. Then <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, preceded by the merchant's daughter, surrounded and attended by the five hundred maidens, with immeasurable arrays of offerings, approached <s>Dharmodgata</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena dharmodgatena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kṛtaśaḥ saptaratnamayaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ kāritamabhūt lohitacandanālaṃkṛtaṃ muktājālaparikṣiptam / caturṣu kūṭāgārakoṇeṣu maṇiratnāni sthāpitāni, yāni pradīpakṛtyaṃ kurvanti sma / catasraś ca dhūpaghaṭikā
body.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> had caused to be built for the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> a many-storied pavilion made of the seven precious substances, adorned with red sandalwood and surrounded by a net of pearls. At the four corners of the pavilion, wish-fulfilling jewels were placed that served as lamps. And four incense burners—

body.text: rūpamayyaścaturdiśamavasaktāḥ, yatra śuddhaṃ kṛṣṇāguru dhūpyate sma yaduta prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjārtham / tasya ca kūṭāgārasya madhye saptaratnamayaḥ paryaṅkaḥ prajñapto 'bhūt / caturṇāṃ ratnānāṃ peḍā kṛtā, yatra prajñāpāramitā prakṣiptā suvarṇapaṭṭeṣu likhitā vilīnena vaidūryeṇa / tacca kūṭāgāraṃ nānācitrapaṭṭadāmabhiḥ pralambamānairalaṃkṛtamabhūt //
body.translated_text: —made of silver were suspended in the four directions, in which pure black <s>aguru</s> (aloe) incense was burned for the worship of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. In the center of that pavilion, a couch made of the seven precious substances was prepared. A casket of four [kinds of] jewels was made, in which the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> was placed, written on golden plates with melted <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl). And that pavilion—

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sārdhaṃ śreṣṭhidārikāpūrvaṃgamaiḥ pañcadārikāśataiḥ taṃ kūṭāgāramadrākṣīdaparimāṇena pūjāvyūhena pratimaṇḍitam / anekāni ca tatra devatāsahasrāṇyadrākṣīt, śakraṃ ca devānāmindraṃ divyairmāndāravapuṣpairdivyaiścandanacūrṇairdivyaiś ca suvarṇacūrṇairdivyaiś ca rūpyacūrṇaistaṃ kūṭāgāramavakirantamabhyavakirantamabhiprakirantam / divyāni ca vādyānyaśrauṣīt / dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - kimarthaṃ tvaṃ devendra anekairdevatāsahasraiḥ sārdhamidaṃ ratnamayaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ divyairmāndāravaiḥ puṣpairdivyaiścandanacūrṇairdivyaiḥ suvarṇacūrṇairdivyaiś ca rūpyacūrṇairavakirasi abhyavakirasi abhiprakirasi? imāni ca divyāni vādyāni devairuparyantarīkṣe pravāditāni? evamukte śakro devānāmindraḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - na tvaṃ kulaputra jānīṣe? eṣā hi sā prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mātā pariṇāyikā, yatra śikṣamāṇā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvaguṇapāramitānugatān sarvabuddhadharmān sarvākārajñatāṃ ca kṣipramanuprāpnuvantīti / evamukte sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - kvāsau kauśika prajñāpāramitā, yā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mātā pariṇāyikā? śakra āha - eṣā kulaputra asya kūṭāgārasya madhye suvarṇapaṭṭeṣu vilīnena vaidūryeṇa likhitvā āryeṇa dharmodgatena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena saptabhirmudrābhirmudrayitvā sthāpitā / sā na sukarā asmābhistava darśayitum / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sārdhaṃ śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhai pañcabhirdārikāśataiḥ samagrībhūtaiḥ, yānyanena puṣpāṇi gṛhītāni mālyadāmāni ca vastraratnāni ca dhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākāś ca suvarṇarūpyamayāni ca puṣpāṇi, taiḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjāmakārṣuḥ, anyatarānyataraṃ ca tataḥ pratyaṃśaṃ sthāpayāmāsuḥ yaduta dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya satkārāya //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, together with the five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter, saw that pavilion adorned with immeasurable splendor of worship. And he saw there many thousands of deities, and <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the Gods, worshipping with divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers, divine sandalwood powder, divine gold dust, and divine—

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāni ca śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhāni pañca dārikāśatāni puṣpadhūpamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ suvarṇarūpyamayaiś ca puṣpairdivyaiś ca vādyaiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ pūrvaṃ pūjayitvā yena dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvastenopasaṃkramya dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiścandanacūrṇaiḥ suvarṇarūpyamayaiś ca puṣpairavākiran abhyavākiran abhiprākiran, divyāni ca vādyāni saṃpravādayati sma dharmapūjāmevopādāya //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, together with those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter, having first worshipped the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with flowers, incense, garlands, unguents, powder, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and pennants, as well as with gold and silver flowers and divine music, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>—

body.text: atha khalu tāni puṣpāṇi dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyopariṣṭānmūrdhni puṣpakūṭāgāraṃ prātiṣṭhan / tāni ca nānāvarṇāni puṣpāṇi suvarṇarūpyamayāni ca puṣpāṇi
body.translated_text: Then those flowers came to rest above the head of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, forming a pavilion of flowers atop his head. And those flowers of various colors, as well as the gold and silver flowers—

body.text: vihāyasi vitānamiva sthitāni / tāny api cīvarāṇi vastraratnāni ca antarīkṣe nānāratnamayo 'bhramaṇḍapa iva saṃsthito 'bhūt / adrākṣītkhalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāni ca pañca dārikāśatāni śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhāni dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyedamevaṃrūpamṛddhiprātihāryam / dṛṣṭvā ca punareṣāmetadabhūt - āścaryaṃ yāvanmaharddhikaścāyaṃ dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yāvanmahānubhāvo yāvanmahaujaskaḥ / bodhisattvacaryāmeva tāvaccarato 'sya kulaputrasyaivaṃrūpā ṛddhivikurvaṇā, kiṃ punaryadāyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho bhaviṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: —remained in the sky like a canopy. And those robes and precious garments stood in mid-air like a pavilion of various jewels. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> and those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter beheld this marvelous display of supernatural power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>—

body.text: atha khalu tāni śreṣṭhidārikāpūrvaṃgamāni pañca dārikāśatāni dharmodgate bodhisattve mahāsattve spṛhāmutpādya sarvāstāḥ samagrībhūtā adhyāśayena anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayāmāsuḥ, evaṃ cāvocan - anena vayaṃ kuśalamūlena anāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bhavema / bodhisattvacaryāṃ ca vayaṃ carantya eteṣāmeva dharmāṇāṃ lābhinyo bhavema, yeṣāṃ dharmāṇāmayaṃ dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo lābhī / evameva ca prajñāpāramitāṃ satkuryāma gurukuryāma, yathāyaṃ dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ satkaroti gurukaroti / bahujanasya ca saṃprakāśayema yathāyaṃ dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saṃprakāśayati / evameva ca prajñāpāramitayā upāyakauśalyena ca samanvāgatā bhavema / pariniṣpadyemahi ca yathāyaṃ dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitayā upāyakauśalyena ca samanvāgataḥ pariniṣpannaś ca //
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter, having generated aspiration toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, all together, with sincere resolve, generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and spoke thus: "By this root of merit, may we in the future become <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. May our <s>Bodhi</s>—"

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāni ca śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhāni pañca dārikāśatāni prajñāpāramitāṃ pūjayitvā dharmodgataṃ ca bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkṛtya dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte sagauravāḥ sapratīkṣāḥ prāñjalīn kṛtvātiṣṭhan / ekānte sthitaś ca sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - ihāhaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāṃ gaveṣamāṇo 'raṇyagato nirghoṣamaśrauṣam - gaccha kulaputra pūrvāṃ diśam / tataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyasīti / so 'haṃ samyak taṃ nirghoṣaṃ śrutvā yena pūrvā dik tena saṃprasthitaḥ / tasya me etadabhūt - samyak ca mayā nirghoṣaḥ śrutaḥ / na ca mayā sa nirghoṣaḥ paripṛṣṭaḥ - kiyaddūraṃ mayā gantavyam, kasya vā antikātprajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyāmi lapsye veti / tasya me mahaddaurmanasyamabhūt / so 'haṃ tena daurmanasyena mahatīmutkaṇṭhāṃ paritapanaṃ cāpanno 'bhūvam / tasminneva pṛthivīpradeśe saptarātriṃdivānyatināmayāmi utkaṇṭhitaḥ / nāhārasamudācāramutpādayāmi / api tu prajñāpāramitāmeva manasi karomi - kiyaddūraṃ mayā gantavyam, kuto vā prajñāpāramitāṃ lapsye śravaṇāya? na ca mayā sa nirghoṣaḥ paripṛṣṭaḥ iti / tato me tathāgatavigrahaḥ purataḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / sa māmevamāha - gaccha kulaputra itaḥ pañcabhiryojanaśatairanupūrveṇa gandhavatī nāma nagarī / tatra drakṣyasi dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ deśayantaṃ prakāśayantamiti / tato 'haṃ mahatodāreṇa prītiprāmodyena samanvāgataḥ / so 'haṃ tenaiva mahatodāreṇa prītiprāmodyena sphuṭastataḥ pṛthivīpradeśānna calitaḥ, tava ca prajñāpāramitāṃ deśayataḥ śṛṇomi / tasya me śṛṇvato bahūni samādhimukhāni prādurbhūtāni /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> and those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter, having worshipped the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and honored the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, and having bowed their heads at the feet of <s>Dharmodgata</s>, stood to one side, reverential, attentive, with palms joined. Standing to one side—

body.text: tatra sthitaṃ māṃ daśadiglokadhātusthitā buddhā bhagavantaḥ samāśvāsayanti, sādhukāraṃ ca dadati - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, ete samādhayaḥ prajñāpāramitānirjātāḥ, yatra sthitairasmābhiḥ sarvabuddhadharmāḥ pariniṣpāditā iti / te māṃ tathāgatāḥ sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya antarhitāḥ / ahaṃ ca tataḥ samādhervyutthitaḥ / tasya me etadabhūt - kuto nu te tathāgatā āgatāḥ, kva vā te tathāgatā gatā iti? tasya ca me etadabhūt - āryo dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dhāraṇīpratilabdhaḥ pañcābhijñaḥ pūrvajinākṛtādhikāro 'varopitakuśalamūlaḥ, prajñāpāramitāyāṃ upāyakauśalye ca suśikṣitaḥ / sa me enamarthaṃ yathāvadvicariṣyati, yataste tathāgatā āgatā yatra vā te tathāgatā gatā iti / so 'haṃ tasya tathāgatavigrahasya nirghoṣaṃ śrutvā yathānuśiṣṭaṃ yena pūrvāṃ dik tena saṃprasthitaḥ / āgacchaṃścāhaṃ dūrata evāryamadrākṣaṃ dharmaṃ deśayantam / sahadarśanācca mamedṛśaṃ sukhaṃ prādurabhūt, tadyathāpi nāma prathamadhyānasamāpannasya bhikṣorekāgramanasikārasya / so 'haṃ tvāṃ kulaputra pṛcchāmi - kutaste tathāgatā āgatāḥ, kutra te tathāgatā gatā iti? deśaya me kulaputra teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ gamanaṃ ca / yathā vayaṃ teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ gamanaṃ ca jānīma, avirahitāś ca bhavema tathāgatadarśaneneti //
body.translated_text: "—as I stand there, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, abiding in the world systems of the ten directions, console me and give their approval: 'Well done, well done, son of good family! These <s>samādhis</s> are born from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Abiding in them, we have brought all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> to perfection.' Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having thoroughly shown me, instructed, encouraged, and inspired me—"

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sadāpraruditaparivarto nāma triṃśattamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the Thirtieth Chapter, called "The Chapter on <s>Sadāprarudita</s>," in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

body.text: ASP_31: dharmodgataparivarta ekatriṃśattamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Thirty-One: The Chapter on <s>Dharmodgata</s>.

body.text: evamukte dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattva mahāsattvametadavocat - na khalu kulaputra tathāgatāḥ kutaścidāgacchanti vā gacchanti vā / acalitā hi tathatā / yā ca tathatā, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra anutpāda āgacchati vā gacchati vā / yaś ca anutpādaḥ, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra bhūtakoṭyā āgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / yā ca bhūtakoṭiḥ, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra śūnyatāyā āgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / yā ca śūnyatā, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra yathāvattāyā āgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / yā ca yathāvattā, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra virāgasyāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / yā ca virāgatā, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra nirodhasyāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / yaś ca nirodhaḥ, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra ākāśadhātorāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / yaś ca ākāśadhātuḥ, sa tathāgataḥ / na hi kulaputra anyatra ebhyo dharmebhyastathāgataḥ / yā ca kulaputra eṣāmeva dharmāṇāṃ tathatā, yā ca sarvadharmatathatā, yā ca tathāgatatathatā, ekaivaiṣā tathatā / nāsti kulaputra tathatāyā dvaidhīkāraḥ / ekaivaiṣā tathatā kulaputra / tathatā na dve na tisraḥ / gaṇanāvyativṛttā kulaputrā tathatā yaduta asattvāt / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra puruṣo grīṣmābhitapto grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse 'bhigate madhyāhnakālasamaye marīcikāṃ paśyet syandamānām / sa tena tena pradhāvet - atrodakaṃ pāsyāmi, apānīyaṃ pāsyāmīti / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra kuta etadudakamāgataṃ kva vā tadudakaṃ gacchati, pūrvaṃ vā mahāsamudraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ vā paścimaṃ vā uttaraṃ vā? sadāprarudita āha - na hi kulaputra marīcikāyāmudakaṃ saṃvidyate / kiṃ punarasyāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate? sa khalu punaḥ kulaputra puruṣo grīṣmābhitapto bālajātīyo duṣprajñajātīyo marīcikāṃ dṛṣṭvā anudake udakasaṃjñāmutpādayati / na punastatrodakaṃ svabhāvataḥ saṃvidyate / dharmodgata āha - evametatkulaputra, evam etat / evameva kulaputra ye kecittathāgatarūpeṇa vā ghoṣeṇa vā abhiniviṣṭāḥ, te tathāgatasyāgamanaṃ ca gamanaṃ ca kalpayanti / ye ca tathāgatasyāgamanaṃ ca gamanaṃ ca kalpayanti, sarve te bālajātīyā duṣprajñajātīyā iti vaktavyāḥ, tadyathāpi nāma sa eva puruṣo yo 'nudake udakasaṃjñāmutpādayati / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi tathāgato rūpakāyato draṣṭavyaḥ / dharmakāyāstathāgatāḥ / na ca kulaputra dharmatā āgacchati vā gacchati vā / evameva kulaputra nāsti tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra māyākāranirmitasya hastikāyasya vā aśvakāyasya vā rathakāyasya vā pattikāyasya vā nāstyāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā, evameva kulaputra nāsti tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapnāntaragata ekaṃ vā tathāgataṃ paśyet, dvau vā trīn vā caturo vā pañca vā ṣaḍvā sapta vā aṣṭau vā nava vā daśa vā viṃśatiṃ vā triṃśadvā catvāriṃśadvā pañcāśadvā śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā, tato vā uttare / sa prativibuddhaḥ san ekam api tathāgataṃ na paśyet / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra kutaste tathāgatā āgatāḥ kva vā te tathāgatā gatā iti? sadāprarudita āha - na khalu punaḥ kulaputra svapne kasyaciddharmasya
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: "Indeed, son of good family, <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not come from anywhere or go anywhere. For <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is immovable, and what is <s>tathatā</s>—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, the unborn does not come or go, and what is the unborn—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, no coming or going is recognized of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality), and what is <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, no coming or going is recognized of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), and what is <s>śūnyatā</s>—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, no coming or going is recognized of <s>yathāvattā</s> (things as they truly are), and what is <s>yathāvattā</s>—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, no coming or going is recognized of dispassion, and what is dispassion—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, no coming or going is recognized of cessation, and what is cessation—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, no coming or going is recognized of the space element, and what is the space element—that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Indeed, son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not other than these <s>dharmas</s>. And, son of good family, the <s>tathatā</s> of these very <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s>, and the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>—this is one single <s>tathatā</s>. There is, son of good family, no duality in <s>tathatā</s>. This is one single <s>tathatā</s>, son of good family. <s>Tathatā</s> is not two, not three. <s>Tathatā</s>, son of good family, is beyond enumeration, namely because of non-existence. Just as, son of good family, a man tormented by summer heat, in the last month of summer at midday, might see a mirage flowing. He would run here and there: 'Here I will drink water, I will drink a beverage!' What do you think, son of good family—from where has that water come, and where does that water go? To the east, to the south, to the west, or to the north?" <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said: "Indeed, son of good family, in a mirage there is no water. How then could its coming or going be recognized? That man, son of good family, tormented by summer heat, being of foolish nature and poor wisdom, seeing a mirage, generates the perception of water where there is no water. But water does not exist there by its own nature." <s>Dharmodgata</s> said: "So it is, son of good family, so it is. Just so, son of good family, those who are fixated on the <s>Tathāgata</s> by form or by voice—they imagine a coming and going of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And those who imagine a coming and going of the <s>Tathāgata</s>—all of them should be called of foolish nature and poor wisdom, just like that man who generates the perception of water where there is no water. For what reason? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through his form-body. <s>Tathāgatas</s> are <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body). And, son of good family, <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things) does not come or go. Just so, son of good family, there is no coming or going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Just as, son of good family, there is no coming or going of the body of an elephant, horse, chariot, or foot-soldier conjured by a magician, just so, son of good family, there is no coming or going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Just as, son of good family, a man who has fallen asleep and entered into a dream might see one <s>Tathāgata</s>, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven, or eight, or nine, or ten, or twenty, or thirty, or forty, or fifty, or a hundred, or a thousand, or more. And when awakened, he would not see even a single <s>Tathāgata</s>. What do you think, son of good family—from where did those <s>Tathāgatas</s> come, and where did those <s>Tathāgatas</s> go?" <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said: "Indeed, son of good family, in a dream no accomplishment of any <s>dharma</s> is recognized. For a dream is false speech." <s>Dharmodgata</s> said: "Just so, son of good family. Just so. All <s>dharmas</s> have been declared dream-like by the Blessed One. Son of good family, those who do not truly understand all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like, as taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they—fixating on <s>Tathāgatas</s> through name-body or form-body—imagine a coming and going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Those who, not understanding <s>dharmatā</s>, imagine a coming and going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>—all of them are of foolish nature, ordinary persons. All of them have gone, are going, and will go through the six-fold course of <s>saṃsāra</s>. All of them are far from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. All of them are far from <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. But, son of good family, those who truly understand all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like—'All <s>dharmas</s> are dream-like,' as taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—they do not imagine coming or going, arising or cessation of any <s>dharma</s>. And those who do not imagine coming or going, arising or cessation of any <s>dharma</s>—they understand the <s>Tathāgata</s> through <s>dharmatā</s>. And those who understand the <s>Tathāgata</s> through <s>dharmatā</s>—they do not imagine a coming or going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And those who understand such <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>—they practice near to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. And they practice in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And they are the Blessed One's <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples) who eat the country's alms-food not in vain. And they are worthy of offerings from the world. Just as, son of good family, the gems in the great ocean do not come from the east, nor from the south, nor from the west, nor from the north, nor from the intermediate directions, nor from below, nor from above, nor from any place or direction. Rather, it is based on the wholesome roots of beings that gems arise in the great ocean. Nor do they arise without cause. They are dependent on causes and conditions, arisen through dependent origination. And those gems, when ceasing, do not travel anywhere in the ten directions of the world. Rather, when those conditions exist by which those gems are produced, they are produced; when those conditions do not exist, there is no production of those gems. Just so, son of good family, the bodily accomplishment of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> has not come from anywhere in the ten directions of the world, nor does it go anywhere in the ten directions of the world. Nor is the body of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> without cause. It is brought about by the completion of prior practices, dependent on causes and conditions, arisen from causes, arisen from the ripening of former <s>karma</s>. It does not exist anywhere in the ten directions of the world. Rather, when those conditions exist by which the accomplishment of the body occurs, it occurs; when those conditions do not exist, the accomplishment of the body is not recognized. Just as, son of good family, the sound arising from a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) does not come from anywhere, and when ceasing does not go anywhere, does not travel anywhere, but arises dependent on the conjunction of causes and conditions, dependent on causes, dependent on conditions. That is, dependent on the resonating bowl, dependent on the skin, dependent on the strings, dependent on the plectrum, dependent on the supports, dependent on the bridge, and dependent on the person's appropriate effort—thus the sound of the <s>vīṇā</s> issues forth, dependent on causes, dependent on conditions. And that sound does not issue forth from the bowl, nor from the skin, nor from the strings, nor from the plectrum, nor from the supports, nor from the bridge, nor from the person's appropriate effort. Rather, it is through the conjunction of all of them that the sound is designated. And when ceasing, the sound does not go anywhere. Just so, son of good family, the bodily accomplishment of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> is dependent on causes, dependent on conditions, brought about through the completion of the application of many wholesome roots. It is not from a single cause, not from a single condition, not from a single wholesome root that the production of the <s>Buddha</s>-body occurs. Nor is it without cause.

body.text: pariniṣpattiḥ prajñāyate / mṛṣāvādo hi svapno 'bhūt / dharmodgata āha - evameva kulaputra sarvadharmāḥ svapnopamā uktā bhagavatā / ye kecitkulaputra svapnopamān sarvadharmāṃstathāgatena nirdeśitān yathābhūtaṃ na prajānanti, te tathāgatān nāmakāyena vā rūpakāyena vā abhiniviśya tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā kalpayanti / yathāpi nāma dharmatāmaprajānanto ye ca tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā kalpayanti, sarve te bālajātīyāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ / sarve te ṣaḍgatikaṃ saṃsāraṃ gatāḥ, gacchanti gamiṣyanti ca / sarve te prajñāpāramitāyā dūre / sarve te buddhadharmāṇāṃ dūre / ye khalu punaḥ kulaputra svapnopamān sarvadharmān svapnopamāḥ sarvadharmā iti tathāgatena deśitān yathābhūtaṃ prajānanti, na te kasyaciddharmasyāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā kalpayanti, utpādaṃ vā nirodhaṃ vā / ye ca na kasyaciddharmasyāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā kalpayanti, utpādaṃ vā nirodhaṃ vā, te dharmatayā tathāgataṃ prajānanti / ye ca tathāgataṃ dharmatayā prajānanti, na te tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā kalpayanti / ye ca tathāgatasyedṛśīṃ dharmatāṃ prajānanti, te āsannā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheścaranti / te ca prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranti / te ca bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ amoghaṃ rāṣṭrapiṇḍaṃ paribhuñjate / te ca lokasya dakṣiṇīyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra mahāsamudre ratnāni na pūrvasyā diśa āgacchanti, na dakṣiṇasyāḥ, na paścimāyāḥ, nottarasyāḥ, na vidigbhyo nādhastānnopariṣṭānna kutaściddeśebhyo digbhya āgacchanti, api tu khalu punaḥ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlānyupādāya mahāsamudre ratnānyutpadyante / na va tānyahetukānyutpadyante / hetupratyayakāraṇādhīnāni pratītyasamutpannāni / nirudhyamānāni ca tāni ratnāni ca kvaciddaśadiśi loke saṃkrāmanti / api tu khalu punaryeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ satāṃ tāni ratnāni prabhāvyante, teṣāṃ pratyayānāmasatāṃ na teṣāṃ ratnānāṃ prabhāvanā bhavati / evameva kulaputra teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ kāyapariniṣpattirna kutaściddaśadiśi lokādāgatā, nāpi kvaciddaśadiśi loke gacchati / na ca ahetuko buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kāyaḥ / pūrvacaryāpariniṣpanno hetupratyayādhīnaḥ kāraṇasamutpannaḥ pūrvakarmavipākādutpannaḥ / sa na kvaciddaśadiśi loke 'sti / api tu khalu punaryeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ satāṃ kāyābhiniṣpattirbhavati, teṣāṃ pratyayānāmasatāṃ kāyābhiniṣpattirna prajñāyate / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra vīṇāyāḥ śabda utpadyamāno na kutaścidāgacchati, nirudhyamāno 'pi na kvacidgacchati, na kvacitsaṃkrāmati, pratītya ca hetupratyayasāmagrīmutpadyate hetvadhīnaḥ pratyayādhīnaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma droṇīṃ ca pratītya carma ca pratītya tantrīś ca pratītya daṇḍaṃ ca pratītya upadhānīś ca pratītya koṇaṃ ca pratītya puruṣasya ca tajjavyāyāmaṃ pratītya evamayaṃ vīṇāyāḥ śabdo niścarati hetvadhīnaḥ pratyayādhīnaḥ / sa ca śabdo na droṇyā niścarati, na carmaṇo na tantrībhyo na daṇḍānnopadhānībhyo na koṇānna puruṣasya tajjavyāyāmataḥ śabdo niścarati, api tu khalu punaḥ sarveṣāṃ samāyogācchabdaḥ prajñapyate / nirudhyamāno 'pi śabdo na kvacidgacchati / evameva kulaputra buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kāyaniṣpattirhetvadhīnā pratyayādhīnā anekakuśalamūlaprayogapariniṣpannā ca / na caikato hetuto na caikataḥ pratyayato na caikataḥ kuśalamūlato buddhakāyaprabhāvanā / na ca nairhetukī /
body.translated_text: Arisen through the conjunction of many causes and conditions, it has not come from anywhere. When the conjunction of causes and conditions does not exist, it does not go anywhere. Thus, son of good family, should you understand the coming and going of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Son of good family, you should follow this very <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things) regarding all <s>dharmas</s> as well. When, son of good family, you thus truly understand <s>Tathāgatas</s> and all <s>dharmas</s> as unborn and unceased, then you will become determined in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. You will practice with certainty in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and in skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>)."

body.text:
bahuhetupratyayasāmagryāṃ samutpannā sā na kutaścidāgacchati / hetupratyayasāmagryāmasatyāṃ na kvacidgacchati / evaṃ tvayā kulaputra teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmāgamanaṃ ca gamanaṃ ca draṣṭavyam / sarvadharmāṇām api kulaputra
tvayā iyameva dharmatā anugantavyā / yataḥ kulaputra tvamevaṃ tathāgatāṃś ca sarvadharmāṃś ca anutpannānaniruddhāṃś ca saṃprajñāsyasi, tatastvaṃ niyato bhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / prajñāpāramitāyāmupāyakauśalye ca niyataṃ cariṣyasi //
body.translated_text: When this teaching on the non-coming and non-going of <s>Tathāgatas</s> was being spoken, there was a great earthquake. The entire great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system quaked in six ways with ten great signs—it trembled, trembled greatly, trembled very greatly; it shook, shook greatly, shook very greatly; it quivered, quivered greatly, quivered very greatly; it rumbled, rumbled greatly, rumbled very greatly; it roared, roared greatly, roared very greatly; it thundered, thundered greatly, thundered very greatly. And all the realms of <s>Māra</s> were agitated and became crooked. And whatever grasses, shrubs, herbs, and trees there were in the great three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system—all of them bent toward <s>Dharmodgata</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. And they released untimely flowers. And from above, from the sky, a great rain of flowers fell. And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the four great kings showered and scattered and besprinkled <s>Dharmodgata</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> with divine sandalwood powder and divine flowers. And they spoke these words: "Well said, well said, son of good family! Through your power, son of good family, today we have heard being taught a discourse arisen from the ultimate truth, contrary to the whole world, in which all beings established in the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and all beings fixated on wrong views have no footing."

body.text: asmin khalu punastathāgatānāmanāgatyagamananirdeśe bhāṣyamāṇe mahān bhūmicālo 'bhūt / sarvaś ca trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāramahādaśamahānimittaṃ kampate prakampate saṃprakampate, calati pracalati saṃpracalati, vedhate pravedhate saṃpravedhate, raṇati praraṇati saṃpraraṇati, kṣubhyati prakṣubhyati saṃprakṣubhyati, garjati pragarjati saṃpragarjati sma / sarvāṇi ca mārabhavanāni saṃkṣobhitāni jihmībhūtāni cābhūvan / ye kecana trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ, te sarve yena dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvastena praṇatā abhūvan / akālapuṣpāṇi cotsṛjanti sma / upariṣṭācca antarīkṣānmahāpuṣpavarṣaḥ prāvarṣat / śakraś ca devānāmindraścatvāraś ca mahārājāno dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ divyaiścandanacūrṇairdivyaiś ca puṣpairavākiran abhyavākiran abhiprākiran / evaṃ ca vācamabhāṣanta - sādhu sādhu kulaputra / tava kulaputra anubhāvena adyāsmābhiḥ paramārthanirjātā kathā deśyamānā śrutā sarvalokavipratyanīkā, yatrābhūmiḥ sarvasatkāyadṛṣṭipratiṣṭhitānāṃ sarvāsaddṛṣṭyabhiviniviṣṭānāṃ sattvānām //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>: "What, son of good family, is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of this great earthquake in the world?" The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> said: "Son of good family, through this teaching on the non-coming and non-going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>—through your asking and my explaining—eight thousand beings attained the patience for the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>). And eighty million beings generated the mind directed toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - kaḥ punaḥ kulaputra atra hetuḥ, kaḥ pratyayo 'sya mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvāya? dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva āha - imaṃ kulaputra tathāgatānāmanāgatyagamananirdeśaṃ tava ca pṛcchato mama ca nirdiśato 'ṣṭānāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt / aśīteś ca prāṇiniyutānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannāni, catuḥṣaṣṭeś ca prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ virajāṃsi vigatamalāni dharmeṣu dharmacakṣūṃṣi viśuddhāni //
body.translated_text: And sixty-four thousand beings had their <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (dharma-eyes) purified, free from dust, free from stain, regarding <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ paramodāreṇa prītiprāmodyena samanvāgato 'bhūt - lābhā me paramasulabdhāḥ, yasya me prajñāpāramitāmimaṃ ca tathāgatānāmanāgatyagamananirdeśaṃ paripṛcchataḥ iyatāṃ sattvānāmarthaḥ kṛtaḥ / etadevāsmākaṃ paryāptaṃ kuśalaṃ bhavedanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ pariniṣpattaye / na ca me bhūyo vicikitsā pravartate 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ / niḥsaṃśayamahaṃ tathāgato bhaviṣyāmyarhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / sa tenaiva prītiprāmodyena samanvāgataḥ saptatālaṃ vihāyasamabhyudgamya saptatāle sthitvā evaṃ cintayati sma - kenāhametarhi antarīkṣe sthitaḥ dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ satkuryāmiti? atha khalu śakro devānāmindra sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamabhyudgataṃ dṛṣṭvā cetasaiva cāsya cittamājñāya divyāni cāsmai māndāravāṇi puṣpāṇyupanāmayati sma, evaṃ cāvocat - ebhistvaṃ kulaputra divyaiḥ puṣpairdharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> was filled with supreme and noble joy and gladness: 'My gains are supremely well-gained—that while asking about <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and this teaching on the non-coming and non-going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the welfare of so many beings has been accomplished. This alone would be sufficient wholesome merit for the perfection of unsurpassed perfect awakening. And no more doubt arises in me about unsurpassed perfect awakening. Without doubt, I shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One.' Filled with that very joy and gladness, he rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees, and standing at the height of seven palm trees, he thought: 'With what shall I, standing in the sky, honor the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>?' Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, seeing the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> risen aloft and knowing his mind with his own mind, offered him divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers and said thus: 'With these divine flowers, O son of good family, honor the <s>bodhisattva</s>—'

body.text: mahāsattvaṃ satkuru / satkartavyo hi kulaputra asmābhistava parigrāhakaḥ / tava hi kulaputra anubhāvena adya bahūnāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāmarthaḥ kṛtaḥ / durlabhāḥ kulaputra evaṃrūpāḥ sattvāḥ, ye sarvasattvānāṃ kṛtaśo 'prameyānasaṃkhyeyān kalpānutsahante mahāntaṃ bhāramudvoḍhuṃ yathā tvayā utsoḍham //
body.translated_text: '—<s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. For, O son of good family, your benefactor is to be honored by us. For through your power, O son of good family, the welfare of many thousands of living beings has today been accomplished. Rare, O son of good family, are such beings who, for the sake of all beings, are willing to bear a great burden for immeasurable and incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, as you have borne it.'

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śakrasya devānāmindrasyāntikānmāndāravāṇi puṣpāṇi gṛhītvā dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamavākirat, abhyavākirat, abhiprākirat / svakena ca kāyena dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamabhicchādayati sma / evaṃ ca vācamabhāṣata - eṣo 'haṃ kulaputra adyāgreṇa tavātmānaṃ niryātayāmi upasthānaparicaryāyai / sa ātmānaṃ niryātya dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya purataḥ prāñjaliṃ kṛtvāsthāt //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, having received the <s>māndārava</s> flowers from <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, scattered them, showered them, and strewed them upon the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. And he covered the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> with his own body. And he spoke these words: 'I, O son of good family, from this day forward offer myself to you for service and attendance.' Having offered himself, he stood before the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> with palms joined.

body.text: atha khalu sā śreṣṭhidārikā tāni ca pañca dārikāśatāni sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - etā vayam api kulaputra tavātmānaṃ niryātayāmaḥ, vayamapyanena kuśalamūlena eteṣāmeva dharmāṇāṃ lābhinyo bhavema, tvayaiva ca sārdhaṃ punaḥ punarbuddhāṃś ca bhagavato bodhisattvāṃś ca satkuryāma gurukuryāma / āsannībhūtāś ca tavaiva bhavema / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śreṣṭhidārikāṃ tāni ca pañca dārikāśatānyetadavocat - yadi me yūyaṃ dārikā adhyāśayamanuvartadhvam, adhyāśayena ca mahyamātmānaṃ niryātayata, evamahaṃ yuṣmān pratīccheyam / dārikā āhuḥ - anuvartiṣyāmahe tava vayamāśayenādhyāśayena ca / vayaṃ tavātmānaṃ niryātayāmo yathecchākaraṇīyatāyai / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāni śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhāni pañca dārikāśatāni sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitāni kṛtvā tāni ca pañca rathaśatānyalaṃkṛtya sarvāṇi ca tāni dharmodgatāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya niryātayati sma upasthānaparicaryāyaiḥ - imāḥ kulaputra ahaṃ tavopasthāyikā niryātayāmi, imāni ca pañca rathaśatāni niryātayāmi paribhogāyeti //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant's daughter and those five hundred maidens said this to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'We too, O son of good family, offer ourselves to you. May we too, through this wholesome root, become recipients of these very <s>dharmas</s>, and together with you, again and again honor and revere <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And may we always remain near to you.' Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> said this to the merchant's daughter and those five hundred maidens: 'If you, O maidens, follow my resolve and offer yourselves to me with sincere aspiration, then I shall accept you.' The maidens said: 'We shall follow your intention and aspiration. We offer ourselves to you, to be used as you wish.' Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, having adorned those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter with all ornaments, and having decorated those five hundred chariots, offered them all to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> for service and attendance: 'I offer these attendants to you, O son of good family, and I offer these five hundred chariots for your use.'

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindrastasmai kulaputrāya sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu kulaputra / bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sarvasvaparityāgibhirbhavitavyam / evaṃrūpeṇa ca tyāgacittena bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / evaṃ ca dharmabhāṇakāṇāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā śakyaṃ prajñāpāramitāmupāyakauśalyaṃ ca śrotum / tair api kulaputra paurvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caradbhirevaṃrūpa eva tyāge sthitvā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ samudānītā prajñāpāramitāmupāyakauśalyaṃ ca paripraśnayadbhiriti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, gave his approval to that son of good family: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! <s>Bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> should be those who give up everything. With such a generous mind, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> quickly attains unsurpassed perfect awakening. And by making such offerings to <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, it is possible to hear <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means). Those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones too, when formerly practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> course, standing in just such generosity, attained unsurpassed perfect awakening while asking about <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāni śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhāni pañca dārikāśatāni pañca rathaśatāni sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kuśalaparipūrimupādāya pratigṛhṇīte sma / pratigṛhya ca sadāpraruditāyaiva kulaputrāya pratiniryātayāmāsa / atha khalu dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanāt svakaṃ gṛhaṃ prāvikṣat sūryasya cāstaṃgamanakālo 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> accepted those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter and the five hundred chariots for the fulfillment of <s>Sadāprarudita</s> <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s wholesome merit. Having accepted them, he gave them back to the son of good family <s>Sadāprarudita</s> himself. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> rose from his seat, entered his own dwelling, and the time of sunset arrived.

body.text: atha khalu sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaitadabhūt - naitanmama sādhu pratirūpaṃ bhavet, yadahaṃ dharmakāmatayā āgatya niṣīdeyam, śayyāṃ ca parikalpayeyam / yannvahaṃ dvābhyāmeva
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'It would not be good or fitting for me, having come out of desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, to sit down or prepare a bed. I should rather spend the time in just two postures—

body.text: īryāpathābhyāṃ sthitvā sthānena caṃkrameṇa ca kālamatināmayeyam, yāvaddharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svakādgṛhānnirgato bhaviṣyati yaduta dharmasaṃprakāśanāyeti //
body.translated_text: —standing and walking—until the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> comes out from his dwelling to teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sapta varṣāṇyekasamādhisamāpanna evābhūt / aprameyairasaṃkhyeyairbodhisattvasamādhisahasraiḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyanirjātairvyāhārṣīt / sadāprarudito 'pi bodhisattvo mahāsattva sapta varṣāṇi dvābhyāmeva īryāpathābhyāṃ kālamatināmayan na styānamiddhamavakrāmayāmāsa / sapta varṣāṇi ca kāmavitarkamutpādayāmāsa, na vyāpādavitarkaṃ na vihiṃsāvitarkamutpādayāmāsa, na rasagṛddhiṃ na cittaudbilyamutpādayāmāsa / api tu kadā nāma dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'smātsamādhervyutthāsyati, yannu vayaṃ dharmodgatasya bodhisattva mahāsattvasya dharmāsanaṃ prajñapayiṣyāmaḥ, yatrāsau kulaputro niṣadya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyatīti / taṃ ca pṛthivīpradeśaṃ susiktaṃ sumṛṣṭaṃ ca kariṣyāmo nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇam, yatra pṛthivīpradeśe dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāmupāyakauśalyaṃ ca saṃprakāśayiṣyatīti cintayāmāsa / tāny api śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhāni pañca dārikāśatāni sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyānuśikṣamāṇāni dvābhyāmeva īryāpathābhyāṃ kālamatināmayāmāsuḥ sarvāḥ kriyāstasyānuvartamānāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> entered a single <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) for seven years. He was absorbed in immeasurable, incalculable thousands of <s>bodhisattva-samādhis</s> born from <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s>. The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> too, for seven years, spent the time in just two postures and did not succumb to torpor and drowsiness. For seven years he did not generate any thought of sensual desire, nor thoughts of ill-will, nor thoughts of harmfulness; he did not generate craving for tastes nor mental elation. Rather, his only thought was: 'When will the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> arise from this <s>samādhi</s>? We shall then prepare a <s>Dharma</s>-seat for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, where that son of good family, being seated, will teach the <s>Dharma</s>.' And he thought: 'We shall make that spot of earth well-sprinkled, well-swept, and strewn with various flowers, where the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> will expound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s>.' Those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter too, following the example of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, spent the time in just two postures, following all his practices.

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo divyaṃ nirghoṣamaśrauṣīt - itaḥ saptame divase dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'smātsamādhervyutthāsyati, vyutthāya ca madhyenagarasya niṣadya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyatīti / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastaṃ divyaṃ nirghoṣaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātastaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ śodhayāmāsa sārdhaṃ śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhaiḥ pañcadārikāśataiḥ, dharmāsanaṃ ca prajñapayāmāsa saptaratnamayam, svakaṃ cottarāsaṅgaṃ kāyādavatārya tasyāsanasyopari prajñapayati sma / atha khalu tā dārikāḥ svakasvakānuttarāsaṅgān kāyādavatārya pañcottarāsaṅgaśatāni tatrāsane prajñapayāmāsuḥ atrāsane dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvo niṣadya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyatīti / evaṃ tāś ca sarvā dārikā dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dharmāsanamāstīrya tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasya jātā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> heard a divine voice: 'Seven days from now, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> will arise from this <s>samādhi</s>, and having arisen, he will sit in the middle of the city and teach the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, having heard that divine voice, became pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with happiness and gladness, and he cleaned that spot of earth together with the five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter. He prepared a <s>Dharma</s>-seat made of the seven precious substances, and removing his own upper robe from his body, he spread it upon that seat. Then those maidens too, removing their own upper robes from their bodies, spread five hundred upper robes upon that seat, thinking: 'On this seat the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> will sit and teach the <s>Dharma</s>.' Thus all those maidens, having spread the <s>Dharma</s>-seat for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, became pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with happiness and gladness.

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ sektukāmaḥ / na codakaṃ samantātparyeṣamāṇo 'pi labhate, yena taṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ siñcet / yathāpi nāma māreṇa pāpīyasā tatsarvamudakamantardhāpitamabhūt, apyeva nāma asya sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyodakamalabhamānasya cittaṃ khidyeta, duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ ca bhavet, cittasya vā anyathātvaṃ bhavet, yenāsya kuśalamūlasyāntardhānaṃ bhavet, na vā pūjā bhrājeran //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> wished to sprinkle that spot of earth. But searching everywhere, he could not find any water with which to sprinkle it. For <s>Māra</s> the Evil One had caused all the water to disappear, thinking: 'Perhaps this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, unable to find water, will become distressed, and grief and sorrow will arise, or his mind will change, whereby his wholesome roots may be destroyed, or his offerings may not shine forth.'

body.text: atha khalu sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaitadabhūt - yannvahamātmanaḥ kāyaṃ viddhvā imaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ rudhireṇa siñceyam / tatkasya hetoḥ? ayaṃ hi pṛthivīpradeśa uddhatarajaskaḥ / mā rajodhāturito bhūpradeśāddharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kāye nipatet / kiṃ vā anenātmabhāvenāvaśyaṃ bhedanadharmiṇā kuryām? varaṃ khalu punarmamāyaṃ kāya
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'I shall pierce my own body and sprinkle this spot of earth with my blood. Why is that? For this spot of earth has dust rising from it. Let not the dust from this patch of ground fall upon the body of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. And what would I do with this body that is subject to breaking anyway? Rather, let this body of mine—'

body.text: evaṃrūpayā kriyayā vinaśyatu, na tu niḥsāmarthyakriyayā / api ca kāmahetoḥ kāmanidānaṃ bahūni me ātmabhāvasahasrāṇi punaḥ punaḥ saṃsāre saṃsarato bhinnāni, na punarevaṃrūpeṣu sthāneṣu saddharmaparigrahasya kṛtaśaḥ / yadi punarbhidyante, kāmamevaṃrūpeṣu bhidyantāmiti / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattva iti pratisaṃkhyāya tīkṣṇaṃ śastraṃ gṛhītvā svakāyaṃ samantato viddhvā taṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ svarudhireṇa sarvamasiñcat / tāny api śreṣṭhidārikāpramukhāni pañcadārikāśatāni sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyānuśikṣamāṇāni sarvāṇi tāni tīkṣṇāni śastrāṇi gṛhītvā svakasvakāni śarīrāṇi viddhvā taṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ svakasvakairlohitaiḥ sarvamasiñcan / na ca sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tāsāṃ vā sarvāsāṃ dārikāṇāṃ cittasyānyathātvamabhūt, yatra sa māraḥ pāpīyānavatāraṃ labhet kuśalamūlāntarāyakaraṇāya //
body.translated_text: '—perish through such an act, rather than through an act of helplessness. Moreover, for the sake of sensual desires, on account of desires, many thousands of my bodily existences have been destroyed again and again as I wandered in <s>saṃsāra</s>—but never for the sake of embracing the true <s>Dharma</s> in such circumstances. If they must be destroyed, let them be destroyed in circumstances such as these!' Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, having thus reflected, took a sharp weapon and pierced his own body all over, and sprinkled that entire spot of earth with his own blood. Those five hundred maidens led by the merchant's daughter too, following the example of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, all took sharp weapons, pierced their own bodies, and sprinkled that entire spot of earth with their own blood. And neither in the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> nor in any of those maidens did any change of mind occur by which <s>Māra</s> the Evil One might find an opening to obstruct their wholesome roots.

body.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhūt - āścaryaṃ yāvaddharmakāmaścāyaṃ sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, yāvaddṛḍhasamādānaś ca yāvanmahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhaś ca anapekṣaḥ kāye jīviteṣu bhogeṣu ca, anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheradhigamāya adhyāśayasaṃprasthitaḥ / yaduta sarvasattvān mocayiṣyāmyaparimāṇataḥ saṃsāraduḥkhādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeti / atha khalu śakro devānāmindrastatsarvaṃ lohitodakaṃ divyaṃ candanodakamadhyatiṣṭhat, samantācca tasya pṛthivīpradeśasya acintyaṃ paramodāraṃ gandhaṃ yasya divyasya candanodakasya paripūrṇam / yojanaśataṃ gandho vāti //
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>: 'Wondrous indeed is how much this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> loves the <s>Dharma</s>, how firm is his resolve, how great is the armor he has donned, without regard for body, life, or possessions, having set forth with aspiration toward the attainment of unsurpassed perfect awakening, thinking: "I shall liberate all beings without limit from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening."' Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, transformed all that blood-water into divine sandalwood water, and all around that spot of earth was filled with the wondrous and supremely noble fragrance of that divine sandalwood water. The fragrance wafted for a hundred <s>yojanas</s>.

body.text: atha śakro devānāmindraḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputra / sādhu te kulaputra acintyaṃ vīryam, sādhvī ca te anuttarā dharmakāmatā dharmaparīṣṭiś ca / evaṃrūpeṇa kulaputra adhyāśayena evaṃrūpeṇa vīryeṇa evaṃrūpayā ca dharmakāmatayā taiḥ paurvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ samudānītā //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, said this to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! Well done is your inconceivable vigor, O son of good family, and well done is your unsurpassed desire for the <s>Dharma</s> and your quest for the <s>Dharma</s>. O son of good family, with just such aspiration, just such vigor, and just such desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones attained unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: atha khalu sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaitadabhūt - prajñaptaṃ mayā dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dharmāsanam / ayaṃ ca pṛthivīpradeśaḥ susiktaḥ susaṃmṛṣṭaś ca kṛtaḥ / kuto nu khalvahaṃ puṣpāṇi labheyam, yairahamimaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇaṃ kuryām, dharmodgataṃ ca bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ dharmaṃ deśayantaṃ dharmāsane niṣaṇṇamabhyavakireyam? atha khalu śakro devānāmindraḥ sadāpraruditaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - imāni te kulaputra pratigṛhāṇa divyāni māndāravāṇi puṣpāṇi / ebhistvamimaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇaṃ kuru, dharmodgataṃ ca bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ dharmaṃ deśayantaṃ dharmāsane niṣaṇṇamabhyavakira / sa tasmai divyaṃ khārīsahasraṃ divyānāṃ māndāravapuṣpāṇāmupanāmayati sma / atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāni puṣpāṇi gṛhītvā anyataraiḥ puṣpaistaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇamakārṣīt, anyataraiś ca puṣpairdharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamabhyavākirat //
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>: "I have prepared a <s>dharma</s>-seat for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>. And this spot of ground has been well sprinkled and well swept. But where might I obtain flowers with which I could scatter this spot of ground with flowers, and [honor] <s>Dharmodgata</s>—"

body.text: atha khalu dharmodgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saptānāṃ varṣāṇāmatyayena tataḥ samādhervyutthāya yena dharmāsanaṃ tenopasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat, anekaśatasahasrayā parṣadā parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ deśayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, at the end of seven years, arose from that <s>samādhi</s>, approached the <s>dharma</s>-seat, and sat down on the prepared seat. Surrounded and attended by an assembly of many hundreds of thousands, he taught the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sahadarśanenaiva dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tādṛśaṃ sukhaṃ pratilabhate sma, tadyathāpi nāma prathamadhyānasamāpanna ekāgramanasikāro bhikṣuḥ / tatreyaṃ dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitādeśanāyaduta sarvadharmasamatayā prajñāpāramitāsamatā / sarvadharmaviviktatayā prajñāpāramitāviviktatā / sarvadharmācalanatayā prajñāpāramitācalanatā / sarvadharmāmananatayā prajñāpāramitāmananatā / sarvadharmāstambhitatayā prajñāpāramitāstambhitatā / savadharmaikarasatayā prajñāpāramitaikarasatā / sarvadharmāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / sarvadharmānutpādatayā prajñāpāramitānutpādatā / sarvadharmānirodhatayā prajñāpāramitānirodhatā / gaganāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / samudrāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / meruvicitratayā prajñāpāramitāvicitratā / gaganākalpanatayā prajñāpāramitākalpanatā / rūpāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / pṛthivīdhātvaparyantatatā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / evamabdhātutejodhātuvāyudhātvākāśadhātvaparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / vijñānadhātvaparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / vajropamadharmasamatayā prajñāpāramitāsamatā / sarvadharmāsaṃbhedanatayā prajñāpāramitāsaṃbhedanatā / sarvadharmānupalabdhitayā prajñāpāramitānupalabdhitā / sarvadharmābhibhāvanāsamatayā prajñāpāramitābhibhāvanāsamatā / sarvadharmaniśceṣṭatayā prajñāpāramitāniśceṣṭatā / sarvadharmācintyatayā prajñāpāramitācintyatā veditavyeti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, upon merely seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>, experienced such happiness as a monk who has entered the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) with one-pointed attention. And this teaching of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s> was namely [concerning] all <s>dharmas</s>—

body.text: atha khalu sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tathāniṣaṇṇasyaiva tasyāṃ belāyāṃ sarvadharmasamatā nāma samādhirājo jātaḥ / yataḥ sarvadharmaviviktaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmācalanaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmāmananaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmāstambhitaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmaikarasaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmāparyantaś ca nāma samādhi, sarvadharmānutpādaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmānirodhaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, gaganāparyataś ca nāma samādhiḥ, samudrāparyantaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, meruvicitraś ca nāma samādhiḥ, gaganākalpaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, rūpāparyantaś ca nāma samādhiḥ / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānāparyantaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, pṛthivīdhātvaparyantaśva nāma samādhiḥ, evamabdhātutejodhātuvāyudhātvākāśadhātvaparyantaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, vijñānadhātvaparyantaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, vajropamaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmāsaṃbhedaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmānupalabdhiś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmāvibhāvanāsamatā ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmaniśceṣṭaś ca nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmācintyaś ca nāma samādhiḥ / evaṃpramukhāni ṣaṣṭiḥ samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇi sadāpraruditena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pratilabdhānyabhūvanniti //
body.translated_text: Then, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> was seated thus, at that very moment there arose in him the king of <s>samādhis</s> called 'equality of all <s>dharmas</s>'; and the <s>samādhi</s> called 'detachment from all <s>dharmas</s>'; and the <s>samādhi</s> called 'immovability of all <s>dharmas</s>'; and the <s>samādhi</s> called 'non-ideation of all <s>dharmas</s>'; and the <s>samādhi</s> called 'stability of all <s>dharmas</s>'; and the <s>samādhi</s> [called 'all <s>dharmas</s>']—

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ dharmodgataparivarto nāmaikatriṃśattamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the Thirty-First Chapter, called "The Chapter on <s>Dharmodgata</s>," in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

body.text: ASP_32: parīndanāparivarto dvātriṃśattamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter Thirty-Two: The Chapter on Entrustment.

body.text: sahapratilabdhānāṃ ca subhūte ṣaṣṭyāḥ samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇāṃ sadāprarudito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi, dakṣiṇasyāṃ paścimāyāmuttarasyāṃ diśi, vidikṣu adha ūrdhvaṃ ca diśi daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopamān buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyati sma bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtān bodhisattvaguṇapuraskṛtān etaireva nayairebhireva nāmabhiretairevākṣarairimāmeva prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣamāṇān / tadyathāpi nāma ahametarhi asminneva trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau dharmaṃ deśayāmi bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛto bodhisattvagaṇapuraskṛtaḥ, ebhireva nayairebhireva nāmabhirebhirevākṣarairimāmeva prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣe / so 'cintyena bāhuśrutyena śrutasāgaratayā ca samanvāgato 'bhūt, sarvāsu ca jātiṣu na jātu buddhavirahito 'bhūt / yatra yatra buddhā bhagavantaḥ saṃmukhībhūtā bhavanti, tatra tatropapadyate sma / avirahitaś ca bhavati sma buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ, antataḥ svapnāntaragato 'pi / sarve ca anena akṣaṇā vivarjitāḥ, kṣaṇasaṃpaccārāgitā //
body.translated_text: And, <s>Subhūti</s>, together with the sixty hundred thousand <s>samādhi</s> doors he simultaneously obtained, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s>, in the eastern direction, the southern, western, and northern directions, in the intermediate directions, below and above—in the ten directions—in <s>Ganges</s>-river-sand-like numbers of tri-thousand great-thousand world systems, beheld <s>Ganges</s>-river-sand-like numbers of <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones—

body.text: tatra khalu punarbhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma - tadanenāpi te ānanda paryāyeṇa evaṃ veditavyam - ityapīyaṃ prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ sarvajñajñānasyāhāriketi / tasmāttarhi ānanda bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sarvajñajñānaṃ pratilabdhukāmairasyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritavyam / iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā deśayitavyopadeṣṭavyoddeṣṭavyā svādhyātavyā likhitavyā / tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena mahāpustake pravyaktapravyaktairakṣaraiḥ sulikhitāṃ kṛtvā satkartavyā gurukartavyā mānayitavyā pūjayitavyā arcayitavyā apacāyitavyā puṣpairdhūpairgandhairmālyairvilepanaiścūrṇaiścīvarairvādyairvastraiśchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ, samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ, bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ / iyamasmākamantikādānanda anuśāsanī / tatkasya hetoḥ? atra hi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarvajñajñānapariniṣpattirbhaviṣyati / tatkiṃ manyase ānanda śāstā te tathāgataḥ? ānanda āha - śāstā me bhagavan, śāstā me sugata / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - śāstā te ānanda tathāgataḥ / paricarito 'smyānanda tvayā maitreṇa kāyakarmaṇā manaāpena, maitreṇa vākkarmaṇā manaāpena, maitreṇa manaḥkarmaṇā manaāpena / tasmāttarhi ānanda yathaiva tvayā mamaitarhi tiṣṭhato dhriyamāṇasya yāpayato 'smin samucchraye prema ca prasādaś ca gauravaṃ ca kṛtam, tathaiva tvayā ānanda mamātyayādasyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ kartavyam / dvir api trir api te ānanda parīndāmi anuparīndāmi enāṃ prajñāpāramitām, yatheyaṃ nāntardhīyeta, yathā nāsyāṃ tvamanyaḥ puruṣaḥ syāḥ / yāvadānanda iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā loke pracariṣyati, tāvattathāgatastiṣṭhatīti veditavyam / tāvattathāgato dharmaṃ deśayatīti veditavyam / avirahitāste ānanda sattvā buddhadarśanena dharmaśravaṇena saṃghopasthānena ca veditavyam / tathāgatāntikāvacarāste ānanda sattvā veditavyāḥ, ya enāṃ prajñāpāramita
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "By this method too, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should understand that this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the nourishment for the <s>sarvajñajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge) of <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who wish to attain <s>sarvajñajñāna</s> should practice in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—"

body.text: śroṣyantyudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti pravartayiṣyanti deśayiṣyantyupadekṣyantyuddekṣyanti svādhyāsyanti likhiṣyanti satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyantyarcayiṣyantyapacāyiṣyanti puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ, samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ, bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiriti //
body.translated_text: "—they will hear, take up, retain, recite, master, propagate, teach, instruct, explain, study, write, honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and esteem it, with flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, unguents, powder, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and pennants—"

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān āttamanāḥ / te ca maitreyapramukhā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ āyuṣmāṃś ca subhūtirāyuṣmāṃś ca śāriputraḥ āyuṣmāṃścānandaḥ śakraś ca devānāmindraḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One, delighted. And those <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> led by <s>Maitreya</s>, and the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the Gods, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ parīndanāparivarto nāma dvātriṃśattamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the Thirty-Second Chapter, called "The Chapter on Entrustment," in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //

body.text: samāptā ceyaṃ bhagavatyā āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitā sarvatathāgatajananī bodhisattvapratyekajinaśrāvakāṇāṃ mātā, dharmamudrā dharmolkā dharmanābhirdharmabherī dharmanetrī dharmaratnanidhānam akṣayo dharmaḥ acintyādbhutadarśananakṣatramālā sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvalokavanditā sarvasukhaheturiti //
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the Blessed Mother of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Mother of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>—the Seal of the <s>Dharma</s>, the Torch of the <s>Dharma</s>, the Hub of the <s>Dharma</s>, the Drum of the <s>Dharma</s>, the Guide of the <s>Dharma</s>, the Treasury of the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, the Inexhaustible <s>Dharma</s>, the Inconceivable and Wonderful Garland of Stars, venerated by the world of gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, the Cause of All Happiness—

body.text: prajñāpāramitāṃ samyagudgṛhya paryavāpya ca dhārayitvā pravartya enāṃ viharantu sadārthina iti //
body.translated_text: Having properly taken up, mastered, retained, and propagated the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, may they abide in it, ever seeking its meaning. //

body.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhāvā hetusteṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
body.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes—their cause the <s>Tathāgata</s> has proclaimed;

body.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: And that which is their cessation—thus speaks the Great <s>Śramaṇa</s>. //

body.text: deyadharmo 'yaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyinyāḥ paramopāsikasaurājrasutalakṣmīdharasya / yadatra puṇyaṃ tadbhavatvācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṃgamaṃ kṛtvā sakalasattvarāśeranuttarajñānāvāptaye iti //
body.translated_text: This is the religious gift of the most excellent <s>Mahāyāna</s>-devoted supreme laywoman <s>Saurājrasutalakṣmīdhara</s>. Whatever merit there is herein, with teachers, preceptors, and parents foremost, may it be for the attainment of supreme knowledge by all assemblies of beings. //
